Consumer complaint narrative: I am writing to file a formal complaint against XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX # XXXX, located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, MO XXXX ) regarding what I believe to be unfair and potentially deceptive business practices related to a mortgage refinancing agreement. XXXX XXXX XXXX has Endeavor Capital , LLC as their legal corporate name. On or about XX/XX/year>, I received a letter ( attachment 1 ) with the header XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX. The letter notified me that I was pre-approved for a new federal guideline loan program with an additional {$30000.00} in cash and a new monthly payment of {$2200.00} at 5.25 % to 5.98 % APR, 30-year fixed. I wanted to know more about the offer and followed the contact information given in the letter which led me to a Loan Advisor by the name of XXXX XXXX. I disclosed to XXXX XXXX that I worked with XXXX XXXX XXXX at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX who originated the mortgage on my current property and that I was satisfied with her service. It was only later that I learned that XXXX XXXX worked for another institution ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ), not XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The letter that I received stated this fact but only in the small print on the back of the first page. I think this practice potentially misrepresents who is the service provider by seemingly hiding in fine print, and on the backside of a page, the letters originating entity. In talking to XXXX XXXX, I ( along with my wife ) proceeded with the refinancing process and timely complied with all requests for information and signing of documents. The company then told me that I qualified for specific loan terms ( attachment 2 ). They gave a current home loan estimate of {$370000.00}, a proposed new payment including escrow of {$3000.00}, an annual savings of {$4200.00}, stipulated cash that I would receive at closing {$3600.00} and an estimated refund post-closing of {$2400.00}. The new offer letter also stated that Our Bank has approval for XXXX {$0.00} required out of your pocket making this risk free to proceed with our Bank! -I agreed to these terms. This document was an offer, one that I accepted, it detailed considerable monetary value, and had the mutual intent to be legally bound ( in other words, a contract ). After investing considerable time and effort, and despite some unexplained delays by XXXX, I was told that we were clear for closing. Surprisingly, some 2 weeks later ( XX/XX/XXXX ), after being told that we were clear for closing I received an email stating some delays because the company was trying to secure for me with the lowest possible rate (? ). I found this surprising and unacceptable as I had been previously told that we were clear for closing. Furthermore, I was not a floater and had unequivocally agreed to the terms of XXXX initial offer. XXXX XXXX, in an email had even stated that our e-signing of the requested documents would lock in our rate. I approached XXXX XXXX regarding the changes to our agreement. He answered by sending me a new refinancing deal with a significant increase in financing rate. The same was unacceptable and disregarded most of our original agreement. XXXX XXXX said that I could walk away from the deal if I didnt like it. This event started my conversation with XXXX XXXX XXXX, the branch manager and Director of Sales Operations for XXXX. I spoke on the phone with XXXX XXXX XXXX who tried to explain to me why XXXX had changed the terms of the agreement. I found his arguments untruthful ; furthermore, his insistence on talking over the phone rather than providing a paper trail, was worrisome. After reaching no resolution I told him that I would be drafting a formal complaint with the CFPB and the Missouri Division of Finance. XXXX XXXX then spoke to one of the owners of XXXX and came back saying that they would honor the terms of our original loan. Unfortunately, the new contract, again, was significantly different from our original agreement. Due to my previous experience with XXXX XXXX, I insisted that he explained over email why the original agreement was not honored. XXXX XXXX stated that the changes were necessary because in our original agreement they had not procured a payoff amount for our mortgage and had no idea regarding the property taxes ( attachment 3 ). XXXX presumably needed to reassess all the fees once these quantities were known. This was an outward lie from XXXX XXXX as the payoff amount was clearly stated in their original letter of offer ( {$370.00}, XXXX ) and I had sent to XXXX XXXX the required information including that for taxes ( attachment 4 ). Thus, both payoff and taxes were already factored into the original offer. In addition, XXXX XXXX did not explain other disagreements with the original offer which stated {$0.00} required out-of-pocket, approximately {$6000.00} in refund money owed to me, etc. XXXX XXXX has acknowledged in a follow-up email that the original letter of offer was based on an FHA loan and that the recent offer from XXXX was structured on conventional financing. Thus far, this is the latest in a list of shifting explanations for their noncompliance with the terms of our original agreement, each one meant to trump the previous one. The lies per se denote the bad faith of XXXX in resolving our disagreement. Throughout my dealings with both XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX it has been repeatedly stressed to me that I have thus far not incurred in any out-of-pocket costs and that I am under no obligation to proceed with XXXX on the current XXXX. They have stated that I can walk away without any penalties. However, because of the XXXX 's actions, I have suffered significant financial harm and inconvenience, including the probable loss of refinancing ( rates have gone up substantially ) from which I was going to save {$4200.00} per year or {$120000.00} for the 30-year term of the loan. As a retired individual living on social security this is a significant amount of money. I believe that XXXX conduct constitutes a failure to act in good faith and raises concerns regarding the accuracy and transparency of its lending practices. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate this matter and assist in determining whether XXXX complied with applicable consumer protection laws and regulations. I also request that the company be required, if appropriate, to honor the terms of their original offer. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Let me know if you need any additional information. I appreciate your assistance and look forward to your response.
Issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Navy Federal Credit Unions denial of my fraud claim involving an unauthorized credit card transaction in the amount of {$1400.00}. On or about XX/XX/year>, I received notification that a charge for {$1400.00} had been placed on my Navy Federal XXXX Rewards credit card. I did not authorize, approve, or make this transaction. Upon receiving notification of the charge, I immediately contacted Navy Federal, reported the transaction as fraudulent, and filed a fraud claim. Navy Federal subsequently closed my card and issued a replacement card. The transaction was associated with a merchant identified as XXXX. I have never conducted business with this merchant. I do not use travel agencies and book all travel directly with airlines through their official applications or by contacting the airline directly. I received no travel itinerary, airline ticket, reservation, confirmation, or travel-related services associated with this transaction. After its investigation, Navy Federal denied my fraud claim, stating that no error had occurred. I requested additional information regarding the basis for the denial. Initially, Navy Federal responded that XXXX transaction data and its internal systems contradicted my claim of unauthorized activity but declined to provide specific details. After repeated requests for clarification, Navy Federal later informed me that its determination was based, at least in part, on records indicating that the transaction had been approved by text message from the phone number associated with my account. During a subsequent conversation with a Navy Federal representative, I was informed that an initial fraud alert had been declined and that a later alert had been approved. I reviewed my mobile phone billing records and confirmed that text activity occurred on the date in question from a five-digit short-code number. However, I do not recall receiving or responding to a fraud alert approving a {$1400.00} transaction with XXXX. The first notification I recall receiving was that a charge had already been placed on my account, at which point I immediately contacted Navy Federal and reported the transaction as unauthorized. Throughout this process, I have consistently maintained the following : I did not authorize, approve, or participate in this transaction. My credit card remained in my possession at all times. I have never conducted business with XXXX. I do not use travel agencies. I received no airline ticket, itinerary, reservation, confirmation, or travel-related services associated with this charge. I reported the transaction immediately upon becoming aware of it. Navy Federal closed and replaced my card following my fraud report. I also attempted to contact the merchant using the telephone number associated with the transaction but was unable to reach anyone. Additionally, I was unable to identify a verifiable business relationship between myself and the merchant. My concern is not that Navy Federal refuses to disclose proprietary fraud-detection methodologies. My concern is that despite multiple requests, Navy Federal has not provided meaningful responses to several critical factual questions that go directly to the basis of its determination. Specifically, I have requested clarification regarding : 1. Why was a second authorization request or fraud alert sent if the first fraud alert was reportedly declined? 2. What evidence exists that I received, used, or benefited from the travel services allegedly purchased through this transaction? 3. Did the merchant provide any passenger name records, airline ticket numbers, rental car/airlines reservation confirmations, itineraries, travel dates, email addresses, phone numbers, or other information connecting me to the services allegedly purchased? 4. What specific facts establish that I knowingly authorized this transaction beyond the assertion that a text response was received from the phone number associated with my account? Despite my requests, Navy Federal has repeatedly responded with generalized statements that its records contradict my claim while declining to address these specific questions. I respectfully request CFPB assistance in obtaining a substantive review of this matter and a clear explanation from Navy Federal regarding the factual basis for its determination that I authorized this transaction. I further request that Navy Federal address the specific questions outlined above and explain how it concluded that I knowingly authorized this charge despite my immediate fraud report, lack of any relationship with the merchant, and lack of receipt of any travel-related services. Thank you for your assistance and review of this complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative: For more than one year, I have been attempting to resolve a dispute with Bank of America concerning unauthorized transactions and the improper handling of my claims. Despite my repeated efforts, the bank 's procedural errors, inconsistent guidance, and mishandling of my case have prevented a fair resolution and have caused me significant financial and personal hardship. The root cause of this matter began when Bank of America incorrectly classified my case as a Fraud Claim ( Claim No. XXXX ) instead of a Billing Dispute. From the beginning, I explained that this was a billing dispute involving unauthorized and disputed transactions. However, the claim was processed under the wrong category, and every subsequent action was affected by that initial error. I followed the bank 's instructions in good faith. Bank representatives instructed me to contact the merchant first before pursuing my dispute with the bank. I followed those instructions, which resulted in substantial delays. Later, I was repeatedly told that certain claims could not be reviewed because more than 60 days had passed. Those delays were not caused by me ; they were the direct result of the bank 's incorrect guidance and handling of my case. After the original Fraud Claim was closed, it was later reopened without my request and then used to classify valid Billing Disputes as duplicate claims instead of reviewing each disputed transaction individually. This prevented a proper investigation of my disputes. The attached documents also reveal serious inconsistencies in the bank 's investigation. For example, one denial letter states that Bank of America was unable to locate a disputed transaction for {$990.00}. Nevertheless, the bank denied the dispute. I respectfully question how a claim can be denied when the bank itself acknowledges that it could not locate the transaction being disputed. Another denial relied on the 60-day notification period even though the bank 's own procedural errors and incorrect claim classification substantially contributed to the delay. It is fundamentally unfair to penalize a customer for delays caused by the institution responsible for handling the dispute. Throughout this process, I received conflicting information from multiple representatives. During one conversation, a representative repeatedly insisted that I did not owe the bank money because my credit card limit was approximately {$1000.00}. However, this completely overlooked the central issue. I repeatedly explained that a substantial portion of the disputed funds represented my own money that had been transferred from my checking account, not ordinary credit card borrowing. This important distinction was never properly understood or investigated. Bank of America eventually returned part of the disputed funds and issued temporary credits, demonstrating that at least some errors were recognized. However, many disputed transactions remain unresolved, and I believe they deserve the same thorough and impartial review. This matter has caused me significant financial hardship, emotional distress, damage to my financial stability, and countless hours spent attempting to correct mistakes that were not of my making. I have contacted customer service, claims departments, management, and executive offices. Despite these efforts, I have not received a complete and fair resolution. I am submitting this complaint because I believe Bank of America 's procedural failures, incorrect claim classification, inconsistent handling, and inadequate investigation deprived me of a fair opportunity to recover my funds. I respectfully request an independent review of the bank 's handling of this matter and appropriate corrective action.

Consumer complaint narrative: On or around XX/XX/year>, Chime automatically deducted {$300.00} from my checking account to repay an outstanding balance on my Instant Loan ( or SpotMe/MyPay advance feature ). The deduction occurred automatically because I had enabled the auto-pay / automatic repayment feature for the loan or advance. The {$300.00} was taken directly from a deposit of my VA disability compensation into the account. VA disability benefits are protected under federal law, specifically 38 U.S.C. 5301 ( the anti-alienation provision ), which states that these payments shall be exempt from the claim of creditors and shall not be liable to attachment, levy, or seizure by or under any legal or equitable process whatever, either before or after receipt by the beneficiary. Although I had authorized automatic repayment through the account terms, Chime should not have applied protected VA disability funds to satisfy the loan balance. This deduction violated the protections afforded to veterans disability compensation. I request that Chime immediately refund the full {$300.00} to my account, provide written confirmation that they will not offset or deduct from future VA disability deposits to repay this or any similar obligation, and update their systems and practices to properly identify and protect VA disability benefits from internal setoffs or automatic repayments.

Consumer complaint narrative: XXXX is continuing to report a fraudulent UpstartXXXX XXXX loan despite the existence of material evidence demonstrating that the very bank account Upstart relied upon to deny my identity-theft claim was itself fraudulent. Upstart previously claimed that loan proceeds were deposited into XXXX XXXX account ending in XXXX and further alleged that payments were made from that same account. Upstart relied upon alleged Plaid verification and the existence of the XXXX XXXX account as proof that I authorized, controlled, benefited from, and had knowledge of the loan. However, after conducting its own identity-theft investigation, XXXX XXXX issued a written determination dated XX/XX/year>, confirming that account ending in XXXX was part of a fraud claim and expressly stated that : I did not open the account. I had no knowledge of the account. I was released from any financial liability associated with the account. This evidence destroys the central basis upon which Upstart denied my identity-theft claim. If the account receiving the proceeds and allegedly making payments was itself fraudulent, then neither the disbursement of funds nor subsequent payments constitute evidence that I opened, authorized, controlled, or benefited from the loan. Despite the existence of this material evidence, XXXX continues reporting the Upstart account as a charged-off account on my consumer file. XXXX 's continued reporting of this account demonstrates either : A failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation ; XXXX upon inaccurate and unreliable information supplied by Upstart ; A refusal to consider material evidence from the originating bank itself ; or A willful disregard of the protections afforded to identity-theft victims under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. XXXX can not simply defer to Upstart when Upstart 's own basis for denying fraud has been disproven by XXXX XXXX. A consumer reporting agency has an independent obligation to assure maximum possible accuracy. Continuing to publish derogatory information after receiving evidence that undermines the furnisher 's conclusions is inconsistent with that obligation. Likewise, Upstart can not continue using a fraudulent XXXX XXXX account as evidence that I authorized this loan when XXXX XXXX itself has determined that I neither opened nor knew about that account. At this point, the continued furnishing and reporting of this account is not supported by competent evidence and renders the tradeline inaccurate, unreliable, and unverifiable. Upstart 's denial became untenable the moment XXXX XXXX institution whose account Upstart relied upondetermined that account ending in XXXX was itself fraudulent. XXXX 's continued publication of the account after the emergence of this evidence raises serious questions regarding whether either company conducted the reasonable investigation required by federal law. The proper remedy is not further verification, but permanent deletion.

Consumer complaint narrative: Subject : Failure to Explain Post-Complaint Cancellation of Force-Placed Insurance, Refund Calculation, and Related Account Adjustments I am submitting this complaint regarding Wells Fargo Bank , N.A.s handling of lender-placed hazard insurance imposed on my mortgage account and Wells Fargos subsequent failure to provide a complete explanation, supporting documentation, or accounting concerning the cancellation of that policy and the resulting refund. This complaint arises from events that occurred immediately after CFPB Complaint No. XXXX was submitted on XX/XX/2026. In CFPB Complaint No. XXXX, I raised specific concerns regarding the lender-placed insurance policy, including the retroactive placement of coverage, policy issuance dates, insurance-related accounting, premium charges, escrow treatment, and inconsistencies regarding the entities identified in Wells Fargos records. Rather than directly addressing those concerns, Wells Fargo later reported that the lender-placed insurance policy had been canceled and that a refund of approximately {$3500.00} had been received. The chronology of events is significant : XX/XX/2026 CFPB Complaint No. XXXX submitted. XX/XX/2026 According to the cancellation notice, the cancellation became effective at XXXXXXXX XXXX XX/XX/2026 Cancellation notice issued. XX/XX/2026 General Change Endorsement issued. XX/XX/2026 Hazard insurance refund processed. XX/XX/2026 Wells Fargo responded to the CFPB and disclosed that the policy had been canceled and that a refund had been received. Despite these events, Wells Fargo failed to explain the circumstances surrounding the cancellation, failed to provide supporting records, and failed to explain the accounting impact of the cancellation and refund. Most notably, Wells Fargo did not explain : Why the policy was canceled. What specific event triggered the cancellation. The date on which the cancellation decision was made. The identity of the individual, department, vendor, insurer, or third party that initiated, requested, approved, or authorized the cancellation. Whether the cancellation was related in any way to issues raised in CFPB Complaint No. XXXX. Whether the cancellation resulted from the foreclosure sale, post-sale review activity, insurer action, servicing review, internal audit, consumer complaint review, or any other event. Why the cancellation became effective XX/XX/2026. Why cancellation documentation was generated after the CFPB complaint was filed. Whether any deficiencies, inaccuracies, accounting errors, servicing errors, or documentation issues were identified during Wells Fargos review of the policy. Wells Fargo further failed to explain the refund that it admits was received. Specifically, Wells Fargo did not provide : The gross refund amount. The calculation supporting the refund. The dates used in calculating the refund. The period of coverage for which premiums were retained. The period of coverage for which premiums were refunded. Any calculation worksheets. Any insurer-provided refund statements. Any records reflecting receipt of refund proceeds. Any records reflecting application of refund proceeds. Any records identifying where the refunded funds were credited. Without these records, there is no way to independently determine whether the refund was accurately calculated, whether the refund was fully credited, or whether the account was properly adjusted following cancellation. The lack of accounting is particularly concerning because Wells Fargo previously charged approximately {$7400.00} in connection with the lender-placed insurance policy. Wells Fargo has therefore acknowledged : A substantial insurance charge. A subsequent cancellation. A subsequent refund. Yet Wells Fargo has not provided the underlying accounting necessary to determine : What amount was ultimately retained. What amount was ultimately refunded. How those figures were calculated. Whether all account balances were properly adjusted. Whether prior escrow calculations were revised. Whether prior default-related calculations were revised. Whether prior foreclosure-related calculations were revised. Whether prior servicing records were corrected. Wells Fargos response effectively asks the consumer and regulator to accept its conclusions without producing the records necessary to verify those conclusions. Equally concerning is the timing. The cancellation became effective only days after CFPB Complaint No. XXXX was submitted. A cancellation notice and endorsement were then generated. A refund was subsequently processed. However, Wells Fargos CFPB response does not explain whether those actions were already pending before the complaint was filed, whether they were initiated after the complaint was received, or whether they resulted from any review conducted in response to the complaint. The omission of this information prevents meaningful evaluation of the circumstances surrounding the cancellation and refund. Accordingly, I request that Wells Fargo provide : 1. The complete lender-placed insurance cancellation file. 2. All records reflecting the decision to cancel the policy. 3. All records identifying the reason for cancellation. 4. All records identifying the person ( s ), department ( s ), vendor ( s ), insurer ( s ), or third parties involved in initiating, requesting, authorizing, or approving the cancellation. 5. Documentation supporting the XX/XX/2026 effective cancellation date. 6. Documentation supporting the XX/XX/2026 cancellation notice. 7. Documentation supporting the XX/XX/2026 General Change Endorsement. 8. Documentation showing when the refund was calculated. 9. Documentation showing when the refund was received. 10. Documentation supporting the refund calculation. 11. Documentation showing where the refund was applied. 12. A complete transaction history and account ledger reflecting all entries associated with : the original lender-placed insurance charge ; all insurance-related advances ; all adjustments ; the cancellation ; the refund ; and all resulting account corrections. 13. Documentation showing the impact of the cancellation and refund on : escrow balances ; escrow shortages ; delinquency calculations ; default calculations ; foreclosure-related accounting ; payoff figures ; and all related servicing records. 14. A detailed explanation addressing why Wells Fargo failed to provide this information in response to CFPB Complaint No. XXXX. This complaint does not challenge Wells Fargos ability to state that a cancellation occurred. Rather, it concerns Wells Fargos failure to explain why the cancellation occurred, how the refund was calculated, how the account was adjusted, and why the supporting records have not been provided despite repeated requests. Until Wells Fargo produces the requested documentation, transaction records, accounting records, and supporting explanations, the circumstances surrounding the cancellation, refund, and resulting account adjustments remain unresolved and disputed. Accordingly, I request that the CFPB require Wells Fargo to provide a complete and substantive response supported by documentary evidence sufficient to verify the accuracy of its representations concerning the cancellation, refund, and related servicing activity.

Consumer complaint narrative: * * Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint * * * * Company : * * Sentry Recovery & Collections , Inc. * * Account Information * * * Balance Reported : {$7000.00} * Highest Balance Reported : {$5700.00} * Date Opened : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Account Status : Open Collection Account * Original Creditor : XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX Remark : Consumer Disputes This Account Information * * Complaint * * I am filing this complaint against Sentry Recovery & Collections , Inc. regarding a disputed collection account being reported on my consumer credit reports. This discrepancy raises serious questions regarding the accuracy of the information being furnished and whether additional charges, fees, penalties, or interest have been improperly added or inaccurately reported. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), furnishers of information are required to provide accurate and complete information to consumer reporting agencies. Furnishers may not furnish information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), upon receiving notice of a dispute, furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation and review all relevant information before continuing to report the account. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f, and 1692g, debt collectors may not use false, deceptive, misleading, unfair, or unconscionable means to collect debts. Debt collectors must possess sufficient documentation to validate the debt, establish the amount owed, and demonstrate their authority to collect it. I dispute this account and request that Sentry Recovery provide : 1. A copy of the signed lease agreement. 2. Documentation proving I am legally responsible for the alleged debt. 3. A complete itemized accounting of the balance. 4. Documentation explaining how the balance increased to {$7000.00} when the highest balance reported is {$5700.00}. 5. Documentation supporting any rent charges, lease termination fees, damage charges, cleaning charges, utility charges, legal fees, collection fees, penalties, or interest added to the account. 6. Documentation showing all payments, credits, security deposit credits, adjustments, and offsets applied to the account. 7. Move-out statements, inspection reports, invoices, repair receipts, photographs, and supporting records used to calculate the balance. 8. Documentation establishing Sentry Recovery 's authority to collect the debt. 9. Documentation establishing the date of first delinquency. 10. Copies of all records used during prior investigations or disputes. 11. Verification that all i nformation furnished to consumer reporting agencies complies with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Metro 2 reporting standards. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has repeatedly emphasized that debt collectors and furnishers must maintain adequate records supporting the accuracy and integrity of information reported to consumer reporting agencies. If Sentry Recovery can not provide competent evidence validating the debt and supporting the amount being reported, continued reporting may constitute the furnishing of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information. * * Requested Resolution * * I request that Sentry Recovery conduct a thorough investigation and provide complete documentation supporting the validity, ownership, and accuracy of the alleged debt. If the account can not be fully validated and verified, I request immediate deletion of the account from all consumer reporting agencies. I further request correction of any inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information currently being reported and written confirmation of the results of the investigation.

We are requesting assistance regarding a service error by JP Morgan Chase Bank that resulted in a wrongful foreclosure action against our home. We filed a XXXX XXXX bankruptcy in XX/XX/XXXX. We successfully completed all required payments under our confirmed plan, and the bankruptcy was discharged in XX/XX/XXXX. As part of the XXXX XXXX plan, Chase Bank was to receive approximately {$5200.00} in post-petition payments related to our second mortgage ( HELOC ). According to records from the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a series of payments were issued to Chase between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. Prior to bankruptcy, we had both a first mortgage and a second mortgage ( HELOC ) with Chase. During the bankruptcy, Chase transferred the first mortgage to another lender. After our bankruptcy discharge, we began receiving statements from Chase indicating that more than {$5000.00} remained due on the HELOC account. Because this amount closely matched the post-petition balance that had been paid through the XXXX XXXX plan, we repeatedly contacted Chase and requested that the account be researched and audited. As a result, Chase refused to properly credit the account, stopped accepting our regular monthly payments of approximately {$230.00}, returned our payment checks, and initiated foreclosure proceedings in XX/XX/XXXX based on an alleged delinquency of {$5800.00}. In XX/XX/XXXX, after additional escalation efforts, a Chase Escalations representative informed us that Chase 's internal review had confirmed that the Trustee payments had in fact been received. Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint to request correction and resolution of inaccurate and unverified information currently appearing on my consumer credit report. Several items being reported are incorrect, incomplete, or lack proper verification, including inaccurate payment history, unauthorized inquiries, collection reporting without sufficient documentation, and incorrect personal information. These errors are negatively impacting my credit profile and do not meet the legal standards required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies are required to follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy. The continued reporting of inaccurate late payments, unverified accounts, and incorrect personal data demonstrates a failure to comply with this obligation. I previously disputed these items directly with the credit reporting agency and/or furnishers and requested proper investigation and documentation. However, the reporting remains unchanged, and I have not received adequate proof validating the accuracy of the disputed information. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i, credit reporting agencies must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and delete or correct any information that can not be verified. In addition, any credit inquiries reported without proof of permissible purpose violate 15 U.S.C. 1681b and must be removed. Furnishers also have a duty under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 to report complete and accurate account information. Late payments or derogatory marks reported without documentary support are inaccurate and misleading.
Product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports

XXXX ) prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce. Continuing to bill a consumer after explicit, repeated cancellation constitutes an unfair practice causing substantial, unavoidable injury. Restore Online Shoppers Confidence Act ( ROSCA ), XXXX XXXX. XXXX requires companies offering negative-option/recurring billing to provide simple cancellation mechanisms and honor them. Violation of XXXX Statutory Timelines ( XXXX Finance Code 392.202 ) Under XXXX Finance Code 392.202, when a consumer disputes a debt in writing, a third-party debt collector has exactly 30 days to investigate and respond to the specific inaccuracies. It has now been over 30 days since my XX/XX/XXXX written dispute. LVNV is knowingly collecting on and reporting a time-barred debt to all three credit bureaus XXXX XXXX and XXXX while implying it must be paid. This is misleading, deceptive, and a direct violation of the FDCPA and FCRA. Following their insufficient validation response, I sent a second letter a cease and desist combined with a formal deletion demand citing both their failure to properly validate the debt and their admission that the debt is time-barred. Consumer complaint narrative: CFPB COMPLAINT AGAINST XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I am submitting this complaint regarding an apparent collection attempt by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, a XXXX collection law firm, concerning an alleged XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX account . I do not admit that I owe this account, I do not admit that XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX has any lawful right to collect it, and I do not admit that XXXX XXXX has any valid enforceable claim against me. Several years ago, XXXX XXXX received an identity theft complaint from me concerning this XXXX XXXX account. XXXX XXXX was therefore on notice that the account was disputed as the product of identity theft, fraud, unauthorized use, or otherwise not attributable to me. Despite that prior identity theft notice, this account now appears to have been placed with or referred to XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX for collection. That is alarming and requires immediate regulatory review. This account is not presently appearing on my consumer credit reports to my knowledge. The absence of current reporting is significant because it is consistent with the prior identity theft dispute and raises serious questions about whether XXXX XXXX previously suppressed, blocked, ceased reporting, or otherwise recognized the disputed/fraud-related nature of the account. If XXXX XXXX previously received an identity theft complaint and nevertheless later placed the alleged account for collection, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX should be required to explain the legal and factual basis for renewed collection activity. This complaint involves potential violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, Regulation F, Regulation V, and the Consumer Financial Protection Acts prohibition against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. Under the FDCPA, including 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f, and 1692g, a debt collector may not use false, deceptive, misleading, unfair, or unconscionable means to collect a debt. XXXX XXXX XXXX must be able to prove that the debt is valid, that the amount demanded is accurate, that the account belongs to me, that the account is not the result of identity theft, that XXXX XXXX had authority to place the account for collection, and that XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX has lawful authority to collect it. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g and Regulation F, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX must provide complete validation information and must not overshadow or impair my dispute rights. I dispute this alleged debt now. I demand that all collection activity cease unless and until XXXX XXXX XXXX provides competent verification, not merely a billing statement, spreadsheet entry, account printout, placement file, or conclusory creditor assertion. Because XXXX XXXX previously received my identity theft complaint, any attempt to collect this alleged XXXX XXXX debt now must be treated as a heightened compliance matter. The issue is not simply whether XXXX XXXX XXXX can produce a balance. The issue is whether XXXX XXXX and/or XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX can produce admissible, account-level evidence proving that I personally opened the account, personally authorized the charges, personally benefited from the account, and that the account was not the result of identity theft or unauthorized activity. I request that the CFPB require XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX to produce the following : The full account application for the XXXX XXXX, including IP address, device identifiers, application timestamps, phone number, email address, address used, and all identity-verification data relied upon at account opening. All records showing how XXXX XXXX verified that I personally opened the account. All charge records, merchant records, transaction history, statements, payment history, and charge-off records. The complete chain of placement, assignment, referral, or authority showing how this account reached XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. The date XXXX XXXX received my identity theft complaint and all internal notes, dispute codes, investigation records, fraud department records, and account-level conclusions associated with that complaint. Any documents showing XXXX XXXX denied, accepted, closed, suppressed, blocked, or otherwise resolved my prior identity theft complaint. Any records showing that XXXX XXXX provided XXXX & XXXX with notice that the account had previously been disputed as identity theft. Any records showing XXXX XXXX XXXX performed a meaningful review before sending collection correspondence. Any records showing the account is not time-barred, not legally defective, and not subject to identity theft protections. Any records showing that XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX is licensed, authorized, and legally permitted to collect from me in my state. I further request that XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX preserve all records relating to this matter, including the incoming letter, mailing records, collection notes, dialer records, payment portal records, account notes, skip-tracing records, placement records, creditor communications, compliance reviews, and any automated or manual decisioning used to generate the collection letter. I also request that XXXX XXXX preserve all fraud, identity theft, XXXX XXXX application, underwriting, account-opening, transaction, charge-off, reporting, and placement records. Separately, I have reported XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX to the Federal Trade Commission regarding what I believe to be a pattern of apparent fake or inauthentic XXXX reviews. I understand that online review misconduct is primarily an FTC issue, but I am notifying the CFPB because consumer reviews may affect how consumers evaluate a debt collectors legitimacy, reputation, and conduct. If XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX relies on public reviews to present itself as a trustworthy consumer-facing collection operation, then the authenticity of those reviews is relevant to consumer deception concerns. XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX should be required to preserve records sufficient to substantiate that any challenged reviews it solicited, purchased, influenced, promoted, or used in marketing were genuine reviews from actual consumers with real experiences. XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX should be prepared to produce evidence of each customer who provided a review as many of the newer ones are obviously fabricated. I am not asking the CFPB to treat this as a routine debt validation dispute. This is a disputed XXXX XXXX account previously identified to XXXX XXXX as identity theft. A later collection attempt by a collection law firm after prior identity theft notice suggests either a breakdown in XXXX XXXX identity theft procedures, a failure to transmit dispute/fraud information to its collector, a failure by XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX to conduct a meaningful pre-collection review, or an attempt to collect a debt that can not be lawfully verified.

Despite years of requests and multiple appeals, they have never provided a factual explanation or identified any transaction or activity that supports their conclusion. What makes this situation even more frustrating is that Cash App has now gone beyond keeping my original account closed. Every few months, I have attempted to create a new account, hoping the issue had been resolved or that I could simply start over. Instead, I am now told that my phone is linked to an account that violated the Terms of Service, preventing me from creating a new account at all. Once again, no explanation has been provided. At this point, I have effectively been excluded from using a financial platform for years without ever being told why. This has created real and ongoing inconvenience in my everyday life. Family members, including my son 's grandparents, regularly use Cash App to send money or receive money. There have been multiple occasions where I could not conveniently receive money that was intended to help support my family, and I have also been unable to send money to relatives who primarily use Cash App. In today 's world, peer-to-peer payment platforms are a normal part of everyday life, and being permanently excluded from one of the largest services without any meaningful explanation has had a real impact. The most concerning part of this situation is not simply that my account was closed. It is that Cash App has refused, for years, to tell me what I supposedly did. As a consumer, I can not meaningfully challenge, appeal, or correct a decision when I am never told what conduct supposedly led to that decision. Without that information, every appeal becomes little more than asking Cash App to reconsider a decision that I have no meaningful way to address. I can not explain, dispute, or correct conduct that has never been identified. I understand that companies have a legitimate interest in protecting their platforms from fraud and enforcing their Terms of Service. I am not asking Cash App to reveal confidential fraud detection methods or internal security procedures. However, permanently excluding a consumer from a financial platform for years while refusing to identify the conduct that supposedly justified that decision raises serious concerns about fairness, transparency, and a meaningful opportunity to respond. If Cash App has evidence that I violated its Terms of Service, I believe I deserve to know what that conduct was. If it does not, then I do not believe I should continue to be permanently restricted from using its platform.

I respectfully request that Citibank explain how it determined the applicable dispute period in this case, review whether my dispute was evaluated under the appropriate standards for an ongoing service contract, and consider whether the delays in obtaining the documentation that Citibank required should be taken into account in evaluating the timeliness of my submission. Only after exhausting my efforts to resolve the matter directly with the merchant did I file a dispute with Wells Fargo on XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX filed a claim with Wells Fargo . Why the reason associated with my claim had been changed by representatives. How Wells Fargo determined the " expected date '' referenced in its denial letters. Whether XXXX rules were actually controlling the outcome. Why the basis for denial continued to change. These questions were never directly answered. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX received Wells Fargo 's response to my Right to Documentation request. The documentation provided merely established that I authorized the transaction. I have never disputed authorizing the transaction. The documentation did not explain : Why Wells Fargo denied my claim. Why Wells Fargo initially concluded that the merchant needed additional time. Why Wells Fargo later changed its conclusion. What evidence supported any of its determinations. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXWells Fargo advised that additional time was needed to complete its research and stated that it would provide a response by XX/XX/XXXX. I understood this to mean that the issues I had raised were still under review. I later learned that this information appeared only on my monthly billing statements. Because my account was enrolled in AutoPay and payments were being made automatically every month, I did not routinely review those statements. As soon as I discovered these unexpected charges, I contacted Synchrony Bank and explained the entire situation. I requested that the deferred interest charges be removed because the financing terms had never been presented to me as a deferred interest promotion. Synchrony Bank denied my request. Since I could not afford the significantly higher monthly payments while attempting to resolve this dispute, I asked Synchrony Bank to place the remaining balance on the longest available repayment plan with payments of approximately {$100.00} per month. I requested this arrangement only to avoid financial hardship while seeking a fair resolution. It should not be interpreted as an acceptance of the deferred interest charges. Once again, I was told that the promotion offered XX/XX/XXXX months with no interest. No explanation was provided regarding deferred interest, retroactive interest, or the possibility that thousands of dollars in interest could later be added if the balance was not completely paid by the end of the promotional period. This second experience confirmed my belief that the financing program continues to be presented to customers in a way that reasonably leads them to believe they are receiving a true interest-free financing offer. My understanding of the promotion was not based on a misunderstanding on my part, but on the way the financing was explained during the sales process. I have always acted in good faith. I made every payment on time, enrolled in AutoPay to ensure I never missed a payment, and intended to satisfy my financial obligation. I am not attempting to avoid paying for my furniture. My dispute concerns only the unexpected deferred interest charges that were never clearly disclosed to me when I agreed to the financing. I respectfully request that this matter be thoroughly investigated and that Synchrony Bank be required to remove the deferred interest charges from my account. If those charges are removed, I am prepared to pay the remaining principal balance in full immediately. Thank you for your time and consideration. I respectfully request a fair resolution of this matter and look forward to your response

Consumer complaint narrative: XXXX XXXX U.S. Bank Mortgage Servicing ACCT Number : XXXX In XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted U.S. Bank to request information regarding a possible loan modification. He explained that, once the forbearance period ended, I would either have the option to repay the missed payments or have those payments placed at the end of my loan. Based on those representations, I agreed to proceed with the forbearance. Prior to XX/XX/XXXX, I received a letter stating that my forbearance was ending. I contacted U.S. Bank and spoke with a representative who confirmed that my forbearance would, in fact, end on XX/XX/XXXX. A few days later, I called again to confirm that information. During that call, a different representative informed me that my forbearance had not ended because it had been extended. Because I had received conflicting information regarding the status of my forbearance, I requested written documentation outlining the terms, conditions, and effective dates of the alleged extension. I continued making mortgage payments in amounts that I could reasonably afford during the forbearance period based on the representations that, after making the required payments, the remaining missed payments could be placed at the end of my loan. On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted U.S. Bank for a second time and again requested that the loan modification process be initiated. For the second time, a representative discouraged me from pursuing a loan modification. She stated, " Why would you want to do that? It would start your loan all over. '' My understanding of this statement was that she was referring to restarting the loan term, increasing the amount of interest paid over the life of the loan, and increasing the overall cost of the mortgage. I explained that I had previously sought assistance through XXXX XXXX regarding an FHA Partial Claim but had ultimately been denied because I was behind on my mortgage payments. The representative informed me that I could not independently pursue a Partial Claim because U.S. Bank would need to initiate that process with HUD. The representative advised that her system was not displaying any available repayment plans or other loss mitigation options. She instructed me to call back during the week of XX/XX/XXXX, so that an FHA option could be explored. She also suggested that I call back when making my payment, and I agreed to pay my XXXX mortgage payment on XX/XX/XXXX and my XXXX payment at the end of XXXX. In retrospect, these events raise concerns regarding whether foreclosure activity may have already been initiated while I was being advised that no repayment options were available and while I was actively seeking mortgage assistance. Today, I received a debt collection letter from XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, New Jersey. The letter states that, as of XX/XX/XXXX, the full balance of my mortgage, approximately {$66000.00}, is due and that I must respond by XX/XX/XXXX. Immediately upon receiving the letter, I contacted U.S. Bank. The representative initially insisted that the correspondence must be fraudulent. However, I questioned how a fraudulent party could possess the exact balance of my mortgage account. I also noted that the letter was dated XX/XX/XXXX, the same date that I contacted U.S. Bank requesting mortgage assistance while I had been advised that I remained in active forbearance. Prior to calling U.S. Bank, I independently confirmed that XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX is a legitimate law firm. While reviewing my account, the U.S. Bank representative located the attorney 's name within U.S. Bank 's own system, confirming that the attorney was associated with my mortgage account. Despite locating this information, the representative continued to state that U.S. Bank would not have sent such correspondence because, according to the bank 's records, I remained in active forbearance. The representative asked how many pages the letter contained. When I advised her that it consisted of four pages, she stated that an official foreclosure package would have been approximately sixteen pages and instructed me to disregard the letter. Because I was concerned about the conflicting information I was receiving, I conference-called an attorney and added him to the conversation to listen. Although he advised that mortgage servicing was outside his area of practice and was therefore unable to represent me, he heard the representative repeatedly instruct me to ignore the collection letter. The representative continued to advise me to disregard the correspondence and instead wait for a future letter from U.S. Bank requesting payment of approximately {$2400.00}. I advised the representative that I intended to call back and make my payment. After ending the call, I expressed my concerns to the attorney regarding the repeated inconsistencies in the information I had received from U.S. Bank. Specifically, I was concerned that I was repeatedly being advised that I remained in active forbearance while, at the same time, a law firm had apparently been retained to demand payment of the entire mortgage balance. These circumstances raise concerns regarding whether foreclosure activity may have been initiated while I was simultaneously seeking mortgage assistance and relying upon U.S. Bank 's representations concerning the status of my account. Throughout this process, my objective has been to work cooperatively with U.S. Bank, remain in my home, and explore available loss mitigation options. Instead, I have received conflicting information from multiple representatives regarding my forbearance status, repayment options, loan modification requests, FHA assistance, and the status of foreclosure activity. I respectfully request that the New Jersey Attorney General investigate these circumstances, determine whether U.S. Bank complied with applicable federal and New Jersey mortgage servicing requirements, and require U.S. Bank to provide a clear, accurate, and complete explanation regarding the status of my mortgage account.

I am seeking a legal evaluation regarding a failed refinance transaction and the financial damages my husband and I suffered as a result of our lender 's actions. Our sole purpose for refinancing our home was to use our home equity to pay off an IRS tax lien. From the beginning of the transaction, XXXX XXXX was aware that paying off the IRS lien was the primary objective of the refinance. Despite this, she proceeded with the loan process using an estimated lien amount instead of obtaining the official IRS payoff amount, even though the payoff amount was essential to accurately determine the cash required to close. Based on those inaccurate figures, we were advised that our home would not appraise high enough to cover the IRS debt and that " the only way '' to complete the refinance would be for my husband to withdraw approximately {$20000.00} from his 401 ( k ). Relying on that advice, we ultimately withdrew {$25000.00} to account for anticipated taxes and penalties and to ensure sufficient funds would be available for closing. We later learned that the lender had not obtained or reviewed the official IRS payoff amount before providing this financial advice or preparing our Closing Disclosure. XXXX later admitted by text message : " ( we learned of the higher IRS debt balance ) After, we would have never intentionally had him get less money out than what was needed. '' She also admitted : " We didn't see the payoff when it was sent, you're correct that part was our fault. '' Additionally, regarding the figures originally used, she stated : " That is the total lien amount, but is not the payoff amount. '' These admissions appear to confirm that the lender relied on incorrect figures while advising us to liquidate retirement funds and while preparing our loan disclosures. Timeline of Events Unknown date ( initial conversations ) : We contacted XXXX XXXX to refinance our home specifically to pay off our IRS lien. During a phone call, XXXX instructed us not to make our XXXX mortgage payment, stating it would be paid through the refinance. She advised that we would close by approximately XX/XX/XXXX. The refinance did not close as represented. Because we relied on this advice, our mortgage payment became delinquent, resulting in late fees and damage to our credit score. We were never instructed to make the payment after the anticipated closing was delayed. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX requested the balance of my husband 's 401 ( k ). XX/XX/XXXX XXXX informed us that our home 's appraised value would not fully cover the IRS debt. She advised us that the only way to complete the refinance was to withdraw approximately {$20000.00} from my husband 's 401 ( k ). That same day she sent a revised pre-closing package containing a Closing Disclosure showing our required cash to close as {$16000.00}. We relied on those figures and signed the Closing XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX My husband withdrew {$25000.00} from his 401 ( k ) to ensure sufficient funds for closing and to account for taxes and penalties associated with the withdrawal. We notified XXXX, who responded that if the funds were available by XX/XX/XXXX, closing should occur shortly thereafter. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX requested the official IRS payoff letter. I confirmed that the IRS had sent the payoff. XXXX confirmed that the title company received the payoff letter on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX Despite receipt of the official payoff, the lender continued processing the transaction without notifying us that the required cash to close had substantially changed. XX/XX/XXXX The lender was still requesting income verification documentation. XX/XX/XXXX Closing was confirmed for XX/XX/XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX informed us that he could not provide an official final cash-to-close amount before closing and stated that any additional funds could simply be paid after we signed the documents. XX/XX/XXXX ( day of scheduled closing ) Approximately three hours before closing, we were informed that we would need to bring an additional {$15000.00} to closing beyond the amount disclosed in our previously signed Closing Disclosure. We did not receive a revised Closing Disclosure reflecting this substantial increase before closing. We were never given the required opportunity to review revised disclosures before the scheduled closing. Because we could not unexpectedly produce an additional {$15000.00} on only a few hours ' notice, the transaction failed to close. Financial Damages As a direct result of relying on the lender 's advice and representations, we have incurred significant damages, including : Taxes and early withdrawal penalties from the unnecessary 401 ( k ) distribution. Permanent loss of future retirement investment growth on those funds. Mortgage late fees. Damage to our credit score from the missed mortgage payment that we were instructed not to make. Reduced ability to qualify for favorable refinance terms in the future because of the credit score decrease. Loss of the refinance opportunity itself. Considerable financial uncertainty and additional costs associated with restarting the refinance process. Potential Legal Issues for Review I would appreciate your assessment of whether these facts may support claims including, but not limited to : Negligence and negligent misrepresentation. Breach of fiduciary or professional duties, if applicable. Violations of TILA, RESPA, or the TRID Rule. Whether issuing a Closing Disclosure using estimated IRS figures without first obtaining the official payoff complied with TRID disclosure requirements. Whether the approximately {$15000.00} increase in cash required to close should have required a corrected Closing Disclosure and, if so, whether the lender complied with applicable TRID timing requirements, including any required waiting period before consummation. Whether any available TRID " cure '' provisions could have applied and whether the lender failed to properly cure any disclosure violations. Any additional state consumer protection or mortgage lending claims that may be available. The lender has acknowledged in writing that they failed to review the official IRS payoff before advising us to withdraw retirement funds and before preparing the financial figures on which we relied. We believe those admissions, together with the timeline above, demonstrate that we made significant financial decisions based on inaccurate information provided by the lender and suffered substantial financial harm as a result.

Consumer complaint narrative: Complaint : Failure to Provide Proof of Permissible Purpose Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act I am submitting this complaint because a company accessed my consumer credit report and has repeatedly failed to provide competent documentary evidence demonstrating that it had a legally permissible purpose under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681b. After reviewing my credit reports, I discovered that the company placed an inquiry on my file. I do not recognize any credit application, contractual relationship, or transaction that would have authorized this access. I have sent multiple written requests demanding that the company identify the specific permissible purpose relied upon and provide supporting documentation, including any signed application, authorization, contract, or other records demonstrating that it had the legal right to obtain my consumer report. Despite the passage of significant time and multiple opportunities to respond, the company has failed to provide any competent documentary evidence supporting its inquiry. Instead of addressing my requests with documentation, the company has either failed to respond or has provided incomplete and unsupported explanations that do not establish compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681b, a consumer report may only be obtained for a permissible purpose specifically authorized by law. If a company can not demonstrate that such a purpose existed at the time it obtained my report, the inquiry should not remain on my consumer reports. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require the company to : Produce competent documentary evidence establishing the exact permissible purpose relied upon under 15 U.S.C. 1681b. Provide copies of any signed authorization, application, agreement, or other documentation authorizing the inquiry. Explain the factual basis for obtaining my consumer report. If the company can not establish a lawful permissible purpose, immediately request the permanent deletion of the inquiry from all consumer reporting agencies. I believe I have acted in good faith by attempting to resolve this matter directly before seeking regulatory assistance. Because the company has failed to adequately respond after multiple written requests, I am asking the CFPB to assist in ensuring compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and protecting my consumer rights. Thank you for your attention to this matter

This complaint arises from the consumer reporting agencys failure to provide a complete and legally sufficient Method of Verification ( MOV ) in response to my dispute and request for reinvestigation. Pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), including 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) and 1681i ( a ) ( 7 ), I requested a detailed explanation of the procedures used to verify the disputed information appearing on my consumer report, including the specific method of verification employed, the identity of any furnishers or individuals contacted during the investigation, and the documentary evidence relied upon to substantiate the accuracy and completeness of the reported information. Despite this request, the consumer reporting agency has failed to provide the requested information or any competent and verifiable evidence demonstrating that it conducted a reasonable and legally compliant reinvestigation. The FCRA imposes an affirmative duty on consumer reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed information and, upon request, to disclose the method of verification used to confirm the accuracy of the information being reported. A conclusory statement that an account was simply verified does not satisfy these statutory obligations without supporting evidence explaining how the verification was performed, what procedures were followed, and what records or documentation were reviewed. In the absence of competent and verifiable documentary evidence establishing the basis for the agencys verification of each disputed item, the continued reporting of such information undermines the accuracy, reliability, and integrity of my consumer credit file. Moreover, the agencys continued reporting of disputed information while failing to provide the requested verification details or supporting documentation demonstrates an apparent failure to maintain reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of consumer information, as required by 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). Information that can not be substantiated through competent and verifiable records should not continue to appear on a consumer report. The agencys failure to provide a legally sufficient Method of Verification and supporting evidence is inconsistent with its obligations under the FCRA and warrants regulatory review and appropriate corrective action, including the deletion or correction of any information that can not be properly verified through competent documentary evidence.

A reasonable investigation should address the specific issues raised, including the inability to verify the underlying contract documentation. To date, I have not received documentation demonstrating how Mid Atlantic Finance verified the accuracy of the reported information when the underlying contract documentation remains disputed and unreadable. I dispute that this statement resolves the issues presented. Whether Mid Atlantic Finance purchased contractual rights does not, by itself, establish that the documentation being relied upon is complete, legible, accurate, or sufficient to support continued credit reporting. Additionally, the closure of prior complaints by agencies does not constitute a determination that the account documentation is accurate, that the reported information is correct, or that Mid Atlantic Finance has fully addressed the specific concerns raised in this complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding a systemic flaw in credit reporting data pipeline mechanics that unfairly penalizes financially responsible consumers. I do not owe a balance on this account.My complaint is not with the lender 's right to reduce the limit, but with the failure of the system to differentiate the reason for the reduction. Because banks do not transmit a specific 'inactivity ' reason code alongside limit drops, the automated credit scoring models automatically trigger a utilization penalty.The industry already has the trended data to fix this. The scoring models could easily review historical zero-balances to see that a drop was triggered by inactivity, not risk. Treating responsible, zero-balance behavior as an active risk metric creates a distorted reflection of consumer creditworthiness. I request that the CFPB push for data standardization requiring a distinct reporting classification for inactivity-based reductions versus risk-based reductions.

I am filing this complaint because my mortgage servicer, XXXX XXXX, is denying me access to FHA loss mitigation options based on a misapplication of HUD guidelines. I was recently on an FHA Trial Payment Plan ( TPP ). Due to an unexpected banking issue, a trial payment made at the end of the month was returned for insufficient funds ( NSF ). The servicer canceled the trial plan but failed to notify me of the rejected payment or the plan cancellation until after the trial month had fully passed, denying me a timely opportunity to cure the administrative issue. Furthermore, the servicers loss mitigation department stated that per " FHA guidelines, '' I am completely barred and disqualified from applying or qualifying for another loan modification for a full calendar year. This statement directly violates HUD Single Family Housing Policy Handbook 4000.1. Under FHA loss mitigation guidelines, a failed or unexecuted trial payment plan does not trigger a multi-year lockout restriction. The FHA 24-month restriction only applies to permanently executed and finalized loan modifications. Furthermore, FHA guidelines explicitly permit a servicer to evaluate a borrower for an additional home retention option if a hardship continues. The servicer has also filed a foreclosure complaint against my property, yet they are actively blocking me from submitting a new loss mitigation packet based on this inaccurate " one-year rule '' policy.

Consumer complaint narrative: Deceptive Practices and Forced Currency Conversion on Initial Automatic Payments I am filing this complaint against PayPal for engaging in deceptive financial practices, hiding critical transaction options, and forcing non-consensual currency conversion markup fees on consumers. Recently, I authorized a recurring automatic payment agreement via PayPal using my linked international credit card ( Visa/Mastercard ). PayPal intentionally hid the currency conversion toggle during the initial checkout and subscription signup flow. As a result, my very first transaction was automatically processed using PayPals internal, heavily marked-up exchange rate without my explicit, informed consent. When I contacted PayPal Customer Support, they acknowledged that this " locked '' currency conversion on automatic payments is a " well-documented friction point '' where PayPal defaults to its own exchange rate markup. They admitted that the system hides the toggle during signup, forcing users to manually go deep into account settings to change it retroactively for " future transactions. '' However, PayPal explicitly refuses to correct or refund the currency conversion fee for the first transaction, stating that " once the transaction is completed, we will not have any option to make any changes, '' and claiming the process is " correct as per the User Agreement. '' This is a predatory and anti-consumer product design. PayPal is leveraging its interface to intentionally default consumers into a worse financial rate to profit from the conversion spread, while offering no option to avoid it on the first payment. Telling a consumer they can fix a setting after they have already been wrongfully charged does not change the fact that the initial charge was unauthorized in its method of conversion. I request that the CFPB investigate PayPal 's deceptive billing practices and require PayPal to : Refund the excess currency conversion spread/markup stolen from my initial transaction. Fix their user interface to provide a mandatory, transparent currency conversion choice ( PayPal rate vs. Card Issuer rate ) at the exact moment a user signs up for any automatic payment or billing agreement, rather than hiding it to force a retroactive fix.

Approximately one month after I reported the fraud, I learned that the following day after I had reported the fraud to Huntington it had decided to close my account and end our banking relationship. I am asking the CFPB to review Huntingtons handling of this matter, including its fraud detection procedures, its investigation of my disputes, its decision to reimburse some transactions while denying others arising from the same incident, and its refusal to provide provisional credit while the disputes remained unresolved. CFPB Complaint Rebuttal Fair Collections & Outsourcing ( XXXX, Account XXXX ) Related Complaint Number : XXXX This complaint is submitted as a direct rebuttal to the response provided by Fair Collections & Outsourcing regarding my prior request for debt validation. In my original complaint, I specifically requested verification and validation of the alleged debt, including documentation demonstrating that I am legally responsible for the account. This request included, but was not limited to, signed contracts, account agreements, billing records, statements, proof of ownership of the debt, chain of assignment documentation, and any other records that substantiate the validity of the alleged obligation. In response, XXXXair Collections & Outsourcing stated the following : " Verification of the debt will be mailed to the address listed on this complaint upon receipt of this information. '' This response was dated XX/XX/year>. As of the date of this rebuttal, I have not received a single document, letter, statement, validation notice, or any other form of debt verification from Fair Collections & Outsourcing. The company has failed to follow through on the representation it made to both me and the CFPB. Merely stating that documentation will be mailed at some future date is not debt validation. More importantly, making such a statement and then failing to provide the promised documentation leaves consumers with no meaningful way to verify the legitimacy, accuracy, ownership, or collectability of the alleged debt. I respectfully request that the CFPB require Fair Collections & Outsourcing to provide all validation documentation directly through the CFPB complaint portal so that there is a documented record of compliance. Allowing a debt collector to simply claim that documents will be mailed, without producing any evidence that the documents were actually sent or received, undermines the purpose of the complaint process and prevents meaningful consumer review. Specifically, I am requesting the following : Complete validation of the alleged debt. Copies of any signed agreements, contracts, applications, or documents bearing my signature. Complete account statements showing how the balance was calculated. Documentation establishing the date of default, if applicable. Documentation establishing ownership of the debt and the chain of assignment or transfer. Proof that Fair Collections & Outsourcing has the legal authority to collect this debt. Evidence that the validation documents allegedly referenced in their CFPB response were actually mailed, including the date sent and the address used. Copies of all validation materials uploaded directly through the CFPB complaint portal. If Fair Collections & Outsourcing can not provide the requested documentation, then serious questions remain regarding the validity, accuracy, and collectability of this alleged debt. The company 's failure to provide the promised validation documents after representing to the CFPB that they would do so raises concerns regarding its collection practices and its compliance with consumer protection requirements. Consumers should not be forced to accept unsupported collection claims without documentation, nor should debt XXXX be permitted to satisfy validation requests through vague promises that are never fulfilled. I request that the CFPB investigate this matter further and require a complete and documented response through this complaint. Until proper validation is provided, the alleged debt remains unverified and disputed. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this Identity Theft Report because credit inquiries and accounts were opened in my name without my knowledge, authorization, or consent. None of the accounts or credit applications reflected on my report were initiated or approved by me. These inquiries appeared suddenly and without any legitimate connection to my activities. I have been actively monitoring my credit for accuracy, and the presence of these entries clearly indicated fraudulent use of my information. Once I discovered the unauthorized activity, I took immediate action. I contacted the lenders associated with the inquiries to inform them that the applications were fraudulent and that I did not submit or authorize any of them. I provided proof of my identity when required and requested that they close, cancel, or flag these applications as identity theft. These creditors were notified that I am not responsible for any account, application, transaction, or inquiry tied to the fraudulent use of my information. In addition to contacting the lenders, I also placed a fraud alert on my credit file to warn other creditors that my personal information has been compromised. I then placed a credit freeze on my reports to prevent additional unauthorized applications from being processed. These steps were taken immediately to protect myself from further damage and to ensure no additional fraudulent activity could occur using my information. Because this situation involved clear misuse of my identity, I also took the important step of filing a police report with my local law enforcement agency. I provided them with details regarding the unauthorized inquiries and included the names of the companies that appeared on my credit report without my permission. Filing the police report formally documented the identity theft and created an official record of the incident. This report serves as additional proof that I am actively addressing the fraudulent activity and that I am not responsible for the unauthorized use of my identity. Identity theft can occur in many ways, including data breaches, theft of documents, phishing attempts, or unauthorized access to personal information. I do not know exactly how my information was compromised, but I have never knowingly shared sensitive details with any unknown or untrusted individual or entity. Despite taking precautions, someone still managed to access my personal information and attempt to use it to open accounts in my name. This has caused significant stress, inconvenience, and concern, especially because fraudulent accounts and inquiries can negatively affect my credit and financial stability. Since discovering the issue, I have closely monitored my credit and maintained records of the fraudulent activity. I reported the identity theft to the Federal Trade Commission and am submitting this detailed statement as part of the official record and investigative process. My goal is to correct the inaccuracies on my credit report and ensure that no fraudulent information remains.
