Because these applications and inquiries were made without my authorization, I am requesting that all fraudulent accounts, inquiries, applications, and related information be permanently removed from my credit report. I also request that any creditors associated with these fraudulent applications mark them as identity theft and stop all communication or collection efforts related to them. I am not responsible for any financial obligations, charges, or activity associated with the fraudulent use of my identity. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), especially Section 605B, I have the right to request the blocking and removal of any information that resulted from identity theft. The fraudulent inquiries and any associated accounts violate my rights under the FCRA because they are not accurate representations of my credit history or financial behavior. Removing them is essential to restoring the accuracy of my credit file and preventing further harm. This situation has required me to spend time reviewing my credit, filing a police report, contacting creditors, submitting disputes, and securing my personal informationall due to actions someone else took using my stolen identity. These fraudulent entries misrepresent my financial habits and create a misleading impression of my creditworthiness. It is important that the false information be removed promptly so that my credit file accurately reflects legitimate activity. To be absolutely clear, I had no involvement whatsoever with the fraudulent applications or accounts. I did not initiate them, approve them, authorize them, or receive any benefit from them. I am the victim of identity theft, and the fraudulent entries on my credit report reflect the actions of the individual ( s ) who used my information without permission. I am requesting assistance from the Federal Trade Commission, the credit bureaus, and the creditors involved to finalize the removal of the fraudulent data. In conclusion, I respectfully request that all fraudulent credit inquiries, applications, and accounts be investigated and removed from my credit reports immediately. My identity was used without my consent, and the inaccurate information appearing on my report must be corrected to restore the integrity of my credit. I have filed a police report, reported the theft to the FTC, contacted the creditors, and taken all recommended steps to resolve this matter. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this formal complaint against XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) and GM Financial for violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). The company is pursuing a claimed deficiency balance of {$5500.00} on a XXXX XXXX XXXX contract. The documentation provided by the collector contains contradictory math that completely fails accuracy and compliance standards under the FCRA. Specifically, an original deficiency calculation letter from GM Financial states the " Unpaid Amount Financed '' was {$18000.00}, while a secondary typed ledger provided by the collector changes that foundational base principal to {$17000.00}, introducing an unverified {$740.00} " Non-Accrued Interest '' charge simply to force a broken spreadsheet to balance. Most critically, both GM Financial and XXXX XXXX XXXX completely failed to provide the mandatory pre-sale Notice of Intent to Sell/ Plan to Sell Property prior to the disposition of the asset, violating UCC 9-611 through 9-614. I was completely denied my legal right to receive the exact date, time, and location of the auction, stripping me of my right to redeem or monitor the commercial reasonableness of the sale. Under state law, a failure to provide this mandatory pre-sale notice triggers a rebuttable presumption that bars the collection of any remaining deficiency balance. I recently disputed this inaccurate, unverified information directly with Equifax. While the account is marked as " under investigation, '' the trade line continues to display volatile and unverified data modifications in an attempt to bypass compliance standards. Because the collection agency and the original creditor can not produce a valid accounting ledger or the legally mandated pre-sale auction notice, they have no legal authority to report or collect this {$5500.00} balance. Furthermore, this vehicle was a voluntary surrender, not an involuntary repossession, making the company 's aggressive, contradictory calculations and failure to communicate transparently even more inaccurate and non-compliant.

XX/XX/XXXX email from merchant " We have checked the refund status for your order The record shows that we cancelled the order, and after cancellation, the funds should have been automatically refunded to your original payment account. I immediately submitted this documentation to Netspend 's dispute department. This evidence demonstrates that the matter is not merely a disagreement about merchandise or services. ( it never was ). The merchant cancelled the order, showing the purchase was never fulfilled, authorized a full refund, and attempted to process the refund. The issue is that the refund did not successfully reach my account. However, it appears that your card issuer rejected the transaction, so the funds have not yet been credited to your account. Our system is showing the following error message : * * '' Unable to refund processing_error '' * * This error typically occurs when there is an issue with the original payment card or the receiving banks restrictions. Unfortunately, because of this system error, we are currently unable to push the refund through manually from our side. To resolve this and ensure you receive your money, * * we kindly suggest that you contact your bank or credit card provider to file a dispute/claim for this transaction. * * Once you initiate this process with your bank, the funds can be recovered through their system. We are currently unable to push the refund through manually from our side. We kindly suggest that you contact your bank or credit card provider to file a XXXX for this transaction. * * Once you initiate this process with your bank, the funds can be recovered through their system. Proof of Transmission : Attached is the screenshot from our payment processor dashboard showing the status as " Dispute Accepted ''. We chose not to dispute this chargeback claim and have accepted it. Banks typically require time to process and resolve chargeback disputes, and after their assessment, the funds will be returned to his account and the case will be closed. This process is beyond our participation or control. Given that the merchant has already accepted the chargeback dispute ( XX/XX/XXXX ), it is now XX/XX/XXXX, and I urge Netspend to take immediate action to credit these funds to my account. This should be facilitated either through a provisional credit or the prompt release of funds currently held within the payment network ; I expect my money to be returned without further delay. To conclude, the persistent lack of clear communication, transparency, and the failure to resolve this failed refund reflect a significant deficiency in Netspend 's customer service, resulting in considerable frustration. if you would like the emails between me and netspend i can send them to you.

The shipping carrier 's tracking data explicitly confirms that the merchandise traveled back to XXXX and was successfully received and signed for by the merchant.2. Evidence of Persistent Merchant Fraud and Admission : It is well-documented by global consumer protection groups that the " XXXX XXXX '' network ( operating active domains like XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX ) is a known international scam operation. They intentionally stay online to buy social media ads and trick victims, deliberately delaying shipping past a buyer 's timeline to weaponize tracking loops against consumers. The merchant sent me explicit written confirmation via email admitting that they received the inventory back and that I " won the dispute. '' However, they claim a technical glitch in their payment system prevents them from processing a manual refund, stating it would flag as a " double credit. '' The merchant currently physically possesses both my money and the returned merchandise while their storefront remains active online to claim more victims.3. Citibank 's Systemic Negligence and Failure to Act : I filed disputes with Citibank under Case Number XXXX and Case Number XXXXMy specific complaint against Citibank is that each time they opened or reviewed these cases, their dispute department failed to change the dispute category to a returned item issue. They kept the files logged exclusively as " Merchandise Not Received. '' Because Citibank repeatedly submitted the wrong code, the merchant 's automated system simply replied each time with the exact same paperwork showing the original delivery to the transit depot.Citibank 's dispute department actively refused to open a new, separate dispute for XXXX Reason Code XXXX ( Credit Not Issued ), falsely claiming that " additional disputes can not be filed once an original one is filed. " Proving they knew their automated loop was broken, Citibank issued me a {$250.00} token gesture credit on one of the cases, explicitly stating to me on the phone that " there was nothing else they could do '' to force the merchant to pay. They offered nothing for the second case. My cost of items never received were approximately {$750.00} and {$630.00}. This is a severe misapplication of XXXX XXXX XXXX. While a single-dispute limit applies to unauthorized fraud claims, XXXX rules explicitly allow a new Consumer Dispute ( Reason Code XXXX ) if a subsequent event occurs. The return of the merchandise and the merchant 's written acknowledgment of an unissued credit constitute a completely separate violation from the initial delivery timeline. Citibank can not buy out their regulatory obligation with a partial token credit while forcing me to pay the remaining balance for an international scam. Here is how the XXXX XXXX global fraud works. XXXX XXXX scam is a highly coordinated, multi-million dollar global e-commerce fraud network operating across several continents. By utilizing localized storefrontssuch as XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX Torontothey successfully present themselves as upscale local boutiques. In reality, the entire operation relies on deceiving consumers, evading local authorities, and carefully exploiting automated banking loopholes to steal money. According to thousands of consumer complaints tracked on platforms like XXXX and XXXX, the blueprint of how this entire scam operates can be broken down into five distinct phases : Here is how their scam works Phase 1 : The " Bait-and-Switch '' Advertising The scammers steal high-end, professionally shot imagery from legitimate mid-century modern designers and flood social media platforms ( primarily XXXX and XXXX ) with heavily discounted ads . Phase 2 : Missing Electrical CertificationsBecause the items are cheaply sourced overseas, they do not possess required regional safety certifications ( such as XXXX in the XXXX, XXXX in XXXX, or XXXX in XXXX XXXX ). When victims hand these light fixtures to certified local electricians, the professionals legally refuse to install them due to fire hazards and incorrect local voltage. Phase 3 : Silent Customer SupportThe phone numbers listed on their websites are entirely fake. If an order is requested to be canceled immediately after purchase, the system automatically ignores it. Email support is entirely operated by an automated bot system designed to run out the clock, stall for time, or offer offensive, low-ball partial refunds ( e.g., offering {$10.00} back on a {$400.00} broken fixture ). Phase 4 : Weaponizing Shipping Depot LoopsThis is the core phase of their banking exploitation strategy. The network purposefully uses vague shipping windows ( e.g., " 3-5 days or weeks '' ) and fails to provide direct residential door delivery. Instead, they intentionally rout the packages to regional postal depots or transit hubs.By dropping the package at a general depot rather than your home address, they delay delivery just long enough to cause logistical issues.When consumers inevitably can no longer collect the item ( due to a renovation finishing or moving out of the area ), the depot marks the item as " returned to sender. '' Phase 5 : The " Double Credit '' Banking TrapOnce the items travel back to their overseas warehouse, the scammers spring their final credit card loophole : When the victim files a " Merchandise Not Received '' dispute with their bank, the scammers ' automated merchant system immediately uploads the initial shipping barcode showing the package arrived at the regional depot.Because banks use automated software to check basic delivery pings, the merchant wins the automated dispute, and the bank closes the case.Once the case is closed, the merchant emails the consumer politely claiming, " We see you won the dispute, so we can not manually refund you because our system flags it as a double credit risk. '' XXXX XXXX XXXX for the Scammer : The consumer 's bank case remains closed, the merchant blocks the manual refund, and the scammer legally keeps your money and takes back the physical lights to resell to the next victim. The " You Won the Dispute '' email is one of the most calculated and psychologically manipulative steps of the entire XXXX XXXX scam. They use this specific tactic to completely shut down communication, silence the victim, and freeze the banking process so they can pocket your money.Here is exactly how they use this trick to execute the scam:1. When a victim contacts XXXX XXXX to demand their money back after tracking shows the items were returned to XXXX, the scammer sends a highly polite, automated email that looks something like this : " Dear Customer, we have reviewed your account and we see that you have already opened a dispute with your bank and won the case. Because you won, your bank has already reversed the funds and taken the money from our account. Since you have already been credited by your bank, our system blocks us from issuing a manual refund, as that would result in a double credit. Please contact your bank to access your funds. " XXXX. They make it look like they are a good company whose hands are tied by a computer glitch.To Stop You From Emailing : If you believe you are already getting your money back from your bank, you will stop harassing XXXX XXXX XXXX customer support email.To Gaslight You : It forces you into a frustrating cycle where the merchant tells you the bank has the money, and the bank tells you the merchant has the money, causing you to eventually give up out of exhaustion.3. Exploiting the " Double Credit '' Software LoopholeThe scam works because their e-commerce payment platform ( usually a third-party processor linked to XXXX or a similar platform ) does have a safety feature that locks a transaction if a chargeback is active.XXXX XXXX purposely leaves the dispute open or unresolved on their end just long enough to lock the system. They then point to this automated technical lock and tell you, " See? Our computer won't let us click the refund button. '' They deliberately use a real software restriction to cover up the fact that they have no intention of ever returning your money. 4. The Ultimate Financial WindfallBecause the front-line customer service agents at Citibank do not understand this loop, the bank leaves the charge on your statement. Weaponized Admission of Deficient Documentation and Contested Service The servicer has historically attempted to validate foreclosure-related legal charges by asserting that a breach notice was processed and delivered. The servicer must reconcile how these distinct billing dates and separate corporate ledger inputs perfectly copy or obscure the law firm 's flat pricing structures, or confirm if arbitrary corporate markup was applied directly to the borrower 's principal balance. Under RESPA, a servicer is prohibited from masking unearned fees or arbitrary corporate markups. 4. System-Flagged Violations, Administrative Failures, and Intentional Disregard of Internal Controls The underlying third-party invoices submitted with this complaint present an undeniable pattern of bad-faith overcharging. It aligns perfectly with NewRez LLC dba Shellpoint Mortgage Servicings documented corporate track record of regulatory non-compliance and predatory fee assessments. Shellpoint and its associated entities have been the subject of numerous federal class-action lawsuits, FDCPA litigation, and state regulatory consent orders specifically concerning unauthorized account-padding, the inflation of corporate advances, and the misrepresentation of default debt balances. The servicer routinely counts on the assumption that consumers lack the forensic billing records or public court registries necessary to audit their statements. By forcing through MRLP and XXXX invoices that were explicitly flagged by their own automated compliance software as duplicate or excessive, Shellpoint has demonstrated a willful disregard for consumer protection laws. This established history of abusive servicing patterns underscores the urgent need for direct regulatory scrutiny to hold this entity contractually and legally accountable.

This complaint concerns Chase 's handling of a {$7600.00} unauthorized XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX charge on my XXXX XXXX credit card ( account ending XXXX ), and Chase 's documented failure to conduct a reasonable investigation under 12 C.F.R. 1026.13. Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, my card was compromised and numerous fraudulent transactions were placed. Chase removed all fraudulent transactions except one, a {$7600.00} purchase of a camera from the XXXX online store. This purchase was over ten times larger than any previous purchase on the card. I had never purchased anything from the XXXX online store, and I had never purchased any camera equipment. Despite this out-of-pattern huge purchase, Chase did no secondary authorization. Upon discovering the fraudulent charge, I called Chase. Chase removed the charge and others from my next periodic statement, before rebilling the XXXX charge again on the XXXX statement, while acknowledging the others were fraudulent. Chase claimed, based on representation from XXXX, that the camera was delivered to me personally, as evidenced by a XXXX receipt purporting that I signed for the camera at my residence on XX/XX/XXXX, and that I therefore received a benefit from the transaction. I timely sent a letter in writing, to the address on the back of the statement, asserting a billing error under Regulation Z. I attached substantial evidence that I could not have received the package on XX/XX/XXXX, because I was not at my house that day. I included several affidavits from coworkers all of whom happen to be lawyers in good standing with the Georgia barconfirming that I was with them on that day and could not have personally received a package at my house. I also sent calendar appointments showing I was not at my house that day. I also sent a police report, as well as evidence that my email had been subscription bombed on the day the camera was purchased. Given that someone purported to be me and signed for a package under my name, at a time when I demonstrably was not at my residence, there is clear indication of fraud. Further, it is clear that the card was compromised in the relevant time window, as acnkolwedged by Chase. Chase should have considered all this as part of a reasonable investigation, and tried to reconcile how I could possibly have signed for a package ( and thus " received a benefit '' ) at a location where I was demonstrably not present. Chase did not consider my evidence at all. I know this for a fact, because I have recorded calls with the investigator who admitted in clear terms that she closed the investigation without having even received my evidence. As she explained, Chase, as a practice, does not forward evidence sent to the address on the statement ( which is the legally operative address for purposes of Regulation Z ) to its actual investigators. My complaint is about the events that occurred before the transfer and whether my account had already been compromised. The foundation of my complaint has always been the unauthorized changes made to my account credentials and the apparent account takeover that occurred prior to the transfer. Those events are critical because they directly affect whether any subsequent transaction should be viewed as truly authorized. My concern is that Wells Fargo has focused exclusively on the final transaction while repeatedly overlooking the sequence of events that led to it. Specifically : My account credentials were changed without my authorization. I was not notified of those credential changes. I believe my account security had already been compromised before the transfer occurred. I was deceived into believing my funds were at risk and acted under that deception. I provided additional details because the earlier investigation was based on an incomplete understanding of what happened. Despite receiving this additional information, Wells Fargos response still focuses only on the transfer itself and does not meaningfully address the unauthorized credential changes or whether those security events contributed to the loss. I respectfully request that this matter be evaluated as a complete chain of events rather than as an isolated transaction. Specifically, I request that Wells Fargo provide answers to the following questions : 1. What account credentials were changed before the transfer? 2. When were those changes made? 3. How were those changes authenticated? 4. Why was I not notified of those changes? 5. What security monitoring or fraud detection was triggered after those credential changes? 6. Did Wells Fargo investigate whether my account had been compromised before concluding that the transfer was authorized? 7. How did Wells Fargo determine that the transfer represented informed authorization if unauthorized credential changes had already occurred? My complaint is not simply that I transferred money. My complaint is that my account security was compromised before the transfer, and Wells Fargos investigation has repeatedly failed to address that foundational issue. I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether Wells Fargo adequately investigated the alleged account takeover and unauthorized credential changes instead of limiting its review solely to the fact that the transfer originated from my account. I am seeking a review of the adequacy and completeness of the investigation, not merely a repetition of the conclusion that the transfer was initiated from my device.

Consumer complaint narrative: American Express is engaged in willful, knowing, and systematic violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act and is furnishing internally contradictory, unverifiable, and demonstrably inaccurate information to credit bureaus regarding a charged-off account. I am filing this complaint to formally document multiple federal violations and demand immediate correction or deletion. This is part of an active and growing federal record now exceeding 20+ CFPB complaints I have filed documenting systematic credit reporting violations across multiple furnishers. THE CORE VIOLATION MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE BALANCE REPORTING : American Express reports this account as charged off with a balance of {$4800.00}, while simultaneously reporting a past due amount of {$2700.00} a discrepancy of {$2000.00} with ZERO explanation, itemization, or documentation anywhere in their reporting. This is not a minor clerical issue. This is a furnisher reporting two materially different dollar figures for the same single debt obligation, in direct violation of their statutory duty to report accurate information. VIOLATION 1 FCRA 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) DUTY TO REPORT ACCURATE INFORMATION : Furnishers are PROHIBITED by federal law from furnishing information to a credit bureau that they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. American Expresss own reported figures are facially inconsistent with each other, meaning American Express either knows this information is inaccurate or has failed to exercise the reasonable diligence required to ensure accuracy before furnishing it. VIOLATION 2 FCRA 1681e ( b ) FAILURE TO MAINTAIN MAXIMUM POSSIBLE ACCURACY : This is not a close call. A charge-off balance and a past due balance that differ by {$2000.00} on the same account, with the past due figure being actively updated as recently as XX/XX/XXXX on an account that charged off in XX/XX/XXXX, is objectively, mathematically inaccurate reporting that fails the maximum possible accuracy standard required by federal law. VIOLATION 3 FCRA 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 2 ) DUTY TO CORRECT AND UPDATE : If American Express possesses information showing this accounts balance is actually {$2700.00} ( the past due figure ) rather than {$4800.00} ( the charge-off figure ), or vice versa, they have an affirmative legal duty to correct and update this information with all credit bureaus. Their failure to reconcile these figures over multiple reporting cycles spanning nearly 3 years demonstrates either gross negligence or willful disregard of their FCRA obligations. VIOLATION 4 UNEXPLAINED CONTINUOUS ACTIVE PAST DUE STATUS ON A CLOSED ACCOUNT : The payment history shows uninterrupted charge-off coding ( CO ) for every single month from XX/XX/XXXX through XXXX XXXX 33 consecutive months with the past due figure apparently being recalculated or maintained as active the entire time despite the account being closed and charged off. This pattern is consistent with either : ( a ) systematic furnishing of stale, unreconciled data without periodic verification, or ( b ) a failure to apply payments, settlements, or adjustments to the correct balance field, both of which violate FCRA accuracy requirements. VIOLATION 5 FCRA 1681i MANDATORY REASONABLE REINVESTIGATION : I am formally and explicitly disputing the accuracy of this account. American Express is legally required to conduct a REASONABLE INVESTIGATION meaning independent verification, not merely confirming their own internal database against itself. Given that American Expresss OWN two reported figures contradict each other, no investigation that simply re-confirms their existing database entry can satisfy the reasonable investigation standard, because the database itself is the source of the inaccuracy. VIOLATION 6 DEMAND FOR COMPLETE DOCUMENTARY PROOF : I am demanding American Express produce : ( a ) the final account statement immediately preceding charge-off showing the exact calculation of {$4800.00} ; ( b ) complete documentation of any payment, settlement, fee reversal, or credit applied to this account at any point after charge-off that would explain a reduction to {$2700.00} ; ( c ) the specific date any such adjustment occurred ; ( d ) written confirmation of the single, accurate, current balance owed on this account, since reporting two unreconciled figures simultaneously is per se inaccurate ; and ( e ) confirmation of whether this account has been sold, assigned, or transferred to any third party at any point, which would explain discrepant balance reporting. VIOLATION 7 FCRA 1681n WILLFUL NONCOMPLIANCE EXPOSURE : If American Express continues reporting this internally inconsistent, unreconciled information after this formal dispute without correcting it or providing documentation resolving the discrepancy, this will constitute WILLFUL noncompliance with the FCRA not mere negligence because American Express will have been placed on explicit notice of the contradiction and chosen not to resolve it. Willful noncompliance under FCRA 1681n exposes a furnisher to : actual damages OR statutory damages of {$100.00} to {$1000.00} per violation, PUNITIVE DAMAGES in an amount the court deems appropriate, and mandatory costs and reasonable attorneys fees. VIOLATION 8 FCRA 1681o NEGLIGENT NONCOMPLIANCE EXPOSURE ( ALTERNATIVE ) : In the alternative, if American Expresss failure to reconcile these figures is found to be merely negligent rather than willful, this still constitutes negligent noncompliance under FCRA 1681o, exposing American Express to liability for actual damages sustained as a result of the inaccurate reporting, plus costs and attorneys fees. VIOLATION 9 IMPACT ON MORTGAGE QUALIFICATION ACTUAL DAMAGES : I am actively pursuing a home mortgage and this inaccurate, unreconciled charge-off reporting is directly suppressing my XXXX Score XXXX ( currently XXXX ), XXXX Score XXXX, and XXXX Score XXXX the specific scoring models used by mortgage underwriters. Continued inaccurate reporting of this account is causing quantifiable financial harm to my ability to qualify for a mortgage at a reasonable interest rate, which constitutes actual damages under FCRA 1681o and 1681n. VIOLATION 10 PATTERN OF CONDUCT : This complaint is part of a documented pattern across multiple furnishers and credit bureaus where unverifiable, unreconciled, or inconsistent information continues to be reported despite formal disputes. I am building a complete federal record across the CFPB, FTC, and Florida Attorney Generals office, and I am fully prepared to pursue civil litigation under FCRA 1681n and 1681o if this specific discrepancy is not resolved with actual documentary proof. American Express has every opportunity right now to resolve this matter by producing the documentation requested above. Absent that documentation, the only legally defensible outcome is correction of the inaccurate balance or full deletion of this unverifiable account.

Consumer complaint narrative: I purchased goods with a debit card with an online retailer. The retailer placed a temporary hold of funds for items purchased. This process can take as long as it takes for an item to ship so my bank account will not reflect the true amount until it is done. This process is very deceptive, misleading and confusing. This is a well-known situation within banks and card issuers and still persists. The real issue becomes when this causes negative funds due to this deception and false sense of reality. When the bank tells me what my account availability is they're responsible to tell the true honest reality. The retailer, card issuer and bank all need to be in communication with each other at point of sale. Some banks or cards will cause an overdraft fee which is deceptive due to faulty information given because they're not truly reflecting the point of sale because of this " hold and release ''. This situation is wrong and disingenuous. These banks and card issuers could be profiting off of what is well-known false information because of this type of online sale. This needs to be revised and addressed so that when a sale is made the amount is reflected accurately within the bank records to show what is truly available in real time. Returns are just as bad when being refunded to a card. When an item is returned the funding should be instant and not take days to process. Once the item is in the company 's possession a consumer 's funds should not be held up until its decided to be sent back. This should be immediate and a consumer should not have to wait for their own money. Some people need those funds immediately for other purchases elsewhere and need that money right there and have no reason to be without their money.

Affirm repeatedly denied my claim, relying primarily on the fact that the XXXX address, device, contact information, and purchasing pattern matched my prior account activity. Those facts do not establish that I personally operated the device or authorized the loan. They are also consistent with my report that someone accessed my computer without permission. Affirm additionally treated the automatic bank withdrawal as repayment history showing authorization, even though I did not manually initiate or approve that payment. Affirm has also stated that I waited a significant amount of time to report the activity, although I reported it approximately XXXX days after discovering the XXXX withdrawal. Its online portal initially categorized my claim as cancellation or return not processed, which was never my dispute. My claim has always been identity theft and unauthorized use. I provided Affirm with extensive supporting evidence, including a signed and notarized affidavit, an FTC Identity Theft Report, a completed XXXX Police Department XXXX report, a detailed timeline, bank-transaction evidence, and Affirms own loan records. XXXX XXXX XXXX separately completed its research regarding the {$240.00} Affirm withdrawal and credited my account. Affirm has continued to state that I am responsible for the loan and has warned that the loan and payment history will be reported to the credit bureaus. Its response has focused on advising me that I should have secured my device, rather than determining whether I actually authorized the disputed transaction. I request that Affirm cancel the unauthorized loan, reduce the balance to zero, cease collection activity, remove or prevent any adverse credit reporting, and provide written confirmation that I am not responsible for the transaction. Dear, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau I am submitting this complaint regarding the collection of an alleged debt originally associated with XXXX XXXX XXXX and the subsequent collection activities of Bounce AI and XXXX XXXX. Likewise, I never received notice of any subsequent assignment, transfer, or sale of the account to XXXX XXXX or any other entity. Without documentation establishing ownership and authority to enforce the account, I can not determine whether the entity attempting to collect this debt is the proper party in interest. This creates significant uncertainty regarding which entity, if any, possesses legal standing to collect the alleged obligation, negotiate settlement, or pursue litigation. Licensing Concerns Based upon my review of publicly available licensing information, Bounce AI does not appear to be licensed to engage in debt collection activities in the State of New York. Despite this, Bounce AI has attempted to collect this alleged debt while refusing to provide documentation establishing its ownership of the account or its legal authority to collect it. Concerns Regarding Tax Reporting It appears that XXXX XXXX XXXX failed to issue an IRS Form 1099-C for tax year XXXX despite charging off the account. Documentation and Enforceability Concerns I also have concerns regarding improper service of process, deficiencies in documentation establishing ownership and enforceability of the alleged debt, and the failure of the entities involved to produce documentation demonstrating a complete chain of title. Given the absence of proper documentation, I question whether the entity pursuing collection has standing to do so. Explain whether the debt was properly reported to the Internal Revenue Service, including whether an IRS Form 1099-C was required and, if not issued, why. Investigate whether applicable federal consumer financial protection laws governing debt collection, debt ownership, consumer disclosures, and account documentation have been followed. If the companies can not establish a complete chain of ownership, demonstrate legal authority to collect the alleged debt, provide proper debt validation, and establish compliance with applicable federal and state consumer protection requirements, I request that all collection activity immediately cease, that any inaccurate credit or account reporting be corrected, and that the alleged obligation be XXXX if it can not be legally substantiated.

Consumer complaint narrative: Attn : XXXX XXXX, Chairman and CEO Attn : XXXX XXXX XXXX, Lead Independent Director Attn : Audit and Examination Committee Attn : Risk Committee To the Wells Fargo Board of Directors : I am writing to bring to your attention what I believe may present a compliance, consumer protection, and reputational risk for Wells Fargo. I have been a Wells Fargo customer since XXXX. During that time, I maintained deposit accounts, a credit card relationship, and an auto loan that was paid in full. Despite past issues that Wells Fargo publicly acknowledged and later sought to remedy, including unauthorized accounts and improperly added products, I continued to maintain my banking relationship because I believed the institution was committed to improving its practices and rebuilding customer trust. Recently, I reviewed my account statements after learning more about Californias Automatic Renewal Law ( Business and Professions Code 17600 et seq. ), which provides important consumer protections related to recurring subscriptions and automatic renewals. In doing so, I identified multiple recurring charges that I believed were unauthorized, improperly continued, or otherwise warranted review. Acting in good faith, I submitted disputes regarding those charges through Wells Fargos established claims process. As a result, I was informed that Wells Fargo had permanently disabled my debit card for a period of twelve months because the volume of claims was considered excessive. I was further informed that the decision was final and not subject to appeal. While I recognize that financial institutions must manage fraud risk and operational costs, I am concerned that Wells Fargos current approach may create the appearance that customers can be penalized for exercising consumer protection rights afforded under California law. Such a policy may discourage customers from reporting potentially unauthorized recurring charges or seeking review of transactions they reasonably believe to be improper. My concern extends beyond my individual circumstances. From a governance and risk perspective, the Board may wish to consider whether policies that restrict access to banking services after customers exercise dispute rights could expose the institution to : Consumer protection complaints and regulatory scrutiny ; Reputational harm arising from the perception that customers are discouraged from reporting questionable charges ; Increased risk of complaints to state and federal regulators ; Potential conflicts between consumer protection objectives and internal account management practices. I have already shared my concerns with Investor Relations because I believe investors should be aware of policies that could create legal, regulatory, or reputational exposure for the company. I also intend to seek guidance from the appropriate state and federal regulatory agencies regarding the treatment of consumers who exercise their rights under applicable law. I respectfully request that the Board review whether Wells Fargos policies appropriately balance fraud prevention with consumer rights and whether sufficient safeguards exist to ensure that customers are not effectively penalized for raising legitimate concerns about recurring charges. For many years, I remained a loyal customer because I believed Wells Fargo would work to correct mistakes and preserve the trust of its customers. Unfortunately, this experience has significantly undermined that confidence. Thank you for your time and consideration. Respectfully, XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: This is not intended as a duplicate complaint. I am submitting this because Robinhood provided a new and different explanation after its prior CFPB response, and I am requesting clarification of that new basis for denial. I am submitting this complaint regarding Robinhood Credit , Inc. and my Robinhood XXXX XXXX dispute for a {$1800.00} charge from XXXX XXXX XXXX. My original concern was that I paid XXXX XXXX XXXX for representation services related to an XXXX issue, but the representation did not occur. I contacted the merchant regarding representation, but I was later told that I had to resolve another issue myself before they could represent me. I did not proceed with the documents required for representation to begin. Robinhood previously denied the dispute using broad explanations such as app activity, customer interaction, and spending patterns. Those explanations did not clearly identify what specific evidence showed that XXXX XXXX XXXX performed the representation services or was entitled to retain the {$1800.00}. After Robinhoods prior CFPB response, Robinhood provided a new and different explanation. Robinhood stated that the dispute was filed beyond 60 days from the transaction statement date and therefore did not qualify for the standard XXXX chargeback process. Robinhood also stated that it reviewed the matter under Claims and Defenses, but that the dispute did not qualify because the full statement balance had been paid off. This newer explanation raises additional concerns because Robinhood has not clearly identified the specific rule, policy, agreement provision, or regulation it relied on. Robinhood also has not explained whether it reviewed any merchant documentation showing that XXXX XXXX XXXX actually performed the services or was entitled to retain the funds. I am also providing additional context regarding the delay. Another person assists with paying my bills and managing payments. Because of this, the statement balance was paid without me personally realizing that this specific {$1800.00} charge from XXXX XXXX XXXX had been paid. Once I became aware of the issue and realized the representation services had not occurred, I disputed the charge. I understand Robinhood may rely on procedural timing rules. However, payment of the statement does not mean the merchant performed the services, and it does not mean XXXX XXXX XXXX was entitled to retain the funds. My concern is not only disagreement with the outcome. My concern is that Robinhood gave broad and inconsistent explanations and has not provided the specific rule, deadline, or merchant evidence relied upon for its prior reasons nor for the most recent one. I am requesting that Robinhood provide a clear written response addressing the following : The exact statement date on which the {$1800.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX charge first appeared. The exact deadline Robinhood says applied to the standard XXXX chargeback process. The specific XXXX rule, Robinhood policy, card agreement provision, or regulation relied upon to deny the dispute as untimely. The specific rule, policy, card agreement provision, or regulation relied upon to deny review under Claims and Defenses because the statement balance had been paid in full. Whether XXXX XXXX XXXX provided a signed agreement, engagement contract, invoice, refund policy, proof of work, or other documentation supporting its entitlement to retain the {$1800.00}. Whether XXXX XXXX XXXX provided evidence that the agreed representation services were actually performed. Whether Robinhoods denial was based only on procedural eligibility, or whether Robinhood made a factual determination that XXXX XXXX XXXX performed the services and was entitled to keep the funds. Why Robinhoods earlier denial explanations referenced app activity, customer interaction, and spending patterns, if the later explanation is that the dispute was denied due to timing and Claims and Defenses eligibility. A fair resolution would be for Robinhood to refund the {$1800.00} charge, including any related interest or fees, because the merchant did not provide the expected representation services. Alternatively, if Robinhood refuses to refund the charge, I request that Robinhood provide a complete written explanation identifying the exact rule, deadline, policy, agreement provision, or regulation relied upon, and confirm whether the merchant provided any signed agreement, invoice, refund policy, proof of work, or other documentation supporting retention of the {$1800.00}.

On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX XXXX PT, I visited the Rapid Cash branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, NV, to apply for a short-term loan in person. Upon arrival, the clerk instructed me to fill out a physical paper application, which I completed and submitted. While waiting, I observed the clerk engaging in profiling behavior, staring at me repeatedly while serving another customer. When it was my turn at the window, the clerk chose not to manually process my paper application. Instead, despite my explicit preference for an in-person, manual review, she instructed me to create an online profile on my mobile device to input my income information, effectively using the automated system to bypass face-to-face manual underwriting. Immediately upon creating the account, the automated system generated a " denied '' status. I showed the screen to the clerk and explicitly asked, " Did they say why? '' The clerk acted unhelpful, stated " No, '' and refused to provide any explanation. She then said, " So that's it, yeah, '' and handed back my identification. The branch completely failed to provide me with any form of documentation regarding this denial. I received : No written or verbal explanation of the specific reasons for denial. No physical Adverse Action disclosure paper at the counter. No automated text, email, or digital confirmation of the application status or disclosure of consumer rights. Under 12 CFR 1002.9 ( Regulation B ), a creditor must notify an applicant of action taken within 30 days of receiving a completed application. When adverse action is taken, the creditor must provide a written statement of specific reasons for the action or a written notification of the applicant 's right to a statement of reasons within a specified timeframe. When I attempted to dispute these transactions and stop the withdrawals, I encountered significant barriers. Giggle Finance primarily relied on text messages and automated communications, making it extremely difficult or impossible to speak with a live representative who had the authority to review my account or resolve my concerns. My repeated attempts to obtain assistance were unsuccessful. I requested explanations regarding the withdrawals, an accounting of my payments, and an opportunity to dispute the transactions. Instead of receiving meaningful assistance, I continued to experience collection efforts while my dispute remained unresolved. As a result, I believe Giggle Finance failed to : * Honor my revocation of authorization for electronic fund transfers. * Properly investigate disputed electronic payment transactions. * Provide accurate information regarding withdrawals from my account. * Maintain reasonable and accessible customer service for consumers seeking to resolve account disputes. * Provide a fair and transparent dispute resolution process before continuing collection activity. I am concerned that Giggle Finances conduct may violate the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E, which provide consumers with protections regarding preauthorized electronic fund transfers and unauthorized electronic withdrawals. I also believe the companys conduct should be reviewed under the Consumer Financial Protection Act for potential unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ), particularly concerning its servicing practices, collection methods, and failure to provide meaningful customer support. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate Giggle Finances business practices, including : * The companys continued electronic withdrawals after consumers revoke authorization. * Its procedures for handling payment disputes and unauthorized electronic fund transfers. * Its customer service practices and failure to provide consumers access to qualified representatives. * Its collection practices while legitimate disputes remain unresolved. * Whether its disclosures and servicing practices comply with applicable federal consumer protection laws. As part of the resolution of this complaint, I request that Giggle Finance : 1. Immediately cease any unauthorized electronic withdrawals from my account. 2. Refund any withdrawals made after my revocation of authorization, if determined to be unauthorized. 3. Provide a complete payment history and accounting of my account, including every debit, payment, fee, and balance calculation. 4. Conduct a formal investigation into my disputed transactions. 5. Correct any inaccurate account records or negative reporting resulting from these disputed transactions. 6. Provide a written explanation of its policies regarding revocation of authorization and electronic payment processing. 7. Ensure consumers have access to knowledgeable live representatives capable of resolving disputes in a timely manner. Consumers should not have to endure unauthorized withdrawals, aggressive collection efforts, and an inability to communicate with a qualified representative when attempting to resolve legitimate disputes. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require Giggle Finance to comply with all applicable federal consumer financial protection laws.

This proves the issue was an internal, real-time technical processing block on the merchant side, not a lack of funds or invalid payment details on my part. Because Affirm and XXXX XXXX share an integrated backend processing system for these transactions, the erroneous XXXX XXXX flag directly caused my valid Affirm payments to be rejected. Statutory Violations : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) - Duty to Provide Accurate Information : Lenders are strictly prohibited from reporting information to a consumer reporting agency if they know or have reasonable cause to believe the information is inaccurate. Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX, I discovered that my JPMorgan investment account had been used to process unauthorized debit card transactions. I immediately reported the fraud, canceled the debit card, and opened a fraud claim. After reviewing my account activity, I identified 314 debit card transactions between XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, totaling {$10000.00}. Only five transactions, totaling {$240.00}, were authorized by me. The remaining 309 transactions ( 98 % ) were unauthorized. The unauthorized activity began shortly after a legitimate debit card transaction I made in New York XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, and continued for approximately nine months. The affected account is an investment account with a balance in the mid-six figures. Because investment balances naturally fluctuate with market performance, I primarily monitored the overall portfolio value rather than each individual debit card transaction. Changes of XXXXl XXXX XXXX over days or weeks are common in an investment portfolio of this size and could reasonably be attributed to normal market fluctuations. I was also unaware that my debit card was linked to this investment account. I had always used my checking account for my everyday purchases, and I rarely used this debit card. I understood that the investment account was intended primarily for investing, and I would access those funds only if I specifically needed to do so. Throughout the investigation, I repeatedly requested an explanation regarding how and why the debit card was linked to this investment account but did not receive a substantive response. The unauthorized activity followed clear and repetitive patterns involving a small number of merchants. One merchant alone accounted for 137 debit card charges totaling {$4100.00}, including as many as eight transactions in a single day, with recurring dollar amounts and purchase-and-return activity. Another merchant accounted for 50 debit card charges, including 14 transactions in a single day. Additional merchants accounted for 35, 19, and 12 debit card charges, respectively, each exhibiting repeated transaction patterns over short periods. A summary of these transaction patterns is attached. Shortly after I reported the fraud, JPMorgan reimbursed {$850.00}, representing only the most recent unauthorized transactions that the bank determined were eligible for reimbursement. The remaining unauthorized transactions continued under investigation for several months. During that time, I fully cooperated with every request made by the bank, including reviewing each transaction and identifying which transactions were authorized and unauthorized. I also repeatedly requested an explanation regarding the banks fraud investigation, the absence of fraud alerts or intervention, the linkage of my debit card to my investment account, and the basis for the reimbursement decision. After approximately five months of investigation, JPMorgan ultimately denied reimbursement for the remaining unauthorized transactions, stating that I was responsible for reviewing my account statements. I respectfully disagree with that determination. While I understand the importance of monitoring my accounts, I also believe banks have an important role in monitoring and investigating unusual account activity. In this case, the bank determined that a portion of the unauthorized transactions warranted reimbursement, yet denied reimbursement for the remaining unauthorized transactions arising from the same prolonged pattern of activity. Despite months of investigation, I have not received a satisfactory explanation regarding the repetitive transaction patterns, the absence of fraud alerts or intervention, the linkage of my debit card to my investment account, or the basis for denying reimbursement for the earlier unauthorized transactions. I respectfully request that the CFPB review JPMorgans handling of my fraud claim and assist in obtaining reimbursement for the remaining unauthorized debit card transactions. I also request that the bank provide a complete explanation of its fraud investigation, fraud monitoring, and claim determination.

I am the victim of an impersonation scam and I am filing this complaint because of how Current ( Finco Services , Inc. ) has handled my fraud claim, including its inconsistent classification of the transaction and its refusal to provide provisional credit or a clear written explanation. The agent then closed the chat. WHY I AM COMPLAINING 1. Inconsistent classification : Current 's own agent repeatedly called this an " unauthorized transfer '' in writing, then denied the provisional credit that unauthorized EFTs are afforded under Regulation E. Current can not treat the transaction as " unauthorized '' for purposes of filing a dispute and simultaneously treat it as ineligible for the protections that apply to unauthorized transfers. 2. No clear written basis : Current has not provided a clear, written explanation of how my claim is classified ( unauthorized EFT vs. authorized/fraud-induced ) or the specific legal and contractual basis for denying provisional credit. 3. Failure to act on a time-sensitive scam : I reported this promptly and asked for a freeze and recall while recovery may still have been possible. The recipient is a scammer who impersonated law enforcement. WHAT I AM ASKING FOR - A clear, written determination of how my claim ( case XXXX ) is classified and the specific basis for the provisional-credit denial, citing the applicable regulation and account agreement provisions. - A full and documented investigation of the unauthorized/fraud-induced transfer, including any attempt to recover funds from the receiving account. - Reimbursement of the {$1000.00}. - Written notice of the resolution and my right to request the documents Current relied on in its decision. I am filing that police report, and I intend to file a complaint with the FBI 's Internet Crime Complaint Center ( IC3 ). Despite submitting extensive evidence over five separate dispute attempts, Goldman Sachs has repeatedly denied the claim on the basis that the purchase was authorized, without adequately addressing whether the goods were counterfeit or materially not as described. -- - # # # Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) Violations/ Non-Compliance Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq. ) and implementing Regulation Z ( 12 CFR 1026.13 ), consumers are entitled to dispute billing errors, including charges for goods that are : - Not delivered as agreed - Defective or materially not as described - Fraudulently represented ( including counterfeit goods ) Specifically, 15 U.S.C. 1666i provides consumers the right to assert claims and defenses against card issuers when goods or services are not delivered as agreed, subject to proper dispute procedures. In this case : - The merchandise received was not authentic as advertised ( counterfeit goods ). - The goods materially differed from the description and branding presented at the time of sale. - The merchant failed to respond or comply with its stated return/refund process. - I submitted timely and repeated dispute notifications with supporting documentation. -- - # # # Failure of Investigation and Improper Dispute Handling Goldman Sachs has failed to conduct a meaningful review of the evidence provided. Each denial incorrectly reduces the issue to authorized purchase, without addressing whether the goods were counterfeit or materially different from what was advertised. This reflects a failure to properly investigate under FCBA and Regulation Z requirements, which obligate card issuers to investigate billing disputes in good faith and consider all submitted documentation. Despite multiple submissions, including : - Photographic and descriptive evidence of counterfeit indicators - Merchant policy violations - Proof of non-response from the merchant - Evidence of widespread consumer complaints regarding identical fraud patterns No substantive analysis of the counterfeit claim has been provided. -- - # # # Additional Consumer Harm & Pattern Evidence The merchant in question has been widely reported by other consumers for : - Selling counterfeit or diluted luxury goods- Using inconsistent or non-verifiable shipping addresses- Failing to honor refund and return policies- Non-response to customer service inquiries These factors further support that this is not an isolated dissatisfaction issue, but a pattern of deceptive commercial conduct. -- - # # # Requested Resolution I am requesting that the CFPB require Goldman Sachs Bank USA to : 1. Reopen and fully reinvestigate this dispute under FCBA and Regulation Z standards 2. Acknowledge and evaluate evidence that the goods were counterfeit and materially not as described 3. Reverse the charge in the amount of {$150.00} 4. Confirm in writing the specific basis for any final determination, including direct response to counterfeit and misrepresentation claims 5. Review internal dispute handling procedures to ensure compliance with FCBA requirements for good-faith investigation I have made repeated good-faith attempts to resolve this issue directly through the card issuer process, providing extensive supporting documentation each time. The continued failure to address the counterfeit nature of the goods or to meaningfully engage with the evidence submitted demonstrates a breakdown in the required dispute resolution process under federal consumer protection law. The company in question is no longer in business due to their fraudulent practices. I have filed cases with the XXXX and the Federal Trade Commission. I respectfully request CFPB intervention to ensure proper handling of this dispute in accordance with the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Failure to exercise ordinary care Despite the obvious and visible nature of the alteration, the financial institution processed the check. During one of these conversations, I spoke with a manager who reviewed the information and expressed confusion regarding the basis for the denial. The manager acknowledged that the explanation provided in the dispute findings did not appear to align with the circumstances of the transaction. This raised further concerns for me about whether a proper investigation was conducted before my claim was denied. Since receiving the denial, I have repeatedly attempted to obtain clarification regarding how Cash App reached its decision and why the dispute documentation contains information that appears inaccurate or unrelated to the actual transaction. Over the past week, I have submitted approximately five separate complaints and follow-up requests seeking answers and a review of the investigation. Despite these efforts, I have not received a meaningful explanation, a corrected investigation, or any substantive update regarding the status of my concerns. My complaint is not only about the loss of the funds from the failed ATM transaction, but also about the apparent lack of care and accuracy in Cash Apps dispute process. I am deeply concerned that my claim may have been denied based on incorrect information without a proper review of the transaction history or the facts I provided. The documentation used to support the denial appears to directly contradict what occurred and what is reflected in my account activity. I believe Cash App has failed to conduct a reasonable and thorough investigation of my dispute. I am requesting that Cash App perform a complete review of the transaction, explain how the original determination was made, provide accurate supporting documentation, and reimburse the funds that were removed from my account for a transaction in which no cash was dispensed. Additionally, I would like Cash App to explain what safeguards are in place to prevent similar errors from occurring in future dispute investigations, especially when inaccurate information can lead to consumers being improperly denied reimbursement. I am seeking a fair resolution, including reimbursement of the disputed funds and a detailed explanation of the investigative process that led to the denial of my claim.

DATE OF LOSS CONTRADICTS XXXXXXXX XXXX OWN RETURN RECORDS The XXXX preliminary appraisal identifies : Type of Loss : Collision Date of Loss : XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX However, I had already returned the vehicle to XXXX at approximately XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. Deceptive practices during loss mitigation occur when mortgage servicers mislead homeowners facing foreclosure or financial hardship. These tactics violate consumer protection laws. Common offenses include " dual tracking '' ( pushing a foreclosure while a modification is under review ), " lost '' paperwork, and charging unauthorized or illegal junk fees. Recognizing deceptive mortgage practices helps prevent the loss of your home. The most common deceptive and illegal behaviors to watch for include : Dual Tracking : The servicer continues the foreclosure process while your complete loss mitigation application is under evaluation. The " Lost Document '' Shuffle : Representatives claim they never received your documents, or continuously ask for new paperwork until your application deadline passes. Deceptive Notices : Sending confusing notices that mislead borrowers into thinking an active trial modification or loss mitigation agreement has been canceled.

However, this response confirms that my understanding of the promotion came entirely from their representative, and that I was not provided with the official terms or conditions at the time of my inquiry. As a result, I reasonably relied on the information provided during our direct communication. If the promotion contained material limitationssuch as exclusions related to credit unions or specific documentation requirementsthose terms should have been clearly and explicitly disclosed at the time I inquired about the promotion, especially after I provided details about the competing offer. By failing to disclose these key eligibility requirements while actively engaging with me about the promotion and encouraging me to submit documentation, the company created a misleading impression that the promotion applied to my situation. I have also provided screenshots of my communications with the companys representative, which demonstrate that : I explicitly referenced the promotion I disclosed the nature of the competing offer The representative encouraged me to submit documentation No exclusions or disqualifying conditions were communicated I believe this constitutes a failure to properly disclose material terms and conditions, and a misleading representation of a promotional offer. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against PayPal regarding unauthorized transactions and account activity that occurred during a period in which I was hospitalized for serious cardiac conditions, including a medically induced coma, and was unable to properly monitor or manage my financial accounts. During my review of PayPal account activity, I discovered numerous transactions involving merchants that I do not recognize and did not authorize, including XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and other unfamiliar entities. As I continued reviewing my records, I discovered that many of these same merchants also appeared in separate disputes involving my XXXX account and other financial accounts. This indicates a broader pattern of unauthorized activity affecting multiple financial platforms rather than an isolated issue involving a single transaction or account. Initially, I believed my phone may have been hacked. However, after reviewing the evidence and the timing of the activity, I now believe it is more likely that an unknown individual obtained access to my phone, financial applications, accounts, and personal information while I was hospitalized and medically incapacitated. Although I can not determine exactly how the access occurred or who was responsible, I did not authorize the disputed transactions. My concern extends beyond individual merchant charges. My PayPal statements reflect a confusing pattern of credits, Mass Pay payments, withdrawals, and merchant transactions that I can not explain and did not authorize. Although funds were credited to the account, I did not knowingly receive, control, spend, transfer, or benefit from those funds. Any credited amounts appear to have been immediately spent, withdrawn, transferred, or otherwise used in transactions that I did not authorize. I am unable to determine where many of these funds ultimately went. I have attached spreadsheets identifying merchant transactions that I do not recognize as well as withdrawals for which I can not determine the destination or purpose. I am requesting that PayPal trace and explain these transactions as part of its investigation. I have also provided supporting documentation, including : Physician documentation confirming my hospitalization and medical incapacity. Fraud determination letters issued by my bank and credit card companies. Account statements and transaction records. Spreadsheets identifying disputed activity. Other financial institutions reviewing substantially similar activity determined that fraud occurred and credited my accounts accordingly. Despite this evidence, PayPal has denied my claims. My dispute is not based on whether the transactions occurred through accounts, devices, or credentials associated with me. My dispute is that I did not authorize the transactions. The fact that activity may have originated from an account or device associated with me does not establish that I personally initiated or approved the activity.

A significant part of my complaint concerns not only the merchant 's conduct, but also Apple Card 's handling of the dispute process itself. The reason I am unable to provide traditional supporting documentation is because the merchant failed to provide it at every stage of the transaction. I never received an order confirmation email, receipt, order number, or any other proof of purchase after being charged. When I returned the item in-store, I specifically requested documentation confirming the return. Store employees informed me that they could not provide a receipt because their printer was broken. Later, when I contacted customer service regarding the missing refund, I was told that the merchant had no record of the transaction at all. In other words, the entire premise of this dispute is that the merchant failed to generate, maintain, or provide basic transaction records. The absence of documentation is not evidence against my claim ; it is the very reason the claim exists. Despite this, Apple Card repeatedly treated the lack of documentation as though it were my responsibility rather than the merchant 's. Over the course of more than two months, I made repeated phone calls, submitted written explanations, responded to requests for information, and attempted to provide every piece of evidence available to me. I also made good-faith efforts to resolve the matter directly with the merchant before involving Apple Card XXXX Each time I contacted Apple Card, I was forced to re-explain the facts from the beginning. On multiple occasions, I was informed that the dispute had been closed or decided despite the fact that the merchant still had not produced basic proof supporting its position. I repeatedly requested that the matter be reviewed and reopened because fundamental questions remained unanswered. Why was the merchant unable to produce a receipt, order confirmation, or transaction record? Why was the merchant permitted to claim I agreed to terms and conditions when it could not even establish the existence of the underlying transaction? Why was the merchant allowed to retain both the returned merchandise and the funds without providing proof that it had fulfilled its obligations? To this day, neither Apple Card nor the merchant has provided me with documentary evidence showing that the merchant has a valid basis for retaining my funds. Instead, Apple Card appears to have accepted the merchant 's position at face value while holding me to an impossible standard : producing documents that the merchant itself failed to provide and now claims do not exist. What I find most troubling is that Apple Card repeatedly relied on the assertion that I agreed to the merchant 's terms and conditions, while simultaneously failing to provide any evidence that such an agreement occurred. If the merchant can not locate the transaction, can not produce a receipt, can not produce an order confirmation, and can not provide a record of the purchase, then it is unclear how Apple Card determined that there was sufficient evidence to deny the dispute. I have been a loyal Apple Card customer for years and have trusted that disputed transactions would be investigated fairly and impartially. Instead, I have spent months repeatedly calling, emailing, reopening disputes, and providing detailed explanations, only to receive conclusions that appear unsupported by the evidence available. Throughout this process, I have cooperated fully, responded promptly, and made every reasonable effort to resolve the issue. The merchant, by contrast, has been unable to produce basic records of either the purchase or the return. The result is that I am being held financially responsible for a transaction that the merchant can not properly document, for merchandise that I no longer possess because it was returned to the merchant, and for a refund that was promised but never issued. I believe Apple Card failed to conduct a reasonable investigation, failed to require adequate substantiation from the merchant, and unfairly placed the burden of the merchant 's recordkeeping failures on me.

Consumer complaint narrative: Subject : CFPB Complaint Against Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC I am filing this complaint against Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC for reporting inaccurate, incomplete, and/or unverified information on my consumer credit reports and for failing to comply with their obligations under federal consumer protection laws. I have disputed this account and requested validation of the alleged debt. Despite my requests, Jefferson Capital has continued to report the account to the consumer reporting agencies without providing sufficient evidence that the debt is accurate, valid, and legally enforceable. I have not received a copy of the original signed agreement, complete account statements, documentation showing the chain of assignment, or proof that Jefferson Capital has the legal right to collect and report this alleged debt. Their actions appear to violate several provisions of federal law, including but not limited to : * * Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) * * * * * 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) * * Prohibits furnishers from reporting information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. * * * 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) * * Requires furnishers to conduct a reasonable investigation upon receiving notice of a dispute from a consumer reporting agency. * * * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) * * Requires maximum possible accuracy in consumer reporting. * * * 15 U.S.C. 1681i * * Requires disputed information to be properly investigated and corrected or deleted if it can not be verified. * * Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) * * * * * 15 U.S.C. 1692e * * Prohibits the use of false, deceptive, or misleading representations in connection with the collection of a debt. * * * 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ) * * Requires debt collectors to communicate that a debt is disputed when reporting it to consumer reporting agencies. * * * 15 U.S.C. 1692f * * Prohibits unfair or unconscionable collection practices. * * * 15 U.S.C. 1692g * * Requires debt collectors to provide proper validation of an alleged debt upon request. If Jefferson Capital can not produce competent evidence demonstrating that the account is accurate and legally enforceable, they should not be reporting the account to any consumer reporting agency. I am requesting that Jefferson Capital Systems immediately : 1. Conduct a thorough and reasonable investigation of this disputed account. 2. Provide complete validation of the alleged debt, including all supporting documentation. 3. Provide proof of ownership and the complete chain of assignment of the debt. 4. Correct any inaccurate information being reported. 5. Delete the account from all consumer reporting agencies if it can not be fully verified. 6. Provide written confirmation of the results of their investigation. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate this matter and require Jefferson Capital Systems to comply with all applicable provisions of the FCRA, FDCPA, and other federal consumer protection laws. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

I stopped making payments only after GreenState failed to explain their own accounting errors and could not provide accurate or consistent documentation. Dispute With the Credit Bureau : I also disputed this account directly with the credit bureau. However, the credit bureau did not conduct a reasonable investigation. They simply accepted GreenStates response without requiring documentation, despite the fact that GreenStates internal records and credit reporting contradict each other. The credit bureau did not address the misreported down payment, the inconsistent delinquency timeline, or the contradictory balances. I believed I had rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, but the credit bureau did not follow proper dispute procedures and did not correct or investigate the inaccurate information. This complaint concerns Navy Federal Credit Unions seizure of an amended federal income tax refund that belonged solely to XXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX originally filed his XXXX federal income tax return through XXXX. At that time, the refund was properly deposited into my Navy Federal checking account because that account information was on file through XXXX processing bank. XXXX later filed an amended federal tax return ( XXXX XXXX ). He reasonably expected the amended refund to be mailed to him. Instead, XXXX processing bank ( XXXX ) reused the previously stored direct deposit information, causing XXXX amended refund to be electronically deposited into my Navy Federal account on XX/XX/XXXX. Immediately upon receipt of the deposit, Navy Federal withdrew virtually the entire amount and applied it toward debts owed solely by me. Newly Discovered Evidence After my previous CFPB complaint was closed, I located Navy Federals official XX/XX/XXXX account statement. That statement clearly identifies my checking account as having : Joint Owner ( s ) : NONE This evidence establishes that XXXX XXXX XXXX was not a joint owner of my account when his amended federal tax refund was deposited and seized. This evidence was not available when I submitted my prior complaint. IRS Documentation The IRS documents establish that the amended refund belonged exclusively to XXXX XXXX XXXX. Specifically : * The IRS XXXX notice is addressed only to XXXX XXXX XXXX. * The amended Form XXXX was filed solely under XXXX XXXX XXXX Social Security number. * My name does not appear anywhere on the amended return. * The IRS determined that XXXX XXXX XXXX was entitled to the amended refund. These documents establish that the refund belonged to XXXX XXXX XXXX and not to me. Contradiction in Navy Federals Position After the seizure, I contacted Navy Federal and was informed by representatives that the funds could be seized because XXXX had previously been a joint owner of my account. However, Navy Federals own XX/XX/XXXX statement establishes that there were no joint owners on the account when the refund was deposited. Later, in its response to my CFPB complaint, Navy Federal changed its explanation and simply stated that it exercised its right of offset against my account. Neither explanation addresses the central issue. The question is not whether Navy Federal may offset funds belonging to me. The question is whether Navy Federal had the legal authority to treat XXXX XXXX XXXX amended federal income tax refund as my property after its own records established he was no longer a joint owner of the account receiving the deposit. t is strictly illegal for collection agencies to change or " re-age '' the Date of First Delinquency ( DOFD ) to make a debt appear newer. By law, all negative information ( including collections ) must fall off your credit report exactly 7 years from the date the account originally became past due. Under the law, making a partial payment or formally acknowledging the debt in writing can legally restart ( " toll '' ) the statute of limitations clock, giving collectors a new window to sue.
