The restriction notice states that my accounts were restricted because I " have not yet provided critical, missing information, '' frames the restriction as something I can " easily lift '' by providing that information, and presents closure as avoidable by a XX/XX/XXXX deadline. It presents the restriction, in other words, as a conditional and preventable consequence within my control. That stated basis is false on Citi 's own record. Citi 's KYC department confirmed on a recorded call the same day that I had already provided the information, that it was accepted in XXXX, and that there was " no block. '' And on XX/XX/XXXX, my own Citi relationship manager confirmed to me in writing that the restriction is procedural, that the case is simply being finalized internally, and that there is " no new needed information '' from me. Citibank nonetheless imposed the full restriction immediately, on a stated basis its own employees had already disproved. The adverse action was taken first. It was not a future consequence I could avert by supplying anything, because Citi confirms there is nothing left for me to supply. Citibank subsequently lifted the restriction on my deposit accounts my joint checking was usable again within days yet it has continued to generate and mail me the same restriction notices. A mailed copy of the XX/XX/XXXX restriction notice reached me about a week later, on or about XX/XX/XXXX. When I called Citibank about it, a representative told me that no further information was needed, that the case was simply being finalized, and that Citibank 's system " will periodically continue to send notices until the case is closed, '' so I should " disregard '' the notice. Citibank is thus mailing a 29-year customer formal notices that state he failed to provide " critical, missing information '' and threaten to liquidate his retirement account, while simultaneously instructing him to ignore those notices because nothing is in fact outstanding. A consumer can not reliably tell a genuine restriction notice from XXXX Citibank will later say to disregard. This was still unresolved as of XX/XX/XXXX. Roughly two weeks after Citibank 's representatives first told me the review was in its " final stages, '' I called Citibank 's KYC department again to confirm my status. A representative told me my accounts were unblocked, but that the review remained open and was in a " disposition '' stage that had been handed to another Citibank department for a final approval she could neither see nor expedite, with no further information needed from me. She again offered to request a written " KYC satisfied '' letter once the review closes a letter I have asked for repeatedly and still do not have. To date, Citibank has never rescinded its XX/XX/XXXX restriction notice in writing. That notice still states on its face that my Citi accounts will be closed, and my retirement account liquidated and mailed to me as a check, if I do not provide information by XX/XX/XXXX the very notice Citibank 's representatives have told me to disregard because nothing is in fact outstanding. More than two weeks after Citibank 's personnel began telling me the matter was in its " final stages, '' Citibank still has not given me a single authoritative written answer reconciling that standing closure-and-liquidation notice with its assurances that I owe it nothing further. Underlying every step of this is a single, systemic failure : Citibank 's automated KYC and account-closure processes took adverse action against a fully compliant 29-year customer, repeated it, and would not release it and no person at Citibank has been able to stop or override it. My assigned financial advisor wrote to me that the closure was " beyond our control. '' My relationship manager advocated for me for weeks, including on weekends and after hours, yet the restriction persisted and the false notices kept arriving. Citibank 's own Florida wealth-management leadership admitted the closure was a system defect, said they had escalated it to senior bank-operations leadership, and still could neither prevent the renewed restriction nor stop Citibank 's systems from mailing me notices they themselves told me to disregard to the point that, in XXXX XXXX, a senior Citibank manager was reduced to escalating internally to try to switch off the bank 's automated " missing information '' messages, which the system continued to generate by default. When a bank 's own advisor, relationship manager, and senior management all acknowledge the customer did nothing wrong and still can not stop the bank 's systems from closing his accounts, freezing his retirement assets, and mailing him false liquidation threats, the failure is systemic not the error of any one employee. I am asking the CFPB to require Citibank to : ( 1 ) produce the recordings of my XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX KYC calls under Reference ID XXXX, and the XX/XX/XXXX call from its wealth-management leadership ; ( 2 ) explain the basis for closing and then restricting my accounts after its own representatives confirmed my compliance and after its own management attributed the closure to a system defect, including how it could restrict my accounts for " missing information '' that its own KYC department confirmed on a recorded call the same day, and that its own relationship manager confirmed in writing on XX/XX/XXXX, had already been provided and accepted ; ( 3 ) reverse any fees or third-party charges ( e.g., stop-payment fees ) caused by the closure ; ( 4 ) correct the inaccurate source-of-wealth/employment records that drove the adverse action ; and ( 5 ) given Citi management 's own statement that this defect is affecting " far too many '' customers, examine whether other consumers have been subjected to the same wrongful closures.

XX/XX/XXXX : Allys portal shows one payment Completed : {$560.00} on XX/XX/XXXX Allys own system sent payment confirmation notices acknowledging receipt XXXX XXXX records show two subsequent returns : {$560.00} returned XX/XX/XXXX, {$560.00} returned XX/XX/XXXX A third payment of {$560.00} cleared via XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX with no return Ally reported XX/XX/XXXX as a 30-day late month Ally accepted and confirmed payment, then clawed funds back and reported delinquency. I am submitting this complaint regarding the servicing of my auto loan and my repeated efforts to resolve the account and retain my vehicle. This complaint is supported by documentation, including payment records, written correspondence, the settlement offer I received, and a recorded conversation in which a CarMax supervisor acknowledged that I had been provided incorrect payment information by a CarMax representative. I became delinquent on my loan but remained in communication with CarMax Auto Finance and actively attempted to bring the account current. During that process, I relied on payment information provided by a CarMax representative that was later acknowledged by a supervisor to be incorrect. Based on that information, I attempted to make my payment within the timeframe I had been given. However, because my account had become sufficiently delinquent, I was unable to make payments through the online payment system and instead had to rely on other payment methods, such as making a payment in person at a CarMax retail location. I relied on the information provided in good faith and would have taken different action had accurate information been provided. After I escalated the issue, I was advised that my account would be reviewed and that I would be notified regarding the outcome. While I was later informed that correspondence may have been mailed, I was not made aware of the outcome of that review at the time and did not receive any communication clearly advising me that the account remained charged off or explaining what action was required on my part. As a result, I remained uncertain regarding the status of my account and what steps were necessary to preserve it. During that period, I did not know whether the charge-off had been reversed, whether the account had been returned to active repayment status, whether I should resume regular monthly payments, whether a different payment amount was required, or how any payment I made would be applied while the account review remained unresolved. Because I could not make payments online, I depended on clear communication from CarMax regarding the amount required and the appropriate method of payment. I did not know whether a payment other than a regular monthly payment would reduce the delinquency, be applied toward reinstatement, or otherwise preserve the account. It was not until later that I learned the account remained charged off and that approximately {$6000.00} was being requested to bring the account back on track. Had I been made aware of the outcome of the review sooner, I would have been in a better position to understand what payment was expected, how it would be applied, and what actions were required to preserve the account. Despite these events, I continued acting in good faith to resolve the account. After the representative error and subsequent charge-off, I paid {$260.00} and then paid the remaining {$780.00}, completing the full monthly payment of {$1000.00} that had been due when the incorrect payment information was originally provided. I later made an additional payment of {$390.00}, demonstrating my continued commitment to satisfy my loan obligations and retain the vehicle. Throughout my prior dealings with CarMax, I was accustomed to receiving multiple telephone calls when my account became delinquent. During the period in which I believed the account review was pending, I did not receive those customary collection calls or any communication explaining the outcome of the review or identifying what payment was required to preserve the account. Instead, I later learned the account remained charged off and was subsequently presented with a settlement offer of approximately {$23000.00} rather than a response to my hardship and reinstatement requests. My efforts to resolve this matter continued despite significant communication issues. A supervisor contacted me regarding my account, but when I returned the call approximately five minutes later, I was advised by a customer service representative that the supervisor was unavailable and that no solution was available. I requested another call and was told I would receive a return call within 48 hours, but I did not receive that call. I submitted multiple written requests seeking clarification regarding the account review, my account status, hardship assistance, reinstatement, re-aging, extension, repayment options, repossession status, and GAP insurance information. I also forwarded two of those emails to a supervisor after being informed that CarMax generally does not respond to emails. Despite these efforts, I have not received a substantive response addressing my requests or identifying a reasonable repayment solution. At every stage of this process, my objective has remained the same : to retain my vehicle, continue making payments, and resolve the accountnot to avoid my financial obligations. I have recently returned to work and am now in a position to resume regular payments if a reasonable repayment arrangement can be established. I respectfully request that CarMax conduct a comprehensive executive review of my account ; review the acknowledged representative error and the subsequent servicing and communication issues ; provide a written explanation of the outcome of the prior account review ; respond to my outstanding hardship requests ; explain the basis for the approximately {$6000.00} reinstatement demand and the subsequent settlement offer of approximately {$23000.00} ; evaluate my account for any available hardship assistance, reinstatement, re-aging, extension, loss mitigation, or repayment programs ; clarify the status of repossession activity ; provide clarification regarding my GAP insurance and any applicable refund ; and work with me to establish a reasonable repayment arrangement that would allow me to retain my vehicle while continuing to satisfy my loan obligations. I believe I made repeated good-faith efforts to resolve this account, continued making payments despite the servicing issues, consistently sought guidance regarding how to preserve the account, and repeatedly requested assistance rather than avoiding my financial obligations. I respectfully request that the CFPB ask CarMax to investigate these issues, address each of the concerns raised in this complaint, and provide a detailed written response explaining its findings and any available options for resolving this matter. Due to the CFPB attachment limits, I have not been able to upload every email and document related to this matter. However, I have retained additional correspondence documenting my continued efforts to resolve the account, request hardship assistance, seek clarification regarding my account status, and communicate with CarMax representatives. I am prepared to provide those additional materials upon request.

Consumer complaint narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Complaint Regarding American Expresss Handling of a Billing Dispute I am submitting this complaint regarding the manner in which American Express handled a dispute involving charges that I know I did not authorize. I have been an American Express Business Cardmember since 1999. After discovering the disputed charges, I followed every process made available to me through American Express. Over the course of multiple dispute reviews, numerous telephone conversations, written submissions, and escalation to the American Express Executive Office, I repeatedly sought to understand the basis upon which American Express determined that I remained financially responsible for these charges. The underlying facts of the matter, together with all supporting evidence and documentation, were fully presented to American Express during the Executive Review process ( see attached ). Despite receiving this information and conducting both the dispute review process and an Executive Office review, American Express ultimately concluded that I remained financially responsible for the disputed charges. My concern is the process by which that outcome was reached. In its written correspondence to me, American Express acknowledged the following : We did not identify documentation showing that an independent forensic review of the agreement or its execution data was performed. Despite this acknowledgment, American Express nevertheless relied upon that same agreement as the basis for holding me financially responsible for the disputed charges. The existence of an initial authorized transaction or a prior business relationship does not, in itself, establish authorization for subsequent disputed charges. Nevertheless, American Express chose to uphold the charges despite acknowledging that it had not identified any independent verification of the agreement upon which those charges relied. I respectfully submit that this raises an important consumer protection concern. The question I respectfully ask the CFPB to consider is whether it is fair and reasonable for a financial institution to hold a customer financially responsible for disputed charges while acknowledging that it did not independently verify the very agreement upon which its determination relied. American Express had before it all of the information I was able to provide, including documentation and evidence supporting my position. However, despite acknowledging that it had not identified any independent verification of the agreement or its execution data, it nevertheless chose to rely on that agreement to uphold the charges. I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether American Expresss handling of this matter was fair, reasonable, and consistent with the protections consumers should expect when disputing charges they know they did not authorize. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, XXXX

General statements regarding routing, automated system flags, or deposit size do not legally justify a 100 % freeze.Breach of 12 CFR 229.21 ( Civil Liability ) : By making the funds fully available at XXXX XXXX and subsequently pulling them back after I spent {$250.00}, the bank has exposed my business to immediate financial distress. The most serious issue occurred at closing. Navy Federal did not have the closing package prepared in time, resulting in a delay of the scheduled closing. Even on the day of closing, critical documents were still outstanding and the transaction was not ready to proceed as scheduled despite the lender having had possession of the file for months. As a veteran using a VA loan, I expected Navy Federal to possess a strong understanding of VA lending requirements and eligibility documentation. Instead, I experienced repeated challenges regarding a valid funding fee exemption, last-minute personnel changes, poor communication, and a delayed closing caused by the lender 's failure to have the loan package ready. I am requesting that Navy Federal explain : Why my VA funding fee exemption was repeatedly questioned despite a valid COE. Why key personnel assigned to my loan were changed immediately before closing. Why communication regarding the status of my loan was inadequate throughout the process. Why the loan package and closing documents were not completed in time for the scheduled closing. What corrective actions Navy Federal will take to prevent similar issues from affecting future VA borrowers. Veterans should be able to rely on lenders that actively market VA loan expertise. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against Equifax Information Solutions , Inc. for maintaining a corrupted XXXX XXXX tradeline on my credit file that contains multiple mathematical impossibilities and logical contradictions when cross-referenced against XXXX and XXXX. This is not a dispute about whether I owe a debt. This is a complaint about data integrity failures that violate Metro 2 formatting standards and the CDIA Credit Reporting Resource Guide. I previously filed a CFPB complaint against Equifax on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX. Equifax closed that complaint as " Company Responded '' but did NOT delete the account or correct the data corruption. It has now been more than 60 days and the corrupted tradeline remains on my report, actively damaging my credit score. CROSS-BUREAU METRO 2 FIELD VIOLATIONS XXXX XXXX ( Account ending in XXXX ) : Field XXXX ( Credit Limit ) Mathematical Impossibility : Equifax reports a Credit Limit of {$9000.00}. XXXX reports {$10000.00}. XXXX reports {$9000.00}. This is a {$1300.00} variance ( 14.8 % discrepancy ) between Equifax and XXXX on the same account, same reporting date ( XX/XX/XXXX ). Per the CDIA Credit Reporting Resource Guide Section 3.4.1, the Credit Limit must remain constant across all repositories when sourced from the same primary ledger. A 14.8 % variance proves the data is estimated, not verified from actual contract documentation. Equifax is maintaining a figure that can not be reconciled with XXXX XXXX reporting of the same obligation. Field XXXX ( Payment Status ) Logical Contradiction : Equifax reports Status " Charge-off. '' XXXX reports " Account charged off. {$10000.00} written off. {$10000.00} past due as of XX/XX/XXXX. '' XXXX reports " Charged off as bad debt. '' These are three distinct status descriptions for the same event. Per CRRG Section 3.4.17, Payment Status codes must be standardized. Equifax uses a generic " Charge-off '' label while XXXX adds contradictory sub-elements ( " written off '' AND " past due '' simultaneously ). XXXX uses yet another variant. This terminology inconsistency proves the furnisher is not transmitting standardized Metro 2 data, and Equifax is applying its own interpretive framework rather than maintaining the " Maximum Possible Accuracy '' standard required by 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). Field XXXX ( Current Balance ) Ledger Exactness Failure : All three bureaus report {$10000.00} Current Balance. However, Equifax reports this against a {$9000.00} Credit Limit. XXXX reports it against {$10000.00}. The balance-to-limit ratio is 117.1 % on Equifax ( over-limit by {$1500.00} ) versus 102.1 % on XXXX ( over-limit by {$200.00} ). These are two different utilization calculations for the same account. Per CRRG Section 3.4.11, utilization percentages must be mathematically derivable from the reported fields. When the same balance produces two different utilization rates due to limit variance, the underlying data is corrupted. Equifax 's 117.1 % utilization on a revolving account is a mathematical impossibility without documented credit line increase, fee capitalization, or interest accrual records none of which appear in any field. Field XXXX / XXXX ( Account Type ) Product Classification Error : Equifax reports " Revolving . '' XXXX reports " Credit Card. '' XXXX reports " Revolving account. '' Per Metro 2 standards, " Credit Card '' and " Revolving '' are distinct portfolio classifications with different data structures. A " Credit Card '' implies specific payment calculation methods ( minimum payment based on balance + interest ). A " Revolving '' account implies open-ended credit line behavior. Equifax and XXXX classify this as " Revolving '' while XXXX classifies it as " Credit Card. '' This product type inconsistency across repositories proves the furnisher is transmitting ambiguous data, and Equifax is not applying standardized classification rules. Per CRRG Section 3.4.1, Account Type must be consistent. Variance indicates data tape corruption or mixed-file contamination. Field BS-25 ( Payment History Profile ) Incomplete Furnishing / Ghost Data : XXXX reports `` No payment history available to display. '' Equifax shows a partial grid with codes 90, 120, 120, CO. XXXX shows a more complete grid with 90, 120, 150, CO , CO , CO plus ND markers. Per CRRG Section 3.4, a negative-status account MUST include the complete Payment History Profile to validate the path to delinquency. XXXX XXXX blank grid means the " Charged off as bad debt '' status has no underlying history matrix to prove how the account reached charge-off. This is " ghost '' data a negative result without the proof. Equifax 's partial grid ( missing 150-day code that XXXX shows ) is incomplete furnishing. The XXXX CFPB Consent Order against XXXX ( XXXX ) found that furnishers violated Metro 2 requirements by reporting accounts with inaccurate payment history profiles, causing consumers to be reported as delinquent when they were not. Equifax is accepting similarly corrupted payment history data without verification. XXXX XXXX ( Account Status / Open-Closed ) : Equifax reports " Closed . '' XXXX reports " Closed. '' XXXX reports " Closed. '' However, Equifax lists " Highest balance '' as blank ( ) while XXXX shows {$10000.00} and XXXX shows {$10000.00}. The Highest Balance field ( XXXX ) is mandatory for closed revolving accounts to document the maximum extension of credit. Equifax 's blank field means the account record is incomplete. A closed account with a {$10000.00} balance but no documented highest balance can not be scored accurately by FICO algorithms, which rely on High Credit to calculate utilization trends. This missing field renders the tradeline unverifiable for credit scoring purposes. Field XXXX ( Comments ) Factual Contradiction : Equifax comments : " CHARGED OFF ACCOUNT / ACCOUNT CLOSED BY CREDIT GRANTOR. '' XXXX comments : " Canceled by credit grantor. '' XXXX comments : " Account closed at credit grantor 's request. '' These are three different events : " Charge-off '' is an accounting write-off. " Account closed by credit grantor '' implies voluntary closure by the lender. " Canceled by credit grantor '' implies revocation of credit privileges. " Account closed at credit grantor 's request '' implies the consumer complied with a closure request. These are mutually exclusive factual events per CRRG definitions. An account can not be simultaneously " charged off '' ( default ) and " closed by request '' ( non-default ). Equifax 's compound comment merges two incompatible statuses, creating a misleading impression that violates the " clear and accurate '' disclosure standard established in XXXX v. Equifax Information Services. Field XXXX ( Date Opened ) Temporal Consistency : All three bureaus report XX/XX/XXXX. This is the only field that matches exactly across repositories. However, given that every other field contains variance, this single matching date is suspicious it suggests the furnisher transmitted only the origination date correctly while corrupting all subsequent data elements. Per CRRG Section 3.4, consistency in one field does not validate corruption in all others. Field XXXX ( Date of Last Payment ) Missing Critical Data : None of the three bureaus report a Date of Last Payment. For an account opened XX/XX/XXXX and charged off in XXXX, there should be a documented last payment date that triggered the delinquency sequence. The absence of this field across all repositories means the delinquency timeline can not be verified. Per Metro 2 standards, Date of Last Payment is required to calculate the 180-day charge-off window. Without it, the charge-off timing is unverifiable. SYSTEMIC FAILURE PATTERN : The CFPB 's XX/XX/XXXX Consent Order against Equifax ( XXXX ) found that Equifax " failed to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy, '' used " ineffective systems and flawed processes with excessive deference to furnishers, '' and had " coding errors '' that caused miscalculations in consumer credit scores. The CFPB ordered Equifax to pay {$15.00} XXXX for these failures. I am experiencing the exact same systemic failures with this XXXX account. Equifax is maintaining data with : 14.8 % Credit Limit variance against XXXX Inconsistent Payment Status terminology across three repositories 117.1 % utilization rate ( mathematically impossible without documentation ) Product classification inconsistency ( Revolving vs. Credit Card ) Incomplete Payment History Profile ( missing 150-day code vs. XXXXXXXX XXXX complete blank ) Blank Highest Balance field on a closed account Mutually exclusive Comments fields merged into a single misleading statement Missing Date of Last Payment required for delinquency verification Equifax 's `` investigation '' of my previous complaint ( XX/XX/XXXX ) consisted of nothing more than accepting XXXXXXXX XXXX automated response without examining these cross-bureau mathematical impossibilities. This is exactly the " excessive deference to furnishers '' that the CFPB already sanctioned Equifax for in XX/XX/XXXX. The CFPB is currently litigating against XXXX ( CFPB v. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX. XXXX. ) for " sham investigations '' and failure to properly verify disputed data. Equifax 's conduct with my account mirrors this pattern automated verification without human review of obvious mathematical contradictions.

Consumer complaint narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of a fraud incident involving my accounts and my daughter 's accounts by Randolph-Brooks Federal Credit Union ( RBFCU ). At the time of this incident, a total of {$18000.00} was held across five accounts belonging to me and my daughter. On XX/XX/year>, I received a phone call that appeared to originate from RBFCU 's XXXX XXXX, Texas phone number. The caller identified himself as " XXXX '' from RBFCU and stated that there was suspicious activity on my account originating from XXXX, Georgia. He asked whether I had authorized any transactions from that location. I responded that I had not and that I wanted to dispute any unauthorized activity. During the call, the individual provided personal information that appeared to verify he was associated with my bank, including my account information, date of birth, Social Security number, and the answer to my account security question. When I expressed concern about providing information over the phone, I specifically stated that I would not give out my personal information. The caller responded that RBFCU would never ask me to provide personal information and that he was simply reviewing suspicious activity. The caller placed me on hold several times while claiming to investigate and dispute transactions. He then provided what he described as a fraud claim number ( Case No. ____________ ) and scheduled a follow-up appointment for the following day. He informed me that my online banking access would be unavailable for 24 to 48 hours while the fraud investigation was being processed, but stated that our debit cards would continue to work. On XX/XX/year>, the caller contacted me again and informed me that my account had been compromised. He stated that an unauthorized individual had obtained my account number and routing number and that I would need to establish a new account. He advised me that funds had been moved in three transactions : {$5000.00}, {$5000.00}, and {$5900.00}. The caller instructed me to log into my online banking account. When I did so, I discovered that my daughter 's checking account, my daughter 's savings account, and my savings account had all been reduced to XXXX. My checking account showed a balance of {$15000.00}, which did not equal the total amount that had previously existed across our five accounts. Based on the balances that existed before the incident, approximately {$18000.00} should have been present across those accounts. This means that approximately {$2800.00} was unaccounted for at the time I reviewed the balances. This discrepancy further increased my concern that unauthorized transactions had occurred and that funds were missing from our accounts. At this point I was in a state of panic and believed I was working directly with an RBFCU fraud representative. The caller instructed me to verify my username and then directed me to process transfers involving the amounts he had identified. He represented these actions as necessary steps to move funds into a new secure account. He then scheduled another appointment for XX/XX/year>, to establish new account information. No one from RBFCU contacted me on XX/XX/XXXX as promised. I attempted to call the credit union but was unable to remain on hold because of work obligations. Later that evening, my daughter informed me that her debit card no longer worked and that neither of us could access our online banking. On XX/XX/year>, I contacted RBFCU and explained what had occurred. I was informed by an employee that RBFCU would never call customers in the manner I described regarding fraud activity. She asked whether I had provided my username and indicated that customers should never provide that information. However, during the same conversation she immediately requested my username to verify my account, which I found confusing and inconsistent. I was then transferred to the fraud department where a fraud claim was opened. The representative informed me that one transaction had already been flagged as suspicious and that I might be able to recover those funds. However, she did not obtain a complete statement regarding the events that occurred, did not ask for a detailed timeline, did not provide meaningful guidance regarding securing my accounts, did not offer assistance opening replacement accounts, and did not explain how I could regain access to my online banking. On XX/XX/year>, I contacted RBFCU again and spoke with a fraud department employee named XXXX. I informed him that a fraud claim had been opened the previous day. After reviewing my account, XXXX initially stated, " Ma'am, there is no fraud claim on this account. '' I then provided him with the fraud claim number I had been given. Only after I supplied the case number did he acknowledge that a claim existed and state that he could see it in the system. During that conversation XXXX asked me to answer my account security question. He informed me that my answer was incorrect. He then changed my security question to a new one. This raised serious concerns because the answer I provided had previously been correct. The fact that my security question had apparently been altered suggests that unauthorized changes may have been made to my account security settings. At no point during the conversation did XXXX address how or when the security question had been changed, who had changed it, or whether this indicated additional unauthorized access to my account. I also asked XXXX whether my daughter needed to open a separate fraud claim because her accounts had also been affected. XXXX specifically advised that she did not need to file her own claim because our accounts were linked. However, when my daughter later visited RBFCU on two separate occasions, two different employees informed her that she should have opened her own fraud claim. This conflicting information created confusion and raises concerns regarding whether her losses were properly documented and investigated. During the same call, XXXX instructed me to open a new checking account and a new savings account, which I did. I asked where any recovered funds or reimbursement would be deposited once the investigation concluded. XXXX responded that the funds would go into " either one '' of the accounts but did not provide a clear answer, confirmation, or documentation regarding where reimbursement funds would be deposited. Additionally, despite the fact that I repeatedly explained that I was unable to access my accounts, XXXX did not provide meaningful assistance in restoring my online banking access or helping me regain control of my accounts. On XX/XX/year>, I sent a detailed written statement to RBFCU 's fraud department outlining my concerns regarding the incident and investigation. In that communication, I explained that I disagreed with any characterization of this matter as merely a scam in which I voluntarily authorized transactions. I explained that the caller possessed sensitive account information before I ever disclosed my username and appeared to have access to information that should not have been available to an unauthorized individual. I am concerned that unauthorized access to my account occurred before I disclosed any information and I request that the credit union investigate whether an account compromise, security failure, or other unauthorized access event occurred. Throughout this process I have received conflicting information from multiple RBFCU employees regarding the existence of my fraud claim, account security changes, whether my daughter required her own claim, and how reimbursement funds would be handled. These inconsistencies have made it extremely difficult to understand the status of the investigation and have undermined my confidence in the credit union 's handling of this matter. My concerns include the following : 1. RBFCU did not obtain a complete statement regarding the fraudulent activity before beginning its investigation. 2. RBFCU employees provided inconsistent and contradictory information regarding account security, fraud reporting requirements, and investigation procedures. 3. I was not provided timely or adequate assistance in securing my accounts or regaining access to my banking services. 4. My daughter and I were left without reliable access to our accounts and banking services. 5. Apparently unauthorized changes were made to my account security settings, including my security question, and these changes were not adequately investigated or explained. 6. I am concerned that RBFCU may be improperly treating these transactions as authorized solely because I was deceived by an individual impersonating a bank employee. 7. I request confirmation that RBFCU is conducting a full Regulation E investigation into all unauthorized electronic fund transfers associated with this incident. 8. I request that RBFCU provide any provisional credit required under Regulation E while the investigation remains pending. 9. I request a full accounting of all transactions, account changes, security setting modifications, login activity, and investigative findings related to this incident. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau review RBFCU 's handling of this matter, ensure that a thorough investigation is conducted, and require the credit union to provide a clear explanation of its findings and compliance with applicable consumer protection laws and Regulation E requirements. Thank you for your assistance. XXXX XXXX

To Whom It May Concern, This correspondence concerns Loan Number XXXX, originally held by my mother, XXXX XXXX XXXX, deceased. I am XXXX XXXX XXXX, her lawful successor in interest regarding the property secured by this loan. Since I apparently have to go to great lengths to spell this out, I want this matter clearly documented. Select Portfolio Servicing has repeatedly contradicted itself, changed its story, lost or disregarded documents, and continued creating problems since my mother passed away. Shortly after my mother died, I was told that the house was going to be closed, that SPS was forcing the matter, and that SPS would not do business with me. SPS also put that position in writing. I went to great lengths to explain what was going on and to provide the documentation required by law, yet SPS still refused to properly communicate with me. Sending me threatening letters, of intent to foreclose At the same time, SPS continued sending letters and correspondence while refusing to properly recognize my rights as successor in interest. I called SPS out on that, told SPS to cease and desist from improper handling, and SPS appeared to follow that directive only after I made the issue clear. I have submitted the required legal documentation numerous times, including the death certificate and the recorded XXXX XXXX deed / enhanced life estate deed. SPS specifically stated that those documents would suffice, and under the law, those documents are sufficient to establish my successor in interest status and ownership interest. I have submitted those documents four separate times. The first two times, SPS claimed it could not locate them, did not receive them, or otherwise could not find them. I then submitted them again. SPS later claimed the documents were not sufficient because the death certificate was supposedly missing, so I submitted both the death certificate and the XXXX XXXX deed again. After that, I was informed that only the death certificate was supposedly invalid, for whatever reason. SPS has repeatedly claimed the death certificate was invalid while never properly disclosing to me that SPS considered the XXXX XXXX deed improper or invalid. In fact, at no time before SPS responded to the CFPB did SPS disclose that it was claiming the XXXX XXXX deed was invalid. I have had numerous emails, calls, and letters back and forth regarding this entire situation, and not once did SPS clearly disclose that position to me before then. SPS has consistently changed its story. SPS also provided, in writing to the CFPB, the basic legal definition of a XXXX XXXX deed : that the original owner retains control of the property during life while naming a beneficiary or remainder person to receive the property upon death if the deed is not revoked or otherwise changed. That is exactly the type of deed involved here. The contradiction is obvious. SPS acknowledged the legal function of a XXXX XXXX deed while refusing to properly accept and process the deed that establishes my interest in the property. That is unreasonable, inconsistent, and appears to be a blatant violation of federal mortgage servicing law. Under Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.30 ( d ), a confirmed successor in interest must be treated as a borrower for purposes of the applicable mortgage servicing protections. Federal mortgage servicing rules also make clear that a successor in interest does not have to formally assume the mortgage loan before being treated as a borrower for those servicing protections. SPS has repeatedly told me, in writing and on recorded lines, that I can not be helped and that I am being forced to assume the mortgage. That is not what federal law requires. SPS can not use formal assumption as an excuse to deny basic servicing rights, communication, review, or assistance once successor in interest status is established. Additionally, 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 requires mortgage servicers to maintain reasonable policies and procedures to provide accurate and timely information, investigate and respond to complaints, communicate with potential and confirmed successors in interest, determine what documents are reasonably required, and promptly make a determination. This is not my failure to provide contact informationit is their failure to use accurate information to attempt contact. Having incorrect contact information in their system does not validate their claim or excuse their collection efforts. A debt collector 's inability to reach a consumer due to their own failure to maintain accurate records is not a defense to the underlying dispute. I was and remain reachable at my correct contact information. This response suggests Harris and Harris conducted minimal investigation into this debt claim and proceeded with collection activity without proper verificationa violation of FDCPA Section 809 ( b ), which requires debt collectors to provide notice of the debt within five days of initial contact and acknowledge disputes. 3. REQUEST FOR IMMEDIATE ACTION I demand that Harris and Harris immediately : 1. 1. Cease all collection activity on this account 2. 2. Remove the debt from their active collection portfolio 3. 3. Confirm in writing that this debt claim is closed 4. 4. Provide evidence of their investigation into payment status if they dispute that the debt was paid 4. VIOLATION OF CONSUMER PROTECTION LAW Harris and Harris ' actions appear to violate multiple consumer protection statutes : the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. ), the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ), and applicable state debt collection laws. By attempting to collect a debt that has been paid without proper verification and by accepting responsibility for their own record-keeping failures, they are engaging in prohibited collection practices. 5. WHY THEIR RESPONSE IS INADEQUATE Harris and Harris has not disputed the core fact : that I paid this debt directly to XXXX. They have not provided any documentation showing the debt is outstanding. They have not explained why they held outdated contact information. They have not provided evidence of reasonable investigation before sending collection notices. Simply asserting that a debt is 'valid ' is not the same as proving it. A professional debt collector should maintain accurate records, respond appropriately to disputes, and provide clear documentation when challenged.

I am submitting this complaint regarding MOHELAs handling of my federal student loan account, specifically its failure to provide accurate information, maintain adequate account records, timely process borrower requests, and provide reasonable access to customer service representatives. On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a XXXX XXXX to Repayment application relating to my law school loans. My application is based on allegations that my law school made representations that I believe misled students regarding aspects of the educational program. After submitting the application, I sought information from MOHELA regarding how the application would affect my account and whether any forbearance would be applied while the application remained pending. Before attempting to contact MOHELA by telephone, I utilized the servicers online messaging and email platform to ask questions regarding my XXXX XXXX application, the status of any associated forbearance, and whether applying for a new income-driven repayment plan would affect that forbearance. Instead of receiving responses that addressed my specific questions, I received generic, boilerplate replies that did not correspond to the subject matter of my inquiries and provided no meaningful assistance. The responses failed to answer the questions I asked and left me without the information necessary to make informed decisions regarding my student loans. Because MOHELAs written communication platform did not provide substantive assistance, I was effectively forced to contact the servicer by telephone. Approximately XXXX week after submitting my XXXX XXXX application, I called MOHELA because I had become aware of numerous reports from borrowers indicating that applying for a new income-driven repayment plan was resulting in the loss of existing forbearances. At the time, I was in SAVE-related forbearance. Due to the ongoing transition away from the XXXX XXXX, borrowers were being required to select alternative repayment options before XX/XX/year>. Before submitting a new application, I wanted confirmation that doing so would not interfere with any forbearance associated with my pending XXXX XXXX application. After waiting approximately XXXX hours to reach a representative, I explained my concerns and specifically asked whether applying for a different income-driven repayment plan would affect any XXXX Defense-related XXXX XXXX The representative advised me that applying for a new repayment plan should not impact that forbearance. The representative further stated that if any issue did arise, MOHELA could correct it. Based on those representations, I proceeded to submit an application for the XXXX repayment plan. Later, I discovered that I was being removed from forbearance. This was contrary to the information I had been provided and created significant confusion regarding the status of my account. As a result, I contacted MOHELA again. This second call required approximately XXXX and a half to XXXX hours of waiting before I was able to speak with a representative. When I finally reached someone, the representative initially stated that she could not locate any record of my XXXX XXXX application. After placing me on hold again, she eventually located the application but informed me that there were no notes on my account reflecting my prior telephone call, despite the fact that I had spent approximately XXXX hours waiting to obtain guidance before submitting my XXXX application. The representative then informed me for the first time that XXXX XXXX forbearance would not automatically take effect for approximately XXXX days after submission of the application. This critical information had never been disclosed during my earlier conversation with MOHELA, despite the fact that it directly related to the questions I had asked and the decisions I was attempting to make regarding my repayment options. When I expressed concern about receiving inconsistent information, the representative advised that a processing forbearance could be placed on my account and asked whether I wanted that option applied. I agreed. However, I then had to ask additional questions regarding when that forbearance would appear on my account because I had little confidence that the information I was receiving was accurate. As of the date of this complaint, I remain concerned that the forbearance may not have been properly applied and that I may be forced to endure another multi-hour wait simply to verify the status of my account. My complaint is not limited to these individual interactions. Rather, it concerns a broader pattern of inadequate customer service, inconsistent information, poor account documentation, and excessive barriers to obtaining assistance. MOHELAs written communication system appears designed to generate automated responses rather than meaningfully address borrower inquiries, leaving borrowers with no practical option other than enduring multi-hour telephone wait times to obtain account-specific information. Borrowers should not be required to wait XXXX to XXXX hours simply to obtain basic information regarding federal student loan programs. Borrowers also should not receive conflicting guidance from different representatives regarding issues that can significantly affect repayment obligations, forbearance status, and account administration. I am fortunate to work remotely and have the flexibility to remain on hold for several hours. Many borrowers do not have that luxury. Individuals who work in XXXX, education, retail, manufacturing, transportation, and other occupations may be unable to spend half a workday waiting to speak with a loan servicer. MOHELAs current customer service practices create substantial barriers to obtaining information and accessing federal student loan benefits. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate MOHELAs handling of XXXX XXXX applications, its communication practices regarding forbearance eligibility and processing timelines, its account documentation procedures, its responsiveness to borrower inquiries submitted through its online communication platform, and the excessive wait times borrowers experience when attempting to obtain assistance regarding their federal student loans.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Chase 's handling of a XXXX transfer that was sent to an unintended recipient and the bank 's subsequent denial of my claim despite evidence that I reasonably relied on information presented through the bank 's XXXX service. On XX/XX/year>, I initiated a XXXX payment in the amount of {$400.00} to a contact that I selected from my phone 's contact list. Upon further investigation, I discovered that the payment had been delivered to a different individual. I immediately began gathering evidence and taking screenshots of the transaction details and recipient information displayed within the bank 's system. At the time of the transaction, the bank 's website displayed confirmation information that led me to believe the payment was being sent to my intended recipient. However, there was another confirmation with the same amount but listing a business name that I did not recognize. I have retained screenshots documenting what was shown to me before and after the transaction. Based on the information presented by the bank 's system, I had no reason to believe the funds would be delivered to a different person initially. I contacted Chase bank and was told to contact XXXX. XXXX informed me that the matter must be handled by my financial institution because the transaction was processed through the bank 's XXXX service. I then contacted Chase bank and was advised that the matter would be researched and to allow time for the transaction to post because it was still pending. Despite waiting several weeks, I received little or no meaningful communication regarding the status of the investigation. Because I was unable to obtain a resolution, I formally filed a claim with the bank. The bank ultimately denied my claim. However, the denial did not adequately address the evidence I submitted, including screenshots and documentation showing the recipient information presented through the bank 's system. The bank also failed to explain how a payment selected from my contact list and confirmed through its interface was ultimately delivered to a different recipient. I do not believe the investigation fully considered the facts of the case or my supporting evidence. I later did a test for {$1.00} that was successfully delivered to my contact ; which proves that no issue was happening with his number and was clearly a bank error. My concern is not simply that the payment reached the wrong person. Rather, my concern is that I relied on information displayed by the bank 's XXXX platform when initiating the transfer, and the bank has failed to adequately explain the discrepancy or conduct a thorough investigation into how the payment was routed to an unintended recipient. I respectfully request that the CFPB review the bank 's handling of this matter and require the bank to : Provide a complete explanation of how the payment was directed to the unintended recipient. Provide all records and findings from its investigation. Review the screenshots and evidence I submitted. Reconsider its denial based on the information available. Reimburse the transferred funds if the evidence demonstrates that the bank 's system displayed inaccurate or misleading recipient information or otherwise contributed to the misdirection of the payment. I have supporting documentation, including transaction records, screenshots, correspondence with the bank, correspondence with XXXX, and evidence that the intended recipient never received the funds. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Rather than ignore the letters, I immediately forwarded them to our XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and specifically sought guidance regarding whether any action was required. Submitted the requested insurance documentation. XXXX. Received written confirmation from the bank that the issue was resolved. XXXX. Forwarded subsequent notices to the bank 's XXXX XXXX representative. XXXX. Requested guidance regarding any further action needed. Neither XXXX XXXX nor anyone else from U.S. Bank informed me that : The new notices allegedly concerned a separate wind insurance requirement ( which to our knowledge, had never been required in the past ) The bank considered us non-compliant ; Force-placed insurance was being contemplated ; Failure to take additional action could result in over {$5000.00} dollars in charges being added to the HELOC ; or Immediate action was required to avoid force-placement. Because I had already received written confirmation that the insurance issue was resolved and because I had escalated the subsequent notices to the bank 's XXXX XXXX representative and heard nothing back, I reasonably believed the matter had been addressed. Importantly, I did not ignore the notices. I forwarded them to the bank and asked for assistance. No one including XXXX XXXX called me or emailed me to explain there was still a problem. Force-Placed Insurance On XX/XX/year>, we received a letter dated XX/XX/year>, informing us that U.S. Bank XXXX XXXX wind insurance on the property retroactive to XX/XX/year>, at a cost of {$5400.00}. This was the first time we understood that U.S. Bank believed any insurance issue remained unresolved. I immediately contacted XXXX XXXX and sought assistance and although he had been my primary contact at the bank for about a decade he referred me to the loan department and was unwilling to help me. A U.S. Bank loan representative in the loan department then informed me that the bank had repeatedly communicated by phone with our insurance carrier regarding the alleged deficiency. However, neither my husband nor I received a direct phone call or email, from U.S. Bank explaining that force-placed insurance was imminent or that a {$5400.00} charge would be imposed. Again, no one in XXXX XXXX, who had handled everything for us for over a decade, communicated a word to us despite repeated inquiries! Had anyone just explained that wind coverage was allegedly missing and that force-placed insurance would otherwise be purchased, we would have immediately resolved the issue or simply closed the unused HELOC. Excessive Insurance Cost After learning of the force-placed coverage, our insurance agent quoted us {$1700.00} for comparable wind, hurricane, etc. coverage. U.S. Bank charged {$5400.00} for force-placed coveragemore than XXXX times the quoted market cost. Contradictory Information Regarding HELOC Closure Once I became aware of the issue, I immediately and repeatedly requested closure of the unused HELOC. I was pleased that in XX/XX/year>, U.S. Bank sent me a written letter stating that nothing was due on the HELOC and that I simply needed to sign and return a document if I wished to close the account. Seemed clear that they waived the forced placed insurance fee. However, when I subsequently contacted the bank to complete the closure process, I was told that the {$5400.00} force-placed insurance charge had to be paid before the HELOC could be closed. These contradictory statements created further confusion. On XXXX hand, the bank 's written communication stated that nothing was due and only a closure form was required. On the other hand, bank representatives informed me that a substantial balance had to be paid before closure would be allowed. Unauthorized Duplicate Withdrawal On XX/XX/year>, a U.S. Bank loan servicing representative, XXXX ( Badge # ZVQ ), advised me that paying the {$5400.00} charge would stop additional insurance-related charges from accruing while my request for review, refund, and closure remained pending. Based on that representation, I authorized a single payment of {$5400.00} and again requested closure of the HELOC. The following day, U.S. Bank generated notices showing that XXXX separate withdrawals of {$5400.00} had been initiated from my linked XXXX XXXX Bank account. I authorized only XXXX payment. The second withdrawal was unauthorized. When I contacted U.S. Bank, I was informed that the bank would not immediately return the improperly withdrawn funds and that I would instead have to wait approximately XXXX weeks for reimbursement by paper check. As a result, U.S. Bank removed an additional {$5400.00} from my account without authorization and retained possession of those funds while requiring me to wait for the bank 's internal correction process. Why I Believe U.S. Bank Acted Improperly This situation appears to involve potential violations of federal mortgage-servicing and consumer-protection requirements, including : Failure to provide clear and effective notice before charging force-placed insurance as required under Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.37 ; Failure to exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining insurance information already provided by the borrower ; Unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, including sending written confirmation that an insurance issue was resolved while later imposing force-placed insurance based on allegedly unresolved coverage concerns ; Providing contradictory information regarding whether any balance was due before HELOC closure ; Unauthorized electronic fund withdrawal and failure to promptly correct the error after removing funds that were not authorized by the account holder. I request that regulators investigate whether U.S. Bank 's actions complied with applicable federal servicing, force-placed insurance, and consumer-protection requirements.

Consumer complaint narrative: Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), My name is XXXX XXXX XXXX I am a Citibank customer and a XXXX. I am submitting this complaint regarding Citibanks handling of a check deposit transaction, specifically its risk notification practices, the presentation of deposit status within its mobile application, and deficiencies in its complaint response process. I. Background On XX/XX/year>, I deposited a check in the amount of {$8600.00} into my Citibank account. According to Citibanks subsequent written response, the deposit was flagged for review by its XXXX XXXX Department shortly after it was submitted, and restrictions were placed on my account. Citibank further stated that the check was ultimately returned on XX/XX/year>. However, during the entire review period, I did not receive any telephone call, text message, email, mobile application alert, or other real-time notification informing me that the deposit was under fraud review or at risk of being returned. I only became aware of Citibanks concerns when I received a mailed letter on XX/XX/year>. What further contributed to my confusion was the manner in which the transaction was displayed within the Citi Mobile App. Initially, the deposit appeared as Pending. After approximately two days, the Pending status disappeared and was replaced with Deposit Teller. As an ordinary consumer, I reasonably interpreted this change to mean that the deposit had been successfully processed and credited to my account. Based on that understanding, I made subsequent financial arrangements and suffered actual financial loss. After discovering the issue, I contacted Citibank and submitted complaints, but the bank failed to provide meaningful responses to my concerns. II. Issues of Concern A. Failure to Provide Timely Risk Notification Citibank has stated that the deposit was flagged by its Fraud Prevention Department shortly after submission. Nevertheless, from the date of deposit until I received the mailed letter on XX/XX/XXXX, I received no warning of any kind regarding the transaction. In todays banking environment, Citibank has the ability to communicate with customers through telephone calls, text messages, emails, and mobile application notifications. Yet none of these methods were used. I respectfully request clarification regarding : 1. Whether Citibank maintains procedures requiring customer notification when a deposit is flagged for fraud review ; 2. If such procedures exist, whether they are sufficient to reasonably protect consumers ; 3. Why no timely notification was provided in this case ; and 4. Whether Citibank believes that relying solely on ordinary mail satisfies its obligation to provide meaningful notice of significant account risks. B. Potentially Misleading Deposit Status Display in the Mobile Application The Citi XXXX XXXX initially displayed the deposit as Pending and later changed the status to XXXX XXXX. A reasonable consumer viewing this status change would likely interpret it as indicating that the deposit had been successfully processed rather than being subject to fraud review or potential return. I respectfully request clarification regarding : XXXX. The specific meaning of the status XXXX XXXX ; XXXX. How Citibank expects consumers to interpret the transition from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ; XXXX. XXXX Citibank believes a reasonable consumer would understand from this display that the check remained subject to fraud concerns or return ; and XXXX. Why the application did not clearly display any warning or risk notice regarding the deposit. C. Deficiencies in Citibanks Complaint Handling Process When responding to my complaints, Citibanks written responses contained several factual inaccuracies and failed to address key issues. For example : XXXX. I deposited the check on XX/XX/year>, yet Citibanks response stated that the deposit occurred on XX/XX/year>. I would like clarification regarding how Citibank determined that date. XXXX. During the relevant period, my long-time Chinese-speaking relationship XXXX XXXX had already left Citibank, but I XXXX never notified. XXXX, the new one mentioned in their response has been assigned after my mother requested after the incident happened. This shows that Citibank conflated separate facts and did not carefully review my complaint. More importantly, Citibank repeatedly declined to answer the central questions raised in my complaints like timely ratification and the meaning of XXXX XXXX. Instead, the bank simply stated that the matter can not be disputed. This demonstrates a lack of basic respect, sincerity, and responsibility on Citibanks part that customers should reasonably expect ( see attachments ). III. Requested Relief I respectfully request that the CFPB review and investigate the following : 1. Citibanks procedures for notifying customers when deposits are flagged for fraud review and whether those procedures provide reasonable and timely consumer protection ; 2. The design and presentation of deposit status information within the Citi Mobile App and whether it enables consumers to accurately understand the status of deposited funds ; 3. Citibanks complaint handling procedures and the reasons for factual inaccuracies in its responses ; 4. Why Citibank declined to address key questions raised in my written complaints ; 5. What steps Citibank intends to take to improve these practices and better protect consumers ; and 6. I also request that Citibank consider reimbursement for the financial losses I suffered relating to the reasons above. I am not challenging Citibanks authority to review or return a potentially fraudulent check. Rather, my concern is whether Citibank provided timely notice, accurate account status information, and a meaningful complaint review process consistent with consumer protection principles. I respectfully request a formal explanation from Citibank regarding these issues and ask the CFPB to determine whether the banks practices are consistent with consumer protection standards. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint because a law firm that collects XXXX assessments has created and is attempting to collect an inflated, largely feedriven debt on my home through misleading and unfair practices. I am a homeowner at XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX subdivision in XXXX, Missouri. My XXXX uses XXXX XXXX XXXX as its XXXX XXXX XXXX and The Rickel Law Firm , P.C . as its thirdparty collection attorney. Rickel identifies itself in writing as a debt collector and advertises XXXX collection services that often come at no cost or no upfront cost to the association because the delinquent owner is charged the fees. Rickel has also been added as power of attorney ( POA ) for the XXXX on my account, and it filed a lien against my property electronically in that role. In XXXX I was sued over XXXX assessments. I was out of town and only learned of the lawsuit a few days before the scheduled hearing. I later discovered that important papers had been sent to an old address, so I was not properly notified in time, was not fully prepared for court, and did not understand the case. At that point, I was told by the attorney that I needed to sign a consent judgment in order to avoid going to court and to save my home. I was never given a proper, detailed, itemized invoice or a full ledger before signing. I was not told that I could dispute the underlying amounts, request validation of the debt, or challenge the collection and attorney fees. I signed under pressure to avoid losing my home, without understanding the full breakdown of charges and without having a fair chance to respond to the lawsuit. Afterward, I paid thousands of dollars under that consent judgment, including an additional large payment to stop a sheriffs levy. Despite these payments, the alleged balance on my account has continued to grow. In addition to the lawsuits and consent judgment, Rickel Law Firm, acting as POA for the XXXX, recorded a lien against my property for more than {$7000.00} for assessments only, and the lien document specifically states that this amount is exclusive of attorney fees and collection costs. That lien was filed electronically by Rickel Law Firm, but it does not have any ledger or detailed account history attached, so I can not verify which assessments were included, which periods they cover, or how that XXXX amount was calculated. Despite this, Rickel has demanded and attempted to collect large additional attorney and collection fees on top of that assessments only lien amount, treating the lien as if it secures a much larger, feeinflated debt that includes charges the lien itself says are not included. The only ledger that I have was provided by email XXXX of XXXX and it show a significant portion of what Rickel was trying to collect consisted of repeated collection, administration, flatfee, estimated localcounsel, and other lawfirm charges, not just regular HOA assessments. Many of these charges were not clearly tied to any actual work performed or to any specific authority in the XXXX governing documents. To this day, I still have not been provided with a complete, accurate XXXXside ledger from the XXXX or XXXX XXXX XXXX that would let me verify exactly which assessments, fees, and charges make up the balance Rickel is trying to collect. The HOAs own Paying Annual Assessments page states that homeowner assessments are billed yearly by late XXXX, due by XX/XX/XXXX, and only become delinquent after XX/XX/XXXX, and it tells homeowners to contact XXXX XXXX XXXX for assistance with their accounts. In my case, I did not receive the regular annual billing, updated ledgers, or clear account statements described there. Instead, assessments appear to have been added to an internal ledger and later treated as delinquent, with XXXX then adding its own fees and costs on top. When I contacted XXXX XXXX XXXX to request statements and a full account history, they refused to provide a complete ledger and directed me back to the law firm, leaving me without a transparent accounting of what is actually owed. On XX/XX/XXXX, I personally appeared in court on the current XXXX XXXX lawsuit. The associations attorney from Rickel Law Firm was not prepared to proceed and asked the court to continue the case to XX/XX/XXXX, which strongly suggested they had expected to obtain a default judgment because they did not expect me to appear. While I was in the courtroom, I watched this same attorney tell another homeowner that they could sign a consent judgment in order to get a payment plan and resolve their XXXX fXXXX issue. This confirmed for me that consent judgments are being used as a routine collection tool, with homeowners pressured to sign quickly under threat of foreclosure, rather than being given a real chance to review and dispute the charges. I believe this conduct violates the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), including the prohibition on collecting any amount ( interest, fees, charges, or expenses ) unless that amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law. In my case, the law firm is demanding payment of large, recurring collection and attorney fees on top of a lien that is explicitly for assessments only and does not include those fees, and these charges go beyond what the XXXX governing documents clearly allow. The lack of proper notice, regular billing, and a complete ledger, along with the pressure used to obtain a consent judgment, have prevented me from understanding and disputing the debt in a fair and timely manner. I am asking the CFPB to review The Rickel Law Firms collection practices, including its role as POA filing electronic liens, its no cost to the association model, the way it adds and labels its fees, its use of consent judgments in XXXX XXXX cases, and XXXX XXXX XXXX role in withholding clear account statements while steering me back to the law firm. I want the inflated and unauthorized charges removed, my account corrected to reflect only lawful assessments and properly authorized charges, and for these practices to be investigated so other homeowners are not subjected to similar harm.

My name is XXXX XXXX and I was a student at XXXX XXXX. I am filing this formal complaint regarding deceptive trade practices and violations of Texas consumer protection laws in my enrollment contract. The Core Issue : General Assembly ( and their financing partner XXXX XXXX ) induced me to sign a financial obligation by explicitly representing it as " not a loan '' and therefore not subject to federal lending protections. However, the contract contains contradictory legal clauses that prove otherwise. Evidence of Deception : Misrepresentation of Product : The " Final Disclosure '' provided by the school states : " Unlike traditional fixed payment installment loans ... an ISA represents your obligation to make payments linked to a specific, fixed percentage. '' This language was used to market the product as a non-loan alternative. Hidden Loan Status ( The " Holder Rule '' ) : Despite marketing this as " not a loan, '' Section 26 ( i ) of my signed agreement includes the FTC " Holder Rule '' notice ( 16 C.F.R. 433.2 ), which is legally required only for consumer credit contracts ( loans ). Contractual Primacy of Misrepresentation : Crucially, Section 26 ( a ) of the Signed Agreement states : " In the event of any inconsistency between this document and the Final Disclosure ... the Final Disclosure controls. '' Because the Final Disclosure explicitly frames the product as " unlike a loan, '' the contract itself mandates that this deceptive definition overrides the legal reality buried in the fine print. This proves that the " non-loan '' narrative was not accidental, but the primary, controlling representation made to the student. Violation of Texas DTPA : Under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act ( DTPA ), it is unlawful to represent that an agreement confers rights or remedies which it does not have. By including the Holder Rule notice ( admitting it is a credit contract ) while simultaneously marketing it as a non-loan ( to avoid Truth in Lending Act disclosures ), the school has engaged in a deceptive act that obscures my federal borrower rights. Evidence of " Timeline Trap '' : The Debt ( ISA ) : I was required to sign the Income Share Agreement ( financial obligation ) on XX/XX/year> ( See attached : Signed_Enrollment_Agreement_Evidence.pdf, Page 8 & 17 ). The Disclosure ( Material Fact ) : The school did not present the " School Performance Fact Sheet '' which revealed a disastrous 25.24 % job placement rate for the previous yearuntil XX/XX/year>, nine days after I had already signed the debt contract ( See attached : XXXX, Page XXXX ). Violation : By withholding this critical risk information until after the financial contract was executed, the school denied me the ability to make an informed decision. Had I known on XX/XX/XXXX that only 1 in 4 graduates found jobs, I would not have signed the agreement. This constitutes " Fraud in the Inducement '' and renders the contract voidable. Relief Requested : I request that the TWC investigate this contradiction. I believe this contract is voidable under Texas law due to these misrepresentations. I am requesting a full audit of this enrollment agreement and a stay on any collection attempts while this investigation is active.

I believe these delays may constitute an unfair practice if payments are not being credited promptly upon receipt. Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666c, and Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.10, creditors are generally required to credit payments as of the date of receipt when payments are made according to the creditor 's requirements. Credit Reporting Accuracy Concerns I am concerned that Chase may not be accurately reporting my account history, payment history, utilization, and account status to consumer reporting agencies. The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, requires furnishers of information to provide accurate information to credit reporting agencies and to investigate disputes regarding inaccurate reporting. If Chase has reported inaccurate payment information, balances, utilization, or account history, I request that such information be immediately corrected with all consumer reporting agencies. Potential Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices The repeated delays in payment processing and the resulting impact on my account may constitute an unfair practice under the Consumer Financial Protection Act 's prohibition against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ), 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536. Consumers should be able to make payments and have those payments processed within reasonable and disclosed timeframes. Delays that interfere with account management, available credit, or credit reporting can create unnecessary financial harm. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require Chase to : Conduct a full review of my account history. Provide a detailed explanation of all payment processing delays. Correct any inaccurate information reported to consumer reporting agencies. Remove any negative reporting caused by improper payment processing delays. Provide written confirmation of any corrections made. Ensure future payments are processed in accordance with applicable federal law and regulatory requirements. I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including account statements, payment confirmations, screenshots, and correspondence with Chase. Thank you for your attention to this matter.
