Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Westlake Portfolio Management 's handling of my auto loan account. Based on the events described below, I believe Westlake has failed to properly administer my loan, failed to provide accurate information regarding my account, failed to respond to written requests for validation and documentation, and engaged in repossession and collection activities without adequately demonstrating its authority to do so. My vehicle loan was originally financed through XXXX XXXX. In approximately late XXXX or early XX/XX/XXXX, my loan was transferred to Westlake Portfolio Management without my knowledge or prior understanding. Shortly thereafter, my vehicle was repossessed. After the repossession, I acted promptly and paid the required amount to secure the release of the vehicle. Payment was made within approximately two weeks of the repossession. At that time, I was informed that the loan would be placed back with XXXX XXXX. Relying on the information provided to me, I believed XXXX XXXX remained involved in the servicing or ownership of the loan. However, I later learned that XXXX XXXX had sold or transferred its auto loan portfolio to Westlake Portfolio Management. Approximately one month after the repossession, I received an email from XXXX XXXX apologizing for communication errors involving the reporting of payment information. The communication indicated that inaccurate information had been provided to credit bureaus and other parties regarding loan payment reporting. This raised immediate concerns regarding the accuracy of the information being maintained and reported concerning my account. At the same time these reporting issues were occurring, I was actively attempting to recover my vehicle. Despite making the required payment within a timely manner, Westlake Portfolio Management refused to release my vehicle. I remained in constant communication with the company and repeatedly requested the return of the vehicle. Nevertheless, the vehicle was not released until XX/XX/XXXX, meaning Westlake retained possession of the vehicle for several months after payment had been made. During that time I was deprived of the use of my vehicle and incurred substantial inconvenience, financial hardship, and losses. In XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Westlake Portfolio Management regarding my account. During that conversation, I was informed that the vehicle would be released once I paid an additional amount that was quoted to me by the representative. The statement made no sense because the vehicle had already been released and was already in my possession. The fact that Westlake representatives appeared to believe the vehicle was still being held strongly suggested that the company 's records were inaccurate and that employees did not have reliable information concerning my account. My concerns grew when I attempted to register the vehicle. During that process, I discovered that the vehicle title was still associated with XXXX XXXX. This raised serious questions regarding Westlake 's authority over the loan and vehicle. If Westlake claimed ownership, servicing rights, or authority to repossess the vehicle, I believed it should have been able to provide documentation establishing its legal relationship to the loan and demonstrating how the loan had been transferred from XXXX XXXX. Because of these concerns, I began requesting documentation from Westlake Portfolio Management. In XX/XX/XXXX, I sent a cease-and-desist letter directing that communications be conducted in writing. This request was ignored. Despite my written instructions, communications continued in a manner inconsistent with my request. In XX/XX/XXXX, I formally requested documentation concerning the transfer of the loan from XXXX XXXX to Westlake Portfolio Management. I specifically requested documents demonstrating the transfer, assignment, servicing rights, ownership rights, and authority to collect on the loan. I also requested proof that Westlake Portfolio Management was legally entitled to act as the finance company responsible for the account. These requests were ignored. Westlake failed to provide the requested documentation, failed to explain the transfer of the loan, failed to provide evidence supporting its claimed authority over the vehicle, and failed to meaningfully respond to my written correspondence. Despite ignoring my requests for documentation and validation, Westlake repossessed the vehicle again in XX/XX/XXXX. Following the XX/XX/XXXX repossession, I made numerous attempts to determine the location of my vehicle, the status of the repossession, and the amount allegedly required for redemption. The information provided by Westlake was inconsistent, contradictory, and unreliable. Each time I contacted the company, I was given different information. Representatives provided six different towing company names, six different phone numbers, and multiple different payoff or redemption amounts. The amount required to recover the vehicle changed repeatedly depending on who answered the phone. No representative appeared to have the same information, and no one could provide a clear explanation regarding the vehicle 's location, status, or the basis for the amounts being demanded. As of the filing of this complaint, I remain deeply concerned that Westlake Portfolio Management has failed to maintain accurate records, failed to provide legally requested documentation, failed to respond to written correspondence, provided inconsistent and contradictory information regarding my account, and repossessed my vehicle despite refusing to provide documentation establishing its authority to enforce the loan. The totality of these events has caused substantial financial losses, loss of transportation, damage to my credit, emotional distress, lost time, and ongoing hardship. I am requesting a full investigation into Westlake Portfolio Management 's handling of my account, including : The transfer of the loan from XXXX XXXX to Westlake Portfolio Management. The reporting of account information to credit bureaus. The XX/XX/XXXX repossession and delayed release of the vehicle. The company 's refusal to provide requested documentation. The company 's failure to respond to written correspondence. The XX/XX/XXXX repossession. The inconsistent and conflicting information provided regarding the vehicle 's location and redemption amount. The identities of all employees, contractors, towing companies, repossession agents, storage facilities, and third parties involved in the handling of my account. I further request that Westlake Portfolio Management provide complete documentation supporting its authority to service and enforce the loan, provide a complete accounting of the account, compensate me for damages resulting from its actions, and take corrective action regarding any inaccurate information reported concerning my account.

Consumer complaint narrative: Complaint Against SoFi Regarding Fraudulent Account Access and Denial of Reimbursement I am submitting this complaint regarding unauthorized access to my SoFi account, the subsequent theft of {$2500.00} from my savings account, and SoFi 's refusal to reimburse me despite evidence that I was the victim of fraud. On XX/XX/year>, I received a phone call from XXXX ( XXXX ) XXXX from an individual identifying herself as " XXXX XXXX, '' who claimed to be a SoFi representative. XXXX informed me that my SoFi account had been compromised and that hackers had gained access to my account. She stated that immediate action was necessary to protect my funds. To establish her credibility, I asked XXXX to verify sensitive information associated with my account, including my account number, credit card number, and the last four digits of my Social Security number. She accurately provided this information, leading me to reasonably believe that she was a legitimate SoFi employee with access to my account records. XXXX advised me that the only way to protect my funds was to transfer them to another financial institution, such as XXXX XXXX or XXXX XXXX, while a new SoFi account was created. Because I had approximately {$2500.00} in my savings account and feared losing my money, I followed her instructions. At her direction, I first transferred {$1.00} to my XXXX XXXX account as a test transaction. She then instructed me to transfer my savings in increments of {$1000.00}. However, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX blocked these transfer attempts. XXXX then suggested using XXXX XXXX, but those transactions were also blocked by SoFi. After these attempts failed, XXXX abruptly ended the call. On XX/XX/year>, I received another call from XXXX from the same phone number. She claimed that unauthorized individuals still had access to my account and that creating a new SoFi account was necessary to protect my funds. She walked me through the process and instructed me to change my password to one she provided. Trusting that she was a legitimate SoFi representative, I followed her instructions. Approximately one minute later, I observed that {$2500.00} had been transferred out of my account to an individual named XXXX XXXX without my authorization. Upon discovering the unauthorized transfer, I immediately contacted SoFi at ( XXXX ) XXXX and reported the fraud. The representative assured me that SoFi would investigate the matter and do everything possible to recover my funds. On XX/XX/year>, I was informed that my dispute had been closed because " no error occurred. '' This was the only explanation provided. Concerned by the lack of information and the denial of my claim, I contacted SoFi again seeking clarification. Although I was not provided with any meaningful explanation, a representative submitted an appeal on my behalf and instructed me to provide all available evidence related to the fraudulent activity. On XX/XX/year>, I received confirmation that my appeal had been opened. As instructed, I submitted all supporting evidence in my possession, including screenshots, documentation, and a voicemail recording left by XXXX XXXX. On XX/XX/year>, XXXX informed me that it had reached a final decision and again denied my claim. The only explanation provided was that " no error occurred. '' XXXX declined to credit any funds back to my account despite the evidence demonstrating that I was the victim of a sophisticated impersonation scheme and unauthorized account access. I believe several issues warrant CFPB review : The individual impersonating a XXXX representative possessed accurate and sensitive account information that would not ordinarily be available to the public, raising serious concerns regarding the security of my account information. XXXX 's own fraud detection systems blocked multiple attempted transfers on XX/XX/year>, indicating that suspicious activity was detected. The transfer of {$2500.00} to XXXX XXXX occurred immediately after I was instructed by the impersonator to change my password, suggesting that my account security was compromised. Despite my prompt reporting of the fraud and submission of supporting evidence, XXXX denied my claim and appeal without providing a substantive explanation beyond the statement that " no error occurred. '' I have not been provided with sufficient information regarding the investigation conducted by XXXX, the basis for its decision, or why the transfer was determined to be authorized despite the surrounding circumstances. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate XXXX 's handling of this matter, review whether XXXX complied with its obligations regarding fraud investigations and unauthorized electronic fund transfers, and require XXXX to provide a detailed explanation of its findings. I also request reimbursement of the {$2500.00} that was fraudulently removed from my account. Thank you for your consideration of this complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative: Thank you for the opportunity to respond. The servicers explanation relies on the business purpose language in the loan documents, but that language does not exempt the loan from XXXX prepaymentpenalty statute. MCL 438.31c does not depend on whether a loan is for consumer or business purposes. The statute contains no exemptions for businesspurpose loans, entity borrowers, or loans labeled commercial. The only condition in the statute is the nature of the collateral. If the security is a singlefamily dwelling, the maximum prepayment penalty is 1 percent within the first three years and zero percent after that. The property securing this loan is a singlefamily dwelling. The servicer has not cited any statutory subsection or case law showing that a businesspurpose clause overrides Michigan law. A private contract can not eliminate statutory protections. The servicers response addresses Truth in Lending Act exemptions, but TILA is not the statute at issue. MCL 438.31c is a state law that applies based on the collateral, not the loan purpose. I am requesting that the CFPB require the servicer to either ( 1 ) correct the payoff to comply with the statutory limit, or ( 2 ) issue a conditional payoff so the closing can proceed while the dispute is resolved. The current payoff is preventing a scheduled real estate closing and causing financial harm.

Executive Customer Relations RE : Formal Complaint Regarding Mortgage Processing Delays, Repeated Documentation Requests, Communication Failures, Escalation Concerns, and Unapplied Relationship-Pricing Benefit Loan Number : XXXX To Whom It May Concern : I am submitting this formal complaint regarding my recent mortgage loan application and the manner in which it was handled by Chase Mortgage . My application process extended from late XX/XX/year> through at least XXXX XXXX. During that time, I was repeatedly required to submit documentation, explanations, supplemental information, and revised disclosures. While I understand that underwriting requirements can be extensive, the volume of requests, repeated document submissions, multiple redisclosures, and lack of clear communication made the process far more burdensome than I reasonably expected. Throughout the process, Chase requested numerous items including signed application packages, XXXX forms, pay stubs, bank statements, disability income documentation, credit inquiry explanations, credit documentation, occupancy verification, rental income documentation, undisclosed property documentation, trust documentation, proof of taxes and insurance on real estate owned, and multiple miscellaneous documentation requests. Several categories of documentation were requested more than once, requiring additional submissions and explanations. In addition to the documentation requests, Chase repeatedly generated new document packages requiring review and signatures. Several previously completed packages were later marked as outdated and replaced with newer versions, creating additional work, confusion, and delays. The transaction involved inherited property, trust documentation, and an equity buyout between family members. While I recognize that these circumstances may require additional review, the process appeared disorganized and poorly coordinated. Requests often seemed to arrive incrementally rather than as part of a comprehensive review, resulting in repeated submissions and prolonged delays. A significant source of frustration was the lack of transparency regarding the status of my loan and the anticipated closing date. On XX/XX/year>, I contacted Chase seeking an update and asking what was causing the delay because we had hoped to close during that month. As time passed, I continued to receive requests for documentation while receiving little clarity regarding what remained outstanding or what specific issues were preventing closing. On XX/XX/year>, I expressed my concerns and informed Chase that the process had been far more haphazard than I expected, involving continued requests for documents and numerous additional demands. I appreciated that a Chase representative acknowledged my concerns and apologized for my experience. However, the underlying issues remained unresolved. Another source of frustration was that Chase was aware from the beginning of two important deadlines. First, my interest rate was locked through XX/XX/year>. Second, my brother, whose ownership interest was being purchased as part of the transaction, had a previously scheduled vacation beginning XX/XX/year>. I communicated early in the process that he wished to be present for closing and that timing was therefore important. I was assured that Chase 's goal was to complete the transaction before the expiration of the rate lock. Because of those known deadlines, I organized my schedule and expectations around the understanding that the loan would close before XX/XX/XXXX. As the weeks passed, however, the process continued to involve additional document requests, supplemental reviews, and uncertainty regarding the closing date. At one point during the process, I was informed that Chase 's legal department required review of the trust documentation associated with the property. I understood that additional legal review might be necessary given the nature of the transaction and was willing to cooperate fully. However, when I was informed that the complete trust document was needed, I immediately advised Chase that the entire trust document had already been provided. I subsequently reiterated that the complete trust document had previously been submitted. From my perspective, this raised concerns regarding whether documents already provided had been fully reviewed, properly routed, or readily accessible to the individuals handling my loan. Because I believed there may have been a misunderstanding regarding the trust documentation, I specifically requested the opportunity to speak directly with the department responsible for reviewing the trust. My intent was not to bypass Chase personnel, but rather to determine whether there was confusion regarding the documents and to help resolve any outstanding issues as quickly as possible. I was not provided direct access to that department, nor was I given an opportunity to discuss the matter with the individuals conducting the review. As a borrower who had promptly supplied all requested documentation and was actively attempting to move the transaction forward, it was frustrating to be unable to communicate directly with the people who appeared to be responsible for the remaining review process. Even after title issues were reportedly cleared and I was informed that legal review of the trust documentation was underway, I continued to struggle to obtain clear information regarding the anticipated closing date, the status of that review, and what specific items, if any, remained outstanding. I also experienced increasing difficulty obtaining updates after raising my concerns regarding the process. I want to be clear that my frustration was not directed at any individual employee. My concerns were with the underwriting process, repeated documentation requests, delays, and lack of communication. However, after expressing those concerns, communication became noticeably more difficult from my perspective. My calls were increasingly directed to voicemail, and I often found it necessary to seek assistance through escalation channels simply to obtain updates regarding my loan status. During multiple escalation conversations, I was advised that if my concerns were not resolved they could be elevated to higher levels of management. On at least one occasion, I specifically requested escalation to the next level. Despite that request, I did not receive contact from a new representative or anyone who appeared to be at a higher level of authority. I also observed that communications increasingly came from individuals other than my original point of contact. While this may have been part of Chase 's normal workflow, it was never clearly explained to me. We discussed the amount of retirement assets that I had available to transfer, and I was informed that, based upon the value of those assets, I would qualify for a 1.25 % discount on my mortgage interest rate. I visited Chase 's website and attempted to submit my concerns through the available customer service options. Review the handling of the trust documentation and determine whether documents already submitted were properly reviewed and routed. 7. Confirm whether the transferred retirement assets satisfied the requirements for that benefit. 9. Consider process improvements for future borrowers whose transactions involve inherited property, trusts, or equity buyouts. 10. Review the accessibility of Chase 's customer assistance and escalation channels for borrowers with active mortgage applications and ensure there is a clear method for submitting concerns, obtaining assistance, and escalating issues when a loan is still in process. Consumer complaint narrative: This is a new complaint involving new evidence, new facts, and new violations that were not included in my prior complaint ( Case No. XXXX ), and I am requesting a new investigation. I am disputing two unauthorized charges totaling {$25000.00} placed on my Synchrony XXXX XXXX by XXXX XXXX. I now have new evidence showing that the merchant violated Wyoming law, Utah law, federal law, and Synchronys own merchant rules, and that the contract is void and the charges must be reversed. This is now my third CFPB complaint because Synchrony has repeatedly failed to conduct a lawful investigation. Synchrony simply forwards my dispute to the merchant and then relies entirely on whatever the merchant claims, instead of performing an independent investigation as required under the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z. Because of the seriousness of these violations and Synchronys repeated failure to investigate properly, I am also filing a simultaneous complaint with the FDIC, the federal regulator responsible for supervising Synchrony Bank. The entire transaction occurred at my Wyoming residence, where the contract was signed and the work was performed. Under Wyoming law, any contract affecting real property or creating a potential lien on a Wyoming home must comply with Wyomings requirements for validity, signatures, and disclosures, and the merchant did not comply with any of these requirements. The salesperson represented the financing as 132 months at 9.99 % and did not disclose that the APR would increase to 26.99 % after the promotional period. He did not provide any Truth in Lending Act disclosures, APR sheet, amortization schedule, or written explanation of the reamortization trigger. The 26.99 % terms only appeared after I disputed the charge, proving the contract was never delivered and was altered after the fact, which is a material violation of TILA and Regulation Z. Although the contract contains a Utah choiceoflaw clause, the merchant did not comply with Utahs Home Solicitation Sales Act. The salesperson controlled the contract on his laptop and left without giving me a copy of the contract, financing terms, TILA disclosures, or the required threeday cancellation form. Under federal, Wyoming, and Utah law, failure to deliver these documents makes the contract void, and the rescission period never began. In addition, the contract creates a security interest in our jointly owned Wyoming home, and under Wyoming property law, any contract that could encumber marital real estate requires both spouses to sign. My wife did not sign anything, did not receive the contract, and did not receive the cancellation form, making the contract void and unenforceable under Wyoming law. I also have new evidence showing that XXXX XXXX and their salesman did not hold the required XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX solicitor license, which is mandatory for doortodoor sales in Wyoming municipalities. A contract formed through unlicensed solicitation is void and unenforceable. I have attached documentation confirming this, including a certified letter I sent to the merchant notifying them that they are no longer licensed in multiple states and that they misrepresented their licensing status. XXXX XXXX is also operating illegally in California without the required XXXX XXXX license, and they were operating illegally in Arizona with a suspended license. Their Utah contractor license expired, their Idaho license lapsed, their Nevada license is glazingonly and does not authorize window installation, and their Oregon license number is incorrect. This is a pattern of multistate illegal contracting activity. I also obtained a licensed home inspection report documenting improper installation, damage, and unsafe workmanship. The inspector found limited visibility around the new windows suggesting that no waterproofing or flange has been installed and warned this may lead to potential water infiltration issues ( Inspection Report, p. 6 ). The report also found excessive gaps around the window trim allowing for pests, water, and other nuisances to enter the property ( p. 6 ), missing clapboard, flashing, and caulking at the bottom of the window ( p. 7 ), window screws fastened at an excessive and sharp angle compromising stability ( p. 7 ), excessive gap between the original framed window and the replacement window ( p. 7 ), excessive polyurethane foam usage ( p. 8 ), and daylight shown through the polyurethane foam to the outside with no flashing ( p. 9 ). These findings confirm that the installation was unsafe, unprofessional, and noncompliant with industry standards. The merchant claims the contract was signed on XX/XX/year>. Under Utah law and the FTC CoolingOff Rule, the rescission period would not expire until midnight on XX/XX/year>. Synchrony funded the merchant on XX/XX/year>, the first rescission day. Funding before cancellation rights expire violates federal law, Utah law, Wyoming law, and Synchronys own XXXX XXXX rules. I also obtained the merchants written Standard Operating Procedure from their website, which states that charges are processed within 2448 hours and do not get routed to the customer for approval. This is a systemic practice of unauthorized billing and violates the Fair Credit Billing Act. The merchant also treated the second charge as a new purchase on XX/XX/XXXX, even though I did not authorize it, I had requested a freeze on the account, and Synchrony failed to honor the freeze. I was forced to close the account to prevent further unauthorized charges. It is also important to clarify what inperson signing legally means. A valid inperson contract requires the consumer to be presented with the full written agreement, disclosures, financing terms, and cancellation rights in their possession, with the opportunity to review before signing. Signing on a salespersons laptop, where the consumer is not given the contract, can not scroll, can not review disclosures, and is not provided a copy, is not legally considered an inperson signing. It is a controlled electronic execution, and when the merchant withholds the contract, the signing is invalid under federal, Utah, and Wyoming law. After I disputed the charge, new financing terms suddenly appeared showing a 26.99 % APR. These terms were never disclosed at signing and were not part of the original contract. Altering financing terms after the fact is unlawful and confirms the contract was never delivered. I also have XXXX XXXX showing the contract was altered after the dispute. I am attaching a detailed timeline showing the date the merchant claimed the contract was signed, the date Synchrony funded the merchant, the date the rescission period should have expired, the date the unauthorized charges were made, the date I requested a freeze, the date Synchrony failed to honor the freeze, and the date I closed the account. Because the contract was signed in Wyoming, the work was performed in Wyoming, the merchant lacked the required Wyoming solicitor license, my wife did not sign the contract, the contract and cancellation form were never delivered, the true APR was not disclosed, the rescission period never began, Synchrony funded the merchant prematurely, the merchant altered the contract after the dispute, and the installation was defective as documented by a licensed inspector, the agreement is void and unenforceable under Wyoming law, Utah law, and federal law, and the charges are unauthorized. The merchant also used the Model Home Scam, falsely claiming I was receiving a 60 % discount and exclusive custom windows, when in fact these windows are available through every XXXX XXXX XXXX.

'' I know it was not a dropped call because I heard him talking over me and saying he was going to hang up. I have mentioned this incident multiple times in my subsequent messages to Chase customer service, and it has not even been clearly acknowledged, let alone apologized for. That alone is incredible. Given that the fraud was reported less than 24 hours after the wire was sent, the timeliness and effectiveness of the recovery efforts are of critical importance. In Bank of Americas response to my original CFPB complaint, they did not address my specific request for a detailed accounting of the actions they took to recover my funds. Their response focused on when the fraud claim was opened rather than providing the critical details of the recall and recovery process. A fair resolution would be for Bank of America to provide a complete and transparent accounting of all actions taken to recover my funds, including the exact timeline of the wire recall, all communications with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, copies of recall and freeze requests, and documentation showing the specific steps taken during the critical period immediately after I reported the fraud. I specifically request : - The exact date and time the wire recall was initiated ; - The exact date and time Bank of America contacted XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ; - The method of communication used ( including XXXX recall messages, telephone calls, emails, or any other communication ) ; - Copies or records of requests sent to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to freeze, hold, return, or recover the funds ; - Whether Bank of America requested an immediate hold or restriction on the receiving account and, if so, when that request was made ; - A complete timeline of all communications between Bank of America and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ; - Any responses received from XXXX XXXX XXXX Bank, including whether funds remained available at the time the recall was received ; - The names, departments, or teams responsible for handling the recall and recovery efforts ; - Any additional actions taken by Bank of America to attempt recovery of my funds. If the review reveals that Bank of America failed to take timely or appropriate actions that could have prevented or reduced my loss, I request that Bank of America take responsibility for the resulting damages and provide appropriate financial remediation. I have been a loyal Bank of America customer for decades, and this experience has been devastating. Losing more than {$200000.00} due to a sophisticated real estate wire fraud has had a significant financial and emotional impact on my family. What has been equally upsetting is feeling as though I was treated as just another case number rather than a long-term customer who entrusted Bank of America with our financial security. Instead, I received a final determination letter with very little detail, leaving me with unanswered questions after decades of banking with your institution. I respectfully request transparency, accountability, and a complete explanation of how my case was handled so that I can understand whether every possible action was taken to recover my funds. I also reserve the right to pursue any additional avenues available to me to obtain a complete understanding of the handling of this matter and to seek appropriate relief. The original unauthorized transaction dispute resulted in temporary credits being issued and later reversed, which caused substantial financial harm by immediately placing my account deeply in the negative. I was actively trying to repay this balance when I later became an unwitting victim of a fraudulent check scam. Truist failed to fairly consider that many of the events leading to the closure of my account were outside of my control, including disputed unauthorized transactions and later becoming the victim of a fraudulent check scam. I was ultimately held responsible for circumstances that were not entirely caused by my own actions, despite the fact that I was actively attempting to address the negative balance and resolve the situation. Rather than recognizing that I was dealing with multiple events that were outside of my control, Truist treated the situation as though I was solely responsible for everything that occurred, even though I had been actively trying to correct the account balance and cooperate throughout the process. The debt associated with this account was later included in my bankruptcy case and legally discharged. Despite this, I remain unable to establish a banking relationship with Truist. I would like Truist to formally review how my account and disputes were handled, explain the reasoning behind the decisions made regarding my account, and let me know whether there is any path for me to reestablish a banking relationship with Truist in the future, even if that is not possible at this time. I disputed the {$260.00} charge with Capital One. Capital One initially ruled in my favor and issued a credit. On XX/XX/year>, Capital One reversed this decision and rebilled the {$260.00}, citing XXXX XXXX 's chargeback rebuttal. XXXX XXXX 's rebuttal stated only that the baggage service was " fully utilized '' and that no damage report was filed with them directly. Neither point holds up. On the first point : " fully utilized '' means the bag was physically transported, but that does not mean the service was completed as contracted. A prepaid baggage service carries an implied obligation to deliver the bag in a reasonably intact condition at the final destination. My bag arrived with a broken hard-shell and a destroyed wheel, classified as irreparable by a repair expert appointed by the airline itself. A service that destroys the item it is contracted to transport has not been fully delivered. By XXXX XXXX 's logic, an airline could transport a bag in pieces and still claim the service was rendered. On the second point : this was an XXXX XXXX with baggage checked through to the final destination ( XXXX ). Under the XXXX XXXX, XXXX have the right to file damage claims against the final carrier upon delivery of baggage. I exercised this right exactly as intended, filing a damage report with the final carrier 's baggage partner on the day of arrival. XXXX XXXX 's assertion that no report was filed with them specifically does not negate a properly filed claim against the receiving carrier. Expecting a passenger to simultaneously file with every carrier on a multi-leg XXXX XXXX is neither standard practice nor reasonable. XXXX XXXX 's claim that no report was filed with them is therefore irrelevant, not exculpatory. I want to specifically highlight Capital One 's handling of this dispute as a failure of their chargeback process. I provided documented evidence of damage, a timestamped damage report filed the day of arrival, and third-party written confirmation of irreparable damage from the carrier 's own baggage partner. Capital One reversed their initial decision, which was correct, based solely on a merchant rebuttal that does not address the actual claim. XXXX XXXX cited a cancellation policy in response to a damage dispute. These are not the same thing, and a basic review of the documentation would have made that clear. This is not an isolated incident. This is the second time this year that Capital One has reversed an initial ruling in favor of a merchant after I submitted supporting documentation. In both cases, the merchant 's rebuttal was non-responsive to the actual basis of the dispute. Capital One appears to be rubber-stamping merchant rebuttals without conducting a meaningful review of the cardholder 's evidence. This raises serious questions about whether Capital One is fulfilling its obligations under the Fair Credit Billing Act to conduct a reasonable investigation before siding with a merchant. I am a cardholder in good standing who followed every required step. I disputed promptly, provided documentation, and responded within deadlines. Capital One 's process has failed me twice. I am filing this complaint because cardholders should not have to escalate to a federal regulator to receive the basic protections their credit card is supposed to provide.

I attached copy of security breach synopsys previously sent on past XXXX On XXXX XXXX & XXXX fraudulent transactions reocurred. We again notified the bank, disputed the activity, and repeatedly requested the freezing of all accounts, cards, and online access until the matter could be fully resolved. Although the bank reportedly imposed temporary restrictions and reimbursed losses, fraudulent activity resumed later. Importantly, three accounts and the credit card remained outside our monitoring capability, as we only retained visibility through my wifes limited online banking access. As it can be seen, credit card was never blocked by the bank and accounts restriction was relaxed. Inability to Resolve Matter in Person Because we are non-U.S. residents, the banks repeated insistence on an in-person appearance significantly impaired our ability to resolve the matter. We attempted to obtain U.S. visas in order to travel and appear at the bank ; however, visa restrictions affecting nationals of our country prevented travel, leaving us unable to comply with the banks requirement. This was stressed repeated times to the bank in our phone calls. Escalation and Complete Loss of Account Control On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, we noticed fraudulent activity had resumed once again. We contacted the bank immediately, attempted to initiate additional claims, and insisted again on all bank accounts restriction as protective measure. On XX/XX/XXXX my wifes online banking profile was compromised in a similar manner to my account, resulting in the complete loss of access to online banking for both of us. Continued insisting contact by telephone with the bank in order to recover online access for my wife account and to complete claim process for an extra week unsuccessfully. As an alternative, a bank branch assistant in XXXX recommended to action a duly authorized representative under a Power of Attorney ( POA ) for accounts closure. Funds were under restriction until XXXX A POA was prepared authorizing our representative to investigate damages, pursue reimbursement claims, transfer funds, and ultimately close the affected accounts, leaning on a notary recommended and previously used by the bank. On XX/XX/XXXX, our authorized representative appeared at the bank branch with the POA, which was reviewed and approved by the banks legal department. During this intervention, numerous unauthorized charges were identified. Despite this, the bank recommended keeping the compromised accounts active while claims were processed. Partial fund transfers were completed per mandate on POA. Important to note that unauthorized withdrawals continued immediately thereafter, suggesting that the accounts had not been effectively blocked or secured as of yet. Adulterated contact information present at the time on the profile was also captured for investigation. On XX/XX/XXXX, the bank recommended opening entirely new accounts with new account numbers and migrating remaining funds in an effort to mitigate the ongoing compromise, preserve account history, and facilitate claim accounting. During this process, access to my online banking profile was temporarily restored, personal and contact information was updated, replacement debit and credit cards were issued, and additional accounts were opened. There were also indications, however, of ongoing unauthorized access remaining visible, including the re-appearance of same unknown email address associated with my banking profile and unresolved verification issues affecting my legitimate email account which I had previously verified and confirmed, ( re done again at this time ). All this immediately notified by my agent to the bank. By XX/XX/XXXX, I had once again lost access to online banking following the verbal notification by the bank to my agent of POA being objected. Power of Attorney Disputes and Continued Obstruction Following consultations with lawyers, a revised Power of Attorney was prepared to address deficiencies allegedly raised by the bank. On XX/XX/XXXX, our representative returned to the bank, regained temporary access to the accounts, and resumed the process of fraud claims, accounting, and reconciliation. During this intervention, the bank was able to preliminarily corroborate the estimated amount of stolen funds, being over XXXX XXXX XXXX mostly effected during the months of XXXX and XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, the bank issued a letter objecting to the Power of Attorney, effectively halting the process, and once again leaving us without online access while retaining funds out of dispute. On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted the bank seeking restoration of online banking access per prompt message provided by the system upon trial access. Despite completing identity authentication, access was denied and instructed to appear in person at a branch once again. At that time, I learned that another online user ID, business-type profile not requested or authorized by me, was associated with the accounts and that could not be explained by them, being another indication that system might stiil be under perpetrator 's influence. There was also mention of funds restriction, something that can not be trusted for a fact. On XX/XX/XXXX & XXXX, XXXX, I received written communications from the bank ( dated XX/XX/XXXX ) stating that its fraud investigation had concluded and that reimbursement would be denied because the disputed transactions were deemed consistent with account activity, effectively closing the claim despite the prolonged history of reported account compromise and prior reimbursement determinations as well as inconsistency with prior consumer activity history. On XX/XX/XXXX, I mailed formal claim appeal letters to the bank while requesting all supporting documentation for my evaluation as well as funds restriction to all of the accounts to prevent further draining of remaining legitimate funds under threat. There is still a balance of funds pending in my favour not reflected yet in claims and appeals ( have no access to records ). Continued further contact attempts with bank via telephone for all accounts funds restriction confirmation unsuccessfully till present. Retention of Legitimate Funds In addition to disputed fraudulent transactions, the bank continues to restrict and retain access to legitimate funds that were never subject to fraud claims, disputes, or investigation, effectively depriving us of access to our own property. More concerning to that is the fact of forcing us to keep our assets under its custody despite its proven inability to secure them, directly contradicting what is in dispute and its ongoing assurances. As a result, we currently remain without practical control over both disputed and non-disputed funds despite repeated good-faith efforts to authenticate identity, cooperate with the bank, provide documentation, appoint authorized representation, and resolve the matter through appropriate channels. Escalation of Security Risks and Threats During the last week of XX/XX/XXXX, circumstances escalated significantly when members of my immediate family began receiving threats through social media platforms and telephone communications from individuals believed to be associated with criminal activity, pressuring us to withdraw or discontinue claims related to the fraudulent activity affecting the bank accounts. Although the precise source remains subject to investigation, the timing and nature of these threats raise serious concerns regarding misuse or exposure of sensitive personal information, particularly given the prolonged unauthorized access to our banking profiles and personal data further supported by the bank with its inaction providing preference to criminals over us as legitimate owners. Due to concerns for personal and family safety, the matter required escalation to local police authorities for reporting and protective attention, representing an additional and serious consequence of the prolonged compromise. Principal Concerns Identity theft and account takeover, including unauthorized modification of account credentials, personal information, and account access ; Repeated fraudulent withdrawals and unauthorized transactions despite repeated notice to the bank and explicit requests for protective measures ; Failure by the bank to adequately secure compromised accounts, freeze access, or prevent recurrence after multiple fraud reports and still unresolved after almost a year ; Failure to investigate or remediate the root cause of the compromise, resulting in repeated unauthorized activity over an extended period ; Deprivation of banking benefits to legitimate owners in favour of criminals ; Denial of reimbursement despite prior acknowledgments of fraud and reimbursement history ; Continued restriction and retention of legitimate, non-disputed funds, preventing access to assets not subject to investigation or claim ; Procedural barriers and repeated invalidation of Powers of Attorney, effectively preventing meaningful resolution for non-resident account holders ; Escalation into personal security concerns, including threats directed at immediate family members requiring police involvement. Communication cut off. Really concerning sending letters, notices, emails, phone calls without a single formal response from the bank addressing the main issue. A written notice restricting total accounts funds and online access until resolving should be the golden standard for cases like this, upfront and at the very least. Financial and Consequential Impact Consequences : Current estimated direct losses exceed USD {$40000.00}, subject to reconciliation and updated accounting. In addition to disputed losses, the bank continues to retain access to other legitimate funds not subject to fraud or claim, resulting in prolonged deprivation of financial resources. This matter has caused significant hardship, including prolonged inability to access personal funds, disruption of financial obligations, extensive time, effort and expenses associated with fraud reporting and legal arrangements, and substantial emotional and physical distress affecting my family seeing the savings of our life at fraudsters mercy with bank 's support. Unbelievable! On top of that, the prolonged exposure of sensitive personal information to criminals and the subsequent threats directed toward family members have elevated the matter from a financial dispute to one involving personal safety and security concerns for our living in a very high risk country.

I searched every XXXX location in my area for this transaction and found no matching receipt. This strongly suggests the charge did not originate from a legitimate in-store purchase at any local XXXX. I have since contacted U.S. Bank and a fraud claim has been opened. However, I am filing this complaint for the following reasons : 1. U.S. Bank 's failure to deactivate a replaced debit card is an operational security failure that directly enabled unauthorized access to my account. 2. Consumers reasonably expect that when a bank issues a replacement card, the prior card number is closed. U.S. Bank 's failure to meet this expectation, and to communicate otherwise, constitutes an unfair practice that exposes customers to preventable fraud. 3. I want this incident on record in the event this is not an isolated failure and other U.S. Bank customers have experienced or may experience the same vulnerability. I am requesting that the CFPB : - Ensure U.S. Bank fully resolves my fraud claim and returns the unauthorized {$330.00} promptly - Investigate whether U.S. Bank 's card replacement procedures meet federal consumer protection standards- Determine whether this failure has affected other U.S. Bank customers I am happy to provide additional documentation, account details, or transaction information upon request.

XXXX - Rebuttal To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency ( PHEAA/AES ) : I am submitting this rebuttal in response to AESs Closed with Explanation determination dated XX/XX/year>. The companys response does not resolve the issues raised, does not address the core compliance failures, and does not provide the documentation required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and applicable servicing standards. A further review is warranted. 1. Failure to Address Servicer Delay and Pending Relief Request AES acknowledges that my forbearance request was received on XX/XX/year> and not processed until XX/XX/year>, an eightday delay. During this period, AES continued to advance delinquency status and report negative information to the credit bureaus. AES did not address why adverse credit reporting continued while a relief request was pending, nor did it explain why no temporary hold, pause, or notification of missing documentation was issued. Servicers are required to provide notice of incomplete applications and allow borrowers an opportunity to cure deficiencies before adverse action is taken. This omission renders the reporting incomplete and therefore inaccurate under FCRA 623. 2. Failure to Provide Documentation Supporting Outbound Communication Claims AES asserts that calls and letters were made to notify both me and my cosigner of delinquency. However, AES provided : No call logs No timestamps No copies of letters No proof of delivery No record of successful contact A conclusory statement is not sufficient to establish compliance. Under CFPB servicing standards, a servicer must provide verifiable documentation when asserting that required notices were sent. AES did not do so. 3. Failure to Address CoSigner Harm My complaint specifically raised the issue of harm to my cosigner, including negative credit reporting and lack of notice. AESs response merely restates her name and provides no analysis, justification, or evidence of compliance with coborrower notification requirements. This is a material omission and does not satisfy the requirement for a complete and responsive investigation. 4. Failure to Address the Impact of Immediate Cure AES acknowledges that I remitted payment on XX/XX/year>, curing the delinquency through XX/XX/year>. This demonstrates goodfaith borrower behavior and contradicts any implication of ongoing or intentional delinquency. AES did not explain why this cure was not considered in evaluating the appropriateness of continued negative reporting. 5. Incomplete and Unsupported Determination of Accurate Reporting AES concludes that the reporting is accurate but provides no supporting documentation, no verification records, and no explanation of how the investigation was conducted. A bare assertion of accuracy does not satisfy FCRA obligations. Given the servicer delay, lack of notice, pending relief request, and immediate cure, the reporting is at minimum misleading, and therefore not accurate under federal law.

After contacting Affirm, the dispute was reopened for a second review. When the dispute was reopened, Affirm assigned an incorrect dispute reason stating that my purchase had not been delivered or had been delivered late. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against Discover Card, issued by Discover, a division of XXXX XXXX XXXX, because Discover is treating an old identity-theft claim like a brand-new matter and is shifting the burden back onto me even though a sworn FTC Identity Theft Report already identified the Discover account as fraudulent. I already have a sworn FTC Identity Theft Report identifying the Discover account as fraudulent. Asking me to complete another company-specific affidavit a year later appears duplicative, delay-based, and designed to shift the burden back onto me instead of resolving the identity-theft claim. Discover should not claim that the account is valid merely because it has my name, address, Social Security number, date of birth, phone number, or other identifying information. Identity theft often involves real consumer information. Identity matching is not proof that I opened, authorized, used, benefited from, ratified, or accepted liability for the account. Discover should not claim that its transaction list proves liability. The XX/XX/XXXX affidavit packet includes a list of transactions and payments, including XXXX, Dollar General, Caseys, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX payments, and payment representments. A transaction list is not proof that I opened the account, received the card, activated the card, authorized the charges, benefited from the charges, or knowingly accepted liability. Discover should not treat payments or payment representments as automatic ratification. Payment activity does not prove that I knowingly opened, authorized, used, benefited from, ratified, or accepted liability for the account. Identity theft can involve compromised payment sources, stored credentials, automated payments, or account access by someone other than the consumer. Discover must prove authorization, not merely point to payment activity. Discover should not use local merchant names as proof of liability. Transactions appearing near where I live do not prove that I personally made them. Discover must provide actual evidence, such as application records, identity-verification records, device records, IP address records, card-delivery records, card-activation records, merchant-level evidence, signatures, camera evidence if available, and payment-source verification. Discover should not claim that no current Discover credit-report entry means there is no harm. My Experian report dated XX/XX/XXXX showed no Discover charge-off, no Discover collection, no closed accounts, no collections, no inquiries, and XXXX accounts ever late. My later credit reports also do not show a Discover negative account, yet Discover is still sending identity-theft paperwork in XXXX for an account it says it is investigating. Discover should not keep this account open, unresolved, collectible, transferable, or capable of future reporting while demanding more paperwork from me. Discover has had more than enough notice to investigate the identity-theft claim and either provide real proof of liability or close and block the account as fraud. This conduct appears unfair, deceptive, and potentially fraudulent by omission because Discover is implying that my investigation depends on submitting another affidavit, while omitting that a sworn FTC Identity Theft Report already identified the Discover account as fraudulent in XXXX and that the dispute was already raised through the CFPB/Experian process. I dispute the Discover account ending in XXXX, the related Discover account number XXXX, all alleged balances, all alleged transactions, all alleged payments, all payment representments, all fees, all interest, all collection activity, all furnishing, all account status information, and any claim that I opened, authorized, used, benefited from, ratified, or accepted liability for this account.

Subject of Complaint : Failure to Provide Meaningful Debt Verification and Continued Collection Activity Following Dispute II. BACKGROUND AND CHRONOLOGY OF EVENTS On or about XX/XX/year>, I received an email communication from Resurgent Capital Services, XXXX ( Resurgent ) regarding an alleged debt. Immediately upon receiving this communication, I submitted a written dispute and request for validation of the alleged debt pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g. In my dispute, I requested documentation sufficient to establish the existence, amount, ownership, and collectability of the alleged debt, including documentation demonstrating Resurgents authority to collect and a complete accounting of the balance claimed. Rather than providing meaningful verification, XXXX responded by sending account statements that merely repeated information already in their possession. The documents provided identified XXXX XXXX as the creditor but failed to identify either Resurgent Capital Services, L.P. or LVNV Funding LLC as the legal owner of the alleged debt. The documents also failed to establish any chain of assignment, transfer, or sale demonstrating how ownership of the alleged debt passed from XXXX XXXX to LVNV Funding LLC or how Resurgent obtained authority to collect on XXXX behalf. As a result, the materials provided failed to establish that XXXX or LVNV possesses a legal interest in the alleged debt or has standing to collect it. The documents did not address the substantive issues raised in my dispute and failed to provide evidence sufficient to establish that the debt is valid, accurately calculated, legally collectible, or owned by the entities attempting to collect it. XXXX. SPECIFIC LEGAL VIOLATIONS A. Failure to Provide XXXX XXXX of the Alleged Debt. 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) After receiving my timely dispute, Resurgent was required to cease collection efforts until it obtained and mailed verification of the debt. The materials provided by Resurgent consisted primarily of account statements and failed to provide documentation establishing : The basis for the amount allegedly owed ; Documentation demonstrating Resurgents ownership of, or authority to collect, the alleged debt ; Documentation demonstrating that LVNV Funding LLC owns the alleged debt ; A chain of title, assignment, or transfer from XXXX XXXX to LVNV Funding LLC ; Information sufficient to verify the accuracy of the balance claimed ; Documentation addressing the specific disputes and requests raised in my validation request. Notably, the account statements identify XXXX XXXX as the creditor and do not establish that either Resurgent Capital Services, L.P. or LVNV Funding LLC owns the alleged debt. Without documentation establishing ownership and authority to collect, the materials provided fail to demonstrate that either entity has standing to pursue collection of the alleged debt. By merely providing account statements that repeated the amount claimed without adequately responding to the issues raised in my dispute, XXXX failed to provide meaningful verification of the alleged debt. B. Continued Collection Activity Following an Inadequate Response. 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) Despite receiving my dispute, XXXX treated its limited response as sufficient verification and continued efforts to collect the alleged debt. Because the documentation provided failed to meaningfully verify the debt, establish ownership, demonstrate authority to collect, or address the issues raised in my dispute, XXXX actions undermined the protections afforded to consumers under 1692g ( b ). C. False, Deceptive, or Misleading Representations. 15 U.S.C. 1692e By representing that the account statements supplied constituted sufficient verification of the alleged debt, XXXX created the misleading impression that it had adequately substantiated its claim when it had failed to provide documentation reasonably demonstrating the validity, ownership, standing, and accuracy of the debt. Such conduct constitutes a false, deceptive, or misleading representation in connection with the collection of a debt in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e. D. Unfair Collection Practices. 15 U.S.C. 1692f Attempting to collect a disputed debt without providing documentation reasonably sufficient to verify the debt, establish ownership, demonstrate authority to collect, and address the consumers dispute constitutes an unfair and unconscionable collection practice. Resurgents conduct deprived me of a meaningful opportunity to evaluate the legitimacy, ownership, standing, and accuracy of the alleged debt before collection efforts continued, in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692f.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against Capital One regarding an unauthorized electronic fund transfer in potential violation of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. BACKGROUND : I had enrolled in XXXX on multiple Capital One credit card accounts. I designated my savings account as the payment source. Despite this, Capital One 's mobile application repeatedly drafted payments from my checking account instead, resulting in multiple returned payments through no fault of my own. I attempted to correct the payment source and cancel XXXX multiple times through the Capital One app, but the system failed to honor these changes each time. THE VIOLATION : I contacted Capital One customer service to resolve the issue. During that call, a Capital One representative explicitly confirmed that XXXX had been successfully cancelled on my account. I have an audio recording of this confirmation. Despite the representative 's confirmation, Capital One subsequently processed a {$900.00} ACH draft from my checking account. This payment was returned because the XXXX should not have been processed at all it had been cancelled per Capital One 's own representative. This constitutes an unauthorized preauthorized electronic fund transfer under EFTA. Under 15 U.S.C. 1693e, a consumer has the right to stop payment on a preauthorized electronic fund transfer by notifying the financial institution. Capital One was notified by their own representative confirming cancellation and processed the transfer anyway. Furthermore, under 15 U.S.C. 1693f, financial institutions are required to investigate and resolve errors involving electronic fund transfers. Capital One has not acknowledged this {$900.00} unauthorized draft as an error, has not initiated any error resolution process, and has not provided any explanation for why the transfer was processed after confirmed cancellation. ADDITIONAL HARM : Capital One closed three of my credit card accounts citing returned payments the very returned payments caused by their own defective XXXX system. The {$900.00} unauthorized draft occurred after my initial CFPB complaint was filed, demonstrating that Capital One 's system continued to malfunction even while the matter was under review. I have sustained significant credit damage as a result of account closures directly attributable to Capital One 's platform failure. RELIEF REQUEST ED : 1. Investigate Capital One 's failure to honor a confirmed XXXX cancellation as a violation of EFTA 15 U.S.C. 1693e 2. Investigate Capital One 's failure to initiate error resolution procedures under EFTA 15 U.S.C. 1693f 3. Direct Capital One to reverse all adverse actions taken against my accounts resulting from returned payments caused by their system malfunction 4. Direct Capital One to remove any negative credit bureau reporting related to these events 5. Assess whether Capital One 's XXXX system failures constitute a pattern of unfair and deceptive practices affecting other consumers I have audio evidence of the representative confirming XXXX cancellation and am prepared to provide it upon request. Dear Earnest Legal and Compliance Team:
This letter is a formal reply to Earnest's written response dated XX/XX/XXXX, received in connection with the CFPB complaint I filed on XX/XX/XXXX. I have reviewed that response in detail. It fails to address the central legal violations raised in my original complaint, mischaracterizes the nature of my dispute, ignores my request for hardship accommodation, and is contradicted by updated account evidence showing that the harm I am disputing is ongoing as of the date of this letter. I am submitting this reply both directly to Earnest and as a formal dispute of Earnest's response through the CFPB complaint portal.
I. THE CORE MATHEMATICAL PROBLEM EARNEST DID NOT ADDRESS
Earnest's response describes, in general terms, how interest capitalization works. It does not address the actual financial outcome that I am disputing. The facts are as follows:
	Loan XXXX was disbursed on XX/XX/XXXX, for XXXX. As of Earnest's own records dated XX/XX/XXXX, the outstanding balance is XXXX an INCREASE of XXXX, or 22.3%, over more than four and a half years, despite documented payments made by me throughout that period, including ongoing autopay.
	Loan XXXX was disbursed on XX/XX/XXXX, for XXXX. As of XX/XX/XXXX, the outstanding balance is XXXX an increase of XXXX despite ongoing autopay payments.
	Earnest's own online dashboard displays 'Paid principal: XXXX,' 'Paid interest: XXXX,' 'Total paid: XXXX,' and 'XXXX paid' for both loans. This is not merely a failure to make progress. The true position is that my principal balance grew despite my payments the dashboard cannot display a negative percentage, so it floors the display at XXXX. In substance, I have experienced negative amortization: years of payments that resulted in a larger debt than when I started.
	This outcome is the direct and foreseeable consequence of the undisclosed, unauthorized capitalization events Earnest has now confirmed in writing occurred in XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXXX/XX/XXXX, and XXXXXX/XX/XXXX.
Earnest's XX/XX/XXXX letter explains the mechanics of capitalization but does not explain why a consumer who made consistent good-faith payments should end the period with a larger debt than she started with, nor does it explain why this outcome was not clearly disclosed to me in advance of each triggering event.
II. SUPPLEMENTAL EVIDENCE THIS HARM IS CONTINUING, NOT HISTORICAL
To confirm whether this issue has been resolved going forward, I captured updated screenshots of Earnest's own online dashboard on XX/XX/XXXX twenty days after my originalXX/XX/XXXX screenshots were taken. The comparison is as follows:
	Loan XXXX: Balance increased from XXXX (XX/XX/XXXX) to XXXX (XX/XX/XXXX) an increase of XXXX in twenty days, despite an autopay payment of XXXX made on XX/XX/XXXX and another scheduled forXX/XX/XXXX. Paid principal, paid interest, and total paid all remain XXXX (Exhibit H).
	Loan XXXX: Balance increased from XXXX (XX/XX/XXXX to XXXX (XX/XX/XXXX) an increase of XXXX in twenty days, despite an autopay payment of XXXX made on XX/XX/XXXX. Paid principal, paid interest, and total paid all remain XXXX (Exhibit I).
This is current, real-time confirmation generated by Earnest's own system that my outstanding balances continue to grow despite ongoing autopay payments, more than a year after the last capitalization event Earnest has disclosed in writing. I require a complete, line-item accounting explaining: (a) why my current monthly payments are not reducing principal on a going-forward basis; (b) what portion of each current monthly payment is being applied to interest versus principal; and (c) whether any further undisclosed capitalization has occurred or is scheduled to occur on either loan.
III. EARNEST HAS NOT ADDRESSED MY HARDSHIP OR OFFERED ANY PAYMENT PLAN
My original complaint specifically stated that I became involuntarily unemployed on XX/XX/XXXX, and requested immediate hardship accommodation, including a suspension of payments and a presentation of all available restructuring, modification, or settlement options. Earnest's XX/XX/XXXXresponse does not mention my unemployment, does not acknowledge my hardship, and does not offer a single payment plan, modification, or accommodation option in response.
Instead, Earnest's response focuses exclusively on justifying past capitalization events under the contract and explaining that I previously did not qualify for a hardship forbearance in XX/XX/XXXX because I lacked three consecutive months of on-time principal and interest payments. Earnest does not explain how a borrower who could not reliably access her account due to Earnest's own duplicate-profile error was expected to establish a clean three-month payment record sufficient to qualify for the very hardship relief that error made necessary. This is a direct consequence of Earnest's own servicing failure being used to deny the borrower the relief that failure created the need for.
I am renewing my request for hardship accommodation now, under current and continuing circumstances of unemployment, and I expect a specific, individualized response addressing what options are available to me not a general restatement of past forbearance criteria. I formally request an Economic Hardship Deferment or Forbearance of not less than six months, effective immediately, with full suspension of payments and no further capitalization of interest during that period absent my prior written consent.
IV. THE DUPLICATE SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER ERROR EXISTED FROM THE OUTSET AND ITS START DATE REMAINS UNANSWERED
Earnest's response characterizes the duplicate profile issue as having been 'inadvertently created' and resolved on XX/XX/XXXX, and states that it 'did not prevent me from making payments' because I could pay by phone. Both the characterization and the omission require correction.
A. Duration The Start Date Remains Unanswered
Earnest's response provides only the date the duplicate profile was corrected. It does not provide the date the duplicate profile was created. This issue did not arise shortly before its resolution in XX/XX/XXXX. It existed from the earliest period of my loan history. From the time these loans entered repayment, I was never able to reliably access or view my account online. When I called, Earnest representatives were frequently unable to locate my loan under the correct profile, requiring multiple calls and extended hold times before my account could even be identified. This occurred repeatedly over a period of years, not weeks. I require Earnest to confirm, in writing and with supporting internal records, the exact date on which the duplicate profile or incorrect Social Security number association was first created.
This date is directly relevant to the scope of relief I am entitled to. If the duplicate profile existed since the inception of these loans in XXXX through XXXX, then every capitalization event on these loans not merely the three identified in Section I above occurred during a period in which I lacked the account transparency necessary to monitor, understand, or contest those events.
B. Phone Payment Capability Does Not Substitute for Account Transparency
Earnest's defense that I 'remained fully able to make payments over the phone' misunderstands the nature of my complaint. The harm was never solely an inability to transmit a payment. Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX, criminals took over my XXXX account and initiated an unauthorized {$2600.00} debit from my Navy Federal checking account ( ending XXXX ). I never logged into XXXX, never set up or approved any transfer, and received no money or benefit. I reported it to Navy Federal the same day, XX/XX/XXXX. Navy Federal denied the claim on the theory that I " authorized and/or participated '' because I was deceived into reading a code. This is the exact scenario the CFPB 's Electronic Fund Transfers FAQs ( Unauthorized EFTs, XXXX and XXXX, updated XX/XX/XXXX ) define as an UNAUTHORIZED transfer : XXXX states that a consumer who is fraudulently induced into providing account information " has not furnished an access device '' under Regulation E. When I formally requested the documents relied on under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( d ) ( 1 ), Navy Federal attached no documents ( its message said the documents " if any '' were attached, and none were ) and produced no XXXX records, indicating no real investigation occurred before the denial. On recorded calls, Navy Federal 's own representatives confirmed that my claim was internally miscoded as a " scam '' and was automatically declined by that classification, rather than investigated. A Navy Federal supervisor told me directly that the account-takeover facts I reported were not even reflected in the claim notes, and instructed me to file an appeal so the full facts could be considered. Despite my repeated written and verbal requests, Navy Federal never provided a claim number, which is consistent with the claim never having been properly opened or investigated as a fraud claim. Navy Federal representatives also confirmed that XXXX has stated it will refund the funds once Navy Federal contacts them, so recovery is available and the transaction is not in dispute as fraudulent ; Navy Federal has simply declined to pursue it or to credit my account. On XX/XX/XXXX, Navy Federal stated in writing that " provisional credit will not be issued '' during the appeal. This violates 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ), which requires the institution to provisionally credit the account when it can not complete its investigation within 10 business days of notice. That deadline is XX/XX/XXXX, measured from my XX/XX/XXXX report. Navy Federal also repeated the position that a transaction a consumer is convinced to make by a third party is not fraud ; that describes a transaction the consumer knowingly makes, which is not my situation. I never accessed my XXXX account or approved any transfer. A third party took over my account and initiated the transfer, which is an unauthorized EFT under Comment 2 ( m ) -3. The stolen funds were my mortgage payment, and the theft left my checking account at {$0.00} immediately afterward. Because Navy Federal denied the claim and refused provisional credit, I was forced to move money out of my savings to cover my mortgage and avoid defaulting. Navy Federal 's provisional-credit obligation falls on XX/XX/XXXX. I am also traveling internationally from late XXXX until XXXX, which makes prompt resolution especially urgent and makes extended delay particularly harmful.
