I am filing this complaint regarding U.S. Bank 's systematic assessment of monthly service fees on a business checking account that was functionally unusable due to the bank 's own transfer restrictions. I opened a XXXX XXXX Checking Account on or about XX/XX/XXXX under my company : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, intending to take advantage of a promotional offer requiring a {$25000.00} deposit. I had these funds readily available in my linked XXXX XXXX XXXX account. From the outset, U.S. Bank made funding the account impossible in any normal or routine manner : I was required to complete a manual PDF form just to deposit an initial {$300.00}. After linking my XXXX XXXX XXXX account ( which contained well over {$25000.00} ), U.S. Bank blocked external ACH transfers. I was informed by U.S. Bank employees that I could only fund the account through repeated small incremental transfersan impractical and burdensome process. I reasonably assumed that after depositing the {$300.00}, the linked XXXX XXXX XXXX account would allow the full {$25000.00} transfer. When this failed, I became frustrated and concluded the account was unusable for its intended purpose. I stepped away, reasonably believing my {$300.00} would remain safe until I could resolve the matter. U.S. Bank then assessed XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX monthly " dormancy '' fees * * against this account for over one year, systematically draining the entire {$300.00} balance and pushing the account to a negative balance. I received no noticeno mail, no email, no alertthat fees were accruing or that my balance was being depleted. When I discovered the negative balance, I immediately contacted U.S. Bank. They refunded only {$90.00} as a " courtesy '' ( actually only {$30.00} was refunded, not the {$90.00} they verbally claimed ), but refused to refund the remaining $ XXXX in fees. The bank 's own letter dated acknowledges the fees were charged and that they could reverse them, yet they have arbitrarily chosen not to fully reverse the wrongful charges. The bank 's advertising encouraged a {$25000.00} deposit with a cash bonus, while their systems made that deposit impossible. The bank then penalized me for inactivity on an account they made unusable. This is a bait-and-switch scheme that systematically traps consumers. Legal Violations A. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ), 12 U.S.C. 5536 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ) U.S. Bank 's conduct constitutes an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice ( UDAAP ) : Unfair Conduct : The bank knowingly imposed transfer restrictions that made the account unusable The bank assessed fees for inactivity while the account was unusable The bank provided no meaningful notice of accruing fees The bank 's $ XXXXmonth fee on a {$300.00} balance ( 10 % per month ) is disproportionate and causes substantial injury Deceptive Conduct : The bank advertised a bonus requiring a {$25000.00} deposit while making the required funding impossible The bank represented that linking an external account would enable transfers, then blocked them The bank 's letter acknowledges fees were " assessed correctly '' while also partially refunding themcontradictory representations The CFPB has previously fined U.S. Bank {$37.00} XXXX for similar misconductopening unauthorized accounts and engaging in deceptive sales practices. In that enforcement action, the CFPB found that U.S. Bank 's conduct caused " substantial injury to consumers in the form of fees, negative effects on credit reports, and the loss of control over their personal information ''. B. New Hampshire Consumer Protection Act ( RSA 358-A:2 ) Under New Hampshire 's Consumer Protection Act, it is unlawful to use " any unfair or deceptive act or practice in the conduct of any trade or commerce ''. Specifically, the statute prohibits : Claiming that goods or services have certain characteristics or benefits when they do not ( the bank advertised a bonus offer while making the {$25000.00} deposit impossible ) Falsely representing sponsorship, approval, status, or affiliation Advertising goods or services with the intent not to sell them as advertised The bank 's bonus offer was made with the intent to attract deposits, yet their systems were designed to block those deposits. This is precisely the type of deceptive conduct the NH Consumer Protection Act was designed to address. C. Truth in Savings Act ( 12 U.S.C. 4301 et seq. ) Banks are required to clearly and conspicuously disclose terms, fees, and charges. U.S. Bank 's fee structure $ XXXXmonth on a {$300.00} balancewas buried in fine print and not meaningfully disclosed. The bank 's $ XXXXmonth fee on a {$300.00} balance is 10 % per month120 % annuallyfar exceeding any reasonable service fee structure. The CFPB has noted that " dormancy fees, latency fees, or any other administrative fees or service charges that have the effect of reducing the total amount for which the holder may redeem '' are prohibited, and while this provision specifically addresses gift certificates, the same unfairness principles apply to bank dormancy fees. D. Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing Every contract includes an implied duty of good faith. U.S. Bank 's conductmaking the account unusable, charging fees for inactivity, and providing no noticeviolates this fundamental duty. The bank can not create the conditions that led to dormancy and then penalize the consumer for dormancy. U.S. Bank 's History of Misconduct : XX/XX/XXXX : The CFPB fined U.S. Bank {$37.00} XXXX for opening fictitious accounts without customer consent from XXXX to XXXX. The CFPB found the bank illegally accessed credit reports and opened checking, savings, credit card, and line of credit accounts without permission. Pattern of Fees : A CFPB report found that U.S. Bank 's average annual fees per account were among the highest of examined institutions, with overdraft fees of {$36.00} at U.S. Bank compared to {$0.00} at other institutions. Consumer complaint narrative: Dear Sir or Madam, I am filing this complaint against Eastern Bank regarding a misleading new checking account bonus promotion. I opened a new Eastern Bank checking account based on its advertised new account bonus offer. I followed the stated requirements, including opening the account, depositing the required funds, and maintaining the required balance for the required period of time. After I completed the requirements, Eastern Bank refused to pay the bonus. The bank stated that I was not eligible because only one person at the same address or household could receive the bonus. I believe this restriction was not clearly and prominently disclosed. This was a material eligibility limitation, but it was not presented in a clear or conspicuous way during the advertisement or the online account-opening process. During the online application process, there was no warning, eligibility check, or notice telling me that my address or household would make me ineligible for the bonus. If Eastern Bank had clearly disclosed this restriction before or during the application process, I would not have opened the account or kept my funds in the account for the promotional period. Instead, I relied on the advertised bonus, completed the deposit and balance requirements, and only later learned that the bank would deny the bonus based on a condition that was not clearly presented. I already filed a complaint directly with Eastern Bank, but Eastern Bank refused to resolve the issue. I believe this practice is misleading and unfair to consumers. The bank benefited from my account opening and deposit activity, while denying the bonus based on a hidden or inadequately disclosed restriction. I respectfully request that Eastern Bank be required to pay the advertised bonus

Consumer complaint narrative: am submitting this complaint regarding Equifax 's failure to comply with the identity theft blocking requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2. Facts:

On XXXX XXXX, the buyer messaged me acknowledging receipt of the eyeglasses in writing. After I declined his return request on grounds I considered unjustified (the alleged "smell" was a normal property of a 70-year-old acetate frame that he himself had asked about before purchase), he wrote: "let's let PayPal handle it."
The buyer then filed an "Item Not Received" claim not "Significantly Not As Described." This is a critical category mismatch: an INR claim is by definition refuted by the buyer's own written acknowledgment of receipt.
I submitted a 25-page evidence package including the carrier's tracking confirmation, the buyer's own written shipping instruction, his pre-purchase inquiry about acetate "XXXX XXXX" (demonstrating he was a self-described expert), his post-delivery written acknowledgment of receipt, his proposal of in-person return in XXXX XXXX, photographs of the package at pickup taken by the XXXX XXXX courier (a verifiable third party named on the official waybill), and a side-by-side comparison of the package box across listing, pre-shipment, and pickup photographs.

PayPal nevertheless ruled in the buyer's favor.

My concerns:
A) PayPal appears to have adjudicated an INR claim without weighing the buyer's own written acknowledgment of receipt. A claim of non-receipt cannot stand against contemporaneous messages from the claimant himself stating he received the item.
B) The buyer appears under multiple names across the transaction (XXXX XXXX on the PayPal payment side, XXXX XXXX as the shipping recipient, a XXXX PayPal address vs. a XXXX XXXX delivery address). PayPal does not appear to have made any inquiry into this identity inconsistency.
C) PayPal's one-month review delay well beyond the system's own estimate foreclosed my ability to obtain XXXX XXXX station-level CCTV footage as additional evidence (the retention window had expired).

As a long-tenured PayPal customer I am unable to identify what about the buyer's one-sentence INR claim outweighed dozens of pages of contemporaneous documentary evidence including the buyer's own written admissions.

Consumer complaint narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint I am submitting this complaint regarding Freedom Mortgage 's handling of an escrow refund check associated with mortgage account ending in XXXX. What concerns me most is that I contacted Freedom Mortgage on multiple occasions and was specifically informed that the company does not become involved in disputes between borrowers and would not reissue funds to only one party. Despite those representations, Freedom Mortgage later reissued the entire refund to Borrower # 2 only, effectively determining ownership of jointly issued funds. The divorce decree between myself and XXXX XXXX XXXX does not award the escrow refund to either party. There is no court order, judgment, settlement agreement, or provision within the divorce documents directing Freedom Mortgage to issue the funds solely to one borrower. I acknowledge that XXXX XXXX XXXX was awarded ownership of the property pursuant to our divorce decree. However, the award of the property did not include any provision awarding the escrow refund funds solely to her. The escrow refund arose from funds that accumulated in the mortgage escrow account while both borrowers were obligated on the loan. Therefore, the transfer of ownership of the property should not, by itself, have been treated as authority to reissue the entire escrow refund to one borrower while excluding the other. If Freedom Mortgage relied upon the property award as justification for its decision, I request that it identify the legal or contractual basis for doing so. I contributed to the escrow account for more than fourteen years and had a legitimate ownership interest in those funds. By reissuing the check solely to Borrower # 2, Freedom Mortgage deprived me of access to funds that were originally issued jointly. Freedom Mortgage 's decision to reissue the entire refund to Borrower # 2 was not a neutral administrative action. It effectively determined ownership of jointly issued funds despite the company 's prior representations that it would not involve itself in disputes between co-borrowers. I am requesting that Freedom Mortgage : 1. Provide a detailed written explanation of why the escrow refund was reissued solely to Borrower # 2. 2. Provide copies of all documentation, authorizations, court orders, requests, internal records, policies, and communications relied upon when making that decision. 3. Explain the policy or authority that permitted reissuance to a single borrower after representatives advised me that Freedom Mortgage would not intervene in disputes between co-borrowers and would not reissue funds to only one party. 4. Identify whether Freedom Mortgage considered my ownership interest in the escrow funds before reissuing the refund and, if so, how that determination was made. 5. Take appropriate corrective action to address my ownership interest in the escrow refund. I further demand that Freedom Mortgage compensate me for my ownership interest in the escrow refund funds that were reissued solely to XXXX XXXX XXXX. If Freedom Mortgage contends that it was authorized to issue the entire refund to Borrower # 2, I request that it provide all documentation and legal authority supporting that determination. If no such authority exists, I demand that Freedom Mortgage reimburse me for my share of the escrow refund and provide a written explanation of how it intends to resolve the financial harm caused by its actions. I am seeking transparency regarding Freedom Mortgage 's decision-making process, accountability for the inconsistent handling of jointly owned funds, and a fair financial resolution of this matter. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require Freedom Mortgage to provide a substantive written response addressing the concerns outlined above. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint because PNC failed to protect my checking account after I promptly reported active fraud, refused to take account-level protective action while additional fraudulent transactions were still pending, and then used my next paycheck to cover a negative balance caused by transactions I had already reported and disputed as fraud. On XXXX, XX/XX/year>, I received a low-balance alert on my PNC checking account, which is the account where my paycheck is deposited and where I pay bills. I discovered that approximately {$2300.00} in unauthorized XXXX XXXX transactions had drained the account to about {$28.00}. I immediately locked the debit card, went to a PNC branch, and had the debit card canceled/replaced. That did not stop the problem. Additional unauthorized transactions continued to appear as pending even after the card was canceled. I contacted PNCs fraud department and customer support multiple times while the transactions were still pending. PNCs fraud department refused to speak with me because the transactions had not yet posted and sent me back to customer support. When I escalated to a XXXX named XXXX and asked for the entire account to be frozen or otherwise protected so no additional fraudulent activity could hit the account, she refused, stating that it was card-level fraud. At that point, my account had already been drained and was effectively useless to me, so there was no practical reason to leave the account open to additional activity. After PNC refused to take stronger action, approximately another {$1100.00} in unauthorized transactions hit the account, causing it to go negative. Once the transactions posted, I went back to my branch and formally disputed the fraudulent charges. PNC confirmed in writing that the disputes were being handled under Regulation E. PNC also did not charge overdraft fees because the negative balance was tied to disputed fraudulent transactions. The most serious harm occurred when my paycheck was deposited into the same PNC account after the fraud had already been reported and disputed. I had attempted to move my direct deposit to a new bank account because I no longer trusted PNC with my money, but payroll had already locked. When my paycheck was deposited, PNC immediately used part of it approximately {$1000.00} to cover the negative balance caused by the disputed fraudulent charges. In practice, PNC made me front the loss for fraud I had already reported, on an account PNC knew was compromised. I called PNC again and requested that the provisional credit be expedited so I could recover the paycheck funds PNC had taken to offset the negative fraud balance. During that call, XXXX, a PNC XXXX, confirmed that an expedited request had been submitted to a back-office team and that funds might be made available within XXXX hours, but also explained PNCs urgency standard in a way that showed how narrowly PNC viewed the hardship. When I asked about being told the request was not urgent because I supposedly had funds available, XXXX explained that if there is no immediate need giving the example, if I dont pay for this, Im gon na starve PNC generally would not rush the credit and would instead follow the normal Regulation E timeframe. That response is unacceptable. I had already told multiple PNC representatives that my account had been drained to {$0.00}, that I could not afford bills until my next paycheck, and that additional fraudulent transactions were still being allowed to hit the account after I reported the fraud. PNC refused to freeze or protect the account, told me to wait until the charges posted, allowed the account to become negative, and then used my paycheck to cover the negative balance created by the same disputed fraud. I am asking the CFPB to investigate PNCs handling of this matter, including : 1. Why PNC refused to take account-level protective action after I reported active fraud and specifically asked for the account to be frozen ; 2. Why PNC required me to wait for pending fraudulent transactions to post while additional fraud was still draining the account ; 3. Why PNC allowed my paycheck to be used to offset a negative balance caused by transactions already reported and disputed as fraud ; 4. Whether PNCs handling of the provisional credit request complied with Regulation E and its obligations to consumers reporting unauthorized electronic fund transfers ; 5. Whether PNCs practice of treating expedited provisional credit as reserved only for extreme hardship, such as a customer being unable to buy food, is consistent with its obligations when a consumers paycheck has been taken to cover disputed fraudulent charges.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this formal complaint pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ), the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. ), the Consumer Financial Protection Act ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536 ), and all other applicable federal and state consumer protection laws. The company named in this complaint has reported, furnished, maintained, and/or verified information that is inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, unverifiable, and materially misleading in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), 1681i, 1681s-2 ( a ), and 1681s-2 ( b ). Despite prior disputes, the company has continued to publish information to consumer reporting agencies without providing competent evidence, admissible business records, or legally sufficient validation establishing the maximum possible accuracy required by federal law. Any investigation conducted appears unreasonable under the standards established by FCRA and applicable federal case law. Reporting information that can not be fully substantiated constitutes negligent and/or willful noncompliance under 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o. To the extent this matter involves a debt, I dispute the debt in its entirety and demand strict validation pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1692g. Mere verification through automated systems, database reviews, XXXX transmissions, internal records, or conclusory statements does not satisfy the legal requirements imposed by federal law. If the furnisher can not produce complete documentary evidence supporting every element of its reporting, continued reporting constitutes the furnishing of false, deceptive, misleading, incomplete, and inaccurate information prohibited by federal law. Furthermore, reporting information known or reasonably believed to be inaccurate violates 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), while failure to conduct a reasonable investigation after notice of dispute violates 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). I demand immediate deletion of all disputed information that can not be fully verified through competent documentary evidence, immediate correction of any inaccurate reporting, immediate cessation of any unlawful furnishing activities, and full compliance with all obligations imposed by the FCRA, FDCPA, and Consumer Financial Protection Act. I further demand copies of all documents, records, contracts, account-level records, payment histories, applications, signatures, investigative procedures, and evidentiary materials relied upon to verify the disputed information. Failure to remove unverifiable information constitutes continued publication of inaccurate consumer information and may expose the company to liability for statutory damages, actual damages, punitive damages, attorney fees, costs, and all other remedies available under federal and state law. I request that the CFPB require the company to conduct a lawful investigation, provide substantive documentary evidence supporting its position, and permanently delete any information that can not be verified in strict compliance with federal law. I expect a complete written response addressing every issue raised in this complaint and confirming corrective action taken to ensure compliance with all applicable consumer protection statutes and regulations.

Consumer complaint narrative: NOT A DUPLICATE THIS IS A DIRECT REBUTTLE TO RESPONSE ON CFPB Complaint Rebuttal Complaint Number : XXXX I am submitting this rebuttal because XXXX XXXX and National Credit Adjusters have failed to adequately investigate my fraud claim and have failed to provide sufficient evidence that I incurred, authorized, received, or benefited from this alleged debt. I continue to dispute this account in its entirety. This account is fraudulent, does not belong to me, and was opened by an unknown third party using my personal information without my knowledge, authorization, or consent. The documentation provided in response to my complaint does not validate this debt. Instead, it raises additional questions regarding the identity of the individual who actually applied for and received the loan proceeds. The documents provided indicate that this was an online loan application allegedly submitted on or about XX/XX/year> using an electronic signature. However, an electronic signature is not proof of identity. The entire purpose of identity theft is that a fraudster uses another person 's personal information to obtain credit or funds. Simply producing loan documents containing my personal information and an electronic signature does not establish that I was the person who completed the application. Further, the address listed on the application was not my residence at the time of the alleged transaction. I did not reside at that address on the application date, nor was it my current address. This discrepancy alone should have raised significant concerns regarding the identity of the applicant and should have triggered additional verification procedures. Most importantly, the loan documents state that the proceeds of the loan were deposited via ACH into the following bank account : Routing Number : XXXX Account Number : XXXX The routing number corresponds to XXXX XXXX. I have never owned, opened, controlled, or maintained account number XXXX. I have never had any banking relationship associated with this account. This fact alone should have resulted in a thorough fraud investigation. The most basic and obvious question remains unanswered : Who received the money? XXXX XXXX funded this loan into account number XXXX, an account that I have never owned or controlled. Therefore, the identity of the individual who actually received and benefited from the loan proceeds should be readily identifiable through the receiving financial institution. Despite my fraud claim, neither XXXX XXXX nor National Credit Adjusters has provided any evidence establishing that account number XXXX belonged to me. They have not provided account ownership records, account opening records, bank verification records, XXXX XXXX records, identification associated with the account, IP address records, device identification records, geolocation data, funding verification records, or any other documentation demonstrating that I owned, controlled, received, or benefited from the account that received the loan proceeds. If XXXX XXXX maintains that I am responsible for this debt, it should be able to produce evidence showing that account number XXXX belonged to me at the time the loan was funded. To date, no such evidence has been produced because the account is not mine. The documentation provided also raises concerns regarding XXXX XXXX XXXX identity verification procedures. The records indicate that a consumer report was obtained through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a specialty consumer reporting agency commonly used in connection with alternative lending products, including payday loans, installment loans, and other higher-risk online lending transactions. Given the prevalence of identity theft and online lending fraud within this industry, creditors have a heightened responsibility to verify the identity of applicants before extending credit and disbursing funds. The loan documents themselves acknowledge the need for identity verification and state that applicants may be required to provide identifying information and government-issued identification documents, including a driver 's license or other forms of identification. The documentation specifically states that applicants may be asked to provide documentation verifying their identity before a loan is funded. This raises another critical question : What identity verification was actually performed before this loan was funded? If XXXX XXXX obtained a driver 's license, government-issued identification, selfie verification, Know Your Customer ( KYC ) documentation, bank account verification records, or any other identity verification records, those records should be reviewed immediately as part of a fraud investigation. If such records exist, they should establish the identity of the individual who applied for and received the funds. If such records do not exist, then serious questions arise regarding whether reasonable identity verification procedures were followed before credit was extended and funds were disbursed. XXXX XXXX should be required to identify the individual who owned account number XXXX at XXXX XXXX when the loan proceeds were deposited. The name, address, identification information, account opening records, and ownership records associated with that account would identify the person who actually received the funds. A reasonable investigation would include obtaining and reviewing that information rather than continuing to report a fraudulent debt against an identity theft victim. The burden should not be placed upon an identity theft victim to prove a negative. Rather, the burden is on XXXX XXXX and National Credit Adjusters to demonstrate that the person receiving the funds was, in fact, me. To date, they have failed to do so. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires furnishers of information to conduct reasonable investigations and to ensure maximum possible accuracy when reporting information to consumer reporting agencies. Continuing to report this account without evidence that I applied for the loan, received the funds, controlled the receiving bank account, or benefited from the transaction is neither reasonable nor accurate. After receiving notice that this account was fraudulent, XXXX XXXX and National Credit Adjusters had a duty to conduct a meaningful investigation. Instead, they merely supplied copies of loan documents that contain disputed information while failing to address the most important fact in this case : the loan proceeds were deposited into a bank account that does not belong to me. The inability to connect the receiving account to me is compelling evidence that I was not the individual who received or benefited from the loan proceeds and further supports my claim that this account resulted from identity theft and fraud. Accordingly, I request : Immediate and permanent deletion of this account from all consumer reporting agencies. Immediate cessation of all collection activity related to this alleged debt. Classification of this account as identity theft/fraud. Written confirmation that all reporting associated with this account has been removed. Documentation demonstrating ownership of account number XXXX if XXXX XXXX contends that it belonged to me. Documentation demonstrating what identity verification procedures were performed prior to funding this loan. Until XXXX XXXX can establish that I owned account number XXXX, personally completed the application, personally received the funds, and personally benefited from the transaction, there is no legitimate basis for reporting this debt against me. This account remains disputed in its entirety and should be permanently deleted from my credit reports. I have uploaded the documents that were provided in their response. In XX/XX/XXXX I financed a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX through this lender. The retail installment contract expressly states it is governed by Arizona law. The vehicle was repossessed on XX/XX/XXXX and sold at a disposition on XX/XX/XXXX, generating an alleged deficiency of approximately {$9000.00}. This complaint is about the lenders failure to comply with Arizona repossession law. It is not a credit reporting dispute, and no credit reporting agency has any role in the issue I am raising. Under A.R.S. 47-9611 and 47-9614, before selling repossessed collateral the lender was required to send me a written pre-sale notice of disposition. The lender never sent this notice before the XX/XX/XXXX sale. When I contacted the lender, a representative confirmed the notice was not sent and pointed to a verbal cease-and-desist I had previously placed as the reason. That is not a lawful excuse : a cease-and-desist limits collection communications only and does not suspend the lenders independent statutory duty to send a disposition notice before sale. The lenders reliance on the cease-and-desist to justify not sending the notice is itself an admission that the required notice was never sent. Under A.R.S. 47-9616, the lender was also required to send a post-sale explanation of how the deficiency was calculated. It never did. Under A.R.S. 47-9626, a secured party that fails to send the required pre-sale notice can not recover the deficiency. The time to send that notice was before the XX/XX/XXXX sale, and it can not be cured now. I previously raised this issue ( complaint ID XXXX ). In response, the lender did not address any of these facts. It submitted a generic statement directing me to dispute with a credit reporting agency. That response was nonresponsive my complaint concerns the lenders violation of Arizona repossession law, which a credit reporting agency has no role in resolving. I am asking that the lender substantively address whether it sent the A.R.S. 47-9614 pre-sale notice before the XX/XX/XXXX sale.

The remaining $ XXXX added to my principal balance represents a hidden finance " dealer fee '' bundled into the principal. In the fine print of the attached Truth in Lending Disclosure, GoodLeap explicitly admits to this practice, stating : " Your Contractor may have opted to pay GoodLeap a fee in order for GoodLeap to offer you credit on the terms in this Agreement. Your purchase price set by the Contractor may include your Contractor 's various costs, including this fee. '' By allowing XXXX to bake a five-figure finance fee directly into the principal to buy down the interest rate to 1.99 %, GoodLeap facilitated a deceptive lending practice that failed to separate the true cash price of the goods from the cost of the financing, violating the disclosure mandates of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). My initial payments were set at {$120.00}, based on the deceptive assumption that I would surrender a 30 % federal tax credit as a voluntary prepayment to hit a " Target Balance '' of {$29000.00} by XX/XX/XXXX. Because I retained my {$12000.00} tax refund rather than handing it over to pay down an already fraudulent, inflated principal, GoodLeap automatically re-amortized the loan. My monthly payment immediately spiked 44 % out-of-pocket, jumping from {$120.00} to {$180.00}. Under the Federal Trade Commission 's Holder Rule ( 16 C.F.R. 433 ), which governs this consumer credit contract, GoodLeap as the holder is fully subject to all claims and defenses that I could assert against the original seller, XXXX . Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding what I believe were misleading and deceptive debt collection practices. I have been communicating with this collection agency in an effort to resolve an old debt. During negotiations, the agency requested detailed information about my financial hardship, including my unemployment status, medical condition, lack of income, and inability to pay the full amount owed. Following these discussions, the collector presented a settlement amount of approximately {$15000.00} and indicated that the account could be resolved through a payment arrangement. Based on these representations, I believed that payments made under the settlement agreement would be applied toward satisfying the negotiated settlement balance. I subsequently agreed to make a payment of {$5000.00} as part of the settlement arrangement. However, when I contacted the agency to finalize payment, I was informed by telephone that the {$5000.00} payment would be applied to the original balance of approximately {$35000.00} rather than the negotiated settlement amount of {$15000.00}. This information was not disclosed during the settlement negotiations and directly contradicted my understanding of the agreement. Had I proceeded with the payment without asking additional questions, I would have paid {$5000.00} under the belief that it was reducing the negotiated settlement balance when, according to the collector, it would instead have been applied to the original debt balance. I believe this was misleading and potentially deceptive because a reasonable consumer would understand a settlement payment to be applied toward the agreed settlement amount, not toward a larger original balance that was supposedly being settled. I have retained emails documenting the settlement negotiations, the collectors requests for financial hardship information, and the settlement discussions. The conflicting information regarding how the payment would be applied was disclosed only during a telephone conversation immediately before payment was to be made. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter, review the collectors representations regarding settlement terms, and determine whether the agency engaged in unfair, deceptive, or misleading debt collection practices. I am prepared to provide all supporting documentation and correspondence upon request. Thank you for your consideration.

Summary of Misrepresentation : The merchants website advertises this " XXXX XXXX '' using images that depict a roll of flexible tape. Based on these professional images, a consumer reasonably expects a product with the properties of tapespecifically flexibility and adhesion. However, the product received is functionally useless : The product page for the " XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX '' presents a fundamental conflict between its marketing title and technical specifications. While the title prominently uses the word " Metallic, '' which implies a high-sheen, reflective, and brilliant finish, the body text contradicts this by describing a " soft satin finish. '' In the context of professional cake decorating, these terms represent two entirely different aesthetic tiers. A bank claim can be supported by the argumen t of Material Misrepresentation, as the merchant used a high-value descriptive keyword to trigger a sale while delivering a product that lacks the primary light-reflective properties promised in the heading. Furthermore, there is a significant discrepancy regarding the product 's structural performance. The primary marketing photograph depicts the ribbon as a rigid or semi-rigid material capable of holding sharp, upright loops and architectural folds on a cake. Conversely, the description labels the material as " soft and flexible '' edible lace. Physics dictates that a soft, lace-like material can not maintain the structural integrity shown in the photo without internal support, which is not mentioned. This constitutes Deceptive Visual Advertising, as the consumer is induced to purchase based on a " structural '' use case that the actual physical material is incapable of performing. The listing further fails the consumer by utilizing subjective terminology in place of technical dimensions. By labeling the ribbon as " Wide '' without providing specific measurements in inches or millimeters, the merchant creates a " dimensional ambiguity '' that makes it impossible for a professional to determine if the item is fit for their specific project. In banking disputes, this is categorized as a Failure of Disclosure. Without exact specifications, the term " Wide '' is a subjective claim rather than a factual description, leading to a purchase of an item that may not meet the necessary physical requirements for the intended application. Transparency regarding safety is also a major fault, as the page lacks a visible ingredient list or allergy warning. For an edible product, particularly one using XXXX and metallic pigments, which often contain iron oxides or specific dyes ( like XXXX XXXX ), the omission of this data is a critical safety gap. '' This creates a " Liability Shield '' where the merchant avoids accountability for the products failure to perform, like the equipment shown in the photos. By proving the product is materially different from its description, the merchants " No Return '' policy becomes legally unenforceable in a dispute. 1. Misleading " Metallic '' Representation The primary selling point is the " Metallic '' finish, but the merchant includes a contradictory fine-print disclaimer. This is a bait-and-switch tactic where the title promises a high-shine finish that the merchant knows the product can not achieve. My argument : " The merchant 's own documentation admits the product does not meet the standard defined by its own title. This is deceptive advertising. '' 2. Unfair " No Returns '' Policy for Defective Goods XXXX XXXX XXXX typically refuses returns on edible items regardless of quality. Discrepancy Between Promotional Photos and Reality The photos on the XXXX XXXX XXXX website show a flawless, high-gloss finish. The XXXX : Most bank dispute departments look for a " What I Ordered vs. What I Got '' comparison. If the ribbon looks like matte plastic or dark grey rather than " XXXX XXXX, '' I should claim Visual Misrepresentation. My argument : " The merchants marketing materials use edited or enhanced photography to depict a high-gloss metallic finish that is physically impossible to achieve with the actual product provided. This constitutes a material misrepresentation of the goods. '' XXXX. Violation of the " Implied Warranty of Merchantability. '' Under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), goods sold by a merchant must be " merchantable, '' meaning they must pass without objection in the trade under the contract description. Consumer complaint narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX I financed a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX through this lender. The retail installment contract expressly states it is governed by Arizona law. In XX/XX/XXXX I verbally requested the lender cease and desist contact on this account. The vehicle was then repossessed on XX/XX/XXXX and sold at a disposition on XX/XX/XXXX. The lender claims a resulting deficiency of approximately {$9000.00}, now reported on my credit file as a charged-off balance. Under Arizona law ( A.R.S. 47-9611 and 47-9614 ), before disposing of repossessed collateral the secured party must send the debtor a pre-sale notice of disposition. I never received any such notice before the XX/XX/XXXX sale. When I asked the lender about this, a representative indicated the notice was not sent and pointed to my cease and desist request as the reason. That is not a lawful excuse : a cease and desist limits collection communications only it does not suspend the lender 's independent statutory duty under 47-9611/47-9614 to send a disposition notice before sale. The lender 's reliance on my cease and desist to justify not sending the notice is itself an admission the required notice was never sent. The lender was also required under A.R.S. 47-9616 to send a post-sale explanation of how the deficiency was calculated. I never received that either. I attempted to obtain these documents directly. I gave the lender verbal authorization to lift the cease and desist for the limited purpose of email communication to my email address the same verbal method by which the cease and desist was originally placed. The lender refused to accept my verbal authorization to send me documents, while continuing to treat the cease and desist as valid against me. This asymmetric application honoring a verbal instruction when it lets the lender withhold required documents, but rejecting a verbal instruction when it would require the lender to provide them is an unfair and abusive practice and a deliberate barrier to my consumer rights. Consumer complaint narrative: I.C. System, Inc. is furnishing a collection account in my name to the credit bureaus ( account number XXXX, original creditor XXXX XXXX balance {$260.00} ). I am filing this complaint because I.C. System received a written dispute and validation request from me, failed to validate the debt, and has nonetheless continued to report it conduct that violates both the FDCPA and the FCRA. On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent I.C. System a written dispute and request for validation of this debt by XXXX XXXX Mail. XXXX tracking confirms delivery to I.C. System 's XXXX XXXX, MN XXXX address on XX/XX/XXXX. Proof of delivery is attached. I.C. System can not claim it did not receive my dispute ; the certified record establishes receipt as a matter of fact. In response, I.C. System did not provide validation of this debt. It did not produce a copy of the original signed agreement or account-level records from XXXX, an itemization showing how the {$260.00} balance was calculated, or documentation of its authority to collect this specific account. A form letter or a bare restatement of the alleged balance is not validation It fails to establish that I am the correct party obligated on this debt, that the {$260.00} balance is accurate and properly itemized, or that I.C. System actually owns or was assigned the right to collect it which requires a documented chain of assignment from the original creditor, XXXX, to I.C. System. These are the core elements that validation under the FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), is meant to confirm, and they are also the facts that the FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, obligates I.C. System to verify as a furnisher before continuing to report the account. Without a documented chain of assignment, I.C. System has not shown it has lawful authority to collect this debt under XXXX, and it can not certify the account as accurate or verifiable under XXXX yet it continues to report it. I.C. System 's continued reporting is improper on XXXX independent legal grounds, and I ask that each be addressed separately : First, under the FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), my written dispute obligated XXXX. System to obtain and mail verification before continuing collection activity. It did not do so. Continuing to collect on, and report, a disputed debt without providing that verification violates XXXX ( b ). Second, and independently, under the FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, I.C. System is a furnisher of information to the credit bureaus. Once it received my dispute, it had a duty to conduct a reasonable investigation and to refrain from continuing to report information it has not verified as accurate. Reporting an account it has been unable to validate and that remains on my report nearly XXXX months after my dispute was delivered is a failure of that duty. This FCRA obligation exists regardless of any timing argument I.C. System might raise about the FDCPA validation window, so a response addressing only the FDCPA does not resolve this complaint. To be clear about what a sufficient response requires : a general statement that I.C. System " verified '' the account, or that it " confirmed '' the balance with its records, does not answer this complaint. The only adequate responses are either ( a ) production of the specific documents identified above the original XXXX agreement, a full itemization of the {$260.00} balance, and proof of I.C. System 's authority to collect or ( b ) deletion of the account. This account is materially damaging my credit and obstructing my ability to obtain financing. I.C. System has now reported it for approximately XXXX months after receiving a documented, delivered dispute, without ever producing the documentation required to validate it.

FACTS OF THE COMPLAINT On XX/XX/XXXX, a client payment of {$290.00} was sent to my XXXX account as compensation for professional photography services rendered in connection with my upcoming XXXX XXXX expedition. XXXX placed an immediate hold on these funds without prior notice and without any transaction-specific explanation. XXXX further informed me that the funds would be automatically released on XX/XX/XXXX exactly 21 days after the hold was placed regardless of any verification. II. BASIS FOR COMPLAINT The following concerns form the basis of this complaint : 1. Lack of specific justification. Internal contradiction in stated rationale. XXXX claimed the hold exists to protect against non-delivery of goods or services, yet simultaneously admitted it has no process to verify delivery. Provide a specific, documented reason for the hold not generic boilerplate or acknowledge that no valid basis exists. 3. Review and revise the blanket 21-day hold policy to ensure it is applied only when a legitimate, individualized basis exists, consistent with fair and transparent consumer practices. I have made good-faith efforts to resolve this matter directly with XXXX, without success. I am providing this complaint in the interest of consumer protection and to ensure that XXXX XXXX practices receive appropriate scrutiny. Thank you for your attention to this matter. In XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX was placed into conservatorship by the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ). In XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX involuntarily liquidated XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and transferred operations and member accounts to XXXX XXXX XXXX. In XXXX, a Full Reconveyance was recorded against the second mortgage loan. The Full Reconveyance remained of record for approximately XXXX years. During my first mortgage modification process, records maintained by my first mortgage lender reflected that no second lien existed against the property. In XXXX, the Full Reconveyance was cancelled without notice to me. For many years thereafter, I did not receive meaningful servicing communications, periodic account statements, transfer notices, payment demands, collection efforts, or accountings concerning the loan. On XX/XX/XXXX, I obtained a XXXX XXXX XXXX through CFPB assistance reflecting an alleged balance of approximately {$130000.00}. XXXX days later, on XX/XX/XXXX, a Notice of Default was recorded asserting an alleged indebtedness exceeding {$200000.00}. No meaningful accounting was provided explaining how a HELOC with an original credit limit of approximately {$65000.00} allegedly increased to approximately {$130000.00} and then to more than {$200000.00}. My property was subsequently foreclosed upon on XX/XX/XXXX. Following complaints submitted to CFPB and the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation ( DFPI ), Franklin Credit Management Corporation entered settlement discussions concerning the disputed debt and foreclosure. During approximately XX/XX/XXXX, Defendants demanded approximately {$170000.00} to resolve the dispute. I informed Defendants that financing would be required if the demanded amount exceeded the original HELOC credit limit. I subsequently obtained financing sufficient to satisfy the settlement demand. However, the proposed settlement could not be completed because escrow and title requirements required restoration of title before financing proceeds could be released, while Defendants required payment, dismissal of claims, withdrawal of the lis pendens, and release of title-related rights before restoration of title would occur. As a result, the lender ultimately withdrew and the settlement was not completed. I believe these facts are significant because they demonstrate that this was not a situation where a borrower refused to pay or lacked the ability to resolve the alleged debt. Financing sufficient to satisfy the settlement demand was obtained. The transaction failed because of competing title and escrow requirements. I am also concerned because Franklin Credit Management was previously the subject of a settlement with the Attorney General of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts involving more than XXXX dormant or " zombie '' second mortgages. The circumstances of my loan appear consistent with many of the concerns that prompted governmental scrutiny in that matter, including the enforcement of long-dormant mortgage debt after years of limited borrower communication. In addition, California recently enacted AB 130 ( Civil Code section 2924.13 ) to address unlawful practices involving second-lien mortgage servicing and foreclosure activity. The circumstances of my case appear consistent with several of the consumer-protection concerns that prompted enactment of that legislation, including a dormant second mortgage loan, years without meaningful servicing communications, lack of periodic statements and accountings, substantial unexplained increases in alleged indebtedness, and foreclosure activity following years of dormancy. I respectfully request CFPB review of : The ownership and servicing history of the loan following the NCUA liquidation of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ; Whether required servicing communications, transfer notices, and periodic statements were provided ; The basis for the increase from a {$65000.00} HELOC to alleged balances of approximately {$130000.00} and later more than {$200000.00} ; The accounting supporting the amounts claimed prior to foreclosure ; and The conduct of Franklin Credit Management Corporation and related entities in servicing and enforcing this dormant second mortgage loan. Supporting documents are attached for review.

I am filing this complaint because Citibanks billing dispute department mishandled a credit card dispute by failing to distinguish between an initial outbound delivery and a subsequent customer return. XX/XX/2026 : I made a separate, unrelated purchase from the same merchant for a third item totaling {$420.00}. Subsequent Returns : All three items were initially delivered to my residence, but all three items were subsequently returned to the merchant. Due to the large physical size of the merchandise, each item required an individual return shipping label. I initiated a billing dispute for the XX/XX/XXXX charge of {$850.00} because the merchant failed to issue the appropriate refunds. Citibank subsequently closed the investigation in favor of the merchant. The bank stated that the merchant provided outbound tracking data confirming delivery to my residence, concluding that the merchandise remains in my possession. This conclusion represents a fundamental administrative error by Citibank. Outbound delivery confirmation merely establishes how the merchandise was originally received. It does not invalidate a legitimate " XXXX XXXX '' claim. The core of this dispute rests on the subsequent return shipments tracking back to the merchant 's possession. The comprehensive financial breakdown illustrates the unresolved discrepancy : XXXX XXXX XXXX : XXXX items at {$420.00} each, totaling {$1200.00}. Merchant Documentation : The merchant issued official email confirmations acknowledging the receipt and processing of returns for XXXX out of the XXXX items. They failed to issue a confirmation for the final item, despite tracking verifying its delivery to their warehouse. Credits Posted : My Citibank account statement reflects only XXXX single credit of {$420.00}, which posted on XX/XX/2026. XXXX XXXX XXXX : I am missing a total of {$850.00} in valid return credits. On XX/XX/2026, I submitted a formal appeal via email ( attached ) detailing this timeline and offering the official merchant return labels, distinct return tracking delivery receipts, and the merchants own return confirmations. To date, Citibank has not acknowledged or acted upon this correspondence, leaving the case closed without reviewing the evidentiary data. By allowing a merchant 's initial outbound shipping proof to override explicit evidence of a completed return, Citibank has failed to conduct a proper and reasonable investigation as outlined under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ). The merchant has retained both the returned merchandise and my funds.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am requesting a further review of Cash App 's investigation into over {$4500.00} in unauthorized XXXX transactions and a response regarding whether EcoATM was contacted to verify the ownership and possession status of the device relied upon in determining that those transactions were authorized. During Cash App 's investigation, I provided information to XXXX of the Cash App XXXX XXXX XXXX stating that the device identified as a " known device '' had been sold to XXXX months before the unauthorized transactions occurred. This information was directly relevant to Cash App 's conclusion because the device appears to have been a significant factor in determining that the transactions were authorized. After providing this information, I was never informed whether Cash App contacted XXXX to verify when the device came into its possession or whether the device was no longer in my possession at the time the unauthorized transactions occurred. The following day, my case was closed and the prior determination was maintained. I am requesting that Cash App provide information regarding whether XXXX was contacted as part of its investigation. If XXXX was contacted, I request that the results of that inquiry be provided. If XXXX was not contacted, I request an explanation as to how Cash App determined that activity originating from a device that had been sold months earlier supported a conclusion that the transactions were authorized by me. I am also attaching a police report and case number. The report documents that this matter was reported to law enforcement and supports my position that the transactions were unauthorized. If additional information or verification is needed, I encourage Cash App and/or the CFPB to contact the law enforcement agency listed in the report directly. I have been fully transparent throughout this process and welcome any efforts to independently verify the facts surrounding this case. I am concerned that the information I provided was not fully considered. XXXX advised me that if I had new supporting information, I should provide it for consideration. In response, I immediately provided information obtained through my own investigation showing that the device relied upon as a " known device '' had been sold to XXXX months before the unauthorized XXXX transactions occurred. This information was important because it directly challenged the conclusion that the transactions were authorized simply because they originated from a device previously associated with my account. A device that is no longer in someone's possession can still be used by another person, and activity originating from that device should not automatically be considered authorized by the former owner. After I provided this information, my case was closed the following day and the prior conclusion was maintained. Based on the timing, I have serious concerns about whether this new information was meaningfully investigated before a final determination was made. To date, I have not been provided with evidence showing that I personally initiated, approved, or authorized the disputed XXXX purchases. Instead, the determination appears to rely heavily on the fact that the activity originated from a device that had once been associated with my account, despite evidence that the device had been sold and was no longer in my possession. This situation is no different than if someone took someones phone and transferred money from that Cash App account attached to that phone without permission. The fact that a transaction is completed from a device or account associated with the account holder does not automatically mean the account holder authorized it. Authorization requires the account holder 's knowledge and consent. If another individual accessed my account and conducted these transactions without my permission, then those transactions were not authorized, regardless of what device or account information was used to complete them. Cash App has also continued to maintain that XXXX bears responsibility because the funds originated from my XXXX account. However, regardless of where the funds originated, the disputed XXXX purchases occurred within Cash App 's platform and were processed through my Cash App account and then gone. The transactions involved multiple XXXX purchases occurring within a very short period of time on an account with no history of XXXX activity. Given the nature, speed, and volume of these transactions, I believe they should have triggered additional fraud reviews or security measures. At a minimum, these circumstances appear unusual enough to warrant closer scrutiny before allowing the transactions to proceed. Cash App publicly represents to consumers that it protects users from fraud and utilizes fraud monitoring and proactive security features designed to help prevent fraud before it occurs. In my case, those protections appear to have failed. Multiple unauthorized XXXX purchases were completed despite several apparent indicators of potential fraud. Because of that, I believe it is reasonable to ask what fraud detection measures, if any, were triggered and why the activity was allowed to proceed despite the unusual nature of the transactions. For these reasons, I do not believe responsibility should be shifted entirely to XXXX. While I am also pursuing accountability from XXXX regarding allowing my phone number to be removed and all money quickly transferred, Cash App was the platform that processed the disputed XXXX transactions and had the opportunity to identify potential fraud indicators before those transactions were completed. Cash App has also indicated that the transactions were verified using my debit card information. However, I do not believe this establishes that I personally authorized the transactions. If an unauthorized individual gained access to my Cash App account via the broken XXXX sold to EcoATM, they would have had access to information displayed within the Cash App account, including my whole debit card number on the account. In that circumstance, the ability to provide or verify debit card information would not necessarily prove that the transactions were authorized by me. Rather, it could be consistent with an individual who had already gained unauthorized access to my account via the sold XXXX to XXXXand the information available within it. I am asking for a thorough review of all available evidence, including the attached police report, the information regarding the previously sold device, and any available account access records that may assist in determining the true source of the unauthorized activity. This situation has had a significant impact on my family. That money taken was not just numbers on a screen ; it was money that my family depends on. Since discovering the unauthorized activity, I have spent countless hours trying to understand what happened, report it to the appropriate parties, and recover the funds that were taken. If this happened to you and your family, you would likely be doing exactly what I am doing nowcontacting financial institutions, law enforcement, consumer protection agencies, and anyone else who may be able to help uncover the truth. I am trying to understand how this happened and recover funds that I did not authorize to be spent. I remain fully committed to pursuing this matter until the unauthorized funds are reimbursed and this situation is properly resolved. I simply want a fair and thorough investigation, answers to the questions that remain unanswered, and an accurate determination based on all available facts and evidence provided.

On approximately XX/XX/XXXX, a business credit card account was opened with XXXX XXXX in my name without my knowledge or authorization. I did not apply for this account, did not authorize anyone to apply for it on my behalf, and never received or used the card. The charges on this account, totaling approximately {$31000.00}, are the result of identity theft. I discovered the fraudulent account in approximately XX/XX/XXXX. Upon discovering it, I filed an Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission on XX/XX/XXXX ; my FTC report number is XXXX. I contacted XXXX XXXX to report the identity theft shortly after filing the FTC report. XXXX XXXX informed me that it had completed its investigation and concluded the account was not fraudulent. XXXX XXXX did not provide me with any documentation supporting this conclusion including the original application, the IP address, device information, email address, or mailing address used to open the account, the address to which the card was delivered, or any signature, activation, or verification records. I was told that once XXXX XXXX reached its conclusion, the case could not be reopened. I then submitted a complaint to the CFPB regarding this account. In response to that complaint, XXXX XXXX acknowledged in writing that the account was opened through an online application and that no signed application exists. XXXX XXXX stated it concluded the account belongs to me based on two facts : ( 1 ) a phone number that XXXX XXXX says it confirmed belongs to me was used to activate the account, and ( XXXX ) a payment was made from a XXXX XXXX deposit account that XXXX XXXX says links to me. Both of these reasons are flawed and do not constitute a reasonable investigation. First, the phone number cited by XXXX XXXX has never belonged to me. I have never used, owned, or been assigned that number. XXXX XXXX has not explained how it " confirmed '' the number belongs to me, and I believe its confirmation rests on its own internal records of the fraudulent application meaning XXXX XXXX is treating the phone number the identity thief provided as proof that the account is mine. That is circular reasoning, not verification of identity. Second, the XXXX XXXX deposit account that XXXX XXXX says " links to '' me is also not mine. I do not have, and have never opened, any deposit account with XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX 's response was the first time I was informed of this deposit account 's existence. If this deposit account is being treated as evidence that the credit card account is legitimately mine, then XXXX XXXX has now disclosed a second account opened in my name without my authorization, which is itself an additional instance of identity theft. I am reporting this second account as fraudulent as part of this complaint. Both of XXXX XXXX 's stated reasons rely on records originating from the fraudulent applications themselves. Confirming that an impostor used consistent credentials across multiple accounts they fraudulently opened is not verification that I opened any of them. XXXX XXXX has refused to produce the records that would actually distinguish between me and an impostor : the IP address the application was submitted from, the device identifier, the email address used on the application, the mailing address to which the card was sent, the geolocation associated with the application session, and the originating details of activation. A fraud account manager at XXXX XXXX confirmed to me by phone that no further documentation would be provided. In parallel, I submitted a request to XXXX under Section 605B of the Fair Credit Reporting Act to block the fraudulent account from my credit report, supported by my FTC Identity Theft Report. XXXX confirmed by phone that it had placed the block. XXXX XXXX then caused the block to be undone by certifying to XXXX that the account is accurate. I dispute that certification, and XXXX XXXX has not substantiated it with any evidence that actually identifies me as the applicant. XXXX has since told me it can not act further and that I must resolve the matter with XXXX XXXX, leaving the fraudulent account on my credit report. The fraudulent account has now been reported as charged off with a balance of approximately {$31000.00} and has been placed with a debt collection law firm, Rubin & Rothman , LLC, which is actively contacting me to collect on a debt I am not responsible for. The reporting of this account is causing ongoing damage to my credit, and the collection activity is creating risk of litigation against me on a fraudulent debt. I am requesting that the CFPB direct XXXX XXXX to : 1. Produce the application records and method-of-verification documentation used to open and verify the credit card account, including the IP address, device identifier, email address, mailing address used on the application, address to which the card was delivered, and geolocation associated with the application session. 2. Explain in writing the specific basis on which it concluded the cited phone number belongs to me, including the records relied on to make that determination. 3. Treat the XXXX XXXX deposit account identified in its prior response as also being the subject of an identity theft claim, investigate it as such, and produce the same application and verification records for that account. 4. Conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of my identity theft claim under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, considering whether its prior determination was based solely on records originating from the fraudulent applications themselves. 5. Cease reporting the disputed credit card account to the consumer reporting agencies pending production of the requested records, and withdraw the certification of accuracy it provided to XXXX that caused the Section 605B block on this account to be undone. 6. Cease collection activity on this account and refrain from selling, transferring, or maintaining placement of the alleged debt with any third party for collection while the dispute is unresolved. I have a valid Identity Theft Report filed with the Federal Trade Commission, which has been provided to XXXX XXXX and to the consumer reporting agencies. XXXX XXXX 's refusal to honor that report, combined with its refusal to produce the underlying application records and its reliance on circular reasoning, is the basis for this complaint.

I am filing this complaint again against SoFi Bank regarding the improper handling of my loan application, the failure to make reasonable efforts to verify my identity before issuing a denial, and the resulting hard inquiry on my credit report that I am requesting be removed. They continually are dishonest in their responses. FACTS : On XX/XX/year>, my spouse and I submitted a joint loan application to SoFi. We are exceptionally well-qualified borrowers- combined income of nearly $ XXXX, {$50000.00} in savings and investments, excellent credit, and a debt-to-income ratio that most lenders would consider an easy approval. On XX/XX/XXXX, SoFi placed a single phone call to my spouse in the middle of a workday. The caller ID did not say Sofi, it was a random number and when she googled it - it did not even say it was the Sofi company. She was at work and was unable to answer. That same day - within hours of that one unanswered call - SoFi declined our application citing " inability to verify identity. '' No follow-up call was made. No email was sent. No text was sent. No other outreach of any kind was attempted. We were given no opportunity to resolve the issue. When I contacted SoFi to understand the denial and offer to just simply verify our identity, the representative 's only solution was to tell me to simply reapply. I did exactly what SoFi 's own employee instructed me to do. Upon reapplying, I was immediately declined a second time- this time for " too many inquiries. '' Inquiries that exist solely because SoFi failed to complete a basic verification process and then directed me into a second application. I want to be clear : this is not the first time SoFi has done this to me. This same sequence of events occurred last year, and I did not pursue it at the time. This is a pattern of behavior and a gross misuse of power. VIOLATION : My complaint is not that SoFi ran a credit check without authorization. I authorized the inquiry. My complaint is that the inquiry exists as a direct result of SoFi 's failure to make a reasonable effort to verify my identity before issuing a denial. One unanswered phone call in the middle of a workday, with no follow-up of any kind, does not constitute a reasonable verification effort. A hard inquiry is only justified when a credit decision is made in good faith following a complete, fairly processed application. SoFi 's denial was not that. It was an institutional failure that caused direct, measurable harm to my credit profile. Furthermore, SoFi 's own representative acknowledged the process was flawed by directing me to just reapply - and then SoFi penalized me for following that instruction. SoFi created this problem and then used its own incompetence as grounds for a second denial. DEMANDS : 1. Removal of the hard inquiry from my credit report on the grounds that it resulted from SoFi 's failure to follow reasonable lending and verification practices. This inquiry is not a reflection of my creditworthiness. It is a reflection of SoFi 's process failure. I am submitting this complaint as a follow-up to my previous CFPB filings against SoFi Bank . I am requesting that the CFPB review the pattern of SoFi 's responses to my prior complaints alongside the facts of my case. SoFi 's responses to date have consistently deflected from the actual issue. Rather than address the core complaint - that a hard inquiry exists on my credit report as a direct result of their failure to make a reasonable verification effort - SoFi has repeatedly cited my authorization of the credit pull as justification for their actions. These are two entirely separate issues, and SoFi 's continued conflation of them is either a deliberate misdirection or a failure to properly review my complaint. I have now filed multiple complaints with the CFPB and a complaint with the Colorado Attorney General 's office. SoFi has stonewalled every one. This is not the behavior of a company that believes it acted appropriately - it is the behavior of a large institution that expects consumers to give up. I will not. I am respectfully requesting that the CFPB look beyond SoFi 's boilerplate responses and examine the actual facts of this case, which are documented across my prior complaint filings. The facts have not changed. SoFi 's negligence has not been addressed. The inquiry has not been removed. I am continuing to pursue this matter and will be consulting with a consumer protection attorney regarding potential FCRA violations.

Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/year>, Rocket Mortgage issued a Loss Mitigation Determination Notice for our FHA-insured loan # XXXX that violates FHA loss mitigation waterfall requirements under HUD Handbook 4000.1 and FHA Mortgagee Letter 2025-12. We are filing this complaint because Rocket has refused to evaluate us for the Standalone Partial Claim which is the controlling FHA option for our circumstances and has instead funneled us toward a Short Sale of our primary residence without performing a substantive retention review. The XX/XX/year> notice identifies only three options on which we were " evaluated '' : Disaster FHA Trial ( declined ), Deed-in-Lieu ( declined ), and Short Sale ( conditionally approved ). The notice is completely silent as to the Standalone Partial Claim, which under FHA Mortgagee Letter 2025-12 is the required FHA loss mitigation tool for borrowers who have resolved the cause of default and can resume the contractual monthly mortgage payment but lack the lump sum to reinstate. We meet those criteria. We have been actively pursuing a Standalone Partial Claim through HUD National Servicing Center Ticket # XXXX, and Rocket is aware of this. Their failure to evaluate us for the Partial Claim is a procedural violation of 24 CFR 203.605 and HUD Handbook 4000.1 Part III.A.2.k. The modification denial reason given is " Bypass Mod Option / Not In Use. '' This is not a substantive denial reason under FHA policy it is an internal servicer code indicating the modification review was not performed at all. There is no DTI calculation, no surplus income analysis, no post-modification payment calculation, none of the analytical work that FHA requires before issuing a modification denial. The servicer is required under HUD Handbook 4000.1 to perform a substantive evaluation, not to flag the file with a bypass code. The Deed-in-Lieu denial reason is " Other Foreclosure Alternative currently participating in another alternative to foreclosure, '' referring to our pending XXXX XXXX bankruptcy. That bankruptcy case ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX XXXX ) is being voluntarily dismissed at the direction of the XXXX XXXX Trustee. The predicate for the Deed-in-Lieu denial is moot, but more importantly, Rocket should have evaluated all retention options including Partial Claim and Modification regardless of the bankruptcy status, because retention options preserve the property and are not " foreclosure alternatives '' in the same sense as DIL. The Short Sale conditional approval is procedurally improper. Funneling a borrower directly to a Short Sale before completing the required FHA waterfall analysis, and without ever evaluating for Partial Claim or substantive Modification, violates the spirit and letter of FHA loss mitigation policy. We are not selling the property and we do not accept the Short Sale conditional approval. This complaint references and incorporates by reference the multiple prior CFPB complaints and Notices of Error filed against Rocket Mortgage related to this same loan, including issues regarding payment count miscalculation, denial of 3-in-12 standard modification, refusal to apply payments received, and the underlying loss mitigation eligibility analysis. The XX/XX/year> letter is the latest in a documented pattern of servicer noncompliance with FHA requirements on this account.
