Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint because American Express has repeatedly failed to provide evidence supporting its refusal to award a promised welcome offer after I fully satisfied the spending requirements and paid the annual fee associated with the card. This complaint relates to my prior CFPB complaints : Complaint ID : XXXX Complaint ID : XXXX In both cases, American Express refused to award the advertised welcome offer of XXXX Membership Rewards points after I completed more than {$8000.00} in qualifying purchases within the first six months of Card Membership, as required by the offer terms. American Express provided the same generic explanation in response to both complaints : " In determining eligibility, we considered your history with credit Card balance transfers, your history as an American Express Card Member, the number of credit Cards that you have opened and closed and other factors. '' This statement is entirely conclusory and unsupported by evidence. In my responses to American Express, I specifically addressed each category referenced in its explanation and requested that the company provide the factual basis, records, documentation, account history, or other evidence supporting its determination. American Express either refused or was unable to provide any documentation demonstrating why I was deemed ineligible for the welcome offer. Importantly, during the application process, I did not receive any warning, notification, or pop-up message indicating that I was ineligible for the welcome offer. American Express utilizes an eligibility notification system that is designed to inform applicants before they complete an application if they are not eligible for a welcome offer. Had I received any such notice, I would have had the opportunity to decide whether to proceed with the application. No such warning was provided to me. As a result, I reasonably relied on the advertised offer when applying for the card, paying the approximately {$700.00} annual fee, and directing more than {$8000.00} in spending to the account in order to satisfy the stated requirements. It is fundamentally unfair for American Express to accept my application, collect the annual fee, benefit from my spending activity, and then retroactively deny the promised welcome offer based on undisclosed criteria that were never communicated to me before or during the application process. American Express has now been given multiple opportunities through two separate CFPB complaints to provide evidence supporting its determination and has failed to do so each time. Rather than supplying documentation, records, or specific facts supporting its position, it has repeatedly relied on the same generic and unsupported statement. American Express is effectively asking the CFPB and me to accept its conclusion without evidence while retaining the benefit of my business, the annual fee, and the spending activity required to earn the offer. I believe this conduct raises significant concerns regarding transparency, fairness, and potential unfair or deceptive practices. Consumers should not be induced to apply for a credit card through a specific promotional offer, satisfy all stated spending requirements, pay substantial annual fees, and then be denied the promised reward based on undisclosed criteria that can not be substantiated when challenged. I respectfully request that the CFPB require American Express to do one of the following : 1 ) Produce the specific records, documentation, account history, eligibility analysis, internal decision-making records, and other evidence that formed the basis for its determination that I was ineligible for the XXXX Membership Rewards point welcome offer ; or 2 ) Award the XXXX Membership Rewards points as originally promised after I satisfied the spending requirements associated with the offer ; or 3 ) Refund the approximately {$700.00} annual fee. If American Express can not produce evidence supporting its determination, I believe its refusal to honor the advertised offer constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice that falls squarely within the CFPB 's consumer protection mandate. The CFPB was established to protect consumers from unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts and practices and to promote transparency in consumer financial products. I am requesting the CFPB 's assistance in ensuring that American Express is held accountable for either substantiating its decision with evidence or honoring the promotional offer that induced me to obtain and use the card. I appreciate the CFPB 's assistance and request a substantive response supported by evidence rather than another generic statement that does not explain the basis for American Express 's actions.

The first communication I received about the sale was the XX/XX/XXXX letter 76 days after the sale itself. Navy Federal has not produced any pre-sale notice and bears the burden of doing so. The XX/XX/XXXX letter has additional problems on its face : 1. The " Total Obligation Secured '' is calculated as of XX/XX/XXXX six days AFTER the XX/XX/XXXX sale. The {$2100.00} in " Repossession Expenses Incurred, Including Expenses of Retaking, Holding, Preparing for Disposition, Processing and Disposing of Collateral '' is reported as a single lumped figure with no itemization. Under O.C.G.A. 11-9-616 I am entitled to an explanation of the calculation. An unitemized lump sum is not an explanation. 3. I also want this complaint to address what Navy Federal Credit Union represents itself to be. Navy Federal holds itself out as a member-driven not-for-profit credit union operating on a relationship-based model distinct from for-profit banks. The conduct above silently repossessing collateral, selling it 76 days before notifying me, calculating obligation as of a date after the sale, and producing a deficiency demand without itemization or pre-sale notice is not how a member-driven institution treats a member it is supposed to serve. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a formal complaint against SoFi for an unauthorized account debit resulting from a check encoding error, and for a subsequent refusal to honor federal and state banking regulations regarding properly payable items. On XX/XX/year>, a check I wrote to my landlord for rent cleared my SoFi checking account. The check was written and authorized for the exact amount of {$1600.00}. However, the payee 's depository bank mistakenly requested, and SoFi incorrectly disbursed, an altered/over-encoded amount of {$2600.00}. This resulted in an unauthorized over-debit of exactly {$1000.00} from my personal funds. When I identified the discrepancy and contacted SoFi customer support to dispute the unauthorized transaction, SoFi refused to credit my account or initiate a formal adjustment request through the clearinghouse network. Instead, SoFi representatives instructed me to contact the payee 's financial institution to recover my funds. Under Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) 4-401, a payor bank may only charge a customer 's account for items that are properly payable according to the original tenor of the drawer 's order. SoFi has a clear regulatory obligation to reimburse my account for the unauthorized {$1000.00} debit and utilize the interbank adjustment process to claim the overpayment from the presenting bank. SoFi can not legally delegate this institutional responsibility to the consumer. A digital image of the cleared check, clearly displaying the authorized legal amount of {$1600.00}, is attached to this complaint.

I am filing this complaint against Sunrise Credit Services (XX/XX/XXXXXXXX ) for violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. Sunrise Credit Services appeared on my consumer credit report listing an alleged balance of {$390.00} ( Credit Report Grid Code : G ). After their initial phone contact, I sent Sunrise Credit Services a written debt validation letter formally disputing the debt and demanding verification of the alleged obligation pursuant to my rights under 15 U.S.C. 1692g. That letter demanded they cease all collection activity until the debt was properly validated. Despite receiving my written dispute and validation demand, Sunrise Credit Services continued collection activity including phone calls, without providing any validation of the alleged debt. They have not furnished : proof of an original signed agreement, a complete itemized accounting of the alleged balance, documentation of their legal standing and chain of ownership, or any other verification required to substantiate the alleged debt. This conduct constitutes the following violations : 1. Failure to cease collection activity after written dispute 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ). Once a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing that the debt is disputed, the collector must stop collection activity until it mails verification of the debt to the consumer. Sunrise Credit Services continued contact without providing any such verification. 2. Continued communication after dispute 15 U.S.C. 1692c. Their continued phone contact after receiving my written dispute constitutes unauthorized communication in violation of the FDCPA. 3. False or misleading representations 15 U.S.C. 1692e. By continuing to pursue collection of an unverified, disputed debt, Sunrise Credit Services has made implied misrepresentations about the character, amount, and legal status of the alleged debt. 4. Continued reporting of a disputed debt without notation 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ) and FCRA 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). Reporting a debt to consumer reporting agencies that is known to be disputed, without notating it as disputed, is a violation of both the FDCPA and the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

Consumer complaint narrative: I have decided to pursue this case because I believe this situation was not handled properly, and I want it reviewed fairly. When we received the laptop, the specifications did not match what had been advertised. We contacted XXXX and asked if they could offer a resolution. Since we did not want to lose the promotional offer, we preferred either receiving the correct specifications or receiving a partial refund. XXXX stated that they could not resolve the issue directly and advised us to open a case with Citi because the purchase was made with a Citi credit card. After back and forth between Citi, XXXX, and myself, it was decided that the laptop would be returned for a full refund. XXXX provided a return label, and we used that label to return the laptop. Later, the tracking number showed that the item had been delivered back to XXXX. After that, we contacted XXXX many times regarding the refund. Around this time, my online access became limited for reasons unknown to me. Out of all our attempts, five were successful : two phone calls and three online chats. Each time, XXXX either told us to wait because of processing delays and their XXXX migration, or they stated that the refund should have already been issued and that it was strange it had not been processed yet. Meanwhile, my interactions with Citi became increasingly difficult. The dispute was opened in XXXX. Later, when the dispute was changed from a partial dispute to a dispute for the full amount, Citi failed to properly update that detail. I called Citi twice and informed them of this issue, but it still was not corrected. Because Citi did not properly update the dispute amount, I was charged interest and a late fee. During one phone call, Citi admitted that this was incorrect and told me they would fix it. However, it was not fixed. When I called again in XXXX, I was told there was nothing more they could do, and Citi only refunded the late fee as a courtesy. This was very upsetting because the charges were connected to an issue that was already under dispute and that Citi had failed to update correctly. It felt extremely unfair to be charged interest and fees when I had already made repeated efforts to explain the situation and provide the required information. I have banked in the United States for years, and I have never experienced being asked to provide the same information so many times through so many different channels, including email, fax, mail, and online submissions. In addition to the faxes, mailed letters, and repeated submissions, I also emailed Citi six times regarding this matter. Consumer complaint narrative: I am requesting that the CFPB reopen and review my complaint regarding Cash App 's handling of unauthorized Bitcoin purchases that were processed through my account. On XX/XX/year>, multiple Bitcoin purchases were made through my Cash App account without my authorization. These transactions were entirely inconsistent with my account history, as I had no prior history of purchasing Bitcoin through Cash App. My concern is no longer limited to the unauthorized transactions themselves. It now includes Cash App 's refusal to meaningfully investigate the matter, its reliance on unsupported conclusions, and its refusal to consider significant new evidence that directly contradicts its findings. Cash App conducted an internal review and repeatedly concluded that the transactions were " authorized by you or someone you authorized to use your credentials '' and that " no error occurred. '' However, despite making this determination, Cash App has failed to provide any evidence supporting its conclusion. In its responses, Cash App specifically stated that it reviewed my account history before reaching its decision. If my account history was in fact reviewed, then Cash App would have seen that I had never previously purchased Bitcoin. Rather than explaining how transactions that were completely inconsistent with my account 's historical activity were determined to be authorized, Cash App simply repeated its conclusion without providing supporting facts. Throughout this process, I repeatedly asked Cash App to explain : What evidence was relied upon to determine the transactions were authorized. What specific information from my account history supported that conclusion. What fraud detection measures, alerts, or security reviews were triggered. Why transactions that were inconsistent with my normal account activity were not flagged as suspicious. How Cash App determined that no fraud or unauthorized access had occurred. To date, none of these questions have been answered. Instead, Cash App has continued to rely on unsupported conclusions while refusing to explain the basis for its findings. Simply stating that a transaction was authorized does not establish that it was authorized. Additionally, Cash App repeatedly shifted focus to a related XXXX transaction even though my primary concern has always been the unauthorized Bitcoin purchases that occurred through Cash App itself. My complaint is centered on Cash App 's failure to detect, prevent, or adequately investigate fraudulent activity occurring on its own platform. The most concerning issue is Cash App 's handling of new evidence that became available after its initial decision. Cash App appears to be relying on the fact that the Bitcoin purchases were made from an XXXX that had previously been associated with my account. However, I informed Cash App, including Cash App manager XXXX, that this device had been legally sold to XXXX and was no longer in my possession at the time the unauthorized transactions occurred. I have since filed a claim with XXXX regarding that device and will be providing the XXXX claim number and supporting documentation as part of this complaint. This evidence is directly relevant because it supports my position that the device used to access the account was no longer under my control. Despite being informed that the phone had been legally sold, despite being provided information regarding the XXXX claim, and despite being notified that a formal law enforcement investigation is underway, Cash App refused to conduct any further review. Instead, XXXX informed me that Cash App had already thoroughly investigated the matter and closed the case without addressing any of the new information after requesting new information to be added and investigated. The logic behind Cash App 's determination is deeply concerning. A device having once been associated with an account does not establish that future activity from that device is authorized. If a consumer legally sells a phone and the new possessor later accesses financial applications on that device and sends money to themselves or makes purchases, those transactions would not automatically become authorized simply because the device was once associated with the original owner. Ownership and possession matter. The critical question is who had control of the device and account at the time of the transactions. Rather than investigating whether unauthorized access occurred after the device left my possession, Cash App appears to have treated prior association with the device as proof of authorization. This conclusion ignores the evidence I provided and fails to address the possibility that the account was accessed by an unauthorized party. This matter is now the subject of a formal law enforcement investigation. I have been informed that records from Cash App and XXXX will be requested as part of that investigation. Law enforcement has advised me that the transactions are being treated as unauthorized and efforts are underway to recover the stolen funds. Despite this, Cash App has refused to explain the basis of its findings, provide supporting evidence, answer basic questions about its investigation, or reconsider its position in light of new evidence. I am requesting that the CFPB review Cash App 's handling of this matter, including : Whether Cash App conducted a reasonable investigation before denying my claim. Whether Cash App has documentation supporting its conclusion that the transactions were authorized. Whether Cash App adequately considered my account history and the unusual nature of the transactions. Whether Cash App properly considered evidence that the device used to conduct the transactions had been legally sold and was no longer in my possession. Whether Cash App complied with its obligations when investigating and responding to my dispute. Why Cash App refused to provide meaningful responses to the questions I repeatedly asked regarding its investigation and findings. I am attaching the document Cash App provided as the basis for its decision does not establish that I authorized these transactions. The document merely shows that a XXXX transaction occurred, that funds were used to purchase Bitcoin, and that the transactions were captured by the system. It does not identify who initiated the transactions, who had possession of the device at the time, what authentication methods were used, whether any fraud alerts were triggered, whether any unusual activity was detected, or what evidence Cash App relied upon to conclude that I authorized the activity. In fact, the documentation contains no analysis at all. It is simply a transaction summary. Cash App appears to be treating proof that the transactions occurred as proof that I authorized them, and those are two entirely different issues. The central question in this dispute is not whether the transactions took place, but whether they were authorized by me. The documentation provided by Cash App does not answer that question and does not address the evidence that the device associated with the transactions had been legally sold and was no longer in my possession at the time the Bitcoin purchases occurred. I am seeking recovery of my stolen funds and a full explanation of the evidence and reasoning Cash App relied upon when denying my claim. I will be providing additional supporting documentation, including the XXXX claim information and, correspondence with Cash App management.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of a fraudulent online transaction by both XXXX and Citibank and their subsequent failure to conduct a reasonable investigation despite being presented with evidence of fraud. I purchased XXXX watches from an online seller that had been recommended through XXXX 's platform. The seller represented that the items being sold were wristwatches. Upon discovering the fraud, I promptly notified both XXXX and Citibank and disputed the charges. I explained that this type of scheme is a well-documented fraud commonly employed by overseas scammers. The seller ships a low-value item with a valid tracking number in order to create the appearance of delivery, while never shipping the product actually purchased. Despite my explanation and despite the obvious discrepancy between the goods ordered and the goods received, both XXXX and Citibank declined my disputes. Their decisions appeared to rely solely on the existence of tracking numbers rather than any meaningful investigation into whether the merchandise delivered matched the merchandise purchased. Neither institution requested photographs of the items received, sought evidence regarding the nature of the shipment, nor appeared to undertake any substantive review of the facts presented. Instead, they simply concluded that because a package had been delivered, the transaction was valid. In my view, this falls far short of the reasonable investigative standards that consumers should expect from financial institutions entrusted with handling fraud claims. As a result of their refusal to adequately investigate the matter, I closed my Citibank account and blocked further use of my XXXX account. I have since been subjected to collection threats for charges arising from what I believe to be a clear case of merchandise fraud. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether XXXX and Citibank fulfilled their obligations under applicable consumer protection laws and regulations, including their duties to conduct reasonable investigations of disputed transactions and claims of fraud. I further request that the disputed charges be reviewed and that any collection efforts associated with these transactions be suspended pending a proper investigation. I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including transaction records, dispute correspondence, photographs of the items received, and any other evidence necessary to substantiate this complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sequium Asset Solutions is attempting to collect an alleged debt that I dispute because the obligation was previously satisfied with the alleged original creditor. By continuing to represent that this debt remains due and owing, Sequium Asset Solutions may be misrepresenting the legal status and validity of the alleged debt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), debt collectors are prohibited from using any false, deceptive, or misleading representations in connection with the collection of a debt, including misrepresenting the amount or legal status of an obligation. The purpose of this provision is to protect consumers from abusive and deceptive collection practices and to ensure that debt collection activities are conducted honestly and fairly. If a debt collector knowingly or negligently attempts to collect a debt that has already been satisfied, such conduct may constitute a violation of 1692e and may subject the debt collector to civil liability, including statutory damages, actual damages, and attorney 's fees as provided by law. I discovered that I was not provided with the validation notices and disclosures required under 15 U.S.C. 1692g, including information regarding my right to dispute the alleged debt and request verification of the debt. As a result, I was denied a meaningful opportunity to exercise my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) before the account was reported to consumer reporting agencies. Had I been properly notified, I would have timely disputed the alleged debt and requested validation, particularly because the alleged obligation had already been satisfied with the original creditor. Reporting the account to my credit report without first providing the required notice and opportunity to dispute deprived me of the procedural protections guaranteed by federal law and caused harm to my creditworthiness, reputation, and ability to obtain credit. The FDCPA requires debt collectors to provide consumers with clear notice of their rights so that inaccurate, invalid, or previously satisfied debts can be challenged before adverse collection and reporting actions occur. The failure to provide such notice undermines the purpose of 15 U.S.C. 1692g and may constitute a violation of the FDCPA. I request that Sequium Asset Solutions : 1. As a third party creditor, Please provide me with the contact information on who has firsthand knowledge of my personal business dealings with the alleged original creditor from Sequium Asset Solutions. 2. As a third party creditor, Please provide me with the contact information on who provided Sequium Asset Solutions with any of my private information. 3. As a third party creditor, please provide all the full GAAP accounting records from the inception of this alleged account you claim I owe Sequium Asset Solutions. 4. As a third party creditor, please provide me with the signed application between the alleged original creditor and myself. 5. As a third party creditor, please provide me with a signed contract with my signature with the alleged original creditor. 6. As a third party creditor, please provide me with the purchase agreement between Sequium Asset Solutions and the alleged original creditor with my name and alleged account information on it. 7. As a third party creditor, please verify whether payment was made to the alleged original creditor or Sequium Asset Solutions. Absent of all such evidence, I dispute the alleged debt in its entirety and request its immediate removal from all consumer reporting agencies. Cease and desist of all communications and collection efforts of any unverified alleged debts. Also, provide me a written confirmation of all the actions taken to resolve this matter.I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this complaint and require Sequium Asset Solutions to comply with all applicable consumer protection laws.

Consumer complaint narrative: YOUR COMPLAINT To Whom It May Concern : Pursuant to the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), 12 U.S.C. 2605, its implementing regulation, Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35, and applicable Colorado law including C.R.S. 38-38-103.1 and 38-38-104, I hereby submit this formal Notice of Error. I demand that you immediately cease all foreclosure-related activity and correct each of the violations described below. I. BACKGROUND AND PRIOR MODIFICATION VIOLATIONS This Notice arises in part from your servicer 's prior failure to properly implement and administer the previously approved loan modification on this account. A. VIOLATION OF PRIOR MODIFICATION PAYMENT SCHEDULE On or about XXXX XXXX XXXX, your servicer ( dba XXXX XXXX at the time ) approved a loan modification and issued a Trial Period Plan ( TPP ) for this account. Under applicable law and industry practice, the timing of the required trial payments is governed by when the approval notice was transmitted to the borrower : If sent on or before the XXXX of the month : The first trial payment is due on the first day of the following month. If sent after the XXXX of the month : The first trial payment is due on the first day of the month after the next, allowing the borrower a reasonable buffer period before payments begin. XXXX XXXX transmitted the trial period approval and payment schedule via U.S. Mail ( per the communication preferences established on the account ) on XX/XX/XXXX, stating the trial period payments were due on XX/XX/XXXX. It was also posted within the online portal on XX/XX/XXXX ( falsely stating the upload date was XX/XX/XXXX ) with an inexplicable back-date listed on the actual letter of XX/XX/XXXX. ( Refer to phone recordings documenting repeated attempts to obtain the modification approval in writing. These recordings occurred on XX/XX/XXXX, and XXXX, XXXX. ) This error was reported on multiple occasions, including via several requests to initiate a new application throughout XXXX and XXXX, without remedy. In fact, the servicer contact placed a note in the system stating : " Do not take ( legal Borrower name ) ' requests for a review of their modification start date. They are in foreclosure and may not open any applications for modification. '' All of this was also reported and tracked in real time via direct email correspondence with XXXX XXXX ( contact assigned to case : XXXX ). Despite this, your servicer demanded payment by XX/XX/XXXX, which was premature and inconsistent with the legally required payment schedule. As a direct result of your servicer 's improper administration of the prior modification not any failure on my part that modification was disrupted due to an accelerated timeline, and I was forced to submit the current loss mitigation application now pending before you. B. BACKDATING OF MODIFICATION COMMUNICATIONS I have further identified that your servicer backdated written communications relating to the trial modification approval and payment schedule. Specifically ( but not limited to ) : The letter or notice bearing a stated date of XX/XX/XXXX, was not actually sent, received, or made available to me until on or about XX/XX/XXXX. The backdating of these communications constitutes a separate and independent error and potential misrepresentation that directly harmed me and caused or contributed to the disruption of the prior modification. I retain all records, call recordings, and correspondence that evidence this backdating and reserve the right to present this evidence in any regulatory, administrative, or legal proceeding. This includes the well-documented correspondence and formal reports made to XXXX XXXX during this experience. II. CURRENT ERRORS ASSERTED ERROR NO. 1 FAILURE TO EVALUATE COMPLETE LOSS MITIGATION APPLICATION WITHIN 30 DAYS [ Federal Violation : 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( c ) ( 1 ) ] On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX formally opened a new loss mitigation application necessitated directly by your servicer 's improper administration of the prior modification presumably including all documents and information your servicer requested that were already on-file via the prior modification review. Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( c ) ( 1 ), you are required to evaluate a borrower 's complete application and provide written notice of all available loss mitigation options, including mortgage modification, within 30 days of receipt of a complete application. As of the date of this Notice, more than 47 days have elapsed since submission. You have failed to provide any written determination, approval, denial, or offer of any loss mitigation optionin violation of 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( c ) ( 1 ). You have authorized your law firm to reserve a XX/XX/XXXX Auction Sale date with the XXXX XXXX XXXX. ERROR NO. 2 PROHIBITED DUAL TRACKING [ Federal Violation : 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( g ) ] [ Colorado Violation : C.R.S. 38-38-103.1 ] While my complete loss mitigation application remains pending and without having issued a written denial and allowing the applicable appeal period to expire your servicer has : Scheduled and/or continued to pursue a foreclosure sale of the above-referenced property with an Auction date scheduled for XX/XX/XXXX via the XXXX Trustee Office ; AND Filed or continued foreclosure proceedings in direct violation of applicable law. This constitutes prohibited dual tracking under 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( g ), which expressly forbids a servicer from moving for a foreclosure judgment, order of sale, or conducting a foreclosure sale while a complete loss mitigation application is pending. Under Colorado law, C.R.S. 38-38-103.1, a lender or servicer pursuing foreclosure in Colorado is independently prohibited from dual tracking a borrower who has submitted a complete loss mitigation application. Colorado 's foreclosure process requires the servicer to pause foreclosure activity while a pending application is under review. Proceeding with a Rule 120 hearing or public trustee sale while a complete application is pending violates both federal Regulation X and Colorado 's independent statutory protections. XXXX XXXX also pursued a Rule 120 hearing in XX/XX/XXXX despite verbal communications informing me that the hearing was in violation of dual tracking and would not occur. This prevented me from presenting my case to the court, as I was told by XXXX XXXX the hearing would not proceed due to the pending underwriting approval for modification. Additionally, under C.R.S. 38-38-104, Colorado borrowers have the right to cure and to be treated fairly throughout the loss mitigation and foreclosure process. Your servicer 's conduct including the prior modification mismanagement, backdating of communications, continued foreclosure activity and pursuit of a Rule 120 hearing constitutes a pattern of conduct inconsistent with these rights. ERROR NO. 3 FAILURE TO ASSIGN AND MAINTAIN SINGLE POINT OF CONTACT [ Federal Violation : 12 C.F.R. 1024.40 ] [ Colorado Violation : C.R.S. 38-38-103.1 ] Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.40, a servicer is required to assign a Single Point of Contact ( SPOC ) to any borrower who is potentially eligible for loss mitigation. The assigned SPOC must : ( 1 ) be accessible via direct contact information ; ( 2 ) be capable of coordinating the receipt of all documents required for loss mitigation evaluation ; ( 3 ) inform the borrower of the status of any pending application ; and ( 4 ) refer the borrower to supervisory or managerial staff when appropriate. Under C.R.S. 38-38-103.1 ( 1 ) ( b ), Colorado independently requires that a servicer pursuing foreclosure provide a borrower with a dedicated contact throughout the process. Despite more than a dozen documented requests, I have never been permitted to speak with a consistent, accessible SPOC throughout this entire process. The individual identified as my assigned SPOC has changed no fewer than four times within a 30-day period. I have never spoken with any SPOC, notwithstanding that I have requested access to a SPOC during each and every call to XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX. The pattern of rotating personnel through a nominal SPOC designation without providing any meaningful or direct access constitutes a violation of the substance, and not merely the form, of 12 C.F.R. 1024.40. Whether intentional or a result of systemic failure, the practical effect is that I have been denied the protections this regulation was enacted to provide. III. DEMAND FOR IMMEDIATE CORRECTIVE ACTION Pursuant to 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( e ) and applicable Colorado law, I demand that you : 1. IMMEDIATELY HALT all foreclosure proceedings, including canceling the Rule 120 order and removing it from the public record, and canceling any public trustee foreclosure sale date ; 2. EVALUATE my complete loss mitigation application and provide written notice of all available options, including mortgage modification, within the timeframes required by 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ; 3. CONFIRM IN WRITING within 5 business days of receipt of this Notice that all foreclosure activity has been postponed or cancelled pending resolution of this Notice ; 4. PROVIDE A FULL WRITTEN EXPLANATION of the prior modification payment schedule, including the actual date of transmittal of the trial period approval notice and payment schedule, and acknowledge the error in the payment start date demanded ; 5. ACKNOWLEDGE AND CORRECT the backdating of communications identified above ; 6. COMPLETE YOUR INVESTIGATION and provide a full written response within 30 business days of receipt, as required by 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( e ) ( 1 ) ; and 7. IMMEDIATELY ASSIGN A NAMED SPOC with direct contact information, including a direct phone number and email address, and confirm that assignment in writing within 5 business days of receipt of this Notice. The assigned SPOC must be an identifiable individual not a team designation who has actual authority to access my file, provide real-time application status, and coordinate document review. You must further ensure that this individual remains accessible for the duration of the pending loss mitigation review, consistent with 12 C.F.R. 1024.40 and C.R.S. 38-38-103.1. XXXX XXXX ( 4th SPOC in 30 days ) has never been available and has never contacted me. IV. NOTICE OF LEGAL CONSEQUENCES Failure to comply with RESPA, Regulation X, and Colorado law may entitle me to pursue all available remedies, including : Actual damages caused by your errors, including costs incurred as a result of improper foreclosure activity and the loss of the prior modification ; Statutory damages of up to {$2000.00} per violation where part of a pattern or practice under 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( f ) ; Attorney 's fees and litigation costs ; Remedies available under Colorado law for violations of C.R.S. 38-38-103.1 and 38-38-104, including damages arising from the failure to provide and maintain a genuine Single Point of Contact during active loss mitigation review as required by 12 C.F.R. 1024.40 ; and Emergency injunctive relief in Colorado district court to stop any scheduled public trustee sale. I expressly reserve all rights and remedies under federal and Colorado state law and intend to pursue each and every remedy available if these errors are not promptly corrected. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding Current 's assessment of a {$10.00} Account Closure Fee and its withholding of my remaining account funds. I maintained a Current account that was used normally, including occasional direct deposits. I never received notice of any suspicious, unauthorized, or prohibited activity on the accoun t. After the account was closed, I contacted Current regarding the approximately {$200.00} that remained in the account. Current then informed me for the first time that it intended to deduct a {$10.00} fee before returning my funds, stating : " There is an account closure fee of {$10.00} applied, which is why the balance is {$10.00} less than what you anticipated. '' I did not request that my account be closed. The closure was initiated solely by Current. I reviewed the Current Account Agreement and found that the section discussing account closure refers to situations where the customer elects to close the account. Specifically, the agreement states : " If you elect to close your Account ... '' However, Current has not identified any provision clearly stating that the {$10.00} Account Closure Fee applies when Current unilaterally terminates an account following an internal review. I have repeatedly asked Current to identify the specific contractual basis for charging this fee under these circumstances. Current has not provided a satisfactory explanation and has simply continued to insist that the fee applies. Furthermore, I am aware of another customer who experienced a substantially similar situation. That customer was also asked to submit identity verification documents, subsequently had the account closed by Current, and received the full remaining account balance without any Account Closure Fee being deducted. Current has not explained why the fee was assessed in my case but not in that similar account closure. I respectfully request that Current : Return the full remaining balance in my account without deducting the {$10.00} Account Closure Fee ; Identify the specific provision of the Account Agreement that authorizes charging this fee when Current, rather than the customer, initiates the account closure ; Explain why similarly situated customers appear to have been treated differently with respect to this fee ; and Release my funds without requiring me to accept a deduction that has not been adequately justified. Consumer complaint narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint Company : Wells Fargo Bank Related Claim ID : XXXX Related Executive Escalation Reference : XXXX Related CFPB Complaint Reference : XXXX Complaint Category : Investigation Process / Complaint Handling / Inconsistent Findings Complaint Narrative : This complaint concerns Wells Fargo 's handling of the investigation process itself and the changing factual basis used to support denial of my fraud claim. My original complaint involved unauthorized debit-card transactions totaling approximately {$15000.00} including resulting fees. However, the focus of this complaint is not simply the denial of reimbursement. Rather, it concerns the consistency, accuracy, and reliability of the investigative process utilized to reach that determination. Throughout the handling of the matter, Wells Fargo systems and representatives reflected materially different transaction counts and records. During the course of the investigation, I was presented with approximately 27 transactions, 30 transactions, 35 transactions, and ultimately 39 disputed transactions identified through reconciliation efforts. Because the underlying disputed transaction records changed depending on the representative, department, or system being reviewed, I became concerned regarding the reliability of the data used to support the investigative conclusions. Additionally, Wells Fargo 's written denial specifically stated : " The shipping address provided to the merchant for the disputed transaction ( s ) matches your address on file. '' When I challenged that statement, I explained that the address maintained on file with Wells Fargo was my mother 's residence and that I do not routinely receive packages or merchandise shipments at that address and have not done so for years. Following that challenge, the explanation provided by Wells Fargo changed from shipping address matching to billing address matching. These are materially different facts. A shipping address concerns where merchandise is delivered. A billing address concerns payment verification. As a result, I am unable to determine which factual basis was actually relied upon during the investigation. I also received an executive-level review following my original CFPB complaint. During those discussions, I was advised that the claim had been denied. However, after being informed of the denial, I was then asked multiple additional investigative questions regarding possession of the card, possession of the PIN, access to the account, and related issues. This created additional confusion because it is unclear why substantive investigative questions were still being asked if the determination had already been finalized. Conversely, if the investigation remained ongoing, it is unclear how the matter could already be considered closed. Another concern involves the investigative factors relied upon to support denial. Wells Fargo repeatedly referenced factors including : Continued possession of the physical card ; Continued possession of the PIN ; Geographic similarity ; Merchant similarity ; Digital-card activity ; and Android-device activity. However, the matter also involved a documented impersonation event in which an individual posing as a Wells Fargo representative possessed substantial account-specific information, including personal identifying information and card-related information. During that impersonation event, I was advised that an alleged unauthorized user had been added to the account and was associated with a telephone number utilizing the same XXXX area code as my own number. This raises concerns regarding the degree of weight placed upon geographic-pattern analysis and other account-association indicators when evaluating sophisticated account-compromise scenarios. Additionally, Wells Fargo has repeatedly referenced digital-card and Android-device activity as a basis supporting denial. However, I have not been provided documentation explaining how Wells Fargo determined that the device involved belonged to me rather than an unauthorized actor possessing compromised account information. My concern is that several factors cited in support of denial appear to demonstrate association with an account rather than authorization by the account holder. I am requesting review of Wells Fargo 's investigative and complaint-handling process, including : inconsistent transaction records; changing factual explanations ; conflicting shipping-address and billing-address rationales ; post-denial investigative activity ; the factual basis supporting device attribution conclusions ; and whether the investigative methodology utilized was sufficiently reliable and internally consistent under the circumstances presented. Requested Resolution : I request an independent review of Wells Fargo 's investigative process, the factual basis relied upon in support of denial, and the consistency of the records and explanations provided throughout the handling of this matter. I also request that Wells Fargo be required to clearly identify the specific evidence relied upon to support its conclusions and address the inconsistencies outlined above.

I am filing this complaint regarding Capital Ones handling of my dispute involving a {$55000.00} charge to XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>. I hired XXXX XXXX for a commercial tenant improvement project for XXXX XXXX XXXX. The contractor received three payments totaling {$68000.00}. I am not disputing all of those payments. I specifically excluded the {$4100.00} payment because I acknowledge that some limited preliminary work was completed. My dispute relates only to the XX/XX/year> payments totaling {$64000.00}, including the {$55000.00} charge processed through Capital One. Before I signed the contract, XXXX represented that the project would be completed around XXXX XXXX. I relied on that representation when authorizing payment and moving forward with the project. By XXXX XXXX, the project was nowhere near completion. The work remained limited to early-stage demolition and partial framing while substantial portions of the contracted scope remained unfinished. Major contract items including plumbing rough-in, electrical rough-in, concrete and footings, drywall, doors, trim, paint, and completed usable suites were not delivered as represented. Throughout the project, I repeatedly requested updates, accounting of funds paid, project status information, and an orderly transition when it became clear the project would not be completed as promised. I requested itemized accounting so that payments could be reconciled against completed work. The requested accounting was never provided. I remained willing to resolve the matter professionally and communicated that position in writing. Instead of providing the requested accounting and continuing toward resolution, the contractor stopped work and treated my request as a breach. I was ultimately forced to retain a replacement contractor and incur additional costs to complete substantial unfinished portions of the project. I submitted extensive documentation to Capital One, including payment records, project communications, permit records, photographs, requests for accounting, proof of my efforts to resolve the dispute directly with the contractor, and multiple supplemental dispute letters. I also submitted additional information after Capital Ones initial denial. When I contacted Capital One for clarification, I received differing explanations regarding the denial. I was advised that additional information was needed and that proof of a refund or confirmation from the merchant was required. I could not provide such proof because the merchant disputed my position, never agreed to issue a refund, never issued a refund confirmation, and never provided the requested accounting. Requiring documentation from the merchant who was the subject of the dispute effectively made it impossible to satisfy Capital Ones request. Capital One ultimately denied the dispute and stated only that the information provided was insufficient to validate my claim. The denial letter did not clearly identify what information was missing, did not explain why the extensive documentation submitted was inadequate, and did not explain how Capital One evaluated the evidence demonstrating substantial non-performance of the contracted services. My dispute was never based on a claim that no work occurred. In fact, I specifically acknowledged that some work was performed and intentionally excluded one payment from the dispute. My dispute was based on the contractors failure to complete the contracted services as represented and failure to deliver the scope of work for which payment was made. I am also concerned that the explanation provided by Capital One representatives appears inconsistent with Capital Ones published dispute guidance. Capital Ones public dispute information states that disputes may be filed when a customer paid for a service and did not receive it, only received part of it, or when the service was not delivered as described. My dispute falls squarely within those categories. I never claimed that no work occurred. Rather, I claimed that I only received a limited portion of the contracted services and that the services delivered were not completed as represented. Additionally, Capital Ones published guidance identifies contracts, invoices, photographs, and communications with the merchant as relevant supporting documentation for dispute investigations. I submitted those categories of evidence. Despite doing so, Capital One did not explain why the evidence was insufficient, what additional information was required, or how its denial was consistent with its own published dispute standards. Based on the facts above, I believe Capital One failed to conduct a reasonable investigation, failed to provide a meaningful explanation for its denial, and failed to fairly evaluate the evidence demonstrating substantial non-performance of contracted services. I am requesting that Capital One conduct a full and independent review of the dispute, explain the specific basis for its denial, review all documentation previously submitted, explain how its decision is consistent with its published dispute guidance, and reconsider the dispute based on the evidence demonstrating that the contracted services were not completed as represented.

I also called Robinhood multiple times to report the incident and seek assistance. Rather than treating the unknown device and unauthorized activity as evidence of a compromised account, I was initially told that the activity appeared legitimate because my IP address may have been associated with the login. Despite this, I was told that I would receive follow-up calls regarding my case, yet those promised callbacks never occurred. I do not know the exact technical method used to gain access to my account. However, the facts are clear : an unknown device accessed my account, transactions were conducted that were entirely inconsistent with my history, and approximately {$45000.00} of my funds were placed into prediction market positions without my authorization. These events strongly indicate that my account was compromised by someone other than me. The financial and emotional impact of this incident has been significant. Losing access to approximately {$45000.00} and then struggling to obtain timely and meaningful assistance has been extremely distressing. I trusted Robinhood to safeguard my account and to respond appropriately when suspicious activity was reported. Instead, I have been left seeking answers while a substantial amount of my money remains at issue. I respectfully request that Robinhood : 1. Conduct a full investigation into the unauthorized access and transactions. 2. Provide all records relating to account logins, devices, authentication events, security alerts, and a ccount activity associated with this incident. 3. Explain why access from an unfamiliar device located in XXXX, XXXX XXXX, was not treated as evidence of potential account compromise. 4. Explain why my account was unfrozen after I reported unauthorized access and before the matter was fully resolved. 5. Reimburse all losses resulting from the unauthorized transactions. Requested Resolution : Reimbursement of approximately {$45000.00} in unauthorized losses, a complete investigation into the account compromise, and full disclosure of the information XXXX relied upon in determining that the activity was legitimate despite the presence of an unknown device and transactions that were inconsistent with my account history.

Before releasing the item that was being sold, I contacted Citibank on XX/XX/year>, to verify that the payment had been received. Citibank confirmed the payment. I contacted Citibank a second time on XX/XX/year>, the day the embroidery machine was delivered to the buyer, and Citibank again confirmed that the payment had been received. Based on these confirmations, I released my embroidery machine ( XXXX XXXX, Serial Number XXXX ) to the buyer. I later learned that the payment was reversed on XX/XX/year>. However, Citibank never notified me that the payment had been reversed. I did not receive any alert, email, letter, phone call, or other communication informing me that the payment had been canceled. On XX/XX/year>, when I contacted Citibank to pay the remaining balance on my loan, I discovered for the first time that the {$12000.00} payment had been reversed. This was XXXX days after the reversal occurred and XXXX days after I had delivered the machine based on Citibanks payment confirmations. As a result, I suffered a financial loss of {$12000.00}. Subsequently, law enforcement investigated the matter and determined that the payment was connected to identity theft. The owner of the account used for the payment was a victim of identity theft from New Mexico. Law enforcement informed me that this victim has also been connected to similar fraudulent activity affecting other states and that the suspect appears to be involved in a broader pattern of fraud. My concern is not only the fraud committed by the suspect, but also Citibanks failure to notify me when the payment was reversed. Had I been notified promptly on or shortly after XX/XX/year>, I could have taken immediate action to attempt recovery of the machine and protect myself from further loss. I submitted a formal written complaint to Citibank by certified mail. The bank received my correspondence, but I have not received a satisfactory response regarding : * Why I was not notified when the payment was reversed. * What policies governed the handling of this transaction. * Whether Citibank reviewed the circumstances surrounding the reversal. * What steps, if any, were taken to protect me as the account holder. I respectfully request that Citibank provide a complete written explanation regarding the reversal of the payment, the lack of notification, and the banks handling of this matter. I also request that Citibank review whether its actions or omissions contributed to my financial loss. Thank you for your assistance.

Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/year>, U.S. Bank closed my checking and savings accounts. I explained that these funds were sent by my father, who is my financial sponsor, through a money exchange broker. The funds were intended for my tuition and living expenses in the United States. During the call, I was informed that these funds should have been sent by wire transfer rather than through XXXX. I explained that we had already instructed the broker to stop using XXXX, but several payments had been scheduled in advance and were already outside the brokers control. However, after waiting several weeks, I contacted XXXX and learned that the check had not yet been issued. I was then told that it could take up to an additional 40 days. Later, on XX/XX/year>, XXXX informed me that out of approximately {$20000.00} that had been in my accounts, only about {$11000.00} would be returned to me and that the remaining funds had allegedly been returned to the senders. I requested documentation identifying which transactions had been returned, the amounts involved, the dates of the returns, and the recipients of those returned funds. This information is necessary for me to reconcile my records and communicate with the broker and the original senders. XXXX and U.S. Bank refused to provide this information. As a result, I currently do not know exactly which funds were returned, when they were returned, to whom they were returned, or whether all of the funds were properly accounted for. The amounts provided to me do not clearly reconcile with the account balance that existed before the account closure. In addition, I received inconsistent and conflicting information from different U.S. Bank representatives and branch employees. On XX/XX/year>, XXXX directed me to the XXXX branch to obtain my {$11000.00} cashiers check after I requested to receive it in person rather than by mail. However, when I arrived, the branch manager informed me that no arrangements had been made regarding my visit and provided a different explanation regarding the status of my funds. I was told that the funds were being held in case there were any outstanding debts or obligations associated with the account. Later, XXXX, the branch manager at the XXXX XXXX branch, also informed me that the funds were being held. However, XXXX had previously stated that the remaining funds had already been returned to the senders. Therefore, I received conflicting information regarding whether the funds had been returned or were still being held by the bank. At the XXXX XXXX branch, I provided supporting documentation, including XXXX transaction records, proof of my fathers financial sponsorship, and tuition-related documents demonstrating the legitimate source and purpose of the funds. I also provided copies of the XXXX receipts by email to both XXXX and XXXX. Despite providing this documentation, I still have not received a clear explanation regarding why my accounts were closed, what happened to the funds that were removed from my accounts, or why I am being denied access to transaction information related to those funds. I am also concerned that my accounts appear to have been flagged for fraud despite the legitimate source of the funds and the supporting documentation I provided. I have never been presented with any evidence that fraud occurred. As an international dentist pursuing advanced professional training in the United States, I am concerned that this designation may negatively affect my ability to open bank accounts in the future and may harm my professional reputation. I respectfully request that U.S. Bank : XXXX. Provide a complete written explanation for the closure of my accounts. XXXX. Provide a detailed accounting of all funds removed from my accounts, including the amounts, dates, and destinations of any returned transactions. XXXX. Identify which specific transactions were returned and provide documentation supporting those returns. XXXX. Confirm the status and disposition of all funds that were held in my accounts at the time of closure. XXXX. Provide copies of any records or documentation supporting the banks actions. XXXX Review the conduct and communications of the representatives involved, as I received inconsistent information throughout this process. I have spent significant time attempting to resolve this matter and continue to face uncertainty regarding the location and disposition of my funds. I have attached the cashiers check that was ultimately provided to me, my final account statement, my tuition documentation, and copies of the XXXX receipts. My final statement does not identify the specific transactions that were allegedly returned, which is one of the primary reasons for this complaint.

I am asking the CFPB to compel Wells Fargo to conduct a proper fraud investigation and reimburse me for my total loss of {$1900.00}.

A reasonable investigation would have recognized the correct dispute category as Services Not Provided and given proper weight to the merchants written admission. Credit Karma Money has failed to process the chargeback for the {$1000.00} flight purchase under the applicable XXXX reason codes despite the carriers documented system failure and the DOTs mandatory refund requirements. Under California's Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (Cal. Civ. Code 1788 et seq.) and the Fair Debt Buying Practices Act, debt buyers and collection agencies are legally required to document settlements and provide receipts or statements upon receiving payments. [1]
The specific requirements include:
 Settlement Agreements: All settlement agreements must be reduced to writing, and the collector must ensure a copy of this written agreement is provided to you. [1]Receipts for Payments: For any payment received on a debt, the collector must provide a receipt or statement to the debtor within 30 calendar days. [1]Final Settlement Receipt: If a payment is accepted as payment-in-full or as a final compromise, the collector must provide a final statement that clearly indicates this within 30 calendar days. [1]Mandatory Information: The receipt or statement must explicitly display the amount and date paid, the name of the entity paid, the current account number, the original charge-off creditor, the original account number, and any remaining balance owing. Consumer complaint narrative: FROM : XXXX XXXX XXXX, FL XXXX TO : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau | XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, IA XXXX DATE : XX/XX/XXXX RE : Formal Complaint Against NCB Management Services , Inc. for Violations of the FDCPA and FCRA ACCOUNT NO. XXXX XXXXXXXX I. INTRODUCTION AND STANDING I, XXXX, a consumer and resident of XXXX, Florida XXXX, hereby submit this formal written complaint against NCB Management Services , Inc. ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA XXXX ) for violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., concerning account number XXXX. I submit this complaint in my capacity as a federally protected consumer and respectfully request the full investigatory authority and remedial powers of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau be exercised in this matter. II. BACKGROUND AND FACTUAL BASIS OF DISPUTE On or about XX/XX/XXXX, the Respondent NCB Management Services , Inc. began reporting a debt to one or more consumer reporting agencies and/or attempted to collect an alleged debt that I expressly dispute as inaccurate, unverifiable, and/or not legally owed. Upon becoming aware of this collection activity and adverse reporting, I exercised my statutory rights by submitting a formal written request for debt validation on XX/XX/XXXX, via certified mail, with return receipt requested, directed to NCB Management Services , Inc. at its place of business. The Respondent failed to provide adequate validation of the alleged debt as required under 15 U.S.C. 1692g of the FDCPA. No documentation establishing the nature, amount, or legal basis of the alleged debt was provided within the applicable statutory period. Despite the absence of adequate validation and despite my express written dispute, the Respondent continued its collection and/or reporting activity. III. VIOLATIONS OF THE FAIR DEBT COLLECTION PRACTICES ACT ( FDCPA ) The Respondent 's conduct constitutes one or more violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. Specifically, the Respondent has engaged in the following unlawful acts and omissions : 1. Failure to Provide Debt Validation 15 U.S.C. 1692g : The Respondent failed to provide adequate written verification of the alleged debt within thirty ( 30 ) days of receiving my timely and properly submitted validation request dated XX/XX/XXXX. No documentation was furnished sufficient to establish the amount, origin, chain of ownership, or legal enforceability of the alleged debt associated with account XXXX. 2. Continued Collection Activity After Receipt of Validation Request 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) : Following receipt of my written dispute and validation request, the Respondent continued or failed to cease collection activity, including but not limited to continued adverse credit reporting. Such conduct is expressly prohibited under the FDCPA pending the provision of adequate debt validation. 3. Failure to Report Account as Disputed 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ) : The Respondent failed to communicate to the consumer reporting agencies that account XXXX was disputed by the consumer, or continued to report the alleged debt without disclosing the existence of my valid dispute. Reporting a debt while failing to note the consumer 's dispute constitutes a false, deceptive, or misleading representation in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 8 ). 4. False, Deceptive, or Misleading Representations 15 U.S.C. 1692e : The Respondent used, or is believed to have used, false, deceptive, or misleading representations or means in connection with the collection of the alleged debt associated with account XXXX, in violation of the general prohibition set forth at 15 U.S.C. 1692e. This includes, but is not limited to, misrepresenting the character, amount, or legal status of the alleged debt. IV. VIOLATIONS OF THE FAIR CREDIT REPORTING ACT ( FCRA ) In addition to the foregoing FDCPA violations, the Respondent has violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., in its capacity as a furnisher of information to consumer reporting agencies. Specifically : 5. Furnishing Inaccurate Information FCRA 623 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) : The Respondent is furnishing or has furnished information regarding account xxxx1738 to one or more consumer reporting agencies that is inaccurate and/or can not be verified. As a furnisher of information, the Respondent bears an affirmative duty under FCRA 623 to report only accurate information and to promptly update or correct any information it knows or should know to be inaccurate. 6. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation FCRA 623 ( b ) : Upon receiving notice of my dispute whether directly or through a consumer reporting agency the Respondent failed to conduct a reasonable investigation into the accuracy of the reported information, in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). 7. Failure to Correct or Delete Inaccurate Information FCRA 623 ( b ) ( 1 ) ( E ) : Having received notice of my dispute, the Respondent has failed to correct, update, or arrange for the deletion of the inaccurate or unverifiable information associated with account XXXX from the relevant consumer reporting agency files, as required by law. V. RELIEF REQUESTED In light of the foregoing violations of federal consumer protection law, I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau take all appropriate action within its authority, including but not limited to the following specific relief : 8. Investigation : Conduct a full and thorough investigation into the Respondent 's conduct with respect to account XXXX and its compliance with the FDCPA and FCRA as described herein. 9. Deletion of Tradeline : Order NCB Management Services , Inc. to immediately and permanently delete the disputed tradeline associated with account XXXX from all consumer reporting agencies, including but not limited to XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. 10. Cessation of Collection Activity : Order the Respondent to immediately cease all collection activity with respect to the alleged debt associated with account XXXX, including any direct or indirect contact, reporting, or referral to third parties. 11. Penalties and Remedies : Assess any and all appropriate civil penalties, fines, or remedies authorized by applicable law, including supervisory or enforcement actions consistent with the CFPB 's authority under the Consumer Financial Protection Act of XXXX ( 12 U.S.C. 5481 et seq. ). 12. Public Complaint Record : Maintain this formal complaint in the CFPB 's public Consumer Complaint Database as a matter of public record, and forward a copy to all relevant federal regulatory agencies as appropriate. VI. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND CLOSING STATEMENT Supporting documentation, including certified mail receipts evidencing the timely submission of my validation request dated XX/XX/XXXX, prior written correspondence with NCB Management Services , Inc., applicable credit report excerpts reflecting the disputed tradeline for account XXXX, and any other relevant records, is attached to this complaint and is available in full upon the CFPB 's request. I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the foregoing is true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief. I am a consumer protected under the FDCPA and FCRA, and I have a good-faith basis for each allegation set forth herein. I respectfully urge the Bureau to exercise the full extent of its investigatory and enforcement authority in this matter, and I stand ready to cooperate fully with any inquiry, provide additional documentation, or respond to any requests for information. Respectfully submitted, XXXX XXXX, FL XXXX Date : XX/XX/XXXX Letter 2 of 3 | NCB Management Services , Inc. Account XXXX | XXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX | CONFIDENTIAL

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint because Cash App has effectively prohibited me from using its services and has refused to provide a meaningful explanation or resolution. On XX/XX/year>, my Cash App account was banned. Shortly thereafter, I received communication from Cash App indicating that the restriction was related to activity associated with my former sponsors account. Several years ago, my Cash App account was connected to a sponsor account because I was a minor. However, I am now XXXX XXXX XXXX and have not been connected to that sponsor account for more than two years. I understand that Cash App may have had legitimate reasons to take action against my former sponsors account. However, I do not believe it is fair or reasonable to indefinitely restrict my Social Security Number and device from accessing Cash App based on activity attributed to another individual. Any issues between Cash App and my former sponsor should not permanently prevent me, as an independent adult, from creating and maintaining my own account. After my account was banned, I submitted an appeal in an effort to resolve the matter. On XX/XX/year>, Cash App denied my appeal. The denial did not provide a meaningful explanation of what I personally did wrong, what specific policy I violated, or why I was being prevented from creating a new account independently. Following the appeal denial, I contacted Cash App customer support on multiple occasions. During these conversations, I explained that I was no longer connected to the sponsor account and that I was willing to create an entirely new Cash App account using my own information and a different email address. During one of these conversations, a Cash App representative suggested that creating a new account with a different email address would be a good option to try. However, when I attempted to create a new account, I discovered that my device had also been blocked. I contacted Cash App again and requested assistance with removing the device restriction or otherwise allowing me to create a new account. On XX/XX/year>, I was informed by phone that because my appeal had been denied, there was nothing further that customer support could do. No additional explanation, review process, or path to resolution was offered. I have made multiple good-faith attempts to resolve this issue directly with Cash App. I have requested clarification regarding the reason for the restrictions, sought assistance from customer support, and submitted an appeal through the process provided by the company. Despite these efforts, Cash App has not provided a meaningful explanation regarding why my Social Security Number and device remain blocked, nor have they explained why restrictions associated with a former sponsor account should continue to affect me years after that relationship ended. I am willing to comply with any identity verification requirements, account review procedures, or reasonable requests necessary to demonstrate that I am an independent adult user who is no longer associated with the sponsor account in question. Cash App is an important financial tool that I used for legitimate purposes, including receiving payments related to my work as a server, sending money to family members, and providing financial support to family members when needed. Being unable to access the platform has caused inconvenience and has limited my access to a commonly used financial service. I have documentation from Cash App indicating that the restriction on my account was related to activity associated with my former sponsors account. I also have documentation showing that my appeal was denied. I am providing these documents in support of my complaint. My concern is that Cash App appears to be holding me responsible for actions allegedly connected to another individual, despite the fact that I have not been connected to that sponsor account for more than two years and am now an independent adult. While Cash App may have had valid reasons to take action against the sponsor account, I do not believe it is reasonable to indefinitely prevent me from creating and using my own account based on another persons actions. I believe Cash Apps actions are unfair because I am being denied access to the service without a clear explanation and appear to be suffering ongoing consequences for issues that Cash App itself identified as being related to my former sponsors account rather than my own conduct.
