On XX/XX/XXXX I filed CFPB complaint XXXX against Security Credit Services LLC demanding five validation documents under FDCPA Section 1692g ( b ) for a reported {$850.00} collection ( their account XXXX, contract XXXX ). On XX/XX/XXXX Security Credit Services responded " Closed with explanation '' and produced ( a ) a XXXX merchandise lease agreement signed XX/XX/XXXX and ( b ) a XXXX XXXX XXXX servicing printout dated XX/XX/XXXX. This complaint documents what that production proves and what it fatally omits. FIRST FACTUAL DEFECT, THE CHAIN OF TITLE THEY ADMITTED IS BROKEN : Security Credit Services produced no executed assignment of any kind. The only assignment instrument in its production, the Negotiation and Assignment block on page 8 of the lease, is blank. It is unsigned by the lessor, undated, and no recourse election is marked. Worse, its response letter dated XX/XX/XXXX, signed by Support Supervisor XXXX XXXX, states that Security Credit Services " purchased the account from XXXX XXXX, XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. '' XXXX XXXX, XXXX appears nowhere in the documents it produced. The lease names XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX as the contemplated assignee. No document evidences any transfer from XXXX to XXXX XXXX, from XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX, or from XXXX XXXX XXXX Security Credit Services. The furnisher 's own narrative now requires a four-entity chain ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Security Credit Services ) for which it has produced XXXX executed links, and the third entity in that chain was never disclosed until this response. A debt collector that can not document its own ownership of an account can not validate it under Section 1692g ( b ), can not truthfully represent its right to collect it under Section 1692e, and can not certify the accuracy of the tradeline it furnishes under FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ). RELATED DEFECT, THREE DIFFERENT ORIGINAL CREDITORS : The same response identifies the original creditor three different ways. Its XXXX tradeline reports Original Creditor Name as " No Info. '' The Re : line of its XX/XX/XXXX letter states " Original Creditor : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. '' The body of the same letter states the account " was originally opened with XXXX '' One furnisher, one response, three contradictory identifications of the most basic fact about the account. At least two of the three are false representations under Section 1692e, and the " No Info '' field remains a facial Section 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) accuracy violation. SECOND FACTUAL DEFECT, THE AMOUNT : The {$850.00} it reports is wrong on the face of its own production. Its XX/XX/XXXX letter describes the figure as a " principal balance of {$850.00}. '' That characterization is false by the letter 's own next sentence, which states " the total cost of the lease was in the amount of {$820.00} for 12 payments of {$67.00} with a residual payment of {$47.00}. '' The lease 's capitalized cost, the only figure that could be called principal, is {$310.00}. The {$850.00} figure is the full-term lease total INCLUDING the {$47.00} end-of-lease residual purchase option, the price of an ownership option that was never exercised on a lease that defaulted in its first month ( first payment XXXX XX/XX/XXXX per the XXXX XXXX ). The lease 's own Section 8 early-termination clause requires a lesser-of calculation that was never performed, and the agreement states three different full-term totals across its own pages ( {$800.00}, {$820.00}, and {$850.00} ). Representing {$850.00} as " principal '' and furnishing it as the balance is a false representation of the character and amount of a debt under FDCPA Section 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) and an inaccurate balance under FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 5 ). THIRD FACTUAL DEFECT, THE SERVICER 'S OWN LEDGER : The XXXX XXXX printout Security Credit Services chose to produce shows the account was written off XX/XX/XXXX as XXXX XXXX XXXX - XXXX '' with Times Over 30, Over 60, and Over 90 each recorded as XXXX. Their own evidence contradicts the derogatory severity being furnished. FOURTH FACTUAL DEFECT, STILL UNCURED : The XXXX tradeline continues to report Original Creditor Name as " No Info '' even though Security Credit Services ' own production identifies the originator ( XXXX ) and the named assignee ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ). The furnisher demonstrably possesses the original-creditor information and furnishes a blank field anyway. That is a facial Section 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) accuracy violation independent of validation. FIFTH ISSUE, DATE AUDIT : The XXXX XXXX establishes first delinquency on or about XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX ( first payment XXXX ). The bureaus show this collection " opened XX/XX/XXXX. '' I demand written confirmation of the date of first delinquency being furnished to each bureau under FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 5 ), to confirm the obsolescence clock under Section 605 runs from the true XXXX delinquency and has not been re-aged. SIXTH ISSUE, MISSTATEMENT OF MY RIGHTS : The letter 's " Continued reporting '' paragraph states the FCRA allows reporting " for 7 years from the date the account is charged to profit and loss, or upon the expiration of the 180-day period beginning on the date of the delinquency leading to charge off, whichever is earlier. '' That is not the law. FCRA Section 605 ( c ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( c ) ) runs the 7-year period from 180 days after the commencement of the delinquency that preceded the charge-off, here on or about XX/XX/XXXX, not from the charge-off date, and there is no " whichever is earlier '' election. A debt collector sending a consumer a garbled misstatement of the governing reporting period is a false or misleading representation under FDCPA Section 1692e ( 10 ), and it matters here because anchoring the clock to the XX/XX/XXXX charge-off instead of the XX/XX/XXXX delinquency would unlawfully extend the reporting period by months. SEVENTH ISSUE, THE REFUSALS : The XX/XX/XXXX letter refuses outright to document either ownership or licensure. On licensure it states Security Credit Services " has no obligation to provide you with proof of licensing. '' On chain of title it states " there is no basis in law to substantiate your right to such information, '' citing XXXX v. XXXX, a XXXX XXXX XXXX decision. That authority is not binding in the XXXX XXXX, predates Regulation F ( 12 CFR Part 1006 ), and says nothing about the furnisher investigation duty under FCRA Section 1681s-2 ( b ). Whatever the outer limits of Section 1692g validation, a furnisher responding to a dispute about WHO OWNS the account can not refuse to examine its own acquisition documents. Its licensure is separately before the Florida Office of Financial Regulation under Fla. Stat. 559.553, where " we deny the allegation '' is not proof. The investigation duty here is not abstract. Under binding XXXX Circuit precedent, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ), the Section 1681s-2 ( b ) reasonable-investigation duty squarely covers objectively and readily verifiable facts : whether an executed assignment to Security Credit Services exists , what the contract 's own termination formula yields, and who the original creditor is. Every one of those is answerable from documents Security Credit Services itself selected and produced. FLORIDA STATE LAW : Collecting and furnishing an amount the collector 's own contract does not support, while asserting ownership it can not document, is an attempt to enforce a debt when the collector knows the right being asserted does not exist in the manner claimed, in violation of the Florida Consumer Collection Practices Act, Fla. Stat. 559.72 ( 9 ). Each federal violation above additionally serves as a per se predicate under the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, Fla. Stat. 501.201 et seq. Security Credit Services ' Florida licensure posture is separately before the Florida Office of Financial Regulation under Fla. Stat. 559.553. CONCRETE HARM : This unvalidated and inaccurately stated {$850.00} tradeline is published on my XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX files to every third party that pulls my consumer file in the ordinary course of underwriting, and it has materially depressed my credit standing and the terms available to me. This is a published false representation of my creditworthiness, the concrete reputational and financial injury recognized in this Circuit, not a procedural grievance. Damages : The continued furnishing of an unowned, misstated {$850.00} collection constitutes continuing actual damages within FCRA Sections 616 and 617 for as long as it remains on my files. Feedback-option preservation : If this complaint is closed as " verified, '' " validated, '' " duplicate, '' or any procedural deflection without the executed assignment instruments demanded above, I will treat the closure itself as a Section 1692g ( b ) and Section 623 ( b ) violation and file again. Anti-deflection clause : A second production that omits the executed XXXXXXXX assignment will result in ( a ) supplemental filings with the Florida Office of Financial Regulation ( complaint XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX licensure ) and the Florida Attorney General ( Fla. Stat. 501.201, with these federal violations as FDUTPA predicates ), each updated with the XX/XX/XXXX non-response as evidence, and ( b ) preservation of all of the above for any private enforcement under FCRA Sections 616 and 617 and FDCPA Section 1692k. The pressure on this account does not abate until the chain of title is produced in executed form or the tradeline is deleted.

Consumer complaint narrative: On or about XX/XX/year> I paid for a sew-in hair installation using my Navy Federal debit card. Within three days of the appointment, I noticed that the installation was visibly bumpy and uneven at the top and was not laying flat. The issue was noticeable in photographs and was apparent to others who viewed the style. I promptly contacted the stylist and sent photographs of the problem. My message stated : XXXX XXXX! Can you fix the top of my sew in please? Its not as flat as it was before. The stylist responded, It not flat as before because of the blonde tracks the weft is thick. This response is significant because the stylist acknowledged the reason for the problem rather than denying it existed. However, I was never informed before or during the service that the hair would create a visibly raised, uneven, or bumpy installation. Had I been informed, I could have chosen different hair or a different installation method. Instead, the service was completed and I was left with a defective result. After receiving her response, I attempted to resolve the matter amicably and asked, Can we make it less humpy? The stylist did not respond. After waiting for a response, I followed up again the next day and sent, Hey. Following up. Rather than addressing the issue or scheduling a correction, the stylist responded, I dont talk any work on my days off I will revisit tomorrow. Especially Sunday. I replied, Thats fine. I just didnt want to be left hanging. Ill let you follow up tomorrow. Thanks. Despite stating that she would revisit the matter the following day, the stylist never followed up, never returned my call, never scheduled a correction, and never offered any meaningful resolution. At no point did she offer to inspect the installation, repair the work, or discuss a remedy. I attempted in good faith to resolve the issue directly with the merchant before filing a dispute. I notified her within days of the service, provided photographs, politely requested that the work be corrected, and followed up when I did not receive a response. Because the defective installation was never corrected, I was forced to pay an additional {$190.00} to another professional stylist to remove and redo the service. This expense would not have been necessary had the original service been performed properly or had the merchant honored a reasonable request to correct her work. I submitted photographs, appointment documentation, text messages, and evidence of the additional corrective expense to Navy Federal. Despite this evidence, Navy Federal denied my dispute on the basis that the service was performed and paid for. My concern is that the dispute appears to have been evaluated solely on whether a service occurred, rather than whether the service was defective and whether the merchant failed to remedy the problem after receiving prompt notice. I respectfully request that Navy Federals handling of this dispute be reviewed and that consideration be given to the evidence showing defective workmanship, the merchants acknowledgment of the issue, and the merchants failure to provide a remedy.

Consumer complaint narrative: The incident that I will describe involves USAA Federal Savings Bank. Specifically, this complaint is predicated on a single unauthorized ACH transfer from my USAA checking account to an unknown ( to us ) persons XXXX XXXX credit card via my USAA checking account bill pay application. On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX, I was reviewing our USAA checking account activity online. The first representative, XXXX, explained that they would open a dispute ( Case # XXXX ). I was informed that the dispute investigation resolution could take up to XXXX business days. He said USAA did not have a way of stopping a pending ACH transfer charge from being processed. He said he would be able to stop future transactions with XXXX XXXX. XXXX provided me with the name of the individual who owned the credit card receiving the payment. This person was unknown to us. I asked XXXX to set up a new checking account to avoid any further money being taken out in case of additional fraud. He transferred me to another rep named XXXX. XXXX attempted to open a new account but was unable to add me to it because XXXX reportedly had a glitch in its system. She was unable to see where my wife had signed and could not forward the XXXX forms to me for my signature. After many failed attempts, she decided that it was best to send the documents to my inbox at USAAs site. I was instructed to print the pages, have my wife and me sign them, and send the forms back to USAA via snail mail. She said this process takes at least XXXX business days. XXXX then transferred me to another representative named XXXX. XXXX was unable to fix the system glitch preventing XXXX from working. I asked her, Why cant I.T. ' be called to resolve this glitch? She explained that USAA does not have an I.T. XXXX in real time. I realized I wasnt getting anywhere, so after XXXX hours, I ended the conversation. At XXXX XXXX I called USAA to see if the glitch had been corrected. I spoke with a representative named Destiny. Unfortunately, they were unable to reverse or delete what XXXX had attempted to do, which was to resend the new docs for signatures. On XX/XX/year>, at XXXX XXXX, I discovered that the pending charge had gone through and was now POSTED. I called USAA and spoke with XXXX, who transferred me to XXXX, who transferred me to XXXX. They just repeated the same pleasantries that the other agents said. They want me to sit back and wait for the outcome of the dispute case. I asked for a guarantee that I would recover my money, and they were noncommittal. Seeing that I was getting nowhere. I ended that conversation. At XXXX am on XX/XX/year>, I called back. I spoke with XXXX. She said that USAA does not have a way to process a reversal, even for an unauthorized or possibly fraudulent ACH transfer. USAA has a provisional credit, but they have discretion over who they issue these credits to. It hasnt been issued to me. She suggests that I continually monitor my account. All of this could have been avoided if USAA had not released the funds associated with the unauthorized, possibly fraudulent ACH transfer. This is especially frustrating since I called USAA promptly as required, while the unauthorized ACH bill-pay transfer was still pending and had not yet been completed. I will file a police report regarding this unauthorized ACH transfer as I suspect fraud, compounded by USAAs failure to take timely, meaningful action. I have opened new accounts with other banks based upon my lack of confidence with USAA, despite a XXXX relationship with them.

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> Equifax Information Services LLC XXXX. Box XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. RE : FORMAL NOTICE OF DISPUTE AND DEMAND FOR DEBT VALIDATION To Whom It May Concern : I am in receipt of your collection attempts regarding an alleged debt. I hereby formally dispute this debt in its entirety and demand immediate validation. Despite your collection efforts, you have failed to provide any competent evidence that I owe this debt, that the amount claimed is accurate, or that your company has any legal authority to collect it. Mere assertions, account statements, screenshots, or internal records do not constitute proof of a valid debt. Pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g, I demand that you provide : A copy of the original contract or agreement bearing my signature. Complete documentation establishing my legal obligation for the alleged debt. The name and address of the original creditor. A complete accounting of the amount claimed, including all fees, interest, and charges. Documentation proving your authority to collect this debt, including any assignment or transfer records. Evidence that you are licensed and authorized to collect debts in my jurisdiction, if applicable. Furthermore, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, any information furnished to consumer reporting agencies must be accurate and capable of verification. If you have reported this account to any credit reporting agency without possessing adequate documentation to substantiate your claim, you may be furnishing inaccurate information in violation of federal law. Be advised that I will not acknowledge, assume, or accept liability for this alleged debt without proper validation. Until such validation is provided, you must cease collection activities concerning this account. If you are unable to provide the requested documentation, I demand that you : 1. Immediately cease all collection efforts. 2. Remove any negative tradelines, inquiries, or reporting related to this account from all consumer reporting agencies. 3. Provide written confirmation that the account has been closed and returned to the creditor or permanently withdrawn from collection. Failure to provide competent evidence of this alleged debt while continuing collection efforts or credit reporting may constitute violations of the FDCPA and FCRA. I reserve all rights available under federal and state law, including the right to pursue complaints with regulatory agencies and any remedies available for unlawful collection or reporting practices. This letter is not a refusal to pay. It is a formal dispute and a demand for validation. No admission of liability is made or implied. All future communications regarding this matter must be made in writing. Govern yourselves accordingly. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Rebuttal to CarMax Auto Finance Response ( Case No. XXXX ) I am rejecting CarMax Auto Finances response in its entirety. However, my official bank and transaction records prove that the payoff funds were sent and cleared on time. CarMax either failed to credit the payoff to my account in a timely manner or is improperly penalizing me for a administrative delay on their end after the loan was finalized. CarMax 's claim that they " can not accommodate the request to delete because they must report accurate information '' is an intentional deflection. There is nothing " accurate '' about reporting a consumer 30 days late on a loan that has been completely paid off and closed via a vehicle sale. Certified Mailed out on XXXX XXXX UCC Notice Violation Dispute Letter Certified Mailed To : Carmax, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX Subject : Demanding Immediate Deletion UCC Violations & Inaccurate Credit Reporting To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally dispute the automotive account listed below under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681i, and Delaware 's Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Article 9, Part 6. This vehicle was repossessed and subsequently liquidated. However, the original creditor, CARMAX AUTO FINANCE, failed to provide the mandatory statutory notices required under Delaware law. Specifically, the creditor never sent a Notice of Our Plan to Sell Property ( UCC 9-611 ) prior to the auction, nor did they provide a written Explanation of Calculation of Surplus or Deficiency ( UCC 9-616 ) after the disposition. Disputed Account Details : Creditor Name : CARMAX AUTO FINANCE Account Number : XXXX Reported Balance : {$30000.00} Legal Basis for Deletion : Under Delaware law, strict compliance with UCC Article 9 repossession notice requirements is an absolute prerequisite to establishing any deficiency debt. Because CarMax failed to issue these legally mandated notices, no legal debt or deficiency exists. Furthermore, CarMax is reporting an active balance of {$30000.00} updated as of XX/XX/year>. Reporting the gross loan balance after a vehicle has been sold at auctionwithout crediting auction proceeds or proving a legally established deficiencyconstitutes a blatant and willful violation of the FCRAs requirement for maximum possible accuracy ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ).

Consumer complaint narrative: Date : XX/XX/year> Florida Attorney General 's Office Consumer Protection Division Re : Consumer Complaint Against XXXX XXXX and Bank of America Dear Sir or Madam : I am filing this complaint against XXXX XXXX and Bank of America for misleading and deceptive representations concerning my XXXX XXXX loyalty rewards, elite status benefits, travel vouchers, and related financial losses. Shortly thereafter, I learned that XXXX XXXX had entered bankruptcy proceedings and that my loyalty points, XXXX XXXX benefits, and travel vouchers had effectively become unavailable or worthless. When I subsequently contacted both companies, I was unable to obtain a satisfactory explanation regarding the disappearance of my benefits. Despite the assurances I had previously received, neither company honored the representations made to me or provided an adequate resolution. Had I been accurately informed of the risks, I would have redeemed my points, utilized my vouchers, explored alternative loyalty programs, made different travel arrangements, and taken steps to protect myself from these losses. Subject : Breach of Contract, Consumer Fraud, and Request for Loan Termination Under the FTC Holder Rule ( GoodLeap, LLC ) Complainant State : Arizona To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to file a formal consumer protection complaint against GoodLeap, LLC regarding a solar financing agreement entered into in 2021. 1. Breach of Warranty and Loss of Value The installer, XXXX XXXX, has since gone out of business and entered bankruptcy. Consequently, the critical workmanship and roof warranties associated with my system have been completely severed. I am now left with a financed asset that lacks the essential structural guarantees promised to me at the point of sale. 3. Application of the FTC Holder Rule My contract contains the federally mandated FTC Holder Rule notice ( 16 C.F.R. 433.2 ), which explicitly states : " Any holder of this consumer credit contract is subject to all claims and defenses which the debtor could assert against the seller of goods or services obtained pursuant hereto ... '' Under this federal regulation, GoodLeap, LLC steps into the shoes of the bankrupt installer. Because the installer committed a fundamental breach of warranty, I maintain the legal right to assert that breach against GoodLeap as a complete defense against further payment obligations. 4. Violation of Arizona Consumer Protection Laws As a resident of Arizona, I am further protected by the Arizona Consumer Fraud Act ( A.R.S. 44-1521 et seq. ). GoodLeap partnered with a deceptive contractor to originate this consumer loan, and I am now being forced to pay for a compromised product with XXXX operational support or liability protection for my roof. Furthermore, my system is currently broken, and GoodLeaps frontline customer service has failed to offer a meaningful remedy, instead insisting that I continue paying the full loan balance for an unbacked asset. Requested Resolution : Because the structural and workmanship warranties are permanently lost due to the installers insolvency, I request that the CFPB compel GoodLeap, LLC to fulfill its legal obligations under the FTC Holder Rule by : Canceling the remaining balance of loan account number XXXX Restructuring the loan to heavily discount the balance to reflect the severe loss of asset value and lack of a workmanship/roof warranty. Consumer complaint narrative: On Friday, XX/XX/year>, I deposited a personal check for {$22000.00} from a client into my business checking account at Chase. Funds were initially scheduled to become available on Tuesday, XX/XX/year>, consistent with standard funds availability for a check deposited before a weekend. I received no written notice of this exception hold from Chase. No secure message, no email, no text, no mailed notice. The only disclosure on the original deposit slip was generic boilerplate stating that further review may result in additional delay, which does not constitute the specific notice required under 12 CFR 229.13 ( g ) when a bank invokes an exception hold. The regulation requires written notice stating the specific reason for the hold and the revised availability date. I received none. I only learned about the hold by logging into the Chase app on XX/XX/XXXX, where the transaction page displayed the hold with the following stated reason : " We have not yet collected the money from the paying bank so some or all of your deposit may not be available for withdrawal. '' This stated reason was false at the time it was displayed. I have obtained confirmation from my client that the check cleared the paying bank on Monday, XX/XX/year> the same day Chase placed the exception hold citing inability to collect from the paying bank. The funds had already been debited from the issuing account on the date Chase was representing in writing that collection had not yet occurred. On XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, I spent approximately two hours on multiple phone calls with Chase attempting to understand why availability had been extended. I received conflicting explanations from different representatives, none of which matched the stated reason displayed in the app. One representative stated Chase was unable to verify funds with the issuing bank. Another stated there was a high risk of the check being returned. The in-app reason stated funds had not yet been collected. These are three different explanations across three sources, none of which were accompanied by the written notice the regulation requires, and at least one of which ( the " not yet collected '' reason in the app ) was factually false on the date displayed. Multiple representatives told me there was nothing that could be done on the phone and that I would have to wait until XX/XX/XXXX for funds to release. After multiple escalations on XX/XX/XXXX, a supervisor released the hold during a phone call. This is itself a contradiction of what I had been told repeatedly by prior representatives that nothing could be done on the phone and the hold would not release until XX/XX/XXXX. The supervisor claimed that Chase had previously communicated the hold to me, but was unable to specify when or how that communication occurred. No such communication exists in my Chase secure messages, email, or text. The supervisor also stated that this type of hold could occur again on future deposits. The contradictions here are the core of my complaint. Either the hold was legitimate and required for the full period through XX/XX/XXXX in which case it should not have been released arbitrarily on XX/XX/XXXX after escalation or the hold was not legitimate, in which case it should not have been placed, and certainly not without the written notice the regulation requires. Both can not be true. Further, Chase 's own stated reason for the hold in the app ( " we have not yet collected the money from the paying bank '' ) was contradicted by the actual status of the check on the date the hold was placed. The funds had cleared the paying bank on XX/XX/XXXX, the same day Chase claimed in writing that collection had not occurred. Harm : Chase 's silent exception hold caused me to plan around an availability date Chase later moved without notice. I have {$14000.00} in credit card payments due XX/XX/year>, and additional auto-pays scheduled to debit this account in the coming days. Had the hold not been placed, or had it been released on its original date of XX/XX/XXXX as scheduled, these obligations would have been paid in full from the deposited funds. Because of Chase 's actions, I was preparing to incur credit card interest charges and risk of overdraft fees on auto-pays. I also lost approximately two hours of business operating time pursuing resolution by phone, during which I received contradictory and inaccurate information from multiple Chase representatives including a written representation in the Chase app that the paying bank had not collected funds, when in fact the check had cleared the paying bank on the same day the hold was placed.

I am filing this complaint against IQ Data XXXX XXXX XXXX regarding a residential rental collection account they are reporting on my consumer credit file for an alleged debt connected to XXXX XXXX XXXX. I previously sent IQ Data XXXX a written request for debt validation. This was not a general request for a balance statement. I specifically requested documentation proving that I legally owe the alleged rental debt, including the lease agreement or rental contract, a full itemization of the balance, documentation showing how the amount was calculated, original creditor records supporting the alleged charges, and proof that IQ Data XXXX has authority to collect and furnish this account. IQ Data XXXX has not provided sufficient validation of this alleged debt. They have not provided the lease-level documentation, complete itemization, resident ledger, move-out statement, charge breakdown, or proof of legal obligation necessary to support the balance being collected and reported. This is a serious issue because IQ Data is continuing to report a derogatory rental collection while failing to provide the basic documents needed to prove the account is accurate, legally owed, properly itemized, and authorized for collection. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), once a consumer disputes a debt in writing and requests verification, a debt collector must cease collection activity until verification is mailed to the consumer. IQ Data has not provided complete verification of this alleged rental debt, yet the account continues to be treated as collectible and reportable. IQ Datas continued reporting also raises concerns under 15 U.S.C. 1692e, which prohibits false, deceptive, or misleading representations in connection with debt collection. Continuing to report and collect a rental balance without producing the lease, full ledger, itemized charges, move-out statement, and proof of authority is misleading because it represents the debt as valid and collectible without competent documentation. This also raises concerns under 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) because IQ Data is representing the character, amount, and legal status of a debt that has not been properly verified. If IQ Data can not prove the lease obligation, itemized balance, and supporting charge records, then the amount and legal status of the alleged debt remain unsupported. IQ Datas conduct also raises concerns under 15 U.S.C. 1692f ( 1 ) because a debt collector may not collect any amount unless that amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law. IQ Data has not provided the lease agreement, itemized ledger, or documentation showing that each amount being collected is authorized. The account is also reporting with inconsistent balance information. My earlier credit report dated XX/XX/year> showed the IQ Data account reporting with a balance that differs from the balance later shown on my updated credit report dated XX/XX/year>. This unexplained balance change raises serious concerns about the accuracy and reliability of the information IQ Data is furnishing. If IQ Data is changing or furnishing different balances, they should be able to provide a full account-level itemization showing every charge, payment, credit, deposit, adjustment, fee, utility charge, damage charge, rent charge, or collection cost included in the balance. IQ Data has not provided that documentation. I also obtained a XXXX tenant screening disclosure, which I am uploading as supporting evidence. This alleged rental obligation is not consistently reflected across tenant screening and consumer reporting systems. That inconsistency further calls into question whether the account is complete, accurate, properly verified, and properly reportable. Because IQ Data is furnishing this account to consumer reporting agencies, IQ Data also has duties as a furnisher under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. After a dispute, a furnisher must conduct a reasonable investigation and correct, delete, or modify information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or can not be verified under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). The issue is not simply that IQ Data claims a balance is owed. The issue is that IQ Data is continuing to furnish a damaging rental collection without providing the documents necessary to prove the balance, the lease obligation, the itemization, the date of first delinquency, and their authority to collect and report. IQ Data has not provided : A copy of the original lease agreement or rental contract bearing my signature ; A complete resident ledger ; A move-out statement ; A full itemization of the alleged balance ; Documentation showing how the balance was calculated ; Documentation supporting each charge included in the alleged balance ; Proof of deposits, credits, payments, adjustments, or fees applied ; The original creditors records supporting the alleged debt ; Proof that IQ Data XXXX has authority to collect this account ; Proof that IQ Data XXXX has authority to furnish this account to the consumer reporting agencies ; Documentation confirming the date of first delinquency ; A clear explanation for the inconsistent balance reporting between my XX/XX/year> and XX/XX/year> credit reports. Without those documents, IQ Data can not reasonably claim this account is accurate, legally owed, properly itemized, or properly reportable. I am requesting that IQ Data provide a direct, account-specific response to this complaint. A generic statement that the account is verified or that a balance is owed is not sufficient. I want IQ Data to identify the exact documents reviewed, explain how the balance was calculated, provide the lease and full itemization, explain the balance change, and prove its authority to collect and report this account. If IQ Data can not provide complete documentation proving the alleged rental debt, balance, legal obligation, date of first delinquency, and authority to collect/report, this account should be deleted from all consumer reporting agencies.

Specifically, the bank did not provide : SMS logs showing the alleged confirmation The actual call recording for the alleged XX/XX/XXXX call ( only a transcript was provided ) Authentication logs ( IP address, device, location, login data ) Internal investigation notes Merchant documentation Any evidence demonstrating that I actually authorized the transactions The bank did provide screenshots that appear to contain internal notes from a call in which they claim I confirmed the transactions, as well as a transcript of a call they assert reflects my confirmation. However, internal notes and a transcript are not the underlying evidence required to substantiate such a claim. Without the original call recording or authentication data, I can not verify the accuracy of the banks interpretation or meaningfully challenge its conclusion. Without access to the actual evidence, I can not meaningfully understand, evaluate, or appeal the banks determination. This is similar to being asked to respond to a decision in a legal proceeding without being given the evidence used to reach that decision. RegulationE requires the bank to provide copies of the documents it relied upon, and I am simply requesting the information necessary to review and respond to their findings. The only other documentation the bank provided was : ( 1 ) a list of transactions, which is not evidence of authorization, and ( 2 ) an outsourced Visa investigation packet for a single {$330.00} transaction. The XXXX packet does not satisfy the banks independent obligations under RegulationE and does not address the remaining disputed transactions. I also attempted to file a police report regarding the unauthorized transactions, but was informed that I could not do so because the merchant is based in XXXX XXXX and therefore outside the jurisdiction of local law enforcement. Although a police report is not required under RegulationE, I still made a goodfaith effort to obtain one. I am including this detail so the CFPB is aware that I attempted to provide every form of documentation reasonably available to me. In addition, I made a goodfaith effort to stabilize the account by moving my savings to cover approximately half of the overdraft created by the unauthorized transactions. I did this to prevent further fees and demonstrate that I was not attempting to avoid responsibility for the account while the dispute was pending. This situation has caused significant and ongoing stress, largely because I have been unable to obtain the evidence necessary to understand or respond to the banks determination. I have made every goodfaith effort to resolve the matter, but the lack of transparency has made it difficult to move forward. Finally, I am concerned that the bank issued provisional credit before completing its investigation. Under RegulationE, provisional credit is intended to protect consumers during an investigationnot to serve as a basis for later denying a claim without providing the required evidence. The sequence of events raises questions about whether the investigation was completed in a reasonable and compliant manner.

I am filing this complaint as a follow-up to CFPB Complaint No. XXXX, which was closed without adequate resolution. Goldman Sachs Bank USA 's response to that complaint requested closure on the grounds that their investigation found no bank error and that I failed to provide sufficient evidence of return. That characterization is factually incorrect, and I am requesting this matter be escalated. This dispute concerns a transaction with merchant XXXX ( XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX ) on my Apple Card, Dispute Case No. XXXX, transaction date XX/XX/XXXX, in the amount of {$360.00}. I disputed this charge on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. Goldman Sachs ruled in favor of the merchant each time. The facts are as follows : On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted the merchant at XXXX to initiate a return of Order # XXXX. The item received was defective upon arrival, with a broken belt piece included in the shipment. On XX/XX/XXXX, the merchant responded with return instructions. Within that single email, the merchant twice instructed me to commit customs fraud by declaring the package value at under {$20.00}, despite the actual purchase price being {$360.00}. The instruction appeared first mid-paragraph : " please declare the package value under {$20.00}, which will be helpful to expedite the clearance '' and was then repeated as a standalone notice : " Important : Please declare the package value under {$20.00}, which will be helpful to expedite the clearance. '' This is customs fraud under 18 U.S.C. 542, a federal crime. Deliberately undervaluing a {$360.00} shipment as {$20.00} on a customs declaration is not a technicality or a cultural misunderstanding. It is a deliberate instruction to falsify a federal document. I refused to comply. Additionally, the merchant 's return shipping cost was nearly equivalent to the original purchase price, making the return economically impossible even setting aside the illegal customs requirement. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, I am only required to make a good faith effort to return defective merchandise. I made that effort on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, in documented written communications. The merchant 's only return pathway required me to break federal law. No merchant terms and conditions supersede federal statute. This documented evidence, including the merchant 's XX/XX/XXXX email with the customs fraud instruction appearing twice, was submitted to Goldman Sachs during the dispute process and was also attached to CFPB Complaint No. XXXX. Goldman Sachs ' response to that complaint does not reference, acknowledge, or address this evidence in any way. A financial institution that receives documented proof of a merchant instructing a consumer to commit federal customs fraud and proceeds to rule in that merchant 's favor four consecutive times has conducted a materially incomplete investigation and has failed its obligations under the FCBA. I am also requesting that the CFPB examine whether Goldman Sachs has a broader pattern of failing to properly review consumer-submitted evidence in transaction disputes of this nature. If their investigation process allowed customs fraud documentation to be submitted, reviewed, and dismissed four consecutive times in a single case, it is reasonable to conclude that other consumers may have experienced the same outcome. A systemic failure to engage with evidence of illegal merchant conduct would represent a serious institutional compliance issue that warrants regulatory scrutiny beyond my individual dispute. I am requesting the following : 1. That the CFPB escalate this matte r and not accept Goldman Sachs ' prior closure as resolution. 2. That Goldman Sachs be directed to conduct a new investigation that specifically addresses the customs fraud instruction documented in the merchant 's XX/XX/XXXX email. 3. That the {$360.00} charge be permanently credited to my account. 4. That the CFPB consider whether Goldman Sachs ' dispute review process warrants a broader examination for similar consumer complaints. I was on XXXX XXXX military service during a significant portion of this dispute period and pursued this matter diligently despite those obligations. I have now been fighting this for over seven months across four dispute rounds and one prior CFPB complaint. The evidence is documented, specific, and unambiguous. I am asking the CFPB to hold Goldman Sachs accountable for ignoring clear proof of illegal merchant conduct.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against GoodLeap LLC regarding a solar financing loan of {$30000.00} ( account number XXXX ) that I was induced to enter into in XX/XX/XXXX in connection with a residential solar installation at my home in XXXX, Texas. Background : I entered the original contract with XXXX XXXX, who used Goodleap for financing. That company went out of business before completing the work. GoodLeap then paired me with a second contractor, [ XXXX XXXX ], who completed the physical installation but subsequently also went bankrupt and out of business before the solar system was ever activated or made operational. I received a letter in the mail stating they are out of business, bankrupt and the warranty is void. I was left with a non-functioning solar system, no warranty, no service agreement, and no recourse against either defunct contractor. To date, the solar system has never been operational. I received no benefit from the {$30000.00} loan proceeds. I am now being held responsible for the full loan balance which has grown to {$31000.00} with interest and charges for a product that was never delivered as promised. Legal basis FTC Holder Rule ( 16 CFR 433 ) : Under the FTC 's Preservation of Consumers ' Claims and Defenses Rule ( 16 CFR 433, commonly called the " Holder Rule '' ), when a lender finances a consumer purchase through a seller, the lender takes the loan subject to all claims and defenses the consumer has against the seller. GoodLeap directly facilitated and arranged my contracts with both solar contractors. As the financing entity in a seller-arranged consumer credit transaction, GoodLeap is legally subject to my defenses of failure of consideration, breach of contract, and non-delivery of the promised goods and services. GoodLeap can not hide behind the contractors ' insolvency. The Holder Rule exists precisely to prevent consumers from being trapped paying loans for goods and services that were never delivered. Additional violations and concerns : 1. CFPB UDAAP ( Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ) : GoodLeap 's practice of pairing consumers with solar contractors, collecting loan payments, and then refusing to accept responsibility when those contractors fail to deliver is an unfair practice that causes substantial consumer harm with no countervailing benefit. 2. GoodLeap charged off this account and reported a {$31000.00} derogatory mark to XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX, severely damaging my credit, despite the fact that the underlying obligation is legally disputed under the Holder Rule. 3. I was never informed by GoodLeap of my rights under the FTC Holder Rule at the time of signing, nor was I advised of any consumer protections available to me if the contractor failed to perform. Resolution requested : I am requesting that the CFPB investigate GoodLeap 's practices in this matter and assist me in obtaining the following relief : Full cancellation of the {$31000.00} loan balance under the FTC Holder Rule Immediate deletion of the charge-off and all related derogatory reporting from my credit file at XXXX XXXX, and XXXX A written response from GoodLeap acknowledging my Holder Rule defenses Investigation into whether GoodLeap has engaged in a pattern of similar conduct with other consumers I have supporting documentation available including my original loan agreement, contractor contracts, correspondence showing non-completion of work, and my credit report showing the charge-off. I am prepared to provide these upon request. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

I believe the lack of clear written direction, lack of clear deadlines, and lack of coordinated communication contributed to the loss of the purchase opportunity. I was actively trying to resolve the loan conditions and pursue outside financing, including XXXX XXXX, but the process was not clearly communicated or coordinated. Consumer complaint narrative: This complaint concerns three consecutive billing disputes on my OnePay XXXX XXXX issued by Synchrony Bank. Federal law gives consumers the right to a reasonable investigation of a disputed charge and a clear written resolution stating what was decided and what it means for their account. Across three consecutive disputes I have received neither a completed investigation nor a clear final answer. What I have received are letters that describe an ongoing process, a portal that contradicts the letters, and in one case a letter that calls itself a resolution while pointing to a temporary credit as its only evidence without ever stating what was decided or what happens to my money. A resolution requires a closed file a statement of what was investigated, what was found, and what it means for the account with no conditions attached. What Synchrony has provided instead are letters that describe a process still in motion, using conditional language that preserves their ability to reverse the credit at any time. DISPUTE 1 {$110.00} ( XX/XX/XXXX ) : I filed a dispute on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, the institution issued a temporary credit letter characterizing the adjustment as subject to reversal pending further review. No final determination followed. I made repeated contacts, including a chat on XX/XX/XXXX ( Ref # XXXX ) and a call with a supervisor on XX/XX/XXXX, neither of which produced a resolution. On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a CFPB complaint ( Case XXXX ). Only after that federal complaint was filed did the institution issue a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX stating we have completed our review. That letter does not state what the investigation concluded or what the decision means for the credit on my account. It points to the temporary credit applied on XX/XX/XXXX as if that act constitutes a resolution but that same credit had been characterized as subject to reversal since the day it was issued. The letter also cites the CFPB filing date as the sole inquiry date while omitting documented contacts on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX that preceded it. The account portal shows two entries for this dispute one marked Dispute Completed and one marked Under Review. A consumer looking at their own account can not determine from that whether the dispute is closed or still open. There is no written correspondence that resolves that contradiction. DISPUTE 2 {$130.00} ( XX/XX/XXXX ) : I filed a dispute on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, the institution issued a temporary credit letter using identical language to the {$110.00} dispute characterizing the credit as subject to reversal pending further review. No final determination was ever issued. The written record stops at the temporary credit letter. As of XX/XX/XXXX, this dispute has been open for 91 days, exceeding the maximum investigation period permitted under federal law, and no final determination has been issued. The account portal shows two entries for this dispute for the same date and amount one marked Dispute Completed and one marked Under Review. A consumer looking at their own account can not determine from that whether the dispute is closed or still open. There is no written correspondence that resolves that contradiction. DISPUTE 3 {$70.00} ( XX/XX/XXXX ) : I filed a dispute on XX/XX/XXXX. The institution acknowledged the dispute on XX/XX/XXXX and committed in writing to provide the outcome within 60 days. As of XX/XX/XXXX, that deadline has elapsed. The only written correspondence I have received is a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX characterizing the adjustment as a temporary credit subject to reversal. The institution has not provided the outcome it committed to provide. The account portal shows this dispute as Under Review. This institution has demonstrated across three consecutive disputes that a final written determination only materializes under pressure, arrives with facts selectively presented, or never arrives at all. Dispute 1 required a federal complaint to produce any final letter, and that letter distorted the timeline by omitting documented prior contacts and pointed to a temporary credit as a resolution without stating what was actually decided. Dispute 2 has no final letter the written record stops at the temporary credit. Dispute 3 blew past the institutions own committed deadline with nothing but a temporary credit letter that still leaves the door open to reversal. Synchrony has demonstrated a consistent pattern of avoiding clear, timely, final written determinations and when one is finally forced, presenting a selective account of the facts rather than a straight answer about what was decided and what it means for the consumers account.

Consumer complaint narrative: Subject : PayPal Withholding Business Funds, Repeated Documentation Requests, and Failure to Provide Clear Resolution Process I am submitting this complaint regarding PayPal 's continued withholding of funds belonging to my business and what appears to be an unreasonable and constantly changing documentation review process. My company is a legitimate service-based business that has successfully completed work for customers. Despite providing substantial documentation and repeatedly complying with PayPal 's requests, PayPal continues to hold my funds and request additional information without providing a clear explanation of what specific requirements remain unmet or what is needed to resolve the matter. Over the course of this review, PayPal has requested numerous documents, including : * Business licenses * Service agreements * Customer contracts * Business verification information * Operational details regarding how my company conducts business * Additional supporting documentation related to transactions Each time I submit the requested documents, PayPal either requests additional information or claims that previously submitted documents are insufficient. For example, I have submitted electronically generated contracts that are clearly legible and professionally prepared, yet I have been told they are " not legible '' and asked to resubmit them. This has occurred multiple times. What is especially concerning is that PayPal has requested information that I believe contains proprietary business information and trade practices that are not necessary to verify the legitimacy of completed transactions. While I understand the need for reasonable verification procedures, the scope and ongoing nature of these requests appear excessive and burdensome. The transactions in question involve services, not physical goods. The customer has confirmed on multiple occasions that the services were completed as agreed. Despite customer confirmation and the completion of the contracted work, PayPal continues to withhold payment. As a result of PayPal 's actions, my business has suffered significant financial harm, including : * Inability to access funds earned through completed services. * Disruption of normal business operations. * Cash flow shortages that have prevented me from taking on new projects. * Loss of at least one business opportunity due to lack of access to my funds. * Damage to my company 's reputation with customers and vendors. * Additional legal and administrative burdens associated with collecting payment for services already rendered. Perhaps most frustrating is the lack of transparency throughout this process. PayPal has not provided a definitive list of all documents required for review, nor have they provided a clear timeline for when the review will be completed or when my funds will be released. Instead, the process appears open-ended, with new requests being issued repeatedly over an extended period. I believe consumers and small businesses deserve clear standards, reasonable verification requirements, and timely access to funds once legitimate transactions have been verified. In my case, PayPal 's actions have created unnecessary hardship and uncertainty despite my full cooperation. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and assist in obtaining : 1. A detailed explanation from PayPal regarding the legal and factual basis for continuing to hold my funds. 2. A complete list of all documentation PayPal requires to complete its review. 3. A specific timeline for resolution and release of funds. 4. A review of whether PayPal 's repeated and expanding documentation requests constitute an unfair or unreasonable burden on small business customers. 5. Immediate release of any funds that are not legitimately subject to dispute or regulatory restriction. I have made every effort to comply with PayPal 's requests and resolve this matter directly. However, after repeated submissions and continued delays without meaningful progress, I am seeking regulatory assistance to ensure fair treatment and timely access to funds earned through legitimate business activity. * * Business Name : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX PayPal Account Email : XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX * * Amount Being Held : * * {$6100.00} * * Dates of Review/Hold XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Complaint Against : * * [ PayPal ] ( https : //www.paypal.com Thank you for your attention to this matter. I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, correspondence, customer confirmations, and records of all requests made by PayPal during this review process.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this follow-up complaint because Regional Acceptance Corporation continues to claim that the balance being reported and collected is accurate while failing to provide the documentation and calculations necessary to independently verify that claim. However, the production of documents has created additional questions that Regional has not answered. The primary issue is that Regional continues to provide conclusions without providing the calculations supporting those conclusions. RED FLAG # XXXX NO DEFICIENCY BALANCE CALCULATION Regional repeatedly claims that a principal balance of {$9700.00} remained after the vehicle was declared a total loss, insurance proceeds were applied, warranty-related credits were applied, and the GAP claim was reviewed. However, Regional has never provided a deficiency balance worksheet showing step-by-step how it arrived at the {$9700.00} figure. Instead, Regional has simply provided the ending number and instructed me to accept it as accurate. I am requesting the actual calculation. RED FLAG # XXXX INSURANCE PAYMENT EXCEEDED THE PAYOFF FIGURE SHOWN ON THE GAP DETERMINATION Regionals own GAP determination documents state : Payoff as of date of loss : {$11000.00} Insurance settlement : {$14000.00} Warranty-related credits applied GAP benefit : {$0.00} Regional simultaneously claims that a principal deficiency of {$9700.00} remained after these events. This is precisely why a deficiency calculation is required. I am not claiming the balance is impossible. I am stating that Regional has not explained how these figures reconcile. Regional has produced documents showing the beginning and ending figures while omitting the calculations connecting them. RED FLAG # XXXX NO COMPLETE EXPLANATION OF THE GAP DETERMINATION Regional provided a GAP determination letter but did not provide : The GAP addendum or GAP contract relied upon. The complete XXXX claim file. The supporting calculations used during the XXXX review. The basis for concluding that no XXXX benefit was payable. Regional has therefore provided the result of the review without providing the information necessary to independently evaluate the accuracy of that result. RED FLAG # XXXX XXXX PAYMENT EXTENSIONS WITH NO EXPLANATION OF THEIR FINANCIAL IMPACT Regionals records show : A XXXX extension. XXXX separate XXXX extensions. An additional XXXX extension. Despite relying upon those extensions as part of the explanation for the remaining balance, Regional has never provided a calculation showing : How much additional interest accrued because of each extension. How each extension affected the maturity date. How each extension affected the final deficiency balance. Whether those amounts were excluded from XXXX coverage and, if so, why. Regionals position appears to be that extensions contributed significantly to the remaining balance, yet Regional has never quantified that impact. RED FLAG # XXXX THE BALANCE REMAINED SURPRISINGLY HIGH DESPITE YEARS OF PAYMENTS The transaction history reflects years of payments. However, the principal balance remained substantially higher than one would expect without a detailed explanation regarding the impact of interest accrual, extensions, fees, reversals, and other account activity. Regional has not provided a narrative accounting explaining how payments were applied over time and how those applications ultimately resulted in the claimed deficiency balance. RED FLAG # XXXX NO DIRECT CONTACT INFORMATION Regionals response is signed by XXXX XXXX, Senior Vice President and Process Management Lead. However, no direct email address, extension, department contact information, or other means of documented communication was provided. I am requesting clarification regarding whether XXXX XXXX personally reviewed the dispute, supporting documents, account history, and CFPB materials before issuing the response. If she personally reviewed the matter, then she should be able to address these questions directly. If she did not personally review the matter, then Regional should identify the individual who conducted the investigation and the records reviewed. I am also requesting a valid email address for the department responsible for handling this dispute so that communications can be documented and preserved for my protection and for the accuracy of the record. RED FLAG # XXXX REGIONAL CONTINUES TO REPORT THE BALANCE WITHOUT PROVIDING THE SUPPORTING CALCULATION Regional continues to maintain that the balance is accurate. However, Regional has not provided the actual calculation supporting the amount claimed. The issue is no longer whether documents exist. The issue is whether Regional can clearly explain and substantiate the balance it continues to report and claim is owed. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, furnishers have obligations regarding the accuracy and completeness of information reported to consumer reporting agencies and must conduct reasonable investigations of disputed information. Repeating that the balance is accurate is not the same as demonstrating that the balance is accurate. I am requesting documentation sufficient to independently verify the claimed balance, including a complete deficiency calculation, payoff calculation, XXXX documentation, extension impact calculations, credit reporting information, and an explanation reconciling the figures contained within Regionals own records. Until Regional provides that information, the accuracy and completeness of the reported balance remain disputed.

* * Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint * * * * Company : * * Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC * * Complaint * * I am filing this complaint against Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC regarding the reporting and collection of an alleged debt that I dispute. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), furnishers of information are required to provide accurate and complete information to consumer reporting agencies. Furnishers may not report information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), once a dispute is received, furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation and review all relevant information before continuing to report the account. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f, and 1692g, debt collectors may not use false, deceptive, misleading, unfair, or unconscionable means to collect debts. Debt collectors must possess sufficient documentation establishing the validity of the debt, the amount owed, and their authority to collect the debt. I dispute the validity, ownership, and accuracy of the alleged debt and request that Jefferson Capital Systems provide : 1. Documentation identifying the original creditor. 2. The original account number associated with the alleged debt. 3. Documentation proving I am legally responsible for the debt. 4. Documentation establishing Jefferson Capital Systems ' ownership of the account or authority to collect it. 5. The complete chain of assignment, transfer, or sale of the account. 6. A complete payment history and accounting supporting the balance being reported. 7. Documentation establishing the date of first delinquency. 8. Documentation demonstrating that the amount being reported is accurate and supported by business records. 9. Verification that all information furnished to consumer reporting agencies complies with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and XXXX XXXX reporting standards. 10. Copies of any records used to verify the account during prior disputes or investigations. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has emphasized that debt buyers and debt collectors must maintain adequate records to support the accuracy and integrity of information furnished to consumer reporting agencies. If Jefferson Capital Systems can not provide competent evidence validating the debt, ownership, and balance being reported, continued reporting may constitute the furnishing of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information in violation of federal law. * * Requested Resolution * * I request that Jefferson Capital Systems conduct a thorough investigation and provide complete documentation supporting the validity, ownership, and accuracy of the alleged debt. If the account can not be fully validated and verified, I request immediate deletion of the account from all consumer reporting agencies. I further request correction of any inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information currently being reported and written confirmation of the results of the investigation.

Consumer complaint narrative: * * Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint * * * * Company : * * Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC * * Account Information * * * Balance Reported : {$510.00} * Date Opened : XX/XX/year> * Account Status : Open Collection Account * Original Creditor : Not Reported/ Unknown * Remark : Consumer Disputes This Account Information * * Complaint * * I am filing this complaint against Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC regarding a collection account being reported on my consumer credit reports that I dispute. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), furnishers of information are required to provide accurate and complete information to consumer reporting agencies. Furnishers may not report information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), once a dispute is received, Jefferson Capital Systems is required to conduct a reasonable investigation, review all relevant information, and correct, update, or delete any information that can not be verified. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f, and 1692g, debt collectors may not use false, deceptive, misleading, unfair, or unconscionable means to collect debts. Debt collectors must possess sufficient documentation establishing the validity of the debt, the amount owed, and their authority to collect the debt. I request that Jefferson Capital Systems provide : 1. Identification of the original creditor. 2. The original account number associated with the alleged debt. 3. Documentation proving I am legally responsible for the debt. 4. Documentation establishing Jefferson Capital Systems ' ownership of the account or authority to collect it. 5. The complete chain of assignment, transfer, or sale of the account. 6. A complete payment history and accounting supporting the reported balance of {$510.00}. 7. Documentation establishing the date of first delinquency. 8. Documentation demonstrating that the amount being reported is accurate and supported by business records. 9. Copies of any records used to verify the account during prior disputes. 10. Verification that all information furnished to consumer reporting agencies complies with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Metro 2 reporting standards. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has emphasized that debt collectors and furnishers must maintain adequate records to support the accuracy and integrity of information reported to consumer reporting agencies. If Jefferson Capital Systems can not provide competent evidence validating the debt, ownership, and balance being reported, continued reporting may constitute the furnishing of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information. * * Requested Resolution * * I request that Jefferson Capital Systems conduct a thorough investigation and provide complete documentation supporting the validity, ownership, and accuracy of the alleged debt. If the account can not be fully validated and verified, I request immediate deletion of the account from all consumer reporting agencies. I further request correction of any inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information currently being reported and written confirmation of the results of the investigation.

When asked what would happen if XXXX doesn't provide proof of an independent evaluation, he stated the dispute would be settled in my favor. XXXX has failed to produce evidence of an independent evaluation. Consumer complaint narrative: Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this statement in support of a complaint against XXXX XXXX XXXXComenity Capital Bank and XXXX. The treatment was never completed. To this day, my wife and I still have the Invisalign attachments/buttons/components on our teeth that were placed to hold the Invisalign trays, because the treatment was never properly finished. The office did not provide a proper completion appointment, final removal of the attachments, final review, or clear documentation showing what services were completed versus what services remained unfinished. The original treating doctor later moved to another office. Instead of completing the treatment with the current provider at the original office, we were told to go to the office wherever the doctor moved. Based on my wife 's prior employment experience with the office, we understand the office could and should have finished the treatment with the current provider. We believe the office shifted the burden to us because the production/credit for the case may not have transferred to the current doctor, even though that should not have affected us as patients. My wife, XXXX XXXX, previously worked for the office. Because of that familiarity, we believe the office took advantage of the situation by telling us to follow the doctor to another location instead of properly finishing or correcting the treatment at the office where the services were billed. Most importantly, the dental office later mailed us a refund check with no explanation. If a refund was owed, that shows the account or treatment balance was not properly reconciled. It is unreasonable to issue a partial refund connected to the treatment while also allowing the bank and a debt collector to pursue a remaining balance for services that were not completed. The office manager personally assisted with the credit application and set up the automatic payments. We were assured that the payments would be split evenly and structured so the promotional balance would be paid in full before the promotional period ended. We relied on that representation when agreeing to the financing. That representation was false or misleading because the payment arrangement did not pay off the balance before the promotional deadline and resulted in significant deferred interest and additional charges. We contacted XXXX XXXX XXXXComenity multiple times and filed disputes regarding this account. Each dispute was denied. I believe the investigations failed to address the incomplete treatment, the still-attached orthodontic components the misleading payment setup, the unexplained refund check, and the fact that the underlying services were not completed. The account has now been sold, assigned, or transferred to XXXX, which is threatening legal action. This escalation occurred despite the fact that the treatment was unfinished and despite the unresolved refund and billing issues. WHY I AM REQUESTING CFPB REVIEW XXXX XXXX XXXXComenity should not have treated this as a simple balance or payment issue. The dispute involved incomplete services, misleading financing representations made at the dental office, an unexplained refund, and unresolved treatment components still attached to our teeth. Despite multiple disputes, the account was denied and then sold, assigned, or transferred to XXXX, which is now threatening legal action. I believe the creditor failed to conduct a reasonable investigation and failed to obtain or review the information necessary to determine whether the underlying services were completed. The denials did not address the unfinished treatment, the refund check, or the misleading autopay representation made when the account was opened. REQUESTED RESOLUTION- Conduct a complete reinvestigation of the account and the underlying services.- Provide a full accounting of all charges, payments, credits, refunds, interest, fees, and transfers to any debt collector.- Provide records showing what dental/Invisalign services were completed and what services remained incomplete.- Provide a written explanation of the refund check mailed by the dental office.- Issue a full refund of amounts paid toward the unfinished treatment, cancel any remaining balance, and remove all deferred interest, late fees, collection fees, and related charges.- Recall, withdraw, or correct the account with XXXX and any other collector.- Correct any negative credit reporting related to the disputed account and ensure the account is not reported as undisputed while this matter remains unresolved. I am requesting the CFPB to forward this complaint to the appropriate company or companies and require a written response with supporting records. My requested resolution is a full refund of amounts paid toward the unfinished treatment, cancellation of any remaining balance, removal of deferred interest and fees, withdrawal from collections, correction of any credit reporting, and written documentation explaining the refund and prior investigation results
