Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX, I became aware that something unusual was happening with my bank account. While I was at work, I began receiving text messages and phone notifications containing security codes and authentication requests that I had not initiated. At the time, I was not attempting to log into my online banking account, make any transfers, change any account settings, or conduct any banking activity. Because I was occupied with work responsibilities, I was unable to immediately investigate the issue in detail. However, I recognized that receiving security codes without requesting them could indicate that someone was attempting to access my account. As the day continued, I became increasingly concerned when I noticed activity involving my account that I did not recognize. Once I returned home from work, I immediately contacted PNC Bank to report what I believed was fraudulent activity. During my conversation with the bank, I learned that unauthorized changes had been made to my account information. Specifically, the phone number associated with my account had been changed without my knowledge or authorization. This discovery confirmed my suspicion that an unauthorized individual had gained access to my account. The fact that my phone number had been altered is particularly important because it appears that the individual who gained access to my account used this change to bypass security measures and gain control over account communications. By changing the phone number, the individual prevented me from receiving important security notifications and may have enabled themselves to receive authentication codes intended to protect my account. During my call with PNC Bank on XX/XX/XXXX, I informed the representative that I had not authorized any of the transactions in question and that I believed my account had been compromised. The bank initiated a fraud claim and dispute regarding the unauthorized transactions. I acted immediately upon discovering the issue and did everything within my power to notify the bank and protect my account. In addition to contacting the bank, I also contacted local law enforcement on the same day. A police report was taken documenting the incident. My goal was to ensure that the matter was formally investigated and that there would be an official record showing that I reported the fraud immediately upon discovering it. I understood the seriousness of the situation and wanted to cooperate fully with both the bank and law enforcement authorities. After the initial report, I waited for the banks investigation to be completed. Several weeks later, I contacted PNC Bank to obtain an update regarding the status of my claim. At that time, I was informed that the claim had been denied. According to the explanation provided to me, the bank concluded that the transactions were not eligible for reimbursement because they involved XXXX transfers and because the transactions were allegedly authorized. I strongly disagree with that conclusion. I did not authorize these transactions. I did not initiate the transfers. I did not approve any changes to my account information. Most importantly, I reported the incident immediately after discovering it. The fact that a third-party payment platform such as XXXX was used does not change the fact that the underlying account access was unauthorized. After receiving notice of the denial, I contacted law enforcement again to follow up on the status of the investigation. During that conversation, I learned that a new detective had been assigned to the case. The detective informed me that little or no meaningful investigation had been conducted previously and that additional investigative steps would now be necessary. As a result, I was advised that the investigation would continue and that further time would be required before any conclusions could be reached. More recently, I received a letter from PNC Bank explaining the basis for the denial of my claim. The letter indicated that the bank relied on what it described as a historical pattern of use in determining that the transactions were authorized. I was extremely concerned and frustrated by this explanation because it does not address the key facts surrounding the account takeover. The critical issue is not whether I have used my account or XXXX in the past. The critical issue is that unauthorized access occurred, my phone number was changed without my permission, authentication codes were generated that I did not request, and fraudulent transactions were conducted while I was actively attempting to stop the unauthorized activity. These facts strongly suggest that my account security was compromised by someone other than myself. I subsequently contacted both PNC Bank and XXXX seeking additional information and assistance. Unfortunately, each organization directed me back to the other. XXXX advised that PNC Bank possesses the investigative information and account records. PNC Bank, meanwhile, emphasized that XXXX is a third-party service. As a result, I have been left without meaningful answers regarding who accessed my account, how the unauthorized changes occurred, where the funds were sent, and why my claim was denied despite the evidence that an account takeover occurred. I respectfully request a complete review of this matter. Specifically, I request that all records related to the investigation be reexamined, including account access logs, IP addresses, device information, phone number change records, authentication records, transaction details, and any evidence relied upon to conclude that the transactions were authorized. I also request that the bank consider the fact that I reported the fraud immediately, filed a police report, cooperated fully with all requests, and consistently maintained that I did not authorize these transactions. My objective is simple : to determine where my money went, identify the individual responsible for accessing my account, and recover the funds that were taken without my authorization. I believe the facts support my position that this was an unauthorized account takeover and not a transaction that I knowingly or willingly approved.

At each branch, employees went to the back area, came back, and said a manager was unavailable or that they could not authorize the withdrawal. I was not given a workable alternative, callback, written explanation, or meaningful resolution. Only after I said I would contact the CFPB did she place the call. She placed loss prevention on speakerphone while I was present. I personally heard the loss prevention representative say words to the effect of, Yes, he can withdraw it is up to you. I also heard the representative object to being on speakerphone and say words to the effect of, Dont have me on speakerphone. Despite what I heard, XXXX XXXX denied my withdrawal. During that interaction, the Wells Fargo employee also reviewed disputed amounts aloud and made comments that made me feel as though I was being treated like a criminal instead of an identity theft victim. She also told me the provisional credit was not your money, referring to funds Wells Fargo had credited during the dispute investigation. I believe that statement was false and misleading because provisional credit is supposed to be available to the consumer during the investigation period. Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding a pending account closure scheduled by WesBanco. The institution has communicated that my business banking relationship will be closed within approximately 30 days. This closure decision was represented as being based entirely on a specific internal allegation regarding conduct attributed to me. I dispute the accuracy of this allegation and do not accept it as fact. To my knowledge, the allegation is not supported by objective account activity, transactional records, or independently verifiable documentation. During the relevant period, I maintain residences in multiple locations and was residing abroad for an extended period consistent with that arrangement. I returned to Maryland on XX/XX/XXXX. During this period, I was not in a position to directly manage or immediately respond to banking communications or operational issues in real time. This is part of an established multi-residence living arrangement that necessarily limits immediate responsiveness to banking inquiries and does not reflect disengagement from the account relationship. Separately, during this same period, I experienced significant and unresolved issues with account access and transaction processing. These issues materially disrupted normal business banking operations, including my ability to reliably monitor, access, and manage funds and transactions in support of ongoing business obligations. This occured between approximately XX/XX/XXXX until XX/XX/XXXX, when I returned. I was out of the country before the service interruption. The alleged statement forming the basis of the closure is disputed in its entirety. The communication in question occurred with my spouse present in the vehicle, and the call was conducted on speaker for its duration. I do not believe the allegation reflects an accurate or reliable characterization of what occurred, and I am not aware of any objective documentation supporting the interpretation that has been attributed to me. Based on the information available to me, I understand the institutions decision to initiate closure to be based solely on this disputed allegation rather than on documented account behavior, transactional history, or objective financial risk indicators. There has been no clear presentation of account-based evidence demonstrating that normal banking activity or risk-based criteria support this adverse action. This pending closure and the underlying circumstances are causing and will continue to cause significant and potentially irreparable harm to my business operations, financial continuity, and professional reputation, given the reliance of ongoing business activities on uninterrupted access to banking services and the downstream impact of adverse banking determinations on third-party relationships. This complaint requests supervisory review limited to whether the pending closure is supported by verified and documented account activity, whether appropriate evidentiary standards were applied prior to initiating closure of an active business account, whether account access and transaction handling during the relevant period were properly managed and documented, and whether any internal determinations relied upon are substantiated by objective facts tied to account behavior rather than unverified assertions. Additionally, review is requested to determine whether the adverse action process reflects fair, consistent, and properly documented banking practices consistent with applicable regulatory expectations for business account relationships. The requested outcome is a written explanation of the factual and documented basis for the closure decision, identification of the specific account activity relied upon for the adverse action, a full review of account access and transaction handling during the relevant period, correction of any unsupported internal determinations if identified, and confirmation that any closure action is grounded in verified facts and consistent with fair banking standards.

I am submitting this complaint because Navy Federal Credit Union continues reporting multiple accounts that do not belong to me despite receiving notice of identity theft, an FTC Identity Theft Report, and multiple disputes. I do not own these accounts, I did not authorize these accounts, and I have never accepted responsibility for these accounts. Despite receiving documentation supporting my identity theft claim, Navy Federal Credit Union continues reporting the accounts and associated derogatory information, causing ongoing damage to my credit reports and financial reputation. This complaint concerns multiple Navy Federal Credit Union accounts that continue appearing on my credit reports as charge-offs, collection accounts, and accounts with extensive late payment histories. I discovered these accounts after reviewing my consumer reports and immediately disputed them because I did not recognize them. After discovering the accounts, I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report and submitted disputes to the credit bureaus and Navy Federal Credit Union. Despite these actions, the accounts continue to be reported. According to the prior CFPB complaint records, I repeatedly informed Navy Federal Credit Union that I do not own these accounts and that they are the result of identity theft. The accounts in question are reported with significant derogatory histories, including charge-offs, collections, and numerous late payments. The continued reporting of these accounts falsely suggests that I opened, used, and defaulted on Navy Federal Credit Union accounts when I did not. These inaccurate reports have significantly lowered my credit scores, damaged my financial standing, and created obstacles when applying for credit and other financial products. I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because I believe these accounts were opened or used without my authorization. Once an FTC Identity Theft Report is filed and submitted, federal law provides protections to consumers who are victims of identity theft. I expected Navy Federal Credit Union to review my identity theft claim, investigate the disputed accounts, and provide documentation proving that I personally opened and authorized the accounts. Instead, Navy Federal Credit Union continued reporting the accounts and associated derogatory information. According to Navy Federal Credit Union 's prior response, the company relied primarily on account history and payment activity to conclude that the accounts belonged to me. However, payment history does not establish ownership. The existence of payments on an account does not prove who opened the account, who authorized the account, or who benefited from the account. Identity theft frequently involves accounts that show payment activity before becoming delinquent. The key issue is not whether payments occurred. The key issue is whether I personally opened and authorized the accounts. I repeatedly requested documentation proving ownership. Specifically, I requested signed credit applications, original account opening records, identity verification records, signature records, account origination documentation, and records showing how Navy Federal Credit Union verified the identity of the person who opened the accounts. These are the types of records that would establish ownership. Despite my requests, Navy Federal Credit Union did not provide documentation proving that I personally opened the disputed accounts. The prior CFPB complaint specifically noted that billing statements and account summaries do not establish that a consumer opened or authorized an account. Instead of providing original account documentation, Navy Federal Credit Union relied on account histories and payment records. Those records may demonstrate activity on an account, but they do not prove ownership. They do not establish that I opened the accounts, authorized the accounts, received the proceeds, or personally benefited from the accounts. As noted in my prior disputes, I dispute ownership itself, not merely the payment history associated with the accounts. I also requested a complete Method of Verification regarding the disputed accounts. I asked Navy Federal Credit Union to explain how the accounts were verified, what systems were used, whether the review was manual or automated, who conducted the review, and what documents were examined during the investigation. According to the prior complaint documentation, Navy Federal Credit Union failed to provide a meaningful verification methodology, audit trail, explanation of how identity theft was ruled out, or confirmation of human review. This failure is significant because consumers have the right to understand how disputed information was investigated. A generic statement that an account belongs to a consumer is not sufficient. If Navy Federal Credit Union truly investigated my identity theft claim, it should be able to identify the records reviewed, the investigative steps taken, and the evidence used to determine that the accounts belong to me. To date, I have not received that information. Another major issue involves Navy Federal Credit Union 's continued reporting of the accounts after receiving my FTC Identity Theft Report. Under federal law, identity theft claims trigger specific obligations. Once a consumer provides an identity theft report and disputes ownership of an account, the furnisher and consumer reporting agencies are required to take appropriate action. My prior complaint specifically noted that Navy Federal Credit Union continued reporting the disputed accounts despite receiving notice of identity theft. I believe Navy Federal Credit Union failed to conduct a proper identity theft investigation. A proper investigation should include reviewing original account opening records, examining identity verification procedures, reviewing application information, reviewing signatures, analyzing IP address information when available, examining device information, reviewing contact information used at account opening, and determining whether the person who opened the accounts can be positively linked to me. Based on the documentation provided thus far, it does not appear that Navy Federal Credit Union performed this type of investigation. I am also concerned that Navy Federal Credit Union improperly shifted the burden of proof back onto me. I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, submitted disputes, and provided supporting information. After receiving these materials, the burden shifted to Navy Federal Credit Union to demonstrate that the accounts belong to me. Instead, the company continued to request additional information while failing to provide the documentation necessary to prove ownership. The prior complaint specifically raised concerns regarding improper burden shifting after an FTC Identity Theft Report had already been submitted. The continued reporting of these accounts has caused significant financial harm. The accounts appear as serious derogatory items on my credit reports and create the impression that I incurred debt and failed to repay it. As a result, my credit profile has been negatively affected, my credit scores have been reduced, and my ability to obtain favorable financing has been impaired. These consequences continue every month that the accounts remain on my credit reports. I also dispute the associated late payment histories reported in connection with these accounts. The late payments are derived from accounts that I do not recognize and did not authorize. If the accounts themselves are fraudulent or the result of identity theft, then the late payment histories associated with them are likewise inaccurate and should not continue appearing on my credit reports. Furthermore, Navy Federal Credit Union 's response does not adequately address why multiple disputed accounts continue appearing across different credit bureaus with varying derogatory histories. The prior complaint specifically raised concerns regarding duplicate and inconsistent reporting and requested explanations regarding why the accounts continued to appear despite active disputes. Those concerns remain unresolved. I respectfully request that this complaint be reviewed as a continuation of my ongoing effort to correct inaccurate information resulting from identity theft. I have consistently maintained that these accounts do not belong to me. I have consistently disputed ownership. I have consistently requested documentary proof establishing that I personally opened and authorized the accounts. Despite these efforts, Navy Federal Credit Union continues reporting the accounts. The resolution I seek is straightforward. I want Navy Federal Credit Union to provide competent documentary evidence proving that I personally opened and authorized each disputed account. This evidence should include signed applications, account opening documents, identity verification records, signature records, and any other documentation demonstrating that I knowingly entered into the agreements. If Navy Federal Credit Union can not provide such evidence, then the accounts should be deleted immediately. I also request removal of all associated derogatory information, including charge-off notations, collection reporting, 30-day late payments, 60-day late payments, 90-day late payments, and any other negative account history associated with the disputed accounts. Because I do not own these accounts and filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, the continued reporting of this information is inaccurate and harmful. I have acted in good faith throughout this process. I reviewed my credit reports, identified accounts that I did not recognize, filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, submitted disputes, responded to requests for information, and repeatedly requested proof of ownership. Despite these efforts, Navy Federal Credit Union continues reporting the disputed accounts without providing the evidence necessary to establish that they belong to me. For these reasons, I respectfully request that the CFPB require Navy Federal Credit Union to conduct a complete identity theft investigation, provide all supporting documentation relied upon in its determinations, and remove all accounts and derogatory information that can not be proven to belong to me. My goal is to ensure that my credit reports accurately reflect my true financial history and that fraudulent or identity theft-related information is removed immediately.

The hotel processed a refund of {$170.00} back to the same card on XX/XX/XXXX, at XXXX XXXX confirmed by the hotel 's folio and by the XXXX merchant transaction record ( both already provided to the bank ). The refund never appeared in my account. On or about XX/XX/XXXX, I called the bank by phone to notify it of this disputed transaction. My authorized representative also called the bank the same day, separately, on my behalf. The representatives on both calls handled by two different bank reps on the same day advised us NOT to file a formal dispute, stating that doing so would " make it take longer '' or " elongate the refund. '' This consistent advice, delivered to two separate callers by two different representatives on the same day, steered me away from formally invoking my Regulation E rights at the moment notice was actually given. The fact that the same advice was given by separate representatives on the same day suggests this was not an isolated rep error but a practice or scripted response. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( b ) ( 1 ), oral notice of a Reg E error triggers the bank 's investigation obligation. The bank may require written follow-up only if it informs the consumer of that requirement at the time of the oral notice which is the opposite of what the bank 's representatives did on XX/XX/XXXX. The 10-business-day window from the XX/XX/XXXX oral notice has now elapsed, and the bank has issued no provisional credit. The bank has subsequently stated, in email correspondence, that the dispute could take " 60120 days '' because the bank was " waiting on the merchant to respond. '' This response conflates two separate processes : the XXXX chargeback / back-end merchant settlement process ( which can run 60120 days ) and the consumer 's rights under Regulation E ( which require the bank to either complete its investigation within 10 business days or provisionally credit the disputed amount under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ). The 60120 day chargeback timeline is not a permissible basis to withhold provisional credit on the front end. The documentation already provided to the bank shows that the merchant issued the refund on XX/XX/XXXX, with an authorization number, token, and invoice number. The dispute is not about whether the merchant will refund the merchant has refunded. The question is where that refund went between the merchant 's processor and my account, which is precisely the type of error Regulation E provisional credit is designed to address during investigation. I am filing this complaint regarding three concerns : 1. The bank 's discouragement of a formal dispute filing on XX/XX/XXXX advice given consistently to two separate callers on the same day by different representatives. This pattern steered me away from exercising my Regulation E rights and may constitute a deceptive practice under UDAAP. I am specifically requesting that the Bureau ask the bank whether the " don't file/ it will take longer '' advice was a scripted, trained, or otherwise institutional response, as the consistency of the advice across two different reps on the same day suggests it was not an individual error. 2. The bank 's conflation of merchant chargeback timelines with Regulation E provisional credit obligations, which is being used as a stated reason to withhold provisional credit my account is entitled to under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ). 3. The bank 's failure to follow Regulation E error-resolution procedures, including the failure to disclose my right to a formal dispute at the time of the XX/XX/XXXX oral notice. Relief requested : ( a ) immediate provisional credit of {$170.00} to my account pending completion of the investigation, as required by 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ) ; ( b ) a written explanation of the bank 's Regulation E procedures and whether the XX/XX/XXXX " don't file '' advice reflects scripted or trained representative responses ; and ( c ) any further corrective action the Bureau deems appropriate. Documents available and previously provided to the bank : the hotel folio dated XX/XX/XXXX ; the XXXX XXXX Transaction Manager record confirming the XX/XX/XXXX refund authorization ; email correspondence with the bank 's representative.

Harris & Harris XXXX XXXX is reporting a collection account with a balance of {$390.00} allegedly associated with XXXX XXXX. I dispute the validity, accuracy, completeness, and ownership of this alleged debt and request a thorough investigation. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), furnishers of information are required to provide accurate and complete information to consumer reporting agencies. Consumer complaint narrative: * * Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint * * * * Company : * * Credit Corp Solutions , Inc. * * Balance Reported : * * {$570.00} * * Date Opened : * * XX/XX/year> * * Account Status : * * Open Collection Account * * Original Creditor : * * Not Reported/ Unknown * * Complaint * * I am filing this complaint against Credit Corp Solutions , Inc. regarding a collection account being reported on my consumer credit reports. Credit Corp Solutions is reporting a collection account with a balance of {$570.00}. However, the account information being furnished is incomplete because the original creditor is not identified. Without disclosure of the original creditor, I am unable to determine the origin, validity, ownership, or accuracy of the alleged debt. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), furnishers of information are required to provide accurate and complete information to consumer reporting agencies. Reporting a collection account without identifying the original creditor raises concerns regarding compliance with federal reporting requirements and the completeness of the information being furnished. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), upon receiving notice of a dispute, Credit Corp Solutions must conduct a reasonable investigation and review all relevant information before continuing to report the account. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692e and 1692f, debt collectors may not use false, deceptive, misleading, unfair, or unconscionable means to collect or report debts. Debt collectors must possess sufficient documentation establishing the validity of the debt, the amount claimed, and their authority to collect it. I dispute the validity, ownership, and accuracy of this alleged debt and request that Credit Corp Solutions provide : 1. Identification of the original creditor. 2. The original account number associated with the alleged debt. 3. Documentation proving I am legally responsible for the debt. 4. Documentation demonstrating Credit Corp Solutions ' authority to collect the debt. 5. Documentation showing the complete chain of assignment, transfer, or sale of the account. 6. A complete payment history and accounting supporting the balance being reported. 7. Documentation establishing the date of first delinquency. 8. Verification that all information reported to consumer reporting agencies complies with the FCRA and Metro 2 reporting standards. The CFPB has repeatedly emphasized that debt collectors and furnishers must maintain reasonable procedures to ensure the accuracy and integrity of information furnished to consumer reporting agencies. If Credit Corp Solutions can not validate and verify this account, continued reporting may constitute the furnishing of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information. * * Requested Resolution * * I request that Credit Corp Solutions conduct a thorough investigation and provide complete documentation supporting the validity, ownership, and accuracy of this alleged debt. If the account can not be fully validated and verified, I request immediate deletion of the account from all consumer reporting agencies. I further request correction of any inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information currently being reported and written confirmation of the results of the investigation.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding the handling of disputed transactions funded through my Capital One checking account. Prior to sending the payments, I exchanged messages regarding the ticket sale and received payment instructions. I have screenshots documenting the conversations, the ticket-sale arrangements, and the payment instructions provided to me. I want to make it clear that these payments were not gifts, donations, or personal transfers. I did not send this money to friends or family, nor did I voluntarily give the money away with no expectation of receiving anything in return. The payments were made specifically to purchase tickets that the individuals were advertising and selling. One individual received {$220.00} via XXXX, and another received {$450.00} via XXXX XXXX, for a total loss of {$670.00}. Although the payments were sent via XXXX and XXXX XXXX, the funds originated from, and were withdrawn directly from, my Capital One checking account. The payment platforms were simply the method used to transfer the funds. The underlying source of the money was my Capital One checking account. The individuals represented that they had tickets available for sale and accepted my payments for those tickets. After receiving my money, they failed to provide the tickets as promised and did not issue refunds. They kept the funds while failing to deliver the product that was the basis of the transactions. I have screenshots showing that both payments were directly connected to ticket purchases. These communications establish that the money was sent in exchange for tickets and not as gifts or voluntary transfers. The evidence demonstrates that these were transactions for a product that was promised but never delivered. As soon as it became clear that I would not receive the tickets, I sought assistance through the proper channels. I contacted both XXXX and Capital One and filed disputes regarding the transactions. I provided the available information, including evidence showing that the payments were made for tickets that were never delivered. Despite my efforts and supporting documentation, both claims were denied. My concern is that the dispute process appears to have focused primarily on the payment methods used rather than on the underlying facts of the transactions. The critical issue is that these payments were made to purchase tickets, not to send gifts or personal transfers. The recipients accepted payment for tickets they claimed to be selling but failed to provide them. I was scammed. The individuals accepted payment for tickets they represented they were selling, failed to provide the tickets, and retained my money. I have documentation supporting the transactions, including communications showing the agreements to purchase tickets and the expectation that tickets would be delivered after payment. I am requesting a thorough review of this matter, including consideration of all supporting documentation, screenshots, and communications. I also request a detailed explanation of how the evidence was evaluated and why reimbursement was denied despite evidence showing that the payments were made for tickets that were never delivered. A fair consumer protection process should consider the purpose of the transaction and the available evidence, not solely the payment method used. In this case, the available evidence demonstrates that I paid a total of {$670.00} for tickets that I never received and suffered a financial loss as a result. Thank you for your review of this matter.

Consumer complaint narrative: I opened a savings account with E * TRADE on XX/XX/year>, and funded it with a {$20000.00} wire transfer on XX/XX/year>. A few weeks later, my account was unexpectedly restricted. At the time, I was dealing with several personal matters and was unable to immediately complete the requested verification process. However, on XX/XX/year>, I contacted E * TRADE and was instructed to submit two photos : ( 1 ) a photo of my driver 's license and ( 2 ) a photo of myself holding the driver 's license, ensuring that my face remained fully visible. I carefully followed all instructions, making sure the ID was clear and legible, all corners were visible, and my face was not obstructed. After more than a week passed without any communication, my account remained restricted. When I called on XX/XX/year>, a customer service representative informed me that E * TRADE does not notify customers whether submitted documents have been reviewed, approved, or denied. This was surprising, as I have never encountered a verification process that provides no status updates whatsoever. During that call, I was informed that I also needed to submit proof of address. I promptly provided a recent utility bill. I was further advised that document reviews are handled by a back-office team that can not be contacted directly and that reviews typically take three to four business days. After waiting another week with no updates, I called again on XX/XX/year>, to check the status of my account. To my surprise, I was told that I once again needed to submit a photo of my driver 's license and a photo of myself holding the license. Confused as to why I was being asked to repeat the original verification step, I asked whether my previous submission had been denied and, if so, for what reason. The representative stated that she could not provide any explanation and that I simply needed to resubmit the documents. At this point, I am extremely frustrated by the process. More than a month has passed since I first attempted to verify my account, yet I continue to receive new verification requests without any explanation as to why prior submissions were insufficient. I am also unable to speak with anyone who can provide meaningful assistance or insight into the status of my case. Compounding the issue, I opened this account as part of an E * TRADE promotional offer that requires the account to remain in good standing in order to receive the advertised bonus after the qualifying requirements are met. As a result of these ongoing restrictions and delays, I have been unable to access my funds and may ultimately be disqualified from receiving the bonus despite having fulfilled the funding requirements. Whether these issues stem from poor internal processes or something else, the outcome has been the same : I have been deprived of access to my funds while being subjected to an opaque and seemingly endless verification process.

I am requesting validation of this debt because I have not been provided sufficient documentation proving the debt 's validity, ownership, or accuracy. I request that Jefferson Capital provide : 1. A copy of the original agreement or contract creating the alleged obligation with XXXX. 2. Documentation proving I am legally responsible for the debt. 3. Verification that all information furnished to consumer reporting agencies complies with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and XXXX XXXX reporting standards. 9. Copies of any records used to verify the account during prior dispute investigations. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has repeatedly stated that debt collectors and furnishers must maintain adequate records to ensure the accuracy and integrity of information furnished to consumer reporting agencies. If Jefferson Capital can not provide competent evidence validating the debt, ownership, and balance being reported, continued reporting may constitute the furnishing of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable information. * * Requested Resolution * * I request that Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC conduct a thorough investigation and provide complete documentation supporting the validity, ownership, and accuracy of the alleged debt. Copies of any records used to verify the account during prior dispute investigations. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has emphasized that debt collectors and furnishers must maintain adequate records to ensure the accuracy and integrity of information furnished to consumer reporting agencies. Despite notifying the servicer of my status, they have refused to provide loan documentation, payment history, or other requested information, in violation of 12 C.F.R. 1024.36 and 1024.38 ( servicing policies and procedures ). I was never provided with any foreclosure notices, including Notice of Default or Notice of Trustee Sale. I only became aware of the foreclosure when I contacted the servicer myself. After informing the servicer that I was actively attempting to sell the property, I was told that a third party had entered the property and was there to change the locks without my knowledge or consent. Additionally, the servicer has failed to comply with obligations to maintain accurate information and provide continuity of contact under 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 and 1024.40. My probate attorney has issued a cease and desist letter. The servicer has ignored this and continues to withhold information and proceed without proper notice. These actions constitute potential violations of RESPA ( 12 U.S.C. 2605 ) and its implementing Regulation X, including but not limited to failures regarding successors in interest, requests for information, and foreclosure protections. I demand the following : 1. Immediate recognition of my status as a confirmed successor in interest. 2. Full loan documentation, including note, deed of trust, and complete payment history. 3. Proof of all foreclosure-related notices, including dates, addresses used, and method of delivery. 4. Confirmation of the current legal status of the property, including whether a foreclosure sale has occurred. 5. Immediate suspension of all foreclosure activity pending investigation of these violations. This matter involves potential wrongful foreclosure, failure of required notice, and unlawful interference with property rights, and requires urgent regulatory review.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Truist Bank 's handling of my fraud claim, Claim Number XXXX, and its decision to reverse the provisional credit that was issued during its investigation. During the call, the individual stated that I had missed jury duty, had multiple criminal charges pending against me, and would be arrested if I did not immediately comply with his instructions. The caller provided personal information about me, including my address and Social Security number, and even arranged for a call displaying the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX phone number to appear on my phone as " verification '' of his identity. As a result of these threats, false representations, and fear of immediate arrest, I sent a total of {$3400.00}. I later learned that I had been the victim of a scam and immediately reported the matter. I also filed a police report with the XXXX XXXX Police Department under Report Number XXXX. On XX/XX/year>, Truist issued provisional credit while investigating my claim. Based on the information available, I believed the bank understood that I had been the victim of fraud and was conducting a fair review of the circumstances. However, on XX/XX/year>, I received a letter informing me that Truist had concluded its investigation and would be reversing the provisional credit. According to the letter, Truist determined that I had somehow received a " benefit '' from the transaction. This conclusion is both confusing and deeply concerning. At no point did I receive any benefit from this transaction. I did not receive goods, services, property, financial gain, or any other value in exchange for the {$3400.00} that was taken from me. The funds were sent solely because I was deceived by an individual impersonating law enforcement and acting under false pretenses. The money was obtained through fraud and coercion. After receiving Truist 's decision, I contacted the bank seeking clarification regarding how it determined that I received a benefit from the transaction. Unfortunately, I was unable to obtain a meaningful explanation. I was informed by a XXXX XXXX that there was essentially nothing that could be done regardless of who I spoke with, including supervisors. As a customer seeking answers regarding a significant financial loss, I found this response dismissive, frustrating, and inconsistent with good customer service practices. My complaint is not simply about the loss of funds. My concern is that Truist has failed to adequately explain the basis for its determination while simultaneously reversing a provisional credit that had been issued during the investigation. If Truist believes I received a benefit from this transaction, I believe it should be able to clearly identify and document what that alleged benefit was. To date, no such explanation has been provided. I am requesting that Truist to provide all documentation and evidence relied upon in reaching its conclusion that I received a benefit from the transaction, which they have still failed to do so as well as explain specifically what benefit Truist believes I received. And Reconsider its decision to reverse the provisional credit and reimburse the full {$3400.00} that was lost as a result of this scam. As a long-standing customer with no prior fraud claims, I believe I have acted in good faith throughout this process and have provided all requested documentation, including a police report and supporting evidence.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting a complaint about a high-cost open-end line of credit serviced by NetCredit and issued through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXI opened the account in XX/XX/XXXX. The agreement charges a 10 % Cash Advance Fee each time funds are requested, meaning the amount deposited is less than the amount added to the account balance. For example, a later statement shows a {$400.00} cash advance produced only {$360.00} in advance proceeds, and a {$150.00} cash advance produced only {$130.00} in advance proceeds, while the full {$400.00} and {$150.00} were added to the account balance. In addition to the cash advance fee, the company also charges a recurring Statement Balance Fee every billing cycle while there is a cash advance balance over {$25.00}. My billing cycle appears to be every XXXX weeks. This recurring fee is separate from the 10 % fee charged when money is advanced. The statements combine these charges under Total Fees Charged, which makes it difficult for me to determine how much I paid in one-time cash advance fees versus recurring biweekly statement balance fees. My statements show that I have been charged very large amounts in fees despite the credit limit being around {$1000.00}. XXXX statement from XX/XX/XXXX shows total fees charged in XXXX of {$540.00}. A XX/XX/XXXX statement shows total fees charged in XXXX of {$1000.00}. A XX/XX/XXXX statement shows total fees charged in XXXX to date of {$290.00}. Together, the statements I reviewed show approximately {$1900.00} in total fees charged across XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX to date. The problem is that the recurring biweekly XXXX XXXX Fees appear to be consuming my payments and income without meaningfully reducing the balance. For example, a XX/XX/XXXX statement showed no new cash advances during that billing cycle, but a {$36.00} Statement Balance Fee was still charged. A XX/XX/XXXX statement also showed no new cash advances during that billing cycle, but a {$32.00} Statement Balance Fee was charged. This suggests a significant portion of the total fees are recurring balance fees, not just the one-time 10 % fees charged when funds are advanced. I believe the companys fee structure is confusing, harmful, and potentially unfair or abusive because the account can remain near the credit limit while recurring fees continue to be charged every XXXX weeks. The year-to-date fee totals do not clearly separate one-time cash advance fees from recurring statement balance fees, making it difficult for a consumer to understand how much of their payments are going toward principal versus repeated finance charges. I am asking the CFPB to review whether this high-cost open-end line of credit, including the 10 % cash advance fee and recurring biweekly Statement Balance Fee, complies with applicable consumer financial protection laws and whether the disclosures and statements adequately explain the true cost of the product.

Weekend Due Date Law : My payment due date fell on Friday, XX/XX/XXXX. Because the subsequent days ( XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX ) fell on a weekend when the bank does not process manual payment transfers, under federal law ( Regulation Z ), a payment made on the next business day must be treated as timely. Therefore, making the payment on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX was legally on time. 2. Timely Payment Attempt & Confirmation : On Monday, XXXX XXXXthe very first business day following the weekendI called the bank 's automated system to pay. Because the system was down, I was routed to a live representative. I provided my banking information, and the representative explicitly confirmed the payment had successfully processed. She never stated the payment was late or would incur a fee. 3. Proactive Consumer Follow-Up vs. Bank Inaction : Fifth Third Bank never reached out to me regarding any issues with this transaction. Instead, over the next several days, I was the one who proactively called the bank multiple times out of concern that the funds had not yet left my account. During these calls, I explicitly stated that I was worried about a late fee. Representatives repeatedly told me, " Don't worry about it. You will not get a late fee charge, '' assuring me the system was just processing it. 4. Admitted Bank Typo and Forced Re-payment : When the payment finally failed completely, I called again and escalated the issue to a manager. The bank initially claimed they " didn't know what happened, '' but after auditing the call logs, a representative explicitly admitted to me that the first employee had incorrectly entered my routing number. Because of the bank 's data-entry typo, the original, confirmed transaction could never be processed. I was forced to provide my routing and account numbers all over again to remake the payment from scratchat which point the bank hit me with a late fee. Customer service department is penalizing me for a timeline delay caused entirely by their own staff. I initiated the payment on time on XX/XX/XXXX, followed up on multiple days to fix a problem I didn't cause, and had to manually reissue the payment due to an employee 's data-entry error. While the bank rightfully waived the " reversal fee '' because the mistake was their. refusing to waive the resulting late fee is unacceptable. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: [ XXXX XXXX ] [ XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX [ XXXX XXXX, TN XXXX ] [ XX/XX/year> ] Via Certified Mail [ National credit systems ] [ XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ] [ XXXX Ga XXXX ] RE : Demand for Debt Validation and Notice of Dispute Account Number : [ XXXX } To Whom It May Concern : I am in receipt of your attempts to collect the alleged debt referenced above. To date, your company has failed to provide any competent evidence demonstrating that I have a legal obligation to pay this debt. A mere balance statement, internal records, or unverified account information does not constitute validation. Pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692g, I request that you provide the following : 1. The name and address of the original creditor. 2. A complete accounting of the alleged debt, including principal, interest, fees, and any other charges. 3. Copies of any contract, agreement, application, or instrument bearing my signature that creates a legal obligation. 4. Documentation establishing your authority to collect this debt. 5. Documentation demonstrating the chain of assignment or ownership if the debt has been sold or transferred. 6. Proof that the alleged debt is within the applicable statute of limitations. 7. Evidence that your company possesses legally admissible records linking me to this account. Furthermore, pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, if you are furnishing information regarding this account to any consumer reporting agency, you are required to report complete and accurate information. Reporting a debt that can not be substantiated or verified may constitute a violation of federal law. If this account appears on any consumer credit report, I demand that you conduct a reasonable investigation and provide the evidence supporting the accuracy of the reported information. Failure to provide such evidence may demonstrate that the account is being reported without proper verification. If you can not provide the requested documentation, you should immediately cease collection efforts and remove any information related to this alleged debt from all consumer reporting agencies to which you have furnished data. This letter is not a refusal to pay, nor is it an acknowledgment of liability. It is a formal dispute and request for validation. Nothing in this correspondence shall be construed as an admission of responsibility for the alleged debt. I expect your written response within the time permitted by applicable law. Sincerely, [ XXXX XXXX ]

I am filing this complaint against the First National Bank of Omaha due to a systemic web interface defect, direct employee misinformation, and an unjust refusal to correct a corporate error that combined to strip me of an advertised promotional balance transfer offer, causing me clear financial detriment. 1. I was the recipient of a recent Balance Transfer ( BT ) Offer from FNBO that could be redeemed online or via promotional checks to my bank account. This complaint provides details of a systemic digital glitch and the bank 's refusal to address their error that has caused me financial distress. 2. On XXXX, I attempted to utilize the BT online through the FNBO portal to move funds to my XXXX XXXX checking account. The banks online transfer portal requested my " Bank Name '' and " Account Number '' ( see attachment of what it looks like from the consumer end ). Because I could have done the same thing via check and was using the online platform just for convenience, I assumed there was no problem in doing online what the bank was clearly ok with me doing via check. 3. The transaction went through. Nothing was flagged. I received a confirmation #, the transaction was tagged as " completed '' ( see attached ) and the debit was posted on my FNBO account ( see attached ). 4. I proactively called customer service of FNBO on XXXX at XXXX XXXX. I explicitly informed the agent that if there was any issue with the online transfer, I wanted to cancel it immediately so I could deposit my physical promotional checks before the expiration deadline of XXXX. The agent reviewed my account, saw the transaction marked as validly charged and " Completed '' on their end, and explicitly assured me the transfer was successful. The agent directed me not to use my physical checks. 5. I relied on this explicit corporate assurance to my detriment, allowing my physical checks and the promotional deadline to expire. 6. On XXXX, I checked my FNBO account and found the transfer had been reversed ( see attached ). I called FNBO, and asked to speak to a supervisor. I told her everything that is mentioned in 1-5 above. But that supervisor claimed XXXX XXXX had declined that transfer and there was nothing that FNBO could do. 7. I checked with XXXX XXXX. They do not even have a record of such a transfer, nor does it show up in any form ( such as a decline or error ) on the XXXX XXXX account. They told me that the error had occurred because the FNBO site was set up only for a credit card to credit card type transaction and completely omitted a field for a " Routing Number. '' A standard ACH transfer to a checking account, savings account or line of credit requires a routing number, so this design defect caused the system to erroneously attempt to process the transaction as a card-to-card network push. The receiving bank ( XXXX XXXX ) confirmed to me that because of this incorrect formatting, the transaction never even reached their ACH network to be processed or evaluated. 8. Note that quite apart from my own issues, there is a clear general error on that portal. The site claims the consumer can " Move higher interest debt from credit cards or loan accounts at another institution to this account for a lower interest rate to reduce interest charges. '' But even if that higher interest loan account had been a LOC issued by a bank, and not a checking account, the transaction would have failed because of the same error mentioned earlier. By providing a broken digital mechanism for a balance transfer and actively misinforming me so that I missed my opportunity to use a working alternative and had to take other loans at worse terms, the bank has engaged in unfair and deceptive practices. The bank possesses the administrative capability to grant a " Promotional Exception '' to remedy employee and systemic errors, but has rigidly refused to do so. Desired Resolution : I request that the bank correct this processing and administrative error by honoring the original promotional terms of a 7.99 % rate in perpetuity. I ask that they manually process a promotional check or manual ACH deposit to my XXXX XXXX checking account under those exact original terms by the end of XX/XX/year>.

Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint Issue : Deferred Interest Financing / Credit Card Account ( Comenity Bank Arhaus Credit Card ) I am filing this complaint regarding a deferred-interest promotional financing offer administered by Comenity Bank through the Arhaus credit card program. While I understand and acknowledge that I agreed to the promotional financing terms, I believe Comenity 's notification and disclosure practices surrounding the expiration of the promotion were inadequate and resulted in an unfair financial outcome. In 2024, I financed approximately {$8000.00} of furniture through an Arhaus credit card promotional offer that provided deferred interest if the balance was paid in full within XXXX years. Throughout the entire promotional period, I maintained an excellent payment history, made every required payment on time, and never became delinquent on the account. For approximately 24 months, I consistently made my monthly payments and remained in good standing. Unfortunately, after the promotional period expired, Comenity assessed {$7100.00} in retroactive interest because the remaining balance had not been paid in full by the promotional expiration date. My primary concern is not that the deferred-interest provision existed. Rather, it is the manner in which Comenity communicated the approaching expiration of the promotion and the severe consequences associated with missing the deadline. I had elected to receive paperless statements. The only notice of the approaching promotional expiration appears to have been included within my monthly statements. I did not receive a separate email, text message, phone call, secure message, or other prominent communication specifically warning that the promotional period was ending and that failure to pay the remaining balance in full would result in more than {$7000.00} of retroactive interest charges. Given the significant financial consequences involved, I believe consumers should receive clear, direct, and proactive notifications before deferred-interest charges are triggered. A two-year promotional period is a lengthy timeframe, and it is reasonable that consumers may lose track of an expiration date despite consistently making payments and maintaining their accounts in good standing. Importantly, I had both the ability and intention to pay the remaining balance. Had I received a clear warning explaining that the promotional period was ending and that a {$7100.00} interest charge would be assessed, I would have immediately paid the balance in full. At the time the promotional period expired, my remaining balance was approximately {$6000.00}. Following expiration of the promotion, Comenity assessed {$7100.00} in retroactive interestan amount that exceeded the remaining balance owed. While I understand this may be consistent with the contractual terms of a deferred-interest promotion, the outcome appears disproportionate given my payment history and the fact that I had successfully maintained the account for XXXX years without a single late payment. Additionally, my furniture was not delivered until XX/XX/year>, yet the promotional financing period began in XX/XX/year>. As a result, the promotional period expired before I had even possessed and used the merchandise for a full XXXX years. While this may be permitted under the financing agreement, it contributed to confusion regarding the true duration of the promotion from a consumer perspective. After discovering the retroactive interest charge, I immediately contacted customer service and escalated the matter to management. During that conversation, I was informed that I had an excellent payment history and was considered a valued customer. However, I was also told there was no mechanism available to review, reverse, reduce, or otherwise reconsider the {$7100.00} interest chargeeven if I immediately paid the remaining balance in full. I am not disputing that I agreed to the financing terms. Rather, I am requesting a fair resolution based on my strong payment history, the lack of meaningful advance notification regarding the promotional expiration, and the disproportionate nature of a {$7100.00} interest assessment resulting from a missed deadline after XXXX years of timely payments. Thank you for your review of this matter.

On XX/XX/XXXX, with my account now overdue, I reached out via chat once again trusting I would now be eligible for a medical crisis repayment plan. This time I was connected with XXXX ( AI? ) and then with a Goldman Sachs specialist named XXXX. Consumer complaint narrative: In early 2026, I was working with Federal First Lending to secure a mortgage. Therefore, I am demanding the immediate and permanent deletion of the entire XXXXDepartment of Ed tradeline ( Account ending in XXXX ) from my XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX credit reports. Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/year>, while traveling through XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, I was approached by an employee of a XXXX XXXX identified as XXXX XXXX. I was subjected to an extremely high-pressure sales presentation while attempting to board my flight home. During this encounter, I repeatedly stated that I needed to leave for my flight. However, multiple employees continued to pressure me to remain. Prices were not clearly disclosed before the transactions were processed. The products were never shown to me before purchase. Products were applied to my face and I was instructed to sit while they dried. The products were then packaged and placed into bags without my being shown what was being purchased. I did not knowingly agree to purchase more than {$24000.00} worth of skincare products and beauty devices. Three transactions were charged to my Chase credit card on XX/XX/year> : {$7200.00} {$9300.00} {$7400.00} Total disputed amount : approximately {$24000.00}. One employee ultimately escorted me to my gate carrying one of the bags while my family members were hearing final boarding announcements for me. The circumstances were confusing, intimidating, and did not allow me to make an informed purchasing decision. After returning home, I disputed the charges with Chase and provided detailed written statements, photographs of the products, supporting documentation, and additional evidence. I explained that prices were not properly disclosed, that the products were not shown to me before purchase, and that I believed the transactions resulted from deceptive and misleading sales practices. Chase initially denied the dispute. After I submitted additional evidence, Chase reopened the dispute. I provided further documentation, including photographs of the products, packaging, labeling, evidence of similar public complaints involving this merchant, information regarding FDA warning letters involving similar product branding and medical marketing claims, and other information relevant to the representations made during the sale. Despite reopening the dispute and reviewing the additional materials, Chase denied the dispute again. In its denial letter, Chase stated that I may have a valid complaint with the merchant but nevertheless concluded that the transactions were valid and would remain my responsibility. In addition, I was informed by a Chase representative that there had been an attempted charge or suspicious activity of approximately {$1900.00} associated with the same merchant group or location that Chase had detected and credited. Different Chase representatives later provided conflicting explanations regarding this transaction. One representative stated it was suspicious activity that Chase caught, while another representative stated it was a merchant credit but could not explain what it related to. This raised additional concerns regarding the security of my payment information and the accuracy of Chase 's investigation. I also experienced multiple issues with Chase 's handling of the dispute, including conflicting information from representatives, dispute-related documents that Chase stated were mailed but were never received, and uncertainty regarding the impact of the disputed {$24000.00} balance on my credit while the dispute was pending. I am requesting that the CFPB review Chase 's handling of this dispute and determine whether Chase conducted a reasonable investigation of the evidence I submitted. I am also requesting that Chase provide all documents, merchant responses, receipts, and evidence relied upon in denying my claim. I do not believe Chase adequately addressed the evidence demonstrating that these transactions occurred under deceptive and misleading circumstances, without informed consent regarding the products and prices involved, and under significant pressure while I was attempting to board an international flight. I respectfully request assistance in obtaining a fair review of this matter.

Consumer complaint narrative: CFPB SUPPLEMENTAL RESPONSE TO GOLDMAN SACHS BANK USA Apple Card Account Ending in XXXX XXXXXXXX I am submitting this supplemental response to Goldman Sachs Bank USAs CFPB response and continued position that no banking error occurred in connection with the disputed ACH payment transactions associated with my Apple Card account. I am not requesting a goodwill adjustment. I am not disputing that I remain responsible for the Apple Card balance. I am disputing the derogatory 30-day late payment reporting because Goldman Sachs has not established that the failed ACH payments were caused by consumer fault. Goldman Sachs position appears to be that because the payments were returned as No Account/Unable to Locate Account, and because I entered the payment information through Apple XXXX , the resulting late payment was properly reported. That conclusion is unsupported. A returned ACH payment does not automatically establish consumer-caused nonpayment. A return code explains why a payment did not post. It does not, by itself, prove who caused the payment failure. Goldman Sachs response states that the payments were rejected by the financial institution for No Account/Unable to Locate Account. However, Goldman Sachs never states that I entered an incorrect routing number. Goldman Sachs never states that I entered an incorrect account number. Goldman Sachs never states that I used an account that was not mine. Goldman Sachs never states that I lacked sufficient funds, stopped payment, refused payment, revoked authorization, or failed to authorize payment. Goldman Sachs has only established that the payment failed. Goldman Sachs has not established that I caused the failure. NEWLY DISCOVERED INFORMATION REGARDING ACH RETURN CODE R03 I am attaching ACH return-code documentation concerning R03 No Account/Unable to Locate Account. The R03 return reason does not mean insufficient funds. It does not mean the consumer refused to pay. It does not mean the consumer stopped payment. It does not mean the consumer revoked authorization. It does not mean the consumer intentionally failed to pay. R03 means the account number structure is valid and passes validation, but the account number either does not correspond to the individual identified in the entry or the designated account is not open. That distinction is critical. Goldman Sachs is attempting to use the R03 return as though it proves consumer fault. It does not. An R03 return may involve an account-location issue, name-matching issue, account-formatting issue, savings/share ID issue, transmission issue, routing issue, or other ACH communication problem between institutions. Goldman Sachs has not produced the ACH transmission data showing what account number, routing number, account type, name field, or payment-entry information it transmitted to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Bank XXXX Without that information, Goldman Sachs can not reasonably conclude that the return was caused by me. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ACCOUNT XXXX XXXX XXXX also attaching XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX account documentation. XXXX XXXX records confirm that the XXXX XXXX account ending in XXXX exists, belongs to me, and is a savings account. XXXX XXXX documentation also identifies the account number for direct deposits and electronic withdrawals. This evidence is directly relevant because Goldman Sachs response relies on No Account/Unable to Locate Account, yet XXXX XXXX documentation confirms that the account was real and designated for electronic withdrawals. If Goldman Sachs contends that XXXX XXXX rejected the payment because the account did not correspond to the individual identified in the ACH entry, Goldman Sachs must produce the ACH entry showing exactly what name, account number, routing number, account type, and other identifying information was transmitted. If Goldman Sachs contends that the account was not open or not eligible for ACH transactions, Goldman Sachs must reconcile that claim with XXXX XXXX account documentation showing that the account existed and was designated for electronic withdrawals. GOLDMAN SACHS CUSTOMER AGREEMENT DOES NOT LIMIT PAYMENTS TO CHECKING ACCOUNTS ONLY I am also attaching the Apple Card Customer Agreement. The Apple Card Customer Agreement permits electronic payments from a bank account with a financial institution located in the United States. It defines such an account as a Payment Source Account. The agreement does not state that only checking accounts may be used for payment. It does not prohibit the use of a savings account as a Payment Source Account. Therefore, Goldman Sachs can not shift responsibility to me merely because the XXXX XXXX account was a savings account. XXXX XXXX documentation confirms that the savings account had an account number designated for electronic withdrawals, and Goldman Sachs own agreement does not limit Payment Source Accounts to checking accounts only. THE CAN NOT BE PROCESSED LANGUAGE DOES NOT RESOLVE CREDIT-REPORTING FAULT Goldman Sachs may attempt to rely on language in the Apple Card Customer Agreement stating that an account may be considered in default if the Minimum Payment Due is returned unpaid or can not be processed. That language does not resolve the credit-reporting issue. There is a difference between treating a returned payment as unpaid for internal account-servicing purposes and furnishing a derogatory 30-day late payment to XXXX XXXX and XXXX. I am not disputing that Goldman Sachs may internally treat a returned payment as unpaid. I am disputing Goldman Sachs decision to furnish a derogatory late payment when it has not established that the payment failure was caused by consumer fault. A consumer should not be punished with derogatory credit reporting because Goldman Sachs, Apple XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, or the ACH network could not match, locate, transmit, or process account information when the consumer provided valid payment information. Goldman Sachs can not rely solely on returned unpaid or can not be processed to shift responsibility to the consumer. If Goldman Sachs contends that the late payment was accurately reported, Goldman Sachs must identify the specific consumer-caused error that resulted in the failed payment. Goldman Sachs has not done so. GOLDMAN SACHS RESPONSE DOES NOT SAY THE CONSUMER WAS RESPONSIBLE Goldman Sachs CFPB response states that no Bank error occurred. Goldman Sachs also states that the payments were returned by the customers financial institution for No Account/Unable to Locate Account. But Goldman Sachs response does not state that I caused the payment failure. Goldman Sachs does not identify incorrect information entered by me. Goldman Sachs does not state that the account was not mine. Goldman Sachs does not state that I lacked funds. Goldman Sachs does not state that I stopped payment. Goldman Sachs does not state that I revoked authorization. Goldman Sachs does not state that I refused to pay. Goldman Sachs is attempting to prove only that Goldman Sachs was not at fault. That is not the same as proving consumer fault. There is a third possibility : the payment failure resulted from an ACH account-matching, account-formatting, savings/share ID, transmission, routing, or banking communication issue between institutions that was not caused by the consumer. That distinction matters because derogatory credit reporting should reflect consumer payment behavior. It should not punish a consumer for an unresolved banking communication issue between financial institutions. GOLDMAN SACHS RESPONSE IS ALSO INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT Goldman Sachs CFPB response states that the account was reported accurately. However, Goldman Sachs also states that XXXX XXXX and XXXX were not reporting the payment history correctly and that Goldman Sachs submitted a request to update the payment history. That admission is significant. If the credit reporting agencies were not reporting the payment history correctly, Goldman Sachs must identify exactly what was incorrect, what update was requested, and whether the disputed 30-day late payment was deleted, moved, modified, or otherwise changed. Goldman Sachs can not simultaneously maintain that the reporting was accurate while also acknowledging that all three credit bureaus were not reporting the payment history correctly. REQUEST FOR RELIEF I respectfully request that Goldman Sachs Bank USA be required to : 1. Delete the disputed 30-day late payment from XXXX XXXX, and XXXX. 2. Produce the ACH return records for the disputed payments, including the specific return codes, ACH trace numbers, return files, XXXX records, and payment-processing logs. 3. Produce the ACH transmission data showing the routing number, account number, account type, name field, and identifying information transmitted to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX Bank. 4. Produce all records supporting Goldman Sachs claim that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX Bank rejected the transactions for No Account/Unable to Locate Account. 5. Identify whether Goldman Sachs transmitted the XXXX XXXX account as checking or savings. 6. Explain how Goldman Sachs determined that the failed payments were caused by consumer fault rather than an account-location, account-matching, share ID, routing, transmission, or banking communication issue. 7. Explain what XXXX XXXX, and XXXX were allegedly reporting incorrectly and identify the exact correction Goldman Sachs submitted to each bureau. 8. Produce all records supporting Goldman Sachs conclusion that no banking error occurred. 9. Produce the complete notes, recordings, and internal findings associated with Case No. XXXX and all related cases. Again, I am not requesting a goodwill adjustment. I am requesting deletion of the 30-day late payment because Goldman Sachs has not established that the failed ACH payments resulted from consumer-caused nonpayment. Goldman Sachs has shown only that the payments failed. Goldman Sachs has not shown that I caused the failure. A consumer should not receive a derogatory 30-day late payment because financial institutions could not match, locate, transmit, or process account information within the ACH system when the consumer provided valid payment information and the payment failure was not NSF, lack of funds, stop payment, unauthorized payment, or refusal to pay.

The collector 's claim rests on a misleading characterization of California law. The DMV record the collector itself provided ( dated XX/XX/XXXX ) confirms that the registered owner ( R/O ) remains a third party, not me the title transfer was never completed. Rather than resolve the discrepancy between the unilateral Release of Liability filing and the actual registered ownership, the collector 's notice presents a misleading summary of California Civil Code 3068.2 ( d ), suggesting that a Release of Liability filed without any title transfer overrides legal title. It does so by omitting key statutory requirements. Because title was never transferred and ownership remained with the third party, there is no valid basis to hold me personally liable for charges arising from this vehicle. I pointed out this defect directly in my dispute letter, yet the collector continued to pursue me on the same flawed basis without ever resolving it. 3. Despite receiving both written disputes and notice that I have legal representation, the collector did not cease direct contact. On XX/XX/XXXX more than five months after my second dispute letter I received an automated collection text message from ( XXXX ) XXXX stating : " [ XXXX ], final notice : limited time to arrange payment for towing/storage fees on your XXXX XXXX XXXX . Call immediately, ref acct # XXXX. Reply Stop to opt-out. '' I have a screenshot of this message. I never provided my cell phone number to this collector. I do not know how they obtained it, and I never consented to being contacted by automated text message at this number. Why this is a problem : - The collector continued to contact me directly after receiving written notice that I dispute the debt and have legal representation. My counsel is engaged in ongoing litigation involving this same vehicle. - The collector misrepresented the legal status of the debt ( as detailed above ), continuing to claim I am personally responsible despite its own DMV record showing otherwise and despite my having identified this defect in writing. - The collector contacted my personal cell phone a number I never gave them using what appears to be an automated text messaging system ( " Reply Stop to opt-out '' ), without my consent.
