Account in Dispute : Creditor / Furnisher : XXXX ( Federal Student Loan Servicer ) Account Number : XXXX ( or use your truncated account number ) Loan Award IDs : XXXX and XXXX Disbursement Date : XX/XX/year> Original Balance : {$7400.00} Legal Basis for Dispute : The above-referenced student loan account has been fully and finally discharged by the U.S. Department of Education ( `` ED '' ) through an approved Borrower Defense to Repayment application. A copy of the official notice from ED 's servicer, XXXX, which states : " We have discharged your federal loan ( s ) ... As a result, you do not owe any balance on your federal loan account serviced by us '' and confirms that the " Total Balance Remaining after Discharge '' is " {$0.00} '', is enclosed and incorporated herein. Therefore, the continued reporting of this account with any outstanding balance, past-due status, or inaccurate notation is a direct violation of multiple sections of the FCRA : 1. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to Follow Reasonable Procedures : As a Consumer Reporting Agency ( " CRA '' ), you are required by 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) to " follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of the information concerning the individual about whom the report relates. '' Reporting a discharged debt with an outstanding or delinquent balance is per se inaccurate. In Krueger v. Experian Information Solutions, the Sixth Circuit held that a debtor whose loan was discharged had standing to assert an FCRA claim against a servicer that continued to report the discharged debt as past due, causing an artificially low credit score. 2. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681i Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Reinvestigation : Upon receipt of this dispute, you are statutorily required by 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) to, " free of charge, '' conduct a " reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is inaccurate. '' This reinvestigation must be completed within 30 days from your receipt of this notice. The CRA must then delete or modify the inaccurate item. If you fail to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and the information is not deleted, you will be in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681i. 3. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure of Furnisher ( XXXX ) to Investigate : After you notify XXXX of this dispute, XXXX is required by 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) to " conduct an investigation with respect to the disputed information '' and report the results to all CRAs. Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation may render XXXX liable. As the FTC has noted, " the plain language of the Fair Credit Reporting Act compels the conclusion that there is a private right of action for consumers to enforce the investigation and reporting duties imposed on furnishers of information. '' 4. Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681c Reporting of Obsolete Information ( If Applicable ) : If the delinquency leading to the discharge occurred more than seven years ago, 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( a ) prohibits the inclusion of such obsolete information in your reports. Request for Investigation and Immediate Deletion : Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i, I request that you : 1. Conduct a reasonable reinvestigation into the disputed account described above ; 2. Immediately delete the inaccurate XXXX student loan tradeline from my credit file in its entirety ; 3. Notify me in writing of the results of your investigation within 30 days, and provide me with a free copy of my updated credit report. I have enclosed a copy of the XXXX discharge letter as supporting documentation. Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o, I intend to exercise my statutory right to seek actual, statutory, and punitive damages for any willful or negligent noncompliance with the FCRA, including reasonable attorneys ' fees and costs. Please be advised that I am keeping a careful record of all communications related to this matter. Thank you for your prompt attention. Sincerely,

Consumer complaint narrative: This correspondence constitutes a formal Notice of Error pursuant to Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35. Background In XX/XX/year>, my wife and I contacted your company after experiencing a temporary financial hardship that affected our ability to make our mortgage payments. During that process, your representative informed us that we qualified for a modified monthly payment of approximately {$1900.00} per month. We were specifically told that verbal consent was sufficient and that no additional documentation was required. Relying on the information provided by your representative, we began making the agreed-upon payments and successfully made XXXX consecutive monthly payments in the amount instructed by your company. Several months later, we were informed that our payments were considered insufficient because signed loan modification documents had allegedly been required. We spent numerous hours communicating with your representatives attempting to resolve the issue and explaining that we had been explicitly told no documentation was necessary. During these communications, your representatives repeatedly stated that there was nothing they could do, advised us to abandon our efforts to challenge the issue, and directed us to submit a new hardship application. As a result of your company 's failure to properly administer the loan modification process, we filed a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). Following that complaint, your company admitted that an error had occurred and agreed to honor the original modification terms. Your company then sent us loan modification documents for execution and notarization. Upon review of the documents, we discovered that the notarial certificates and notary acknowledgment sections were improperly placed within the documents, making proper notarization impossible. We signed and returned the documents while notifying your company of the notary-related errors. Instead of correcting the defective documents and allowing us an opportunity to properly execute the modification, your company informed us that the file had been closed and that our only option was to apply for a new hardship modification. Errors Being Asserted We believe the following servicing errors have occurred : Failure to properly implement and administer an approved loan modification after your company acknowledged its prior error. Failure to provide accurate and legally sufficient loan modification documentation capable of being properly notarized. Improper closure of an approved loan modification file due to defects contained within documentation prepared and provided by your company. Improper refusal to correct documentation errors that originated with your company. Improper requirement that we submit a new financial hardship application despite the fact that : The original modification had already been approved ; Your company acknowledged its prior servicing error ; The modification failed to be completed due to documentation defects created by your company ; and We are no longer experiencing the financial hardship that initially gave rise to the modification request. Refusal to accept mortgage payments and/or provide a reasonable method for bringing the account into compliance under the previously approved modification. Requested Resolution We request that your company : Reopen and honor the previously approved loan modification. Provide corrected modification documents free from notarial or execution defects. Permit execution of corrected documents without requiring submission of a new hardship application. Accept and properly apply any payments tendered under the approved modification terms. Correct any negative account status, delinquency reporting, fees, penalties, or default-related consequences that resulted from the servicing errors described above. Provide a complete written explanation of your findings, including copies of all records, notes, recordings, correspondence, and internal communications relating to : The original XX/XX/year> modification approval ; The CFPB complaint response ; The acknowledged servicing error ; The preparation of the modification documents ; and The decision to close the modification file. Please investigate these matters and provide a written response within the time required by applicable federal law.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding American Express 's billing and payment practices, which I believe are misleading and have resulted in improper interest charges on my account. The central issue is not simply the interest charge itself, but that American Express displayed a payment amount in its mobile application that I reasonably relied upon, and then could not clearly explain why that amount was insufficient to avoid interest charges. For the billing cycle ending XX/XX/XXXX, my statement reflects a previous balance of {$17000.00} and payments and credits totaling {$17000.00}, which exceeds the previous balance. Despite this, American Express assessed {$360.00} in interest and indicates that the interest was calculated on a balance of {$16000.00}. American Express has not provided a clear explanation of how that balance was determined. When my payment was due on XX/XX/XXXX, the American Express mobile application displayed a remaining statement balance of {$17000.00}. I relied on that information and paid the amount shown by American Express. Only afterward was I informed that the payment was apparently insufficient to satisfy the prior statement balance. When I contacted American Express to understand and dispute the interest charges, I spoke with three different representatives and attempted to escalate the matter. Rather than providing a clear explanation of how the interest was calculated, the representatives focused on confirming that I had received my statement, understood the statement balance, and that I should know the terms and conditions since I've been a cardmember for several years. American Express repeatedly pointed out that my payment of {$17000.00} was less than the prior statement balance of {$17000.00}. However, no representative could clearly explain whether account credits apply toward satisfying the statement balance, whether posted credits are included in the " remaining statement balance '' displayed within the American Express mobile application, or how the company arrived at the balance used to calculate interest charges. Most importantly, American Express was unable or unwilling to explain why the payment amount presented in its own application differed from the amount it later claimed was required to avoid interest charges. As a consumer, I reasonably relied on the payment amount displayed by American Express within its application. If the amount shown in the application is not the amount required to avoid interest charges, that fact should be clearly disclosed. Instead, I was presented with a payment amount, paid that amount, and was subsequently charged interest without receiving a transparent explanation of how the determination was made. Despite multiple conversations and escalation attempts, American Express did not provide a transparent accounting of its interest calculation or a clear explanation of how consumers should reconcile the payment amount displayed in the mobile application with the amount required to avoid interest charges. As a result, I remain unable to determine whether the interest charges were properly assessed. I am requesting that American Express provide a detailed explanation of how the interest charges were calculated, including how the balance subject to interest was determined ; refund any improperly assessed interest charges ; and correct any misleading payment balance displays so that consumers can clearly determine the amount required to avoid interest charges.

Because my vehicle contained substantial equity beyond the amount owed to TitleMax, I believed that refinancing would allow me to obtain funds necessary to address my financial emergency while paying off the TitleMax loan. Eventually, a payoff transaction was initiated that required cooperation from TitleMax due to title-processing and lien issues associated with the loan. TITLEMAX CONTACTS ME AFTER LEARNING OF THE REFINANCE ATTEMPT After TitleMax became aware that another lender was attempting to refinance and pay off the loan, I was contacted by store XXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX asked whether I would be interested in obtaining another loan through TitleMax instead of refinancing elsewhere. EMAILS DOCUMENTING THE DELAYS Email communications show that I repeatedly notified TitleMax and Community Choice Financial that the Letter of Guaranty did not contain the information required by XXXX XXXX and that corrections were needed. Those communications also show that I specifically warned TitleMax that time was critical because interest was accruing daily and delays were causing financial harm. Multiple TitleMax and Community Choice Financial personnel were copied on these communications, including XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and title-processing personnel. Despite these notifications, delays continued and multiple versions of the required documents allegedly contained errors or omissions. ADVANTAGE FINANCE WITHDRAWS As the delays continued, the transaction became increasingly difficult and complicated. Ultimately, the refinance opportunity was lost, leaving me without access to the funds that I had expected to receive through the refinance process. AUTO NATION VEHICLE PURCHASE ATTEMPT After my financial situation worsened and I became homeless, I attempted to mitigate my damages by selling my vehicle. I contacted XXXX located at : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Texas XXXX XXXX evaluated my vehicle and offered approximately {$22000.00} for its purchase. As a result, I was unable to access the equity in my vehicle despite having a willing purchaser and a substantial amount of equity remaining. XXXX XXXX The consequences of these events have been severe. As a direct result of the failed refinance, delays, title-processing issues, and inability to access the equity in my vehicle : XXXX continued to accrue. I lost access to desperately needed liquidity. I was unable to secure stable housing. I ultimately became homeless and was forced to live in my vehicle. My ability to generate income was substantially impaired. I have been self-employed for approximately XXXX years. My business depends on stable housing, reliable transportation, access to communications, and the ability to conduct operations on a consistent basis. Living in my vehicle has significantly disrupted my ability to maintain normal business operations, serve clients, generate income, and support myself. EFFORTS TO MITIGATE DAMAGES I made repeated efforts to mitigate my damages. These efforts included : Seeking refinancing through third-party lenders. Cooperating with payoff requests. Attempting to sell the vehicle through XXXX. Attempting to use the vehicles substantial equity to secure housing and stabilize my financial situation. Despite these efforts, I was unable to obtain the liquidity needed because the refinance failed and the vehicle sale could not be completed. EVIDENCE AVAILABLE I possess substantial evidence supporting this complaint, including : Audio recordings of conversations with TitleMax personnel. Email communications. I respectfully request that regulators review these recordings as part of a thorough investigation into whether TitleMax employees made inaccurate representations, entered false or misleading information into company systems, failed to follow applicable lending and title-processing requirements, or otherwise engaged in conduct that contributed to the issues described in this complaint, in conjunction with the documentary evidence, internal account notes, emails, and title-processing records maintained by TitleMax and its affiliates XXXX REQUEST FOR INVESTIGATION I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether TitleMax and/or Community Choice Financial engaged in : Unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ). Misrepresentations regarding refinancing or additional financing. Improper handling of payoff and refinance requests. Improper delays or obstruction relating to title-processing activities. Failure to provide accurate information and documentation. Conduct that interfered with legitimate efforts to refinance, sell collateral, or access vehicle equity. I further request that the CFPB obtain and review all internal account notes, scanned documents, recordings, emails, title-processing records, payoff requests, Letter of Guaranty requests , and communications relating to my account. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding two unauthorized or unexplained security incidents on my American Express account, and Amex 's failure to communicate any findings or resolution after 20 days, in apparent violation of their investigative obligations under Regulation E ( Electronic Fund Transfer Act ). Incident 1 : Unauthorized Voice Payment, XX/XX/year> On XX/XX/year>, an unauthorized voice payment was made on my American Express account via Amex 's automated pay-by-phone system. The payment was for the minimum balance due. My account is set up for automatic full statement balance payment via ACH from my linked checking account, which processes automatically a few days after the statement date. Incident XXXX : Unsolicited SMS Payment Link, XX/XX/year> at XXXX I received an SMS message from American Express 's verified number at XXXX on Saturday XX/XX/year> stating " Amex : Here is the link you requested to make a payment. '' I did not request any payment link. When I contacted Amex about this message, they confirmed they have no record of a payment link being generated or sent for any of my cards. The origin of this SMS remains unexplained. Following this call, Amex closed and reissued my card. I have received communication confirming the new card is being sent, but still no findings or update on the XX/XX/XXXX unauthorized voice payment. Security Vulnerability I Am Reporting I personally tested Amex 's pay-by-phone system after these incidents and documented the following authentication chain when calling from a phone number associated with the account : the system asks for the last 4 digits of the Social Security Number, then the last 5 digits of the Amex card number, then offers to process a payment using the linked checking account on file, including stating the bank name and last 4 digits of the checking account. This authentication chain is exploitable through the following means, all of which are readily accessible to bad actors : First, phone number spoofing technology is widely available and free, allowing anyone to spoof a call from a victim 's associated phone number, which grants access to the easier authentication path. Second, the last 4 digits of Social Security Numbers are widely available through numerous large-scale data breaches affecting data brokers, government agencies, and financial institutions, including breaches that affected individuals who never directly interacted with the breached entity. Third, American Express card numbers follow a known, structured format. The last XXXX digits of a card number are not random and can be derived or bypassed via automated brute-forcing or scripted enumeration against the IVR phone system. My affected card was newly issued in XX/XX/year>, making it highly unlikely to have appeared in a legacy data breach, which further supports the conclusion that the card number was obtained through automated brute-forcing or scripted enumeration rather than a breach. The result is that a bad actor with spoofing capability and access to commonly breached personal data can authenticate into Amex 's pay-by-phone system and initiate ACH payments from a victim 's linked checking account without the account holder 's knowledge or consent, and without triggering any out-of-band verification such as a one-time passcode or push notification. What I Am Requesting I am requesting that the CFPB compel American Express to provide the following : XXXX. A full explanation of how the XX/XX/year> voice payment was authenticated, including what verification the caller passed and whether phone number spoofing was considered as the entry point. XXXX. A formal response to the XX/XX/year> SMS payment link that Amex 's own representatives can not account for. XXXX. An explanation of what steps Amex is taking or will take to address the structural authentication vulnerability in their pay-by-phone system described above, given that knowledge-based verification relying on SSN digits and predictable card number formats is no longer a meaningful security barrier in the current data breach environment. 4. A statement confirming whether Amex 's automated pay-by-phone system utilizes telecom attestation data to verify the legitimacy of the incoming Caller ID before granting access to the reduced verification path. I have made multiple good faith attempts to resolve this directly with American Express and have received no substantive response after 20 days.

If Professional Debt Mediation , Inc. is collecting on behalf of an original creditor or another third party, I request compliance with FCRA Section 615 ( g ), 15 U.S.C. 1681m ( g ), including notification to that third party that the account may be fraudulent and resulted from identity theft. Permanently close the account in its records as identity theft. Remove the account from active collection inventory. Notify XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX that the account resulted from identity theft and request deletion of all reporting associated with the account. Stop furnishing or refurnishing the account to any consumer reporting agency. Do not sell, transfer for consideration, forward, assign, or place the account with another collector, debt buyer, servicer, vendor, or third party for collection. Notify the original creditor, current owner, prior owner, and any collection vendor that the account is disputed as identity theft and must not be recycled for collection. Provide written confirmation that the account has been closed as fraud, collection activity has stopped, reporting has been deleted, and the debt will not be sold, transferred for consideration, or placed for collection again.

Complaint Against Synchrony Bank Deferred Interest Financing Practices I am submitting this complaint regarding a deferred interest financing promotion offered by Synchrony Bank that I believe was misleading and resulted in unexpected and excessive charges. In XX/XX/XXXX, I purchased a mattress for approximately {$2500.00} and enrolled in a 24-month deferred interest promotional financing plan. At the time of purchase, I understood this promotion to mean that if any balance remained at the end of the promotional period, interest would begin accruing on the remaining balance going forward. I was not aware that interest was accruing retroactively during the promotional period and would be applied in full if the balance was not paid off completely within 24 months. I set up autopay and consistently made all required minimum monthly payments. However, the minimum payment amounts were variable and decreased significantly over timefrom approximately {$97.00} per month down to as low as {$41.00}. This declining payment structure created the impression that my balance was being reduced appropriately and did not signal that I was at risk of triggering significant deferred interest charges. As the promotional period ended around XXXX XXXX, I did not receive clear or sufficient notification that the deadline was approaching or that failure to pay the full balance would result in retroactive interest being applied. When the promotion expired, Synchrony Bank applied approximately two years of backdated interest at an APR of 29.99 % in a single billing cycle. As a result, my account balance increased dramatically from {$1100.00} to {$2600.00} in one month. This increase was entirely due to retroactive interest charges that I did not reasonably expect based on my understanding of the promotion. The use of the term deferred interest is misleading, as it suggests that interest is postponed rather than accruing in the background and applied retroactively as a lump sum. Had I clearly understood that failing to pay off the balance in full would result in the application of all accrued interest, I would have paid the remaining balance before the promotional period ended. Additionally, the structure of declining minimum payments appears to contribute to this issue by allowing balances to remain higher for longer periods, increasing the likelihood that consumers will not pay off the balance in time and will incur retroactive interest charges. I believe these practices are deceptive and do not provide consumers with a clear understanding of the financial risk associated with these promotions.

Consumer complaint narrative: Subject : Request for Regulatory Investigation into Cash App 's Consumer Protection Practices To Whom It May Concern : I am requesting a formal review and investigation into Cash App 's handling of accidental transfers and its apparent lack of meaningful consumer protections for users who suffer financial losses due to honest mistakes. My husband, XXXX XXXX XXXX, mistakenly sent {$500.00} to the wrong Cash App user. Upon realizing the error, we immediately submitted a refund request through the Cash App platform. The recipient declined the request and retained the funds despite knowing they were not the intended recipient. What is most troubling is not merely the recipient 's refusal to return money that does not belong to them, but Cash App 's complete unwillingness to assist in resolving the matter. When we contacted customer service, we were effectively told that nothing could be done and that our only option was to pursue Small Claims Court. This response shifts the entire burden onto the victim while allowing both the platform and the recipient to avoid accountability. As consumers, we are encouraged to trust digital payment platforms with our hard-earned money. Yet Cash App appears to provide no meaningful safeguards when an obvious mistake occurs. A transaction involving hundreds of dollars can be completed in minutes, leaving little opportunity for a sender to correct an error. Once the recipient refuses a refund request, the sender is left with no practical remedy. This raises several serious concerns : Why does Cash App not have a mandatory review or recovery process for disputed accidental transfers? Why are recipients permitted to knowingly retain funds sent in error without any investigation by the platform? What monitoring exists to identify users who repeatedly receive and refuse to return mistaken payments? Why is there no meaningful escalation process for consumers who suffer financial losses due to accidental transfers? How does Cash App define its responsibility to protect customers who use its platform in good faith? Cash App possesses transaction records, account information, device information, and user identification data. Yet the company appears unwilling to use these resources to facilitate resolution when consumers report mistaken payments. Instead, consumers are directed to courts, creating a costly and burdensome process that many individuals can not reasonably pursue. My concern extends beyond my family 's loss of {$500.00}. I am concerned for every consumer who may find themselves in the same position. A financial platform should not be designed in a way that allows a person to knowingly keep money that was sent in error while the rightful owner is left without assistance. I respectfully request that regulators examine whether Cash App 's policies adequately protect consumers and whether additional safeguards should be required, including : Enhanced recipient verification before transfers are finalized. Longer cancellation or reversal periods for large-dollar transactions. A formal dispute resolution process for accidental payments. Investigation of recipients who knowingly retain funds sent in error. Stronger consumer protections for digital payment platforms operating in the United States. Consumers deserve more than a message stating, " There is nothing we can do. '' We deserve a payment platform that values fairness, accountability, and the protection of honest customers. Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your commitment to protecting consumers. Respectfully, XXXX XXXX On behalf of XXXX XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: This debt collector has done unjustifiable practices of the FDCPA which it prohibits. A consumer may take private legal action against a third-party debt collector or credit bureau for a violation of Chapter 392. In addition, a consumer may file a complaint with the attorney general if the consumer feels that the third-party debt collector or credit bureau has violated Chapter 392 by engaging in a false, misleading, or deceptive act or practice. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this formal complaint against American Express for failing to conduct a reasonable, good faith investigation into a billing error, which violates my consumer rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. Section 1666. 1. Nature of the Billing Error : The transaction involves a bait-and-switch scheme by the merchant, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX The hotel front desk explicitly marketed and sold a " Tacos and Margaritas Night '' experience, promising unlimited tacos and margaritas for a fixed price of {$50.00} per person. Relying entirely on this verbal agreement, I made a reservation. Upon arrival at the restaurant on XX/XX/year>, we were seated and served appetizers before being handed a physical menu. This menu revealed the actual price was {$55.00} per person and explicitly stated that margaritas were excluded and sold separately. When we attempted to leave due to this clear misrepresentation, hotel staff informed us we would be charged a mandatory no-show fee. Because the property is in an isolated location and it was late, we were held to the reservation under financial duress. The goods delivered were not as described ; the food quality was entirely substandard, and the pricing structure completely contradicted the agreement made at the time of the transaction. The following morning, I made a good faith attempt to resolve the issue with local management, who refused to assist. 2. Failure of American Express to Investigate Under the FCBA : Under 15 U.S.C. Section 1666 ( b ) ( 3 ), a billing error includes any reflection on a statement of goods or services not delivered in accordance with the agreement made at the time of the transaction. I timely disputed the {$140.00} charge with American Express under the " goods or services not as described '' category. American Express closed its investigation and rebilled my account on XX/XX/year>, based solely on the merchant 's submission of a copy of the physical menu and a signed payment voucher. American Express concluded that my signature on the voucher constitutes voluntary acceptance of the charge. By relying exclusively on the merchant 's paper trail, American Express completely failed to investigate the core of my dispute : Failure to evaluate duress : American Express ignored evidence that the signature on the voucher was obtained under financial duress via the threat of a predatory hotel no-show fee. Failure to evaluate the timing of the contract : The binding agreement was formed at the front desk when the reservation was sold, not when the merchant modified the terms after seating us. Violation of 15 U.S.C. Section 1666 ( a ) ( B ) ( ii ) : The FCBA requires a creditor to conduct a meaningful investigation before determining a charge is correct. Rubber stamping a merchant 's standard paperwork while actively ignoring a consumer 's documentation of deceptive trade practices and forced compliance does not constitute a lawful, thorough investigation. 3. Remedy Requested : I request that the CFPB compel American Express to properly fulfill its regulatory obligations under the Fair Credit Billing Act. The documentation provided by the merchant merely confirms that a transaction occurred, which I have never denied. It does not validate the deceptive trade practices used to capture the transaction. I request a full reversal of the rebilled {$140.00} charge.

I am filing a formal dispute against USAA for a clear violation of Regulation E ( Electronic Fund Transfer Act ) error-resolution requirements following an unauthorized Electronic Fund Transfer ( EFT ) of {$19000.00}. On XX/XX/year>, fraudsters impersonating the USAA Fraud Department called me. They asked if I had made a {$1000.00} purchase at XXXX and {$500.00} at XXXX. I responded " No '' to both. Then they said there was an additional flag showing that someone had tried to repeatedly make a wire transfer from my account, in-person from a local XXXX bank. They asked if I had my drivers license and debit card in my possession since the only way someone could do the transaction was to physically have those documents. I told them I had them and that I had never been to that bank branch. The fraudster proceeded to tell me that they were going to investigate the account. They sent me a verification text code to 'verify my identity and the account info ' and asked me to read it back to them. They used this code to execute an Account Takeover ( ATO ). Once inside my portal, they quickly altered my account 's custom nicknames to read " Under Investigation '' and changed the viewing preferences so that I could not see my balances at a glance instead, my bank apps Home Screen said " Balances Hidden. '' I later learned that during this time, they also transferred {$20000.00} from my savings account to my checking account and authorized an increase in my daily debit card transaction limit to {$20000.00}. Then the fraudster said that someone at the XXXX bank branch was trying to initiate the wire transfers and that I needed to immediately to go the bank to do a 'test ' transaction and see if the transaction was faulty or if someone at the bank was doing something nefarious. The fraudster kept me on the phone the whole time I drove to the bank, making everything seem urgent and harried. They told me when I got inside the bank to look for anything that seemed suspicious like agents not wearing name badges, on their phone, being nervous, etc. They told me to fill out a deposit slip in the amount {$19000.00}, account number XXXX, and name : " XXXX LLC ''. They said to take it to the teller and ask for a cash transfer from my USAA account to the account on the slip and to get 'both receipts '. I had asked repeatedly if I was going to see any deduction from my account and they assured me I wouldn't. I did the transaction and left the bank. They asked me questions like " was anyone acting suspicious, was everyone wearing their name badge. '' They said to go home and they would show me where on the USAA website to upload the receipts to submit for the fraud claim. When I got home, they said that it appeared that shortly after my transaction at the bank someone tried to initiate a wire with my husband 's information at the same bank. I had been on the phone over an hour and a half. At this point, my husband was listening in on the conversation and we started asking questions. They abruptly hung up the phone. I immediately called USAA and relayed all this to the claims/fraud department. That is when they informed me that someone had gone into my account and raised our debit card limit and transferred money from my savings to my checking account. After filing the claim with USAA, we went back to XXXX bank branch and got a copy of the deposit slip. They said that it was a cash advance, not a wire transfer that was initiated. They said that the money was deposited into a XXXX bank account but that they could not put a hold on the funds being released until they received notification from USAA. XXXX suggested we file a police report, which we did with XXXX XXXX XXXX in Pennsylvania ( in the jurisdiction where the bank operates and we live ). USAA has denied my initial fraud claim and an appeal, arguing that because I provided the 2FA passcode and physically used my card, the transaction was " authorized. '' This is a direct violation of official CFPB Regulation E Guidance ( Electronic Fund Transfers FAQs : Section 2 on Unauthorized EFTs ). The CFPB explicitly states that when a consumer is fraudulently induced into providing validation credentials or passcodes to an entity misrepresenting itself as the financial institution, the resulting transfer is legally Unauthorized. The root cause of this loss was a successful account takeover facilitated by deceptive credential harvesting. The CFPB explicitly states that if a criminal tricks you into giving up account credentials ( like a password or a 2FA code ) by pretending to be your bank, you did not grant permission to be robbed. And Federal consumer protection regulations always override any private bank policies that might state, " If you share your password or 2FA code, you are responsible for all losses. '' I am requesting that CFPB demand that USAA honor federal law, reverse their denial, and credit my account for the {$19000.00}.

I am filing this complaint regarding Bank of Americas handling of a check deposit and the lack of customer service, transparency, and escalation support that followed. Based on that representation, I reasonably expected the funds to become available after the stated clearing period. However, on the day the check was supposed to clear, Bank of America placed an additional hold on the funds for another seven days without providing a clear explanation, meaningful assistance, or a timely resolution. This created a serious hardship because I was relying on access to these funds after being told they would clear. After the additional hold was placed, I asked whether Bank of America could release at least a portion of the funds, such as half or even one-quarter of the deposit, while the remainder stayed under review. I did not receive a reasonable response or any meaningful explanation as to why a partial release could not be considered. The customer service experience made the situation worse. I attempted to speak with a representative for approximately two hours and was not allowed to reach someone who could properly assist me. I was also told that no manager was available. This left me without any practical way to escalate the issue, understand the reason for the extended hold, or receive help with the financial hardship caused by Bank of Americas decision. I believe Bank of America failed to provide clear communication, adequate customer service, and proper escalation options. I am requesting a formal review of this matter, including : 1. A written explanation for why the check was initially represented as clearing within one business day ; 2. A written explanation for why an additional seven-day hold was placed on the funds after the expected clearance date ; 3. A review of whether Bank of America followed all applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies regarding check holds and funds availability ; 4. Immediate release of the funds if there is no lawful or valid reason for the continued hold ; 5. Consideration of a partial release of funds if the full amount can not be released immediately ; 6. Reimbursement of any fees, financial losses, or hardship caused by the delayed access to my funds ; 7. Confirmation that this complaint has been escalated to a supervisor or executive-level complaint resolution department. I also request that Bank of America preserve all records related to this matter, including deposit records, account notes, call logs, customer service communications, hold notices, internal decision records, and any recordings of calls or branch interactions. I am not simply upset about a delay. I am concerned that I was given one expectation, then faced a new hold without proper explanation, while also being denied reasonable access to support, escalation, or a manager. This is unacceptable customer treatment, especially when a consumer is relying on deposited funds and the bank has already communicated an expected clearance timeline. I am requesting a prompt written response and immediate review of this matter.

If XXXX or Midland is using the XX/XX/XXXX date for the seven-year obsolescence calculation, that is illegal re-aging in violation of section 1681c. Midland Credit Management , Inc., 827 F.3d 1295 ( 11th Cir. 2016 ), a case directly against this furnisher, the furnisher 's section 1681s-2 ( b ) reasonable investigation duty is not satisfied by re-confirming internal records ; primary-source documentation must be examined. Midland ( with affiliates Encore Capital Group, Midland Funding LLC, and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) is subject to the XXXX stipulated final judgment with the CFPB ( $ XXXX in consumer redress, a portion suspended ; $ XXXX civil penalty ) building on the XXXX consent order. The compliance terms include required possession of documentation, prohibition on collection of time-barred debts, and full investigation of consumer disputes. The conduct described in this complaint is inconsistent with each of those compliance terms. I am submitting this complaint against American Honda Finance Corporation ( AHFC ) regarding the financing, subsequent servicing, and improper credit reporting of an automobile loan transaction that was originated based on materially inaccurate information, while mandatory documents were withheld, and despite my timely notice of rescission being provided before the transaction was funded. On XXXX XXXX, 2025, I signed documents for the purchase of a vehicle at XXXX of XXXX XXXX XXXX. The first version of the Credit Application was prepared by dealership employees without my participation. Subsequently, dealership employees informed me that the loan had already been approved by the bank and presented this approval as a resolved matter. The XXXXit Application itself was provided to me for the first time only during the process of signing the main transaction documents. While reviewing the Credit Application, I discovered significant errors, including an incorrect Social Security Number ( SSN ) and a fictitious city of residence, after which I pointed out these discrepancies to dealership personnel. A dealership employee corrected the form and immediately printed a second version of the Credit Application. However, upon further review, the second version also contained significant discrepancies from the information I had actually provided to the dealership. Credit Application ( XXXX ) listed a monthly income of {$14000.00} despite the fact that I had previously stated during discussions of the transaction that my monthly income was between {$6000.00} and {$8000.00}. When I raised this issue, the employee stated that it is merely a formality and does not affect anything. A particularly significant circumstance is that key documents, namely the Pre-Contract Disclosure and both versions of the Credit Application, were not included in the package of documents provided to me after completion of the transaction. These documents were first disclosed only on XXXX XXXX, 2025, by the dealerships legal representatives, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ), as part of their official response to complaints that had been submitted to government agencies. Only after receiving both versions of the Credit Application and thoroughly reviewing their contents did I discover that other key parameters also did not correspond to the actual facts. Both versions of the Credit Application contained an incorrect employment duration and materially distorted housing obligations. My monthly housing expenses were listed as {$1500.00}, although my actual expenses were approximately {$2200.00}, a figure that I had disclosed in advance and which is confirmed by my Current Resident Lease agreement ( EXHIBIT XXXX ). The Pre-Contract Disclosure revealed additional products and services totaling approximately {$18000.00} that were not properly disclosed to me and were absent from the package of documents provided to me on the day of signing. Among these products were XXXX separate service contracts with a combined value of approximately {$8800.00}. It is also important to note that both versions of the Credit Application ( XXXX XXXX, pp. XXXX ) contain a pre-entered loan amount, which is technically impossible for a document intended for initial submission to AHFC. A credit application is a form submitted to a lender for review before any approval decision is made. At the time the Credit Application was prepared, the additional products and services that the dealership later offered during the document-signing process had not yet been finally agreed upon with me, meaning that those discussions occurred after the dealership informed me that financing approval had already been obtained. The presence of a pre-entered final financing amount in the application indicates that the structure of the transaction had been determined before negotiations and discussions of its terms with me had concluded. The document was prepared as though the loan terms had already been finalized, even though the application was supposedly only being prepared for submission to AHFC. Furthermore, the absence of the XXXX XXXX and both versions of the XXXX XXXX deprived me of the opportunity to identify additional discrepancies and dispute them before financing was completed. Only after receiving these documents approximately 45 days later was I able to determine the full extent of the inconsistencies between the information I actually provided to the dealership and the information used in the credit documentation. The financial terms of the transaction also raise serious concerns. The manufacturers suggested retail price ( MSRP ) of the vehicle was {$47000.00} ( EXHIBIT XXXX ), while the vehicle price in the contract was increased to {$65000.00}. I was not shown any additional price stickers, dealer addendum stickers affixed to the vehicle, or any other official disclosures explaining the increase of the vehicle price to that amount. At the same time, additional products and service contracts totaling approximately {$18000.00} were listed separately on top of the vehicle price. The total amount financed was {$90000.00} before interest. A substantial discrepancy was also identified regarding the mileage of the vehicle traded in as part of the transaction. According to service records ( EXHIBIT XXXX ), shortly before the transaction the vehicles mileage exceeded XXXX miles, and at the time of the transaction the contract ( EXHIBIT XXXX, p. XXXX ) reflected approximately XXXX miles. However, the transaction documents listed the mileage as XXXX miles. This matter is currently the subject of a separate official XXXX investigation. At the same time, the dealership significantly undervalued my trade-in vehicle. According to the independent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Report ( EXHIBIT XXXX ), its value ranged from {$25000.00} to {$27000.00}. Nevertheless, the dealership valued it at {$20000.00} despite the fact that the outstanding loan balance on that vehicle was approximately {$23000.00}. Thus, the dealership simultaneously inflated the price of the vehicle being sold and undervalued the vehicle being traded in, creating a negative equity amount and adding it to an already inflated financing calculation. Another significant violation concerns the insurance process for the vehicle. Before the transaction was finalized, I expressly informed a dealership employee that my insurance agent did not work on XXXX and that the new vehicle could not be added to my insurance policy on the day of the transaction. In response, the dealership employee informed me that this was not a problem and that the insurance could be arranged later. At the time of the transaction, the dealership possessed only the insurance policy covering the vehicle being traded in. A dealership employee photographed that insurance policy using a mobile phone despite the fact that the policy applied exclusively to the trade-in vehicle and contained no information regarding the vehicle being purchased. At the time the new vehicle was delivered, there was no active insurance policy in the insurance system covering that vehicle, as confirmed by XXXX XXXX documentation ( EXHIBIT XXXX ). Accordingly, the vehicle was delivered to me without confirmed insurance coverage at the time of delivery. These circumstances raise serious questions regarding what information and documents were used during the origination and subsequent financing of the transaction, because the only insurance policy in the dealerships possession related to a different vehicle, while no active insurance coverage existed for the vehicle being purchased at the time it was delivered. After discovering these violations, I immediately returned to the dealership and demanded that the transaction be fully rescinded or revised, but my request was denied. On XXXX XXXX, 2025, before financing was completed by the lender, I sent written Notices of Rescission by certified XXXX mail to both the dealership and AHFC, formally withdrawing my consent to the transaction. Despite receiving written notice that the transaction was being formally disputed and should be rescinded before funding, AHFC proceeded to fund the loan in the amount of {$90000.00}. Additional concern arises from AHFCs conduct after funding the transaction. On XXXX XXXX, 2025, AHFC sent me an official letter ( EXHIBIT XXXX ) stating that it was unable to locate or verify my account based on the information available and requested additional identifying information, including the account number, the last XXXX digits of my SSN, and the vehicle VIN. However, one day earlier AHFC had already assigned an account number to the loan, generated a monthly statement, established a payment schedule, and issued the first payment due under the contract ( EXHIBIT XXXX ). This contradiction raises serious questions regarding the customer identification and verification procedures ( KYC/CIP ) XXXXtilized by AHFC in reviewing the credit application and subsequently servicing the account. To the best of my knowledge, neither before nor after funding did AHFC make any attempt to contact me to verify my identity, confirm personal information, or conduct any additional verification, despite establishing a long-term credit obligation in a substantial amount. After I refused to recognize the validity of this debt, AHFC reported the account to the credit bureaus as a charge-off/collection account with a balance of {$91000.00}. I submitted formal disputes to the credit bureaus and provided supporting documentation, including the Notices of Rescission, proof of delivery, and materials from ongoing government investigations. Despite this, XXXXHFC continued to verify the accuracy of the debt and maintain negative information in my credit history. I respectfully request that CFPB conduct a comprehensive investigation into the actions of American Honda Finance Corporation, determine what information was used in evaluating the financing request, identify which version of the Credit Application was used in approving the loan, determine how the accuracy of the information contained in the credit application was verified, and explain why financing was completed after Notices of Rescission had been received. I further request that AHFC be required to provide the complete set of documents used in making the credit decision, completely cease all collection activity relating to the disputed debt, cancel the account to a XXXX balance, and issue an official demand to the credit bureaus for the complete deletion of the entire negative tradeline associated with this account from my credit history.

Consumer complaint narrative: Formal Dispute Response and Demand for Reversal RE : Account Takeover Fraud Claim XXXX ; Provisional Credit {$4900.00} ; Accounts ending XXXX and XXXX To Whom It May Concern : I write to contest Wells Fargos latest denial of my fraud claim and the stated intent to revoke the {$4900.00} provisional credit. I am a victim of an account takeover. Your own correspondence confirms material facts consistent with my position and inconsistent with the denial. Statement of Facts and Procedural History : Account takeover acknowledged by bank operations. You reported my incident to the Account Takeover Operations group and placed a hard hold on my prior account ending XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, then closed it XX/XX/XXXX, and opened a new XXXX Checking ending XXXX the same day. These actions are consistent with an account-compromise event, not authorized cardholder spending. Timeline and ongoing dispute. I have contested these charges since XX/XX/XXXX, including through the CFPB. Your letter notes I contacted Wells Fargo again on XX/XX/XXXX, and that XXXX reviewed the matter. Banks denial rationale. Your letter states : The card was in your possession at the time the claim was filed and during the time of the disputed activity. The disputed transaction ( s ) occurred at locations or with merchants like your normal card usage. The transactions were types or amounts like your previous purchasing pattern. You intend to deduct the {$4900.00} provisional credit from account ending XXXX because the account was closed on XX/XX/XXXX ( per your notice ). You assert compliance with all federal and state laws and that the claim is closed. You state the Fraud & Claims Management team will provide the documentation used to deny my claim within 30 days of my request. You state, regarding my report that further fraud occurred due to delayed security measures, that you were unable to determine the transaction in question, while adding that situations such as yours can still occur despite your security measures. My undisputed circumstances : I had continuous card possession, but the account was compromised by remote access. The disputed transfer ( s ) represent my entire monthly earnings. I have never transacted {$4900.00} or nearly that amount with the involved merchant. The bank has already provided evidence of unauthorized access from other states prior to the disputed transactions. Why the Denial Is Unsupported Under Regulation E? Card possession is not dispositive. Regulation E ( EFTA ) protects consumers from unauthorized electronic fund transfers initiated by third parties using stolen credentials or account access even if the physical card remains with the consumer. An account takeover with remote initiation squarely fits unauthorized under Reg E. Pattern-of-use assertions conflict with the record. Your blanket statements that merchant type, location, and amounts were like my normal usage are contradicted by : The size of the transaction ( s ) representing my entire monthly income. My history showing no prior transactions with the specific merchant. Prior evidence of out-of-state access to my account before funds were removed. Conclusory assertions are not evidence. I request the specific data, time stamps, device/browser IDs, IP addresses, geolocation, merchant category codes, and historical comparators used to reach these conclusions. Acknowledged account-takeover actions support my claim. Your involvement of Account Takeover Operations, imposition of a hard hold, and forced account closure/opening are consistent with a compromised account, which undermines the theory that the disputed transactions were mine. Investigation completeness and documentation. You state the Fraud & Claims Management team will provide the documentation relied upon within 30 days. Until that documentation is produced and reviewed, it is premature to consider this claim closed. Reg E requires a reasonable investigation ; refusing reimbursement based on unsubstantiated generalities does not meet that standard. Security measures and subsequent loss. You state you were unable to determine the transaction in question that would have been prevented had my account been promptly secured. Please identify which post-report transactions you reviewed, along with the dates/times and holds applied, so this can be reconciled with the logins from other states and resulting debits already documented. Harm and Ongoing Impact : Financial and emotional harm. The unresolved loss of my entire monthly earnings has caused documented mental distress, supported by medical reports. As far as customer relationship, I have been a Wells Fargo customer for over 20 years. The handling of this claim has eroded trust and left me unprotected during and after the takeover. Requests and Demands : Immediate restoration of funds. Reinstate and make permanent the {$4900.00} provisional credit and reverse all disputed transactions attributable to the takeover. Full investigative file. Within 10 business days, provide the complete documentation relied upon in denying my claim, including : Detailed transaction logs for all disputed items ( date/time, merchant descriptors, MCCs, terminal IDs ). Network and device telemetry ( IP addresses, device/browser fingerprints, geolocation, 3-D Secure results if applicable ). Access and authentication logs ( login attempts, password resets, SMS/OTP events, contact-info changes ). Internal notes from the Claims Department, XXXX, and Account Takeover Operations. The specific pattern of behavior analysis, including the baseline period, metrics, and comparators used to assert similarity of merchant, location, and amounts. Merchant recovery status. Provide a written accounting of all recovery efforts regarding the XXXX XXXX merchant, including dates, responses, and amounts recovered or offsets applied. Security remediation. Provide written confirmation of all security actions taken on accounts ending XXXX and XXXX ( dates/times of holds, closures, reopenings ), and assurance that multifactor authentication, alerts, and other safeguards are active. Hold on reversals. Cease any reversal of provisional credits or collections activity until the above documentation is produced and a good-faith review is completed. Notice of Escalation : If these requests are not met within 10 business days, I will : Supplement my CFPB complaint with this response and your failure to produce the investigative file. File complaints with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and my state attorney general. Pursue available legal remedies, including damages for financial losses and documented emotional distress. I request a written response addressing each numbered item above. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX Account ending XXXX ( closed XX/XX/XXXX ) Account ending XXXX ( opened XX/XX/XXXX ; referenced in proposed reversal ) Claim XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: CFPB, I am submitting this complaint regarding JPMorgan Chase Banks handling of a recent check deposit and the repeated, inconsistent information I have received from its representatives concerning the availability of my funds. On XXXX, I deposited a check into my Chase account. After making the deposit, I contacted Chase on multiple occasions to inquire about the status of the deposit and when the funds would become available. During these conversations, I was repeatedly informed by Chase representatives that the funds would be available by XXXX. I was also advised that there was no hold placed on the deposit. Relying on the information provided by Chase representatives, I expected the funds to become available in accordance with the timeframe that had been communicated to me. However, after receiving the same information from multiple representatives, I was later provided with conflicting information by another representative, who indicated that the funds would not be available until a later date. As a consumer, I depend on the accuracy of information provided by my financial institution. When I contact a bank regarding the availability of deposited funds, I reasonably expect that the information I receive will be accurate, consistent, and based on the actual status of my account. Instead, I was provided with conflicting explanations regarding the same transaction. This has left me uncertain as to which information is correct and has undermined my confidence in the information being provided by Chase. My concern extends beyond the timing of this particular deposit. My primary concern is the apparent inconsistency in the information communicated by Chase representatives. If a deposit is subject to a hold, review, or delayed availability, customers should be provided with a clear and consistent explanation. If no hold exists, customers should likewise receive consistent information regarding when funds will become available. Receiving multiple different answers from the same institution regarding the same transaction is unacceptable and creates unnecessary confusion. Additionally, the conflicting information caused me to spend significant time contacting Chase in an effort to obtain a clear answer. Rather than receiving a definitive explanation, I was forced to continue seeking clarification because the information provided by one representative contradicted the information provided by another. Consumers should not have to navigate inconsistent explanations from their bank in order to determine when they will have access to their own funds. I am concerned that there may be deficiencies in employee training, internal communication, account documentation, or customer service procedures that contributed to this situation. If representatives are reviewing the same account information yet providing different answers, that raises legitimate concerns regarding the reliability of the information being provided to customers. I respectfully request that JPMorgan Chase conduct a thorough review of this matter, including a review of account notes, deposit records, call logs, and any recordings of my communications with the bank. I would like Chase to determine why I received conflicting information regarding the availability of my deposit and whether the information provided to me was accurate.

I am filing a formal complaint regarding the reporting of a collection account by Resurgent Capital Services/LVNV Funding ( Account # XXXX ) appearing on my credit reports. This account is being reported in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), including but not limited to : 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to Maintain Maximum Possible Accuracy The account contains incomplete and inconsistent information, including missing payment terms, no monthly payment, no interest details, incomplete payment history, and an inaccurate classification as past due. Such reporting is misleading and can not be considered maximally accurate. 15 U.S.C. 1681i Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation Upon dispute, the credit bureaus must conduct a reasonable investigation and verify the account with competent evidence. Automated verification without documentation from the furnisher does not meet this legal standard. Failure to Establish Legal Ownership / Chain of Title As a debt buyer, LVNV Funding must provide documentation proving full assignment of the alleged debt from the original creditor, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Absent such documentation, the account is unverified and unlawfully reported. 15 U.S.C. 1681c Improper and Potentially Misleading Reporting Period The account fails to clearly identify the Date of First Delinquency, creating ambiguity regarding the reporting period and raising concerns of improper re-aging. Misleading Account Status Reporting this account as past due is inaccurate for a collection account and misrepresents the legal status of the debt.

On XX/XX/XXXX, I incurred a medical charge of {$2800.00} through CareCredit after seeking treatment at XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX, Tennessee. According to my account records, the transaction was processed on XX/XX/XXXX and financed through a promotional financing arrangement. At the time I applied for CareCredit, I was experiencing XXXX XXXX XXXX and was informed by the provider 's office that treatment would not be provided unless I paid in advance. Because I could not afford the cost of treatment upfront, I was encouraged to apply for CareCredit while in XXXX and seeking medical care. The financing was presented as the solution that would allow me to receive treatment. I did not understand that the financing arrangement involved deferred interest that could later be charged retroactively if the promotional balance was not paid in full by the expiration date. I do not recall being informed of the amount of deferred interest accumulating in the background, the magnitude of the potential retroactive interest charge, or the fact that making the required monthly payments would not necessarily pay off the promotional balance before expiration. Throughout the life of the account, I maintained automatic payments and made all but the first required payments on time. My monthly automatic payment was approximately {$45.00} and was successfully withdrawn each month. The promotional period expired on XX/XX/XXXX. At the time of expiration, my promotional balance was approximately {$1300.00}. The XX/XX/XXXX statement showed a deferred interest amount of {$1700.00} associated with the promotional purchase. The following statement reflected a sudden interest charge of {$1800.00}, causing my balance to increase from {$1300.00} to {$3100.00} despite no new purchases being made. My automatic payment also increased from approximately {$45.00} to {$110.00}, which was withdrawn on XX/XX/XXXX and caused an overdraft in my bank account. This was the event that alerted me to the existence of the retroactive deferred interest and the dramatic increase in my balance. After discovering the retroactive interest charges, I contacted Synchrony Bank and requested assistance. During that conversation, I was informed that Synchrony could only provide a courtesy extension until XX/XX/XXXX because, according to the representative, company policy and applicable credit-reporting requirements limited extensions to within approximately 30 days of the promotional expiration date. I found this response particularly troubling because I was not meaningfully alerted to the issue until after my automatic payment was withdrawn on XX/XX/XXXX. My monthly automatic payment had historically been approximately {$45.00}, but the XX/XX/XXXX withdrawal increased to {$110.00} and caused an overdraft in my bank account. Only after that withdrawal did I become aware of the retroactive interest charges, the expired promotional period, and the dramatically increased account balance. Synchrony then effectively informed me that I had only until XX/XX/XXXX, less than XXXX week later, to come up with approximately {$1300.00} to pay off the remaining promotional balance and avoid the retroactive interest. As an unemployed consumer who had been laid off in XX/XX/XXXX and was actively seeking work, this was not a realistic opportunity for relief. I would have been forced to choose between attempting to satisfy the promotional balance and paying essential obligations such as health insurance, transportation, and student loan payments. In my view, it is fundamentally unfair to offer a consumer only a few days to cure a problem after the consumer first becomes aware of it, while simultaneously claiming that broader relief is unavailable because too much time has already passed. This sequence of events raises concerns about whether consumers are receiving meaningful notice and a genuine opportunity to avoid substantial retroactive interest charges before those charges are imposed. My concern is not merely the existence of interest charges. My concern is the manner in which this financing product was marketed, serviced, and administered. During the promotional period I received numerous marketing emails encouraging additional use of the CareCredit account, including promotions encouraging me to use promotional financing again and again, use the card for additional purchases, and locate additional providers. I have been unable to locate any comparable email communications clearly warning me that my promotional period was about to expire, clearly stating the deferred interest amount that had accumulated, or clearly warning me that my balance could more than double through retroactive interest charges. The only recent letter I received from Synchrony prior to this issue was a XX/XX/XXXX credit line reduction notice, which discussed credit-limit changes and credit scoring factors but did not provide any warning regarding the impending expiration of my promotional financing or the deferred interest balance. I believe the product 's structure, disclosures, servicing, and communications created a misleading impression that timely automatic payments were sufficient to maintain the account in good standing, while a substantial retroactive interest obligation continued accumulating in the background. I believe this practice is particularly concerning in the context of medical financing, where consumers often enter these arrangements while experiencing XXXX, XXXX, and urgent healthcare needs. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate Synchrony 's administration of deferred-interest medical financing products and review whether adequate and meaningful notice was provided regarding promotional expiration, deferred interest accumulation, and the consequences of failing to satisfy the promotional balance in full before expiration.

Despite repeated attempts to obtain information and resolve the issue, no department within the bank has been able to explain why my account was frozen, unfrozen, and then frozen again without notice, preventing me from conducting normal business transactions. My account had been in a negative balance status for approximately 119 days. On the XXXX day, I made a deposit specifically to bring the account current and resolve the negative balance. The deposit was accepted by Bank of America but placed on hold. I was informed that the funds would become available on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX. Prior to XX/XX/XXXX, while reviewing my account online, I observed a transaction indicating a forced account closure followed by a reversal of that closure transaction. Concerned by this activity, I contacted Bank of America and was informed that the account was frozen. I subsequently spoke with Client Recoveries and was advised that the account appeared to be in the process of closing. I was instructed to wait 24 to 48 hours for the system to update. After waiting, I contacted the bank again on XX/XX/XXXX and was informed that the account status had returned to open and active. On XX/XX/XXXX, the deposited funds became available as promised, and I began using my debit card and account normally. However, on Saturday, XX/XX/XXXX, I attempted to use an ATM and was informed that no transactions could be processed on the account. I immediately visited a Bank of America branch and spoke with the branch manager. The branch manager advised that the account had been frozen again. She stated there were no alerts, notes, or explanations visible on the account indicating why the freeze had been placed. She further advised that the account appeared to be frozen rather than closed and provided me with the telephone number for Client Protection. I then contacted customer service and spoke with a representative named XXXX. XXXX advised that there were no notes or alerts explaining the situation. He could see that I had been actively using the account and stated that the issue appeared to be an internal Bank of America matter. He further stated that it appeared a simple code correction changing the account status from frozen to open would resolve the issue. XXXX directed me to contact Client Recoveries when they reopened. On Monday, I spent approximately nine hours, from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX., attempting to obtain answers regarding why my account had been refrozen. During these calls, I spoke with multiple representatives and supervisors, including Supervisor XXXX XXXX. I was advised that Client Recoveries was not the correct department and that Deposit Services would instead handle the issue. When transferred to Deposit Services, representatives were unable to explain why the account had been refrozen and, contrary to what Client Recoveries had previously stated, informed me that the account was actually closed. This directly contradicted information I had received from both Client Recoveries and branch personnel, who had repeatedly advised that the account was frozen, not closed. I was then referred back to Client Recoveries, where representative XXXX advised me once again to wait 24 to 48 hours and " see what happens. '' When I asked why I had never received any notice that my account would be frozen, he stated that customers would not receive notice unless the account was formally closed. On XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with another Client Recoveries representative, I. XXXX, who stated that their department could not take any action unless the account was closed and attempted to transfer me yet again to another department. At this point, Client Protection, Client Recoveries, Deposit Services, customer service representatives, supervisors, and branch personnel have all provided conflicting information. No one has been able to explain : Why the account was initially frozen. Why a forced closure transaction appeared and was then reversed. Why the account was returned to open and active status on XX/XX/XXXX. Why the account was frozen again after funds became available and I resumed normal account activity. Whether the account is frozen or closed. Why no alerts, notes, or documentation exist explaining the status of the account. Why I was never provided notice regarding the freeze. As a business owner, I have deposits that need to be made into this account and ongoing business transactions that can not be completed because Bank of America has restricted access to the account without explanation. The bank 's inability to provide accurate information, identify the responsible department, or explain its actions has caused significant disruption to my business operations. I am requesting that Bank of America provide a complete written explanation regarding the status of my account, identify the reason for the freezes and any closure actions, restore access if the account remains open, and explain why no notice was provided. I also request that the CFPB require Bank of America to investigate the conflicting information provided by its various departments and provide a definitive resolution. If Bank of America is unable or unwilling to provide answers regarding this matter, I intend to pursue additional remedies through the Illinois Attorney General 's Office and any other appropriate regulatory agencies.
