Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against ( XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a mortgage broker in XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX # XXXX ), operated by XXXX XXXX ( XXXX # XXXX ) ; and ( 2 ) United Wholesale Mortgage , LLC ( UWM ), the wholesale lender that funded my loan. Both parties engaged in coordinated deceptive and predatory practices in connection with my residential mortgage on XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, closed XX/XX/XXXX, Loan ID # XXXX, original principal {$470000.00} at 7.74 % fixed interest, monthly payment {$4600.00}. VIOLATION 1 UNDISCLOSED LENDER-PAID BROKER COMPENSATION My Loan Estimate disclosed only {$2100.00} in origination fees payable to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX My Closing Disclosure provided only at closing, after I was committed to the transaction revealed an additional {$12000.00} listed as Paid by Others ( L ), meaning United Wholesale Mortgage paid this amount directly to XXXX. This payment was never disclosed on the Loan Estimate as required by Regulation Z, 12 CFR Section 1026.37 ( f ) ( 6 ). Total broker compensation on this transaction was {$15000.00}. The {$12000.00} payment from UWM to XXXX constitutes an illegal kickback under RESPA Section 8 ( a ), 12 U.S.C. Section 2607 ( a ). Throughout the loan process, XXXX XXXX verbally represented to me and to my independent witness that she had no financial relationship with UWM. The Closing Disclosure proves otherwise. VIOLATION 2 NO AFFILIATED BUSINESS ARRANGEMENT DISCLOSURE XXXX XXXX verbally represented she was independently shopping lenders on my behalf. Despite this, the Loan Estimate was printed on United Wholesale Mortgage letterhead identifying UWM as the lender. No Affiliated Business Arrangement ( AfBA ) Disclosure was ever provided to me at any point not during application, processing, or closing. Under RESPA Section 8 ( c ) ( 4 ), 12 U.S.C. Section 2607 ( c ) ( 4 ), and 12 CFR Section 1024.15, a mortgage broker is required to provide an AfBA Disclosure before referring a borrower to any settlement service provider with whom the broker has a financial relationship. XXXX failure to provide this disclosure is a per se RESPA violation. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX had been in operation only eleven months at the time of closing, with one sponsored mortgage loan originator. It could not credibly have conducted a genuine multi-lender market comparison. VIOLATION 3 ANTI-STEERING AND DENIAL OF RIGHT TO CHOOSE Page 1 of 4 CFPB Complaint | XXXX XXXX | Loan # XXXX When I requested to see competing loan options from other lenders, XXXX XXXX communicated that a competing product was slightly worse and that we would stick with the company that we have. She provided no name of the competing bank, no interest rate, no APR, no formal Loan Estimate, and no written terms from any other lender. She substituted her own financially-motivated judgment she was receiving {$12000.00} from UWM for my legal right to independently evaluate and choose among competing loan products. Under Regulation Z, 12 CFR Section 1026.36 ( e ), a mortgage originator may not steer a consumer to a loan product based on the originators compensation rather than the consumers interest. This is a documented anti-steering violation. VIOLATION 4 FRAUDULENT MISREPRESENTATION OF AUTHORITY On XX/XX/XXXX, when I attempted to independently contact competing lenders to verify rates, XXXX XXXX communicated to me directly : No maam, I speak on behalf of the bank. XXXX XXXX is a licensed mortgage broker, XXXX # XXXX. She has zero legal authority to speak for, represent, or act on behalf of any bank or federally insured lending institution. This statement was made specifically to prevent me from independently verifying the loan terms or contacting competing lenders. It constitutes fraudulent misrepresentation of authority under XXXX Civil Code Article 1953 and implicates 18 U.S.C. Section 709 and the FDIC Act Section 18 ( a ) ( 4 ), which prohibit false claims of banking institution affiliation. This statement has been preserved in writing and is available for production upon request. VIOLATION 5 DEFECTIVE LOAN SERVICING TRANSFER NOTICE On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a loan servicing transfer notice stating that my loan servicer would change from United Wholesale Mortgage to United Wholesale Mortgage. This notice is facially defective. Under RESPA Section 6, 12 U.S.C. Section 2605, and 12 CFR Section 1024.33, a Notice of Transfer of Loan Servicing must identify the NEW servicer by name, address, and telephone number and must be provided no later than 15 days before the effective transfer date. A notice identifying the new servicer as the same entity as the current servicer provides no actionable information and constitutes a per se RESPA Section 6 violation. VIOLATION 6 UNDISCLOSED THIRD-PARTY SUBSERVICER On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted UWM by telephone. During that call, a UWM representative identified a third-party entity called XXXX as the entity actually servicing my loan on UWMs behalf, stating : This is Fenlar that services United Wholesale Mortgage . XXXX has never been identified in any loan document, Loan Estimate, Closing Disclosure, or any disclosure provided to me at or after origination. I was never informed that a third-party subservicer would be involved in handling my loan. Under RESPA Section 6, all servicing entities must be properly disclosed to the borrower. As of this filing, I do not know FENLARs full legal name, address, NMLS registration number, whether XXXX is licensed to service residential mortgage loans in XXXX, or when XXXX began subservicing my account. VIOLATION 7 UNDISCLOSED INVESTOR : XXXX XXXX During the same XX/XX/XXXX call, a UWM representative stated : Your investors are XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX status as investor or beneficial owner of my loan was never disclosed at origination, on the Loan Estimate, or on the Closing Disclosure. Under TILA Section 1638, 15 U.S.C. Section 1638, and Regulation Z Section 1026.18, the identity of the creditor must be disclosed to the borrower. This is a material disclosure failure. Page 2 of 4 CFPB Complaint | XXXX XXXX | Loan # XXXX VIOLATION 8 UWM CAN NOT IDENTIFY CURRENT NOTE HOLDER During the XX/XX/XXXX call, UWMs own representatives gave three different and contradictory answers about who currently holds my promissory note : first, that XXXX XXXX is the investor ; second, that XXXX XXXX had sold the loan but the representative did not know to whom ; and third, that UWM XXXX XXXX XXXX is the current servicer. Three contradictory answers in a single call from the servicers own agents raises a threshold question under UCC Article 3, Section 301 about whether UWM has any legal right to demand and receive mortgage payments at all. I can not safely direct payments to a party that can not confirm its legal authority to receive them. VIOLATION 9 PAYMENT GAP : NO PAYEE AVAILABLE XX/XX/XXXX On the XX/XX/XXXX call, the UWM representative explicitly told me not to make a payment yet because the loan transfer was still in process ; to wait for a notice to arrive by mail ; to call the number on that notice to obtain a new loan number ; and that the account would not be set up until after XX/XX/XXXX. This means there was a minimum five-day period XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX during which no party UWM could identify was available to receive my monthly payment of {$4600.00}. This gap was created entirely by UWMs defective transfer process. Under 12 CFR Section 1024.33 ( c ), a transferee servicer must accept payments from the borrower beginning on the transfer date. UWM failed to establish any mechanism for accepting payment during this period. Any adverse credit notation or late payment designation applied to this account for this period would be improper and retaliatory. VIOLATION 10 PATTERN OF PREDATORY CONDUCT On a separate occasion, XXXX XXXX solicited me to refinance a separate investment property through XXXX XXXX XXXX at 11.740 % interest with a 5-year prepayment penalty. She told me no lender could offer better terms. I independently obtained significantly better financing from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX directly contradicting her representation. XXXX also subsequently disclosed in writing that she had a servicing contract with the current lender containing clawback provisions she had never disclosed to me. This pattern of concealing financial relationships, misrepresenting market conditions, and prioritizing her own compensation over my interests mirrors the conduct on the XXXX XXXX transaction and constitutes a pattern of predatory lending under XXXX Unfair Trade Practices Act, XXXX. XXXX. 51:1401. NATIONAL ENFORCEMENT CONTEXT UWM is currently the subject of an XXXX Attorney General lawsuit filed XX/XX/XXXX alleging an identical broker-capture scheme, with {$25000.00} per deceptive act sought. Federal RESPA claims against UWM for the same type of undisclosed broker compensation arrangement survived a motion to dismiss in the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX. My transaction fits this documented institutional pattern precisely. WHAT I AM REQUESTING 1. Investigate XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX # XXXX ) and XXXX XXXX ( XXXX # XXXX ) for RESPA Section XXXX kickback violations, Regulation Z anti-steering violations, compensation disclosure failures, and fraudulent misrepresentation of authority. Page 3 of 4 CFPB Complaint | XXXX XXXX | Loan # XXXX XXXX. Investigate United Wholesale Mortgage , LLC ( XXXX # XXXX ) for paying {$12000.00} in undisclosed broker compensation ; issuing a facially defective servicing transfer notice ; operating an undisclosed subservicer ( XXXX ) ; failing to disclose XXXX XXXX as investor ; and failing to identify the current note holder when directly asked. 3. Order both parties to produce the complete wholesale broker agreement between XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and UWM governing compensation for Loan # XXXX. 4. Order UWM to produce : ( a ) the full legal identity, XXXX number, and licensing status of XXXX ; ( b ) the identity of the current legal holder of Loan # XXXX with complete chain of endorsements ; ( c ) a corrected, legally compliant servicing transfer notice. 5. Prohibit any adverse, delinquent, or negative credit reporting in connection with Loan # XXXX during the pendency of this complaint, per RESPA Section 6, 12 U.S.C. Section 2605 ( e ) ( 3 ), and 12 CFR Section 1024.35 ( i ).

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding Capital One Auto Finances mishandling of my auto loan account following the total loss of my vehicle and failures related to GAP claim processing, which have now resulted in continued collection activity and risk of credit harm. My financed vehicle, a XXXX XXXX XXXX, was declared a total loss on or about XXXX XXXX XXXX Following the total loss, insurance and GAP claim processes were initiated. I completed all requirements requested of me and submitted all documentation requested by the GAP provider, Advantage GAP, on or about XXXX XXXX XXXX On XXXX XXXX XXXX, Advantage GAP informed me that my GAP claim had been denied because Capital One failed to provide required documentation and/or settlement breakdown information necessary to process the claim. I was specifically informed that the denial was not caused by any failure on my part. After learning of the denial, I contacted Capital One multiple times in an effort to resolve the issue. During these calls, Capital One representatives provided inconsistent and contradictory explanations, including that : * Capital One failed to provide required documentation; * documentation had been submitted incorrectly or incompletely ; * there was a mismatch involving the insurance settlement breakdown ; * Capital One would communicate directly with the GAP provider to resolve the issue ; and * no further action was required on my part. During a recorded call on or around XXXX XXXX XXXX, a Capital One representative informed me that Capital One had sent the required documentation to the GAP provider and explicitly stated that I did not need to take any further action. I was told Capital One would work directly with Advantage GAP and that resolution would occur within approximately 710 business days. I relied on these representations in good faith. Despite this, my account continued aging into delinquency and is now approximately 42 days past due with an alleged balance of approximately {$8000.00}. I continue to receive collection calls even after formally disputing the matter and escalating concerns to Capital Ones Office of the President. Capital Ones handling of this matter appears to have materially contributed to the denial and/or delay of my GAP claim, while simultaneously exposing me to delinquency, collection activity, and potential negative credit reporting for circumstances outside of my control. I am requesting the following relief : 1. Immediate executive review of this account and GAP handling ; 2. Suspension of collection activity while this dispute is investigated ; 3. Protection from negative credit reporting associated with this disputed delinquency ; 4. Removal/correction of any negative reporting caused by Capital Ones servicing failures or delays ; 5. This complaint is filed against Solar Mosaic , Inc. ( operating as Solar Servicing ) regarding Loan Number XXXX for violations of the FTC Holder Rule ( 16 CFR Part 433 ) and deceptive debt collection practices. The loan was originated for a principal amount of {$40000.00} to finance a residential solar panel installation by the installer, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( which has since filed for bankruptcy ). A formal public search of the municipal building and electrical permit database confirms that this system was installed completely illegally. Zero mandatory building or electrical permits were ever applied for or issued for this solar installation. Because the system was installed illegally without mandatory municipal safety inspections, it suffered a catastrophic structural and electrical failure, resulting in a fire that created an active life-safety hazard on the property. The company 's official account dashboard currently shows a remaining loan balance of {$37000.00} with a maturity date extending to XXXX/XXXXXXXX, and they continue to collect regular monthly payments of {$200.00}. Under the FTC Holder Rule, Solar Mosaic , Inc., as the holder of the consumer credit contract, is strictly subject to all claims and defenses which the debtor could assert against the seller. A finance company can not legally enforce a contract or collect payments on an unpermitted, illegal home improvement that constitutes a documented fire hazard. I am legally withholding further payments under the Holder Rule due to a total failure of consideration and severe building code violations. I demand that Solar Mosaic , Inc. immediately cease all collection activities, cancel the remaining loan balance of {$37000.00}, and issue a full refund of all payments made toward this hazardous, unpermitted installation.

I believe this delay is unreasonable and has caused substantial inconvenience and financial concern. I respectfully request that Bank of America provide documentation regarding : Whether a check was actually issued ; The issuance date ; The mailing date ; The mailing address used ; Whether the check was returned, voided, cancelled, or reissued. 2. Newly Opened Account Approved After In-Person Verification and Then Closed Overnight Without Notice Recently, I opened a new Bank of America account and was instructed to complete in-person identity verification at a Bank of America branch XXXX I completed the identity verification process successfully, and my account was immediately approved. However, the very next morning, I discovered that I could no longer log into online banking. After contacting customer service, I was informed that the account had already been closed. This raises several serious concerns : If Bank of America intended to close the account, why was the account approved immediately after successful in-person identity verification? Why was I permitted to complete branch verification and receive approval only for the account to be terminated overnight? Why was I not provided any meaningful explanation? Why did I receive no notification whatsoever regarding the closure, including no email, text message, secure message, phone call, or written notice? I understand that financial institutions may reserve contractual discretion to close accounts. However, consumers should reasonably expect transparent treatment, consistent communication, and reasonable notice regarding material account status changes, particularly after successful identity verification and account approval. The circumstances surrounding this closure raise concerns about inconsistent handling and lack of transparency. 3. Poor Customer Service and Contradictory Communication When I contacted customer service regarding the newly closed account, the representative repeatedly stated that Bank of America had the right to close my account at any time. While I understand that banks may have contractual authority to close accounts, the representative failed to meaningfully address my concerns, failed to explain why I received no notice, and failed to provide any reasonable path toward resolution. The representatives handling of the situation felt dismissive, unprofessional, and unhelpful. More importantly, Bank of America has repeatedly provided inconsistent and contradictory information regarding the return of my remaining funds from the previously closed account and has failed to provide any meaningful resolution. 4. Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding CBE Group because the company is reporting a collection account on my consumer credit reports that does not belong to me. I do not recognize this account, I never opened or authorized it, and I have no knowledge of any debt that would justify the reporting of this collection account. After discovering the account on my credit reports, I immediately reviewed my records and attempted to determine whether there was any legitimate connection between me and the alleged debt. Despite my efforts, I could not locate any documentation, agreement, contract, billing statement, payment history, or other evidence showing that I am responsible for this account. Because I do not believe this account belongs to me, I became concerned that my personal information may have been used without my authorization. As a result, I filed a report with the Federal Trade Commission and submitted an Identity Theft Report. I took these steps because I genuinely believe that this account may be the result of identity theft, inaccurate reporting, or a mixed-file error. I wanted to ensure that my rights were protected and that there would be an official record documenting my claim that this debt is not mine. The account being reported by CBE Group is appearing as a derogatory collection account and is causing damage to my credit profile. Collection accounts are among the most harmful items that can appear on a consumer credit report because they can significantly lower credit scores and negatively affect a consumer 's ability to obtain credit, secure housing, obtain favorable financing terms, and pursue other financial opportunities. As a result of this reporting, I have suffered unnecessary stress and financial harm. Upon discovering the account, I disputed the information and requested that it be investigated. I informed the appropriate parties that I did not recognize the account and that I had filed an FTC Identity Theft Report. I requested documentation proving that I am legally responsible for the alleged debt. Specifically, I requested evidence showing the origin of the account, the identity of the original creditor, any signed agreements, contracts, applications, billing statements, account records, payment histories, and documentation demonstrating how CBE Group determined that I am the person responsible for the debt. To date, I have not received sufficient documentation proving that I owe this alleged obligation. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires that information reported to consumer reporting agencies be accurate, complete, and capable of verification. It also requires reasonable investigations when consumers dispute information appearing on their credit reports. When a consumer notifies a company that an account may be the result of identity theft and provides an FTC Identity Theft Report, the company should take the matter seriously and conduct a meaningful investigation. Continuing to report information without proper verification undermines the accuracy and integrity of the consumer reporting system. Despite my dispute and identity theft claim, the account continues to be reported. I believe this is unfair because I have never admitted responsibility for the debt and have consistently maintained that the account does not belong to me. The continued reporting of this collection account suggests that either the account has not been properly investigated or that the reporting is based on incomplete or inaccurate information. I am particularly concerned about the lack of documentation supporting the account. If CBE Group believes that I am legally responsible for the debt, there should be documentation establishing that fact. Such documentation should include a signed application or agreement, records showing when the account was opened, records identifying the original creditor, statements showing transactions associated with the account, and evidence demonstrating that I incurred the debt. Without such evidence, there is no basis for continuing to report the account as a verified collection obligation. In addition to the harm caused by the collection account itself, the continued reporting of inaccurate information creates uncertainty regarding the accuracy of my overall credit file. Consumers have a right to expect that the information appearing on their credit reports is accurate and supported by reliable evidence. When an account that does not belong to a consumer is reported as a collection account, it can have long-lasting consequences that extend far beyond the credit report itself. The reporting of this account has negatively affected my financial reputation and has created obstacles that I should not have to face. Credit reports are routinely used by lenders, landlords, insurance companies, and employers when making important decisions. The presence of a collection account that does not belong to me creates an inaccurate picture of my financial history and unfairly places me at a disadvantage. I have acted responsibly throughout this process. Upon learning of the account, I immediately reviewed my records, disputed the information, filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, and requested verification. I have cooperated fully and have made every effort to resolve the issue through the proper channels. Despite these efforts, the account remains on my credit reports and continues to cause harm. I believe that a thorough investigation would reveal that I am not responsible for this debt. If CBE Group is unable to provide documentation proving that I opened, authorized, or benefited from the account, then the account should not continue to be reported. The burden should not fall on me to prove that I did not incur a debt that I do not recognize. Instead, the burden should fall on the company reporting the information to establish that the debt belongs to me through competent evidence. I am requesting that this matter be thoroughly investigated and that CBE Group provide complete documentation supporting its claim that I am responsible for the alleged debt. If the company can not provide such documentation, I request that the account be immediately and permanently removed from all consumer reporting agencies. I also request that any derogatory information associated with the account, including collection status, delinquency indicators, and negative remarks, be deleted. Furthermore, I request that the company explain the procedures used to verify the account after receiving notice of my dispute and identity theft claim. I would like to know what records were reviewed, what information was relied upon, and how the company concluded that the account belonged to me despite my FTC Identity Theft Report. Transparency is essential in situations where consumers are challenging the accuracy of information being reported about them. I am not attempting to avoid responsibility for a legitimate debt. If there is evidence showing that I am legally responsible for the account, I am willing to review that evidence. However, I have not been provided with any documentation establishing that the account belongs to me, and I continue to maintain that I do not own this debt. Until such evidence is produced, the account should not continue to be reported as a verified collection obligation. The relief I am seeking is simple and reasonable. I want CBE Group to conduct a comprehensive investigation, review my FTC Identity Theft Report, verify the account through competent documentation, and remove the account if it can not be substantiated. I also request that all consumer reporting agencies be notified of any corrections or deletions resulting from the investigation so that my credit reports accurately reflect the outcome. In summary, I do not own the CBE Group collection account that is being reported on my credit reports. I discovered the account during a review of my credit file, disputed it immediately, and filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because I believe the account may be the result of identity theft or inaccurate reporting. Despite these efforts, the account continues to be reported and continues to damage my credit profile. I respectfully request a full investigation, complete verification of the account, and permanent deletion of the account and all associated derogatory information if the company can not establish through reliable documentation that I am legally responsible for the debt. I appreciate the CFPB 's assistance in helping ensure that my credit reports contain only accurate, complete, and verifiable information.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding TRUEACCORD because the company is reporting a collection account on my consumer credit reports that I do not recognize and do not believe belongs to me. I have never knowingly opened, authorized, applied for, or accepted responsibility for this alleged account. After discovering the account on my credit reports, I immediately reviewed my financial records and personal documentation in an effort to determine whether there was any legitimate connection between me and the debt being reported. Despite conducting a careful review of my records, I was unable to locate any contracts, agreements, account statements, billing records, payment histories, or other documentation demonstrating that I am responsible for this account. Because I do not recognize the account and have no knowledge of the debt being reported, I became concerned that my personal information may have been used without my authorization. As a result, I filed a report with the Federal Trade Commission and submitted an Identity Theft Report. I took these actions because I genuinely believe that this account may be the result of identity theft, unauthorized use of my personal information, inaccurate reporting, or a mixed-file error. I wanted to ensure that there was an official record documenting my claim that this debt is not mine and that I am disputing responsibility for the account. The TRUEACCORD account is currently being reported as a collection account with a derogatory status and an alleged balance of approximately {$450.00}. Although the amount may seem relatively small, the impact of a collection account on a consumer credit report is significant. Collection accounts are among the most damaging items that can appear on a credit report and can substantially reduce credit scores, increase borrowing costs, and negatively affect a consumer 's ability to obtain financing, housing, insurance, and employment opportunities. The continued reporting of an account that I do not own has caused unnecessary financial harm and has negatively affected my credit profile. Upon discovering the account, I immediately disputed the information and requested a thorough investigation. I informed the appropriate parties that I did not recognize the account and that I had filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because I believed the debt may have resulted from identity theft. I requested documentation proving that I am legally responsible for the account, including any signed applications, contracts, agreements, billing statements, payment histories, account notes, records of communication, and any documents demonstrating that I knowingly entered into a financial relationship giving rise to the debt. Despite my dispute and identity theft claim, the account continues to be reported on my consumer credit reports. I have not been provided with sufficient documentation establishing that I am responsible for the debt. If TRUEACCORD believes that I owe this obligation, there should be clear evidence supporting that conclusion. Such evidence should include documentation identifying the original creditor, records showing when and how the account was opened, documentation establishing that I authorized the account, records demonstrating that I received goods, services, or funds associated with the debt, and documentation showing the legal basis for any collection activity. To date, I have not received information sufficient to establish that the account belongs to me. Instead, the account continues to appear on my credit reports despite my repeated efforts to dispute it and despite the existence of my FTC Identity Theft Report. I believe this is unfair and inconsistent with the requirement that information reported to consumer reporting agencies be accurate and verifiable. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires that furnishers and consumer reporting agencies maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of information reported about consumers. When a consumer disputes information and provides notice that the account may be the result of identity theft, a reasonable investigation must be conducted. Information that can not be verified should not continue to be reported. The continued reporting of a disputed collection account without adequate verification undermines the integrity of the consumer reporting system and causes unnecessary harm to consumers. I am particularly concerned that my identity theft claim has not been given appropriate consideration. Identity theft is a serious problem that can affect consumers for years if fraudulent information remains on their credit reports. Federal law provides important protections for consumers who become victims of identity theft, and those protections exist to prevent consumers from being held responsible for debts they did not incur. When I filed my FTC Identity Theft Report, I expected that the account would receive heightened scrutiny and that meaningful efforts would be made to determine whether the debt actually belongs to me. Instead, the account continues to be reported, and I continue to experience the negative consequences associated with the derogatory information. Every day that this account remains on my credit reports, it has the potential to affect lending decisions, interest rates, housing opportunities, and other aspects of my financial life. Consumers should not be forced to suffer these consequences while inaccurate or fraudulent information remains unresolved. I have acted responsibly throughout this process. Upon discovering the account, I reviewed my records, disputed the information, filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, and requested verification. I have fully cooperated and have made every reasonable effort to resolve the matter through the proper channels. Despite these efforts, the account remains on my credit reports and continues to damage my financial reputation. I am requesting that TRUEACCORD conduct a comprehensive and independent investigation into this matter. I request that the company review all available records and determine whether there is competent evidence demonstrating that I knowingly opened, authorized, or benefited from the account. If the company can not establish through reliable documentation that I am legally responsible for the debt, the account should be immediately removed from all consumer reporting agencies. I also request copies of all documents relied upon to verify the account. These documents should include the original account application, signed agreements, billing statements, payment histories, records identifying the original creditor, documentation showing assignment or transfer of the debt, and any other materials used to determine that I am responsible for the obligation. If such documents do not exist or can not be produced, the account should not continue to be reported. In addition, I request that any derogatory information associated with this account be deleted. This includes collection status designations, derogatory remarks, adverse comments, delinquency indicators, and any other negative reporting connected to the account. Information that can not be verified should not remain on a consumer 's credit report. I am also requesting transparency regarding the investigation process. If TRUEACCORD claims that the account has been verified, I would like a detailed explanation of the procedures used to reach that conclusion. I would like to know what records were reviewed, what evidence was relied upon, and how the company determined that the account belongs to me despite my FTC Identity Theft Report and formal dispute. Consumers deserve meaningful explanations when companies continue reporting disputed information. The relief I am seeking is straightforward. I want TRUEACCORD to review my identity theft claim, conduct a thorough investigation, verify the account through competent evidence, and remove the account if it can not be substantiated. I also request that any corrections or deletions resulting from the investigation be communicated to all consumer reporting agencies so that my credit reports accurately reflect the outcome. I am not attempting to avoid responsibility for a legitimate debt. If documentation exists proving that I knowingly incurred the obligation, I am willing to review that information. However, I have not been provided with such documentation, and I continue to maintain that I do not own this account. Until competent evidence is produced, the account should not continue to be reported as a verified collection account. In summary, I do not believe the TRUEACCORD collection account belongs to me. I discovered the account while reviewing my credit reports, disputed it immediately, and filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because I believe the account may be the result of identity theft or inaccurate reporting. Despite my efforts, the account continues to be reported and continues to negatively affect my credit profile. I respectfully request a full investigation, complete verification of the account through competent documentation, and permanent removal of the account and all associated derogatory information if TRUEACCORD can not establish that I am legally responsible for the debt. I appreciate the CFPB 's assistance in helping ensure that my consumer reports contain only accurate, complete, and verifiable information.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding the extremely poor customer service and account management I have experienced since Citi assumed management of our business credit card account from XXXX. Payments were processed through AutoPay, account access was straightforward, and customer service was responsive when assistance was needed. We later learned that the account had transitioned to Citi. Resolving this issue required multiple phone calls and significant time spent navigating Citi 's customer service system. After finally making a payment over the phone and restoring the account, a second issue arose. We have been unable to gain online access to our business credit card account. For more than two weeks, I have repeatedly contacted Citi seeking assistance. Our objectives are simple : access our statements, monitor account activity, and establish AutoPay to prevent future payment issues. Each interaction follows the same pattern. After waiting 20 to 40 minutes to reach a representative, I am told that a correction has been made and that access should be restored within 24 hours. However, access is never restored, forcing me to call again and repeat the entire process. To date, the issue remains unresolved. In addition to the ongoing access problems, the quality of customer service has been unacceptable. Hold times are excessive, representatives frequently provide inconsistent information, and several interactions have been unprofessional and unhelpful. As a business owner and financial manager, I find it concerning that a major financial institution can not provide reliable access to a business credit card account or resolve a straightforward online access issue despite multiple requests over an extended period. The cumulative effect of these failures has resulted in unnecessary administrative burden, wasted employee time, disruption to business operations, and a complete loss of confidence in Citi 's ability to manage our account. I am requesting that Citi : Immediately restore full online access to our business credit card account. Ensure AutoPay can be established and verified. Provide an explanation regarding the account freeze and why no notification was provided. Review the customer service failures and repeated inability to resolve this issue despite numerous contacts. Our company intends to move our business relationship elsewhere as soon as practical. However, I believe the CFPB should be aware of the significant customer service and account management deficiencies we have experienced since Citi assumed control of this account.

A reasonable consumer should not be expected to assume that prominently displayed promotional benefits shown within a personalized booking experience do not apply to them. Nor should consumers be expected to search through extensive terms and conditions to determine whether American Express is displaying benefits for which they are ineligible despite knowing the card product associated with the account. The advertised benefits were material to my purchasing decision. Had I known that I would not receive the advertised {$600.00} statement credit, the anticipated XXXX rewards earnings, and the {$250.00} hotel property credit, I would have reevaluated my options and may have booked directly with the hotel or through another provider. During that conversation, XXXX acknowledged that he understood how a reasonable consumer could be confused by the manner in which the promotion was presented. He recognized that the advertising and booking experience could lead a cardmember to believe they were eligible for the advertised benefits. However, despite acknowledging the confusion, XXXX advised that the only resolution he could offer was cancellation of the reservation. He stated that he was unable to provide any goodwill accommodation, statement credit, points adjustment, travel credit, or any other remedy. I respectfully request that American Express review this matter and provide an appropriate resolution. Consumers should be able to rely on promotions displayed within their authenticated account experience without having to independently determine whether American Express is presenting benefits that do not apply to the account they are actively using. Later that morning, after speaking directly with jail personnel, I was informed that I had been the victim of a scam. The officer immediately recognized the fraud pattern and advised me that the payment was not part of the official bond process. At approximately XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>, I immediately contacted Wells Fargo Fraud and reported the incident. Wells Fargo assigned fraud case number XXXX. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau 's Office of Servicemember Affairs specifically serves veterans like myself. Navy Federal markets itself as an institution dedicated to serving the military community and veterans, making their deceptive practices especially egregious.

To Whom It May Concern : SPS 's response fails to address the core issue raised in my complaint. Even after multiple complaints and SPS 's acknowledgment that my privately obtained homeowner 's insurance was in force and costs approximately {$200.00} per month, SPS continued charging me approximately {$760.00} per month for insurance-related escrow collections and continued sending notices regarding force-placed insurance. At this point, I have no other words to describe this experience other than incompetence. I can not believe I am still being required to spend my time correcting servicing errors after repeatedly bringing them to SPS 's attention. Following my most recent call with SPS, I was finally able to speak with a representative who reviewed the account and confirmed that there were significant errors in the servicing and escrow calculations. During that conversation, I was advised that I should expect a credit in excess of {$12000.00} as a result of the mistakes that had been made. This directly contradicts SPS 's written position that no servicing errors occurred. My concern extends beyond my individual account. A borrower who did not have the mortgage knowledge, persistence, or financial resources to challenge these charges could easily find themselves facing severe financial hardship. Repeatedly increasing a borrower 's monthly payment based on inaccurate escrow and insurance calculations creates unnecessary payment shock and can place borrowers at risk of delinquency or foreclosure. The purpose of a mortgage servicer is to accurately administer the loan, protect the collateral, and properly account for borrower funds. Instead, SPS repeatedly demanded payment amounts based on insurance charges that should not have existed and continued doing so after receiving notice that valid insurance coverage was already in place. My original payment obligation was approximately {$2000.00} per month for principal and interest. As a result of SPS 's escrow administration, force-placed insurance charges, and related escrow shortages, my required monthly payment increased dramatically. At one point, SPS demanded monthly payments approaching {$3600.00}. This represents an increase of more than 70 % over the original payment obligation and is entirely inconsistent with the affordability of the loan as originally underwritten. No reasonable borrower would anticipate or budget for such a dramatic increase, particularly when the increase is driven by insurance charges that SPS is now apparently acknowledging were improper. The financial impact of such servicing errors can not be overstated. Many consumers would simply assume the servicer 's calculations were correct and either deplete savings attempting to comply or fall behind on their mortgage obligations. I also repeatedly requested escrow removal through customer service and SPS 's online portal. Those requests were ignored or inadequately addressed. SPS now relies on documentation that appears inconsistent with the account history and the servicing actions taken. SPS attached what appears to be an unsigned escrow acknowledgment document while simultaneously maintaining and administering an escrow account over my repeated objections and waiver requests. Most troubling is that SPS 's response largely restates information already known to me while failing to address the repeated servicing errors, excessive insurance charges, continued force-placed insurance notices, ignored escrow waiver requests, and the substantial financial harm these actions could have caused. Given the apparent admission by SPS personnel that substantial credits are owed due to servicing mistakes, I respectfully request that this matter receive additional regulatory review. The pattern of errors described above raises serious concerns regarding SPS 's escrow administration, force-placed insurance practices, customer complaint handling, quality control procedures, and oversight of borrower accounts. Consumers should not be forced to spend months correcting servicing mistakes or defending themselves against inflated payment demands that were never properly supported. Nor should borrowers be subjected to repeated force-placed insurance notices after valid insurance coverage has been provided and acknowledged. I respectfully request that SPS provide a complete accounting of all insurance premiums charged, all force-placed insurance activity, all escrow analyses, all resulting payment increases, and all credits due to the account. I further request that regulators review whether SPS 's practices in this matter are consistent with its obligations to borrowers and applicable servicing standards. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Subject : CFPB Complaint Against AutoNation Finance, Representative XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX To Whom It May Concern : I am filing this complaint against AutoNation Finance, its representative XXXX XXXX, and its repossession vendor, XXXX XXXX, regarding what I believe to be unfair, unreasonable, and potentially deceptive practices related to the repossession and redemption of my vehicle. After being advised of the amount necessary to redeem my vehicle, I immediately made the payment required by AutoNation Finance. The funds used for the payment were legitimate, deposited into my bank account, available for use, and successfully processed. I provided AutoNation Finance with the documentation requested, including bank statements showing the deposit of funds, proof of payment, and evidence that the funds had cleared through my financial institution. Despite providing the requested information, AutoNation Finance and XXXX XXXX continued to demand additional documentation. After I supplied the exact bank statement requested, I was informed that it was not sufficient and was then asked to provide a running bank statement. After complying with that request, additional questions and documentation requests continued to be made. At no point was I provided with a clear explanation as to why the original documents were insufficient. Each time I complied with a request, new requirements were added. It appeared that the goalposts were continually being moved, creating delays in the release of my vehicle despite my full cooperation and proof that the payment had been made and cleared. I believe these repeated requests were excessive, unreasonable, and inconsistent. As a consumer, I felt as though I was being subjected to scrutiny beyond what would normally be required to verify a legitimate payment. The delays prevented me from promptly recovering my vehicle and caused significant financial hardship, inconvenience, and emotional distress. I am also concerned about the conduct of XXXX XXXX, the repossession company hired by AutoNation Finance. At the time of the repossession, representatives of XXXX XXXX interacted with my daughter regarding the vehicle keys. According to my daughter, she was told that she needed to surrender the keys and that failure to do so could result in additional charges, fees, or other financial consequences. As a result of those statements, she felt pressured and intimidated into complying. She believed she had no choice and that refusing to provide the keys would result in additional penalties. The interaction caused unnecessary stress and emotional distress. I believe consumers and their family members should not be subjected to intimidation or pressure tactics during the repossession process. Additionally, after the vehicle was repossessed, I attempted to locate it through law enforcement channels. I discovered that the repossession had not yet been reported to the police database. Based upon the information available to me, there was approximately a two-to-three-hour delay between the repossession and the reporting of the vehicles location. Because the repossession had not yet been reported, I was unable to determine where my vehicle had been taken through normal channels. Instead, I was forced to use my vehicles tracking technology to locate it myself. I ultimately identified the location and researched the towing company independently. This delay prevented me from promptly locating my vehicle and raised concerns that unnecessary storage fees and additional charges could accrue while I was attempting to determine where the vehicle had been taken. Consumers should not be forced to independently track their own vehicles because repossession information has not been timely reported. When viewed together, the actions of AutoNation Finance, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX created what appears to be a pattern of unnecessary delays and obstacles : My vehicle was repossessed. Payment was made to redeem the vehicle. Proof of payment and bank documentation were provided. Additional documentation requests continued after compliance. The repossession was not immediately reported, making it difficult to locate the vehicle. My daughter was pressured into surrendering the keys under threat of additional fees and charges. Delays continued despite proof that the payment was legitimate and cleared. As a result, I experienced financial damages, loss of use of my vehicle, emotional distress, inconvenience, and additional expenses. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate AutoNation Finance, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX to determine whether their actions complied with applicable consumer protection laws and industry standards. I also request a review of their payment verification procedures, repossession practices, consumer communications, and any actions that may have unnecessarily delayed the release of my vehicle or increased my costs. I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including bank statements, payment confirmations, correspondence, screenshots from vehicle tracking systems, and other records relevant to this complaint. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX

Description of the Problem : I am a long-standing customer of Synchrony Bank holding a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX store credit card. I am filing this complaint regarding a {$4600.00} deferred interest charge that was applied to my account upon the expiration of a promotional financing period that ended XX/XX/year>. Because of this, I was not actively monitoring paper statements for a specific expiration date. I did not become aware that the promotional period had ended and that a deferred interest charge had been applied until my XX/XX/year> statement reflected a balance increase to {$12000.00} a jump that was not consistent with my normal payment activity and immediately flagged my attention. Upon discovering the charge on XX/XX/year>, I contacted Synchrony Bank the same day and offered to pay the remaining principal balance in full in exchange for a one-time courtesy reversal of the deferred interest charge. I was transferred to three separate representatives in an attempt to reach someone with the authority to address my request. Each representative I spoke with was dismissive and declined to escalate the matter meaningfully, despite my documented history as a long-term customer with a perfect payment record and no prior delinquencies. My concerns are as follows : 1. Inadequate notification prior to promotional expiration. I received a single notification of the promotional expiration buried within my XX/XX/year> paper statement. Because I am enrolled in autopay a feature Synchrony itself offers and promotes as a convenience I did not open that statement. I received no email notification, no SMS alert, and no separate mailing drawing attention to the impending expiration of a promotion with a {$4600.00} consequence. A single line in a paper statement, sent to a customer enrolled in autopay, does not constitute clear and conspicuous disclosure under the standard a charge of this magnitude requires. Industry practice for deferred interest expiration notifications includes proactive multi-channel outreach precisely because the financial consequence is severe and retroactive. 2. Deferred interest is an inherently predatory structure. Unlike standard interest which accrues incrementally, deferred interest charges the full retroactive interest in a lump sum, creating a financial shock that bears no relationship to the consumer 's payment behavior. I made every payment on time. I was not delinquent. Yet I was hit with a {$4600.00} charge in a single billing cycle. This practice disproportionately harms consumers who are acting in good faith. 3. Failure to provide meaningful customer resolution. Upon contacting Synchrony on XX/XX/year> the same day I discovered the charge I acted in good faith and offered to pay the full principal balance immediately. Synchrony 's representatives refused to consider any accommodation, offered no path to escalation, and provided no written response or follow-up. This is inconsistent with reasonable customer service standards and suggests a systemic practice of denying reversal requests regardless of individual account history or circumstances. Requested Resolution : I am requesting a full reversal of the {$4600.00} deferred interest charge as a one-time courtesy, with the understanding that I will pay the remaining principal balance in full upon confirmation of the reversal. Alternatively, I am open to a negotiated partial reversal. I am not seeking to avoid my legitimate financial obligation I am seeking relief from a charge that I believe was inadequately disclosed and that Synchrony 's customer service refused to address in good faith. I have been a loyal customer with a perfect payment record and I am asking for the same consideration any reasonable financial institution should extend to a customer in good standing.

The funding bank has paid the company, the consumer has verified the manual labor was completed perfectly, and both accounts have undergone extensive identity matching. Consumer complaint narrative: U.S. Bank is improperly withholding a portion of insurance proceeds from a homeowners insurance claim despite clear documentation showing that part of the insured loss is not related to, and is not secured by, the mortgage collateral. We have provided repeated documentation including parcel maps, deed/loan origination appraisal records, and aerial imagery clearly demonstrating that the damaged outbuildings are located on separate parcels of land that are owned free and clear and are not included in the legal description of the mortgaged property. Despite this, U.S. Bank is holding insurance funds and applying internal repair completion requirements as a condition for release, including requiring proof of repairs based on a third-party inspection that assessed overall percent repaired. These requirements are being applied to the entire insurance claim, including structures that are not part of the mortgaged collateral. Property / Claim Details : * Mortgage covers primary dwelling and approximately XXXX acres of land. * Damaged outbuildings are located on separate parcels not subject to the mortgage deed of trust. * One damaged structure is a portable carport added AFTER loan origination, & is going to be removed from the property. * Dwelling damage has been fully repaired and verified ( ~ {$1400.00} ). We have clearly stated that we are not rebuilding or repairing the outbuildings. All remaining damaged structures will be demolished and removed, and as previously stated, U.S Bank has no legal say or stake in structures belonging to us, and not tied to the mortgage collateral what so ever. Problem : U.S. Bank is refusing to release insurance proceeds associated with non-mortgaged parcels unless internal repair completion thresholds are met ( e.g., percentage-based repair requirements from third-party inspection results ). These conditions are being applied despite the fact that portions of the insured loss are not part of the mortgaged collateral and therefore should not be subject to mortgage servicing control. We have repeatedly provided documentation proving parcel separation and ownership, but the funds continue to be withheld without clear contractual or legal justification. Requested Resolution : We request that CFPB require U.S. Bank to : XXXX. Provide a written contractual/legal basis for withholding insurance proceeds tied to non-mortgaged parcels. XXXX. Immediately release insurance proceeds associated with structures located outside the mortgaged collateral. XXXX. Correct their loss draft handling to ensure insurance proceeds are allocated based on collateral interest, not blanket repair completion requirements. Timeline of Events : * XXXX : Insurance claim filed following storm damage affecting multiple outbuildings and dwelling. * XXXX : Insurance company issued a single claim check payable to both borrower and U.S. Bank due to mortgagee clause requirements. * XXXX : Started the process of mailing claims check to U.S Bank Loss draft department. Was told that day by XXXX different customer representatives that we would qualify for their waterfall process due to the uniqueness of our situation, and would receive the funds in full, mailed back to us in check form, made payable only to us. * XXXX : Bank began holding portion of insurance proceeds under standard loss draft procedures ( approx. funds above {$40000.00} threshold ). Provided initial documentation including parcel maps, appraisal reports, legal descriptions, insurance details, and explanation that damaged structures are located on separate parcels not tied to the mortgage. * Between XXXX and XXXX : received several different phone calls in that time period, all from different representatives offering different information each time. Some stating the first {$40000.00} was being mailed to us, some stating the remaining funds were also being released, others stating no funds would be released until an inspection was complete. * XXXX : Bank ( or loss draft department ) requested third-party inspection to verify repairs. * XXXX : Virtual Inspection completed ; inspector acknowledged issue and indicated understanding that certain structures were outside mortgage scope. * XXXX : After inspection, Bank representative claimed inspection showed approximately 30 % repairs completed and stated XXXX % repair completion required to release remaining funds. We reiterated that no repairs will be made to outbuildings ; structures will be demolished. Only dwelling repairs were completed ( approx. ~ {$1400.00} ) and verified with inspector. * Current : U.S. Bank continues to withhold remaining insurance proceeds despite documentation showing non-mortgaged parcel ownership and lack of collateral interest. We have exhausted normal servicing channels without resolution. We are requesting prompt intervention as this issue can not be resolved through standard servicing channels and continues to result in improper withholding of funds not tied to the mortgage collateral.

Consumer complaint narrative: CFPB XXXX XXXX Rocket Mortgage Mortgage XXXX XXXX XXXX Account XXXX XXXX RESPA / Regulation X Issues Loan No. : XXXX I am filing this complaint against Rocket Mortgage regarding a serious mortgage-servicing and escrow-accounting dispute. Rocket recently increased my monthly escrow requirement and claimed a significant escrow shortage. I submitted a formal Notice of Error and Request for Information / Qualified Written Request asking Rocket to validate the escrow shortage, provide a complete escrow ledger, and support all tax, insurance, and escrow disbursements with documentation. Rocket acknowledged receipt but directed me to contact the Servicing Team by phone instead of providing the requested written documentation and written explanation. This is not appropriate for a formal mortgage-servicing dispute involving escrow calculations, alleged amounts due, tax disbursements, insurance disbursements, payment application, and possible errors in account records. I need written documentation, not only verbal explanations. My concerns include : Rocket has not provided a complete escrow ledger showing all deposits, disbursements, shortage repayments, tax payments, insurance payments, corrections, reversals, and running escrow balances. Rocket appears to be treating a prior escrow shortage as a new shortage without first clearly reconciling all escrow payments already collected from me. Rocket has not fully explained why the shortage repayment structure changed and why the monthly escrow demand increased significantly. Rocket has not adequately supported certain tax disbursements that appear to have created the original escrow shortage. Rockets records appear inconsistent regarding homeowners/hazard insurance disbursements, and I am concerned that an insurance payment may have been duplicated or incorrectly included in the escrow analysis. Rockets online escrow information appears inconsistent with its mortgage statements regarding the escrow balance. Rocket has not identified the current owner/investor of my loan or explained whether Rocket is the loan owner, servicer, master servicer, subservicer, or acting on behalf of another investor. I believe this may involve potential RESPA / Regulation X issues, including failure to properly investigate and respond to a Notice of Error / Request for Information, failure to provide a complete escrow accounting, failure to validate an escrow shortage, possible payment-application errors, and possible unsupported escrow charges. I am not refusing to pay my mortgage. I have continued paying the undisputed monthly amount that Rocket previously accepted and applied. I dispute only the unsupported escrow increase and any additional amount based on an escrow calculation that has not been properly validated. I request CFPB assistance requiring Rocket Mortgage to : Provide a complete written escrow ledger from the time the disputed shortage was created through the present. Provide proof of all tax, homeowners/hazard insurance, and mortgage insurance disbursements charged to my escrow account. Reconcile all escrow payments collected from me and explain how each payment was applied. Explain the basis for the current claimed escrow shortage and the increased monthly escrow requirement. Correct the escrow analysis if any tax or insurance disbursement was duplicated, misapplied, unsupported, reversed, refunded, or incorrectly calculated. Identify the current owner/investor of my mortgage loan. Provide all substantive responses, calculations, and supporting documents in writing. Refrain from late fees, negative credit reporting, delinquency treatment, or collection activity based on the disputed escrow increase while the formal dispute is under review. I am requesting that Rocket Mortgage be required to validate the escrow shortage with complete documentation before demanding or collecting the disputed increased escrow amount.
